This synthon can be incorporated into larger cage architectures through functionalization of the catecholate aromatic rings or through secondary coordination to the arsenic lone pair.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral arsenic(III) catecholate complexes that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. The system features an As(III) center chelated by two catecholate ligands in a tetrahedral geometry, creating a bowl-shaped electron-deficient cavity with significant positive electrostatic potential. The arsenic center's lone pair provides additional Lewis basic character, while the catecholate oxygens can participate in hydrogen bonding. The electron-deficient aromatic rings of the catecholate ligands create strong anion-π interactions with halide or oxoanions, encapsulating them in a tetrahedral arrangement when four such units assemble. The As-O bonds provide moderate covalent character with ionic contribution, making the system redox-active and potentially responsive to electrochemical switching. This synthon combines metal coordination (As-O), anion-π interactions, electrostatic complementarity, and directional hydrogen bonding in a single modular unit suitable for constructing supramolecular cages and capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organoarsenic cations (e.g., tetraphenylarsonium or trialkylarylarsonium) that function as anion-π capsule formers. The synthon exploits two complementary interactions: (1) strong electrostatic and anion-π interactions between the cationic arsenic center (As⁺) and electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, nitroaromatics, or cyanostars) that serve as anion-π acceptors, and (2) secondary C–H···anion or C–H···π contacts from the alkyl/aryl substituents on arsenic that help preorganize the assembly. The tetrahedral geometry of the As⁺ cation directs four aromatic panels into a capsule-like architecture that can encapsulate anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻) via multi-dentate anion-π interactions. This represents an underexplored pnictogen-based supramolecular motif with potential in anion sensing, transport, or templated cage synthesis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) cation (e.g., [Ga(phen)₂]³⁺ or [Ga(bipy)₂]³⁺, where phen = 1,10-phenanthroline, bipy = 2,2'-bipyridine) acting as a cationic, electron-deficient π-acidic face. This face engages in strong, directional anion-π interactions with complementary anionic species (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻) or anionic π-systems (e.g., tetracyanoquinodimethane radical anion, TCNQ˙⁻). The synthon's recognition elements are: 1) the positively charged Ga(III) center, 2) the planar, π-deficient aromatic ligands (phen/bipy) that create an electrostatic potential minimum above their centroids, and 3) the tetrahedral geometry that presents three such π-acidic faces for multi-point binding. This enables the assembly of 3D capsules or cages when combined with multi-anionic connectors or through dimerization with large polyoxometalate anions. It maps to the primitives as: Donor/Acceptor (anion as donor, Ga-π-system as acceptor), Charged (cationic metal center, anionic guest), Shape (tetrahedral geometry, planar π-faces), and can involve Redox if using redox-active anions. This explores the underexplored supramolecular domain using a less common p-block metal (gallium) in a cationic anion-π host role.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boronium cations [R3B]+ (where R = aryl or alkyl groups with electron-withdrawing substituents) that engage in dual interaction modes: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the Lewis acidic boron center, and (2) parallel anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic rings on the R substituents. The tetrahedral geometry of the boronium cation creates a convergent binding pocket that can encapsulate anions like Cl-, Br-, or BF4- through a combination of direct B⁺···X⁻ coordination and peripheral arene···X⁻ interactions. This represents a novel anion receptor motif distinct from traditional ammonium or phosphonium systems, leveraging both the strong Lewis acidity of three-coordinate boron cations and the tunable π-acidity of flanking aromatic groups. The synthon can be mapped to primitives: electrostatics (B⁺-X⁻), dispersion (anion-π), shape (tetrahedral convergence), and tunable through substituent effects on both boron Lewis acidity and arene π-acidity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boronium cations [R₃B-L]⁺ (where L is a neutral Lewis base ligand like pyridine or THF) that engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The cationic boron center (formally B(III) with a formal positive charge) provides electrostatic complementarity to anions, while the tetrahedral geometry directs three aromatic arms (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl, or triazine groups) to form a convergent, capsule-like binding pocket. Recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic attraction between the boronium cation and anionic guests (halides, tetrafluoroborate, etc.), (2) anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-deficient π-systems on the arms, (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from aromatic C–H groups, and (4) geometric preorganization from the tetrahedral core. This system is chemically realistic, drawing from known triarylborane Lewis acids and their boronium adducts, but extends into supramolecular capsule design via convergent anion-π interactions. It maps to primitives: electrostatics (cation–anion), dispersion (anion-π, π-stacking), geometry (tetrahedral), dynamics (guest exchange), and information (convergent recognition).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_bismuthonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral bismuthonium cation [R₃Bi]⁺ (where R = bulky aryl or alkyl groups) that acts as a cationic template for anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system forms a dynamic capsule-like structure where the central bismuthonium cation's positive charge is partially delocalized, creating a strong electrostatic field that organizes four electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or cyanophenyl derivatives) into a tetrahedral arrangement around it. These aromatic panels simultaneously engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with a central anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) located at the capsule's core. The recognition elements include: (1) the tetrahedral bismuthonium cation as a structure-directing cationic center, (2) electron-deficient arenes as anion-π acceptors, and (3) a central anion as the guest. Interaction patterns involve electrostatic attraction, anion-π interactions, and potentially weak C–H···anion contacts. This synthon maps to primitives as: A (bismuthonium cation as +), B (anion as –), C (arenes as planar π-systems), D (tetrahedral geometry), E (capsule as closed assembly), F (electrostatic/anion-π as interaction), and G (dynamic assembly/disassembly as temporal aspect).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boronium cations [R3B]+ (where R = aryl or alkyl groups with electron-withdrawing substituents) that engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The cationic boron center (formally B(III) with empty p-orbital character) provides strong electrostatic attraction for anions, while the planar electron-deficient arene substituents (e.g., tetrafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl) create complementary anion-π binding sites. This creates a 3D capsule-like recognition motif where anions are sandwiched between cationic boron centers and electron-poor π-systems. The synthon exhibits directional bonding preferences due to the tetrahedral geometry of the boronium cation and planar arrangement of the arenes, enabling predictable assembly into larger coordination networks or discrete capsules. Recognition elements: (1) cationic boronium center (Lewis acidic, electrostatic), (2) electron-deficient π-systems (anion-π acceptors), (3) tunable substituents on boron for steric/electronic control. Mappable to primitives: positive charge (boronium), negative charge (anion), π-system (arene), tetrahedral geometry, directional electrostatic interactions, and programmable assembly via substituent modification.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphazenium cations (R3P=N+=PR3) paired with electron-deficient aromatic anions through cooperative anion-π and electrostatic interactions. The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral phosphazenium cation with four cationic centers arranged tetrahedrally around a central nitrogen, creating a strong electrostatic field; (2) electron-deficient polyfluorinated or polynitro aromatic anions (e.g., hexafluorobenzene radical anion, tetracyanoquinodimethane derivatives) that serve as π-acidic platforms; (3) directional anion-π interactions between the cationic centers and the electron-deficient π-systems; (4) additional C-H···π and electrostatic stabilization. This system forms self-assembled capsule-like structures in solution and solid state, with the tetrahedral cation acting as a 'corner' unit and anions as 'face' units, creating a 3D network suitable for anion recognition, encapsulation, and supramolecular catalysis. The synthon maps to primitives: electrostatics (cation-anion), π-interactions (anion-π), directional preferences (tetrahedral geometry), complementarity (charge/π-surface matching), preorganization (rigid cation), cooperativity (multiple interactions), and reversibility (non-covalent assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphazenium cations ([R₃P=N-PR₃]⁺) paired with electron-deficient aromatic anions through cooperative anion-π interactions and electrostatic complementarity. The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral cationic core with four peripheral aromatic arms (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) creating an electron-deficient π-surface; (2) complementary tetrahedral anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻, or BArF⁻) that nest within the cationic cavity via anion-π interactions with the electron-poor aromatic walls; (3) additional C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from alkyl/aryl substituents on phosphorus; (4) geometrically matched tetrahedral symmetry enabling self-assembly into 3D cage or capsule architectures. This system exploits the strong, directional anion-π interactions of electron-deficient aromatics combined with the high charge density and steric definition of phosphazenium cations—a previously unexplored combination for supramolecular capsule formation.

synthons.name: tetracationic_cyclophane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetracationic cyclophane host with extended π-surfaces that forms a capsule-like structure through cooperative anion-π interactions with polyatomic anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or SbF₆⁻). The cyclophane features four positively charged nitrogen centers (quaternary ammonium or pyridinium) integrated into a macrocyclic framework with aromatic panels (benzene, naphthalene, or biphenyl units). The electron-deficient π-surfaces create multiple convergent anion-binding sites, while the rigid geometry enforces a defined cavity. Recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic attraction between cations and anions, (2) anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes, (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from methylene or aromatic C–H groups, and (4) geometric complementarity for anion encapsulation. This synthon maps to primitives: electrostatics (cation–anion), polarization (anion-π), dispersion (π-system stacking), repulsion (steric control of cavity size), coordination (multivalent binding), topology (macrocyclic confinement), and dynamics (reversible anion binding/release).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_stibonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral stibonium cations (R₄Sb⁺) that function as anion-π acceptors, forming encapsulation complexes with electron-rich aromatic anions. The stibonium center possesses a pronounced σ-hole along each Sb–C bond axis due to the electronegativity difference and the formal positive charge, creating directional anion-binding sites. These cations can coordinate with planar polycyano- or polyfluoro-substituted aromatic anions (e.g., tetracyanoquinodimethane radical anion, TCNQ•⁻) through cooperative anion-π interactions and electrostatic complementarity. The tetrahedral geometry predisposes the system to form dimeric or tetrameric capsules that encapsulate anion pairs or clusters, stabilized by additional C–H···anion and π‑stacking interactions. This synthon exploits the underutilized pnictogen bonding capability of antimony(V) in supramolecular anion recognition and cage formation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphazenium cations (R3P=N-P+R3) paired with electron-deficient aromatic anions through cooperative anion-π interactions. The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral phosphazenium cation with four organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, alkyl) creating a cationic core with directional N-P+ bonds, (2) planar polycyano- or polyfluoro-substituted aromatic anions (e.g., tetracyanoquinodimethane derivatives, hexafluorobenzene derivatives) serving as π-acidic platforms, (3) multiple simultaneous anion-π interactions between the cationic phosphorus center's localized positive charge and the electron-deficient π-clouds, (4) secondary C-H···anion and C-H···N contacts from cation substituents, (5) potential for encapsulation of smaller anions or solvent molecules within the tetrahedral cavity, (6) tunable cavity size via substituent bulk on both cation and anion, and (7) redox-active or photoresponsive variants possible through functionalized aromatic systems. This represents a distinct class from previously proposed iodonium/phosphonium capsules due to the P=N-P+ core's unique electronic structure and stronger directionality.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphazenium cations [P(NR₂)₄]⁺ (where R = alkyl or aryl groups) that function as anion-binding hosts through a combination of electrostatic interactions and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon features a tetrahedral cationic core with four extended arms terminating in electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or pyrazine rings) that create a convergent binding pocket for anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻). The recognition elements include: (1) the central quaternary phosphorus(V) cation providing strong electrostatic attraction, (2) directional anion-π interactions between the anion and the electron-deficient π-systems, (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from the N-alkyl/aryl substituents, and (4) tunable cavity size via arm length and π-system selection. This system maps to primitives as: A (anion) + D (π-system) + E (electrostatic) + F (directional) + G (convergent pocket) + potential B (hydrogen bond donor) + C (temporal control via pH or redox changes to the phosphazenium stability).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral telluronium cation [R₄Te]⁺ (where R = aryl or alkyl groups with electron-withdrawing substituents) that acts as a cationic π-acidic surface. The synthon recognizes and encapsulates anions through cooperative anion-π interactions with the four electron-deficient aromatic faces of the telluronium substituents, forming a tetrahedral 'capsule' around the anion. The heavy chalcogen center provides enhanced polarizability and stronger electrostatic contributions compared to lighter analogs, while the tetrahedral geometry creates a preorganized cavity. Recognition elements include: (1) the positively charged tellurium center for electrostatic attraction, (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings on each substituent for anion-π interactions, and (3) potential secondary C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from alkyl/aryl C–H groups. This maps to primitives as: A (telluronium cation) + B (anion) + directional anion-π interactions + tetrahedral geometry creating a cavity (capsule).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphazenium cations (R3P=N+-PR3) that function as anion-π acceptors and capsule-forming building blocks. The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral phosphazenium core with four cationic nitrogen centers arranged in a tetrahedral geometry, creating a positively charged cavity; (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) attached to each arm, providing multiple anion-π interaction sites; (3) tunable alkyl/aryl substituents on phosphorus for solubility and steric control; (4) complementary anionic guests (BF4-, PF6-, ClO4-) that engage in cooperative anion-π interactions within the cavity; (5) self-assembly into dimeric capsules via cation-anion interactions and π-stacking of the electron-deficient panels; (6) potential for temporal control via pH-responsive protonation/deprotonation of the phosphazenium nitrogen; (7) mapping to all seven primitives through directional interactions, complementary surfaces, and dynamic assembly/disassembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral telluronium cations (R4Te+) that function as anion-π acceptors. The telluronium center possesses a σ-hole on the tellurium atom due to its tetrahedral geometry and positive charge, creating strong electrostatic interactions with electron-rich π-systems of aromatic anions (such as carboxylates, phenoxides, or tetraphenylborate derivatives). The synthon combines (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) anion-π interaction between the anion and the electron-deficient region above/below the telluronium-bound aromatic rings (if present), and (3) potential auxiliary C–H···anion or π–π stacking interactions from ligand aryl groups. This system is chemically realistic as telluronium salts are known stable species, and the anion-π interaction with telluronium is underexplored compared to lighter chalcogen analogs. The tetrahedral geometry directs the formation of capsule-like or cage-like assemblies when combined with complementary anionic building blocks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphazenium cations (R3P=N-P+R3) paired with electron-deficient aromatic anions through cooperative anion-π and electrostatic interactions. The synthon features a cationic phosphorus(V) center with four organic substituents arranged tetrahedrally, creating a strong electrostatic field that complements the electron-deficient π-system of anions like tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ) derivatives or nitroaromatics. The recognition elements include: (1) the tetrahedral cationic charge center for electrostatic attraction, (2) electron-deficient aromatic anions with quadrupole moments favorable for anion-π interactions, (3) tunable substituents on both cation and anion for steric matching, and (4) potential for encapsulation behavior when combined with additional π-stacking interactions between aromatic wings. This system maps to primitives through charge (cation/anion), shape (tetrahedral/planar), polarity (electron-deficient π-system), and directional electrostatic/anion-π interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_stibonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral stibonium cations (R4Sb+) that function as anion-π acceptors, forming encapsulation complexes with planar anionic guests. The system features: (1) tetrahedral stibonium cations with four organic substituents (alkyl/aryl) creating a cationic center with σ-hole character on antimony, (2) planar polycyano or polyoxoanions (e.g., [TCNE]⁻, [C4(CN)8]²⁻, or [Mo6O19]²⁻) as π-rich guests, (3) anion-π interactions between the cationic antimony center and the π-system of the anion, (4) complementary electrostatic and dispersion forces, (5) capsule formation through multiple stibonium cations surrounding a single anion, creating a tetrahedral coordination environment. This represents an underexplored pnictogen-bonding variant where the heavy pnictogen (Sb) in a tetrahedral cation acts as an anion-π acceptor rather than a conventional Lewis acid.

synthons.name: diboronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a rigid diboronate ester scaffold featuring two terminal boronate ester groups that can reversibly bind diols, creating a concave, electron-deficient aromatic surface. The central core contains a tetrafluorobenzene or similar electron-deficient arene that provides strong anion-π interaction sites. This system functions as a modular cage synthon where: (1) the boronate ester groups provide reversible covalent/temporal binding of diol-containing linkers, (2) the electron-deficient aromatic surface provides multiple directional anion-π recognition sites for anions like chloride, nitrate, or carboxylates, and (3) the rigid scaffold preorganizes these interactions to form cage-like structures when combined with appropriate complementary components. The seven primitives map as: Atoms (B, O, C, F, H), Bonds (B-O covalent, B-O coordination, anion-π noncovalent), Angles (tetrahedral B, planar arene), Dihedrals (rigid scaffold conformation), Rings (aromatic, boronate ester cycles), Charges (partial negative on anions, partial positive on arene center), and Dynamics (reversible boronate ester formation).

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_azobenzene_anion_π_switch
synthons.description: A reversible temporal synthon system based on azobenzene photoisomerization coupled with anion-π interactions. The system features an electron-deficient tetrafluorophenyl-substituted azobenzene core that can bind anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) via anion-π interactions in its planar trans configuration (λ > 420 nm irradiation). Upon UV irradiation (λ ≈ 365 nm), photoisomerization to the bent cis configuration disrupts the planar π-surface and anion binding pocket, releasing the anion. The cis-to-trans back-isomerization occurs thermally or with visible light, restoring anion binding. This creates a temporally controlled anion binding/release cycle driven by light, with clear recognition elements (electron-deficient arene, azobenzene photoswitch) and interaction patterns (anion-π, photochemical E/Z isomerization). The seven primitives map as: 1) electron-deficient arene (acceptor), 2) anion (donor), 3) π-system (scaffold), 4) photochromic unit (regulator), 5) non-covalent interaction (anion-π), 6) temporal control (light/thermal), 7) reversible binding (switch).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) with aromatic substituents that forms a capsule-like structure through cooperative anion-π interactions with tetrahedral anions (e.g., ClO₄⁻, BF₄⁻). The phosphonium center provides a permanent positive charge, while the extended aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl, naphthyl, or pyridyl groups) orient to create electron-deficient π-surfaces. These surfaces engage in multiple, directional anion-π interactions with the oxygens of perchlorate or fluorines of tetrafluoroborate, leading to a self-assembled capsule with the anion encapsulated within the aromatic cage. The synthon is modular—varying the aromatic substituents tunes the cavity size and electron deficiency, while changing the anion alters the interaction strength. This system exemplifies a charge-assisted, shape-complementary supramolecular motif with potential for selective anion recognition or as a building block for larger porous frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_stibonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral stibonium cation (R₄Sb⁺) that acts as a cationic π-acidic capsule host for anions through cooperative anion-π interactions. The four aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) attached to the central antimony(V) create a convergent, electron-deficient cavity. Anions (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻) are encapsulated via multipoint anion-π interactions with the inwardly-facing π-systems, while the positive charge on antimony enhances anion binding electrostatically. The synthon exhibits preorganized geometry for anion recognition, with the heavy pnictogen (Sb) providing polarizability and Lewis acidic character. This system maps to primitives: (1) tetrahedral cation as core, (2) aromatic rings as π-acidic panels, (3) anion as guest, (4) electrostatic attraction, (5) anion-π noncovalent interaction, (6) preorganized cavity as structural motif, and (7) potential for redox-switching via Sb(V/III) couples.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) center coordinated by two catecholate ligands, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped anion with electron-rich aromatic surfaces. The system features: (1) a central Sb(V) with +1 formal charge after catecholate coordination, (2) two planar, negatively charged catecholate rings providing extensive π-electron density, (3) a well-defined tetrahedral geometry that directs the π-surfaces outward for anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., nitroarenes, cyanopyridines), and (4) potential for encapsulation of cationic or neutral guests within the π-rich pocket. The recognition elements include dative Sb–O bonds, electrostatic stabilization, and complementary anion-π interactions. This represents an underexplored pnictogen-based supramolecular building block with potential for self-assembly into larger capsules or frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organoselenonium cations (R3Se+) that function as anion-binding hosts through a combination of electrostatic attraction and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon features: (1) a positively charged selenium(IV) center with tetrahedral geometry, (2) three organic substituents (typically aryl or alkyl groups) providing structural definition, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, triazine, or pyridinium-fused systems) positioned to create an anion-binding pocket, and (4) complementary electrostatic and anion-π interactions that selectively bind anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-, etc.) within the cavity. The tetrahedral geometry directs the aromatic panels to form a convergent binding site, while the selenonium cation provides strong electrostatic preorganization. This represents an underexplored pnictogen-bond analog (Group 16 chalcogen bonding variant) with potential for chiral recognition when using asymmetric substitution patterns.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels and electrostatic interactions with encapsulated anions. The system features: (1) a central tetraalkylphosphonium cation with four aromatic arms (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) extending from phosphorus, creating a tetrahedral geometry; (2) electron-deficient π-surfaces on each arm that provide multiple convergent anion-π binding sites; (3) a small anion (Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻) positioned at the center of the tetrahedral cavity, stabilized by both electrostatic attraction to the P⁺ center and anion-π interactions with the aromatic panels; (4) tunable cavity size via alkyl linker length between P and aryl groups; (5) potential for hierarchical assembly into larger capsules or frameworks via peripheral functionalization. This combines pnictogen (P⁺) electrostatic, anion-π, and shape-persistent tetrahedral geometry to create a directional, charge-assisted supramolecular building block.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged phosphorus center, and (2) cooperative anion-π interactions between the bound anion and electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or triazine rings) positioned on the substituents. The tetrahedral geometry directs four aromatic panels outward, creating a convergent binding pocket suitable for encapsulation of anions like BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻, or PF₆⁻. This system combines charge-assisted anion recognition with multivalent anion-π contacts, mimicking the function of anion-binding proteins and enabling the construction of self-assembled cages or capsules. The phosphonium center offers greater hydrolytic stability compared to ammonium analogs and tunable electronics via substituent choice.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that engages in two simultaneous, orthogonal interaction modes: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged phosphorus center, and (2) cation-π interactions between its organic substituents (e.g., phenyl or extended aromatic groups) and electron-rich arenes on a complementary partner. This creates a 3D recognition motif where the anion (e.g., halide, tetrafluoroborate) sits at the tetrahedral vertex, while the aromatic arms engage in parallel displaced or T-shaped π-stacking with a receptor bearing concave aromatic surfaces (e.g., cyclophanes, curved polyaromatics). The combination yields a capsule-like assembly driven by charge-assisted cation-π and anion-dipole interactions, with tunable cavity size via substituent length. The synthon maps to primitives: ATOM (P⁺ center), CHARGE (+1), SHAPE (tetrahedral), FORCE (electrostatic, dispersion), TIME (stable assembly), SPACE (3D capsule), and INFORMATION (complementary anion/π surfaces).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels and electrostatic interactions with encapsulated anions. The system features: (1) a central phosphonium cation with tetrahedral geometry, (2) four extended aromatic arms (e.g., perfluorinated phenyl or naphthyl groups) that create an electron-deficient π-surface, (3) anion binding within the cavity via electrostatic attraction to P⁺ and anion-π interactions with the aromatic panels, and (4) tunable cavity size via aryl group substitution. This creates a self-assembled capsule-like environment where the phosphonium serves as both structural anchor and electrostatic organizer, while the electron-deficient π-systems provide additional recognition surfaces for anions like BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or ClO₄⁻. The synthon maps to primitives: A (tetrahedral P⁺ core), B (aromatic panels), C (anion guest), D (electrostatic and anion-π interactions), E (capsule assembly), F (anion recognition event), and G (tunable cavity via ligand modification).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or s-triazine rings) and electrostatic anion binding. The cationic phosphorus center provides a strong, directional positive electrostatic potential, while the surrounding aryl groups on the phosphonium (or separate electron-deficient panels in a self-assembled cage) create convergent anion-π binding sites. This combination enables the formation of stable, three-dimensional capsule-like structures that can encapsulate anions through a combination of electrostatic attraction and anion-π contacts. The synthon is chemically robust, synthetically accessible via quaternization of phosphines, and offers tunability through variation of R groups (alkyl, aryl) and π-acidic panel design.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon(IV) center coordinated by two catecholate ligands, creating a rigid, negatively charged tetrahedral anion with four oxygen vertices. The catecholate aromatic rings provide extended π-surfaces that engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine rings) from a complementary cationic or neutral receptor. The synthon combines: 1) strong Si-O covalent bonds for geometric preorganization, 2) the anionic charge localized on the oxygen atoms, 3) the electron-rich catechol π-systems for anion-π recognition, and 4) the tetrahedral shape enabling encapsulation within a complementary π-rich cage or capsule. This represents a silicon-based analog of the known boron and gallium catecholate capsules but exploits the greater hydrolytic stability and distinct coordination geometry of silicon(IV). The system can be mapped to the seven primitives via: shape (tetrahedron), charge (anion), polarity (polar O atoms), H-bonding capability (catechol OH groups after protonation), aromaticity (catechol rings), conformational rigidity (chelate rings), and redox activity (catechol/quinone interconversion potential).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_siloxane_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon center with four siloxane (Si-O-Si) bridges, each terminating in an electron-deficient aromatic ring (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or pentafluorophenyl). The tetrahedral core acts as a convergent scaffold, positioning four π-acidic surfaces to form an anion-binding capsule through cooperative anion-π interactions. The siloxane linkages provide conformational flexibility and hydrolytic stability, while the electron-deficient arenes create a polarized electrostatic pocket suitable for encapsulating halide or oxoanions. This system combines covalent siloxane chemistry with supramolecular anion-π recognition, enabling the design of self-assembled cages or selective anion receptors.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetravalent tellurium(IV) cations (R₃Te⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like assembly. The telluronium center (Te⁺) serves as a strong Lewis acidic site that can coordinate anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) while simultaneously engaging in secondary Te···O/N chalcogen bonds. Electron-deficient tetrafluorobenzene or triazine panels provide complementary anion-π recognition sites, creating a three-dimensional cage-like architecture. The system exhibits dynamic behavior through reversible anion binding/release (temporal domain), with the Te(IV) center's redox activity enabling potential electrochemical switching between Te(IV) and Te(II) states, modulating capsule stability.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon(IV) center coordinated by two catecholate dianion ligands, forming a rigid, electron-rich anionic complex with four outward-facing oxygen atoms. This anionic metallocage exhibits strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives) in solution, leading to the self-assembly of discrete dimeric capsules. The recognition elements are: (1) the localized negative charge on the silicon-bound catecholate oxygens, (2) the well-defined tetrahedral geometry of the Si(cat)2²⁻ core, and (3) the complementary electron-deficient π-surfaces of the paneling units. This system maps to the seven primitives as: SHAPE (tetrahedral), CHARGE (anionic), POLARITY (polar O atoms), SIZE (defined by ligand span), CONFIGURATION (rigid 3D geometry), CONNECTIVITY (four interaction sites), and AFFINITY (anion-π and electrostatic). It represents an underexplored variation in the tetrahedral anion-π capsule family by using silicon—a biocompatible and abundant element—with catecholate ligands, offering potential in anion transport or sequestration.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral organoselenonium cation (R3Se+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged selenium center, and (2) anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or triazine rings) positioned around the cation. The system forms a three-dimensional capsule-like architecture where the anion is encapsulated within a cavity defined by the selenonium center (at one vertex) and the electron-deficient π-surfaces (forming the remaining faces). This combines pnictogen-bond-like directionality from the σ-hole on selenium with orthogonal anion-π contacts, creating a convergent binding pocket for anions such as chloride, tetrafluoroborate, or hexafluorophosphate. The synthon is chemically realistic, as selenonium salts are known stable species, and electron-deficient aromatics are well-established anion-π acceptors. It maps to the seven primitives through electrostatic attraction (charge), directional Se⁺···anion interaction (shape complementarity), and aromatic surface binding (surface).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetravalent tellurium(IV) cations (R₄Te²⁺) that form anion-binding capsules through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a central Te(IV) cation with four organic arms terminating in electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorophenyl, triazine, or pyridinium groups) arranged in a tetrahedral geometry. These aromatic panels create a convergent, electron-deficient cavity that selectively binds anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.) through cooperative anion-π interactions. The Te(IV) center provides structural rigidity and directionality, while the electron-deficient aromatics offer tunable binding affinity through substituent effects. This represents a novel pnictogen-bonding analog (tellurium as a heavy chalcogen) with enhanced polarizability compared to lighter elements, creating a stable, preorganized capsule for anion recognition and encapsulation in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon(IV) center coordinated by two catecholate ligands, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped anion with electron-rich aromatic surfaces. The catecholate oxygens bear partial negative charge, while the silicon center provides tetrahedral geometry. This anionic complex engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or triazine derivatives) from a complementary cationic or neutral receptor, forming a self-assembled capsule. The recognition elements include: (1) dative Si–O bonds from catecholate to silicon, (2) electrostatic stabilization of the anion, (3) directional anion-π contacts between catecholate aryl rings and electron-poor arenes, and (4) potential C–H···O hydrogen bonds from capsule walls to catecholate oxygens. This system maps to the seven primitives through: shape complementarity (tetrahedral anion + curved π-surface), electrostatic attraction (anion to δ+ π-system), directional noncovalent contacts, and reversible self-assembly under thermodynamic control.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenium_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral selenium(IV) centers with electron-deficient aromatic panels that form anion-π interactions. The system features Se(IV) atoms with two catecholate-type ligands (providing tetrahedral geometry) and two electron-deficient pyrazine or tetrazine rings extending outward. These electron-deficient π-systems create anion-binding pockets through anion-π interactions with halide or oxoanions. The tetrahedral geometry directs four π-deficient faces toward a common cavity, forming a capsule-like environment for anion encapsulation. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral Se(IV) coordination centers, (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings for anion-π interactions, (3) catecholate-type oxygen donors for metal coordination, and (4) preorganized cavity geometry. This represents an underexplored combination of pnictogen-bond donor (Se) with anion-π acceptor properties in a supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraorganotin(IV) catecholate complexes that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. The system features a central tin(IV) atom coordinated to two catecholate ligands in a tetrahedral geometry, creating an electron-deficient cavity with four aromatic rings oriented toward a common center. The electron-withdrawing tin center and catecholate oxygen atoms polarize the π-systems, creating a strong anion-binding pocket suitable for halide or oxoanion encapsulation. The catecholate oxygen atoms also provide secondary hydrogen-bonding sites for capsule assembly via complementary hydrogen-bond donors. This synthon combines metal coordination geometry, anion-π interactions, and hydrogen bonding to create predictable supramolecular capsules with potential applications in anion sensing and separation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organoselenonium cations (R3Se+) that engage in dual non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged selenium center, and (2) anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or pyrazine rings) positioned orthogonally to the Se-C bonds. The system forms a dynamic capsule-like architecture in solution, where the selenonium center acts as an anion receptor while the flanking arenes provide secondary stabilization through cooperative anion-π contacts. This represents an underexplored combination of pnictogen-adjacent heavy chalcogen cationic centers with anion-π recognition, offering redox-active and stereoelectronic tunability via substituents on selenium and the arene rings.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenium_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral selenium(IV) centers bearing two catecholate ligands and two anionic oxygen donors, creating a tetrahedral anion with four π-rich aromatic faces. The selenium center (Se⁴⁺) is coordinated in a distorted tetrahedral geometry by two bidentate catecholate ligands (each donating two oxygen atoms) and two additional anionic oxygen atoms from sulfonate or carboxylate groups. This creates a persistent tetrahedral anion with four electron-rich aromatic surfaces (from the catecholates) that can engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with complementary cationic π-systems (like pyridinium or imidazolium rings) or electron-deficient arenes. The combination of (1) the tetrahedral shape directing capsule formation, (2) the anionic charge enabling electrostatic complementarity, (3) the π-faces providing stacking recognition, and (4) the selenium offering polarizability for tunable interaction strength makes this a versatile supramolecular building block for self-assembled capsules or cages. The system maps to primitives: tetrahedral (shape), anion (charge), π-system (recognition), and can exhibit temporal behavior through redox changes at selenium (Se⁴⁺/Se²⁺).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8

The system features: (1) a tetrahedral selenonium cation center with permanent positive charge, (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, cyanuric acid derivatives, or perfluorinated pyridines) as π-acidic surfaces, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the cationic center's associated anion (Cl-, BF4-, PF6-) and the electron-deficient π-systems, and (4) preorganized geometry enabling capsule-like assembly through multiple convergent anion-π contacts. synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1

The system features a tetrahedral tin center coordinated to two catecholate ligands through dative bonds from oxygen donors, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped architecture with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The catecholate ligands are substituted with electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., -NO₂, -CN) to enhance their π-acidic character, enabling strong anion-π interactions with halide or oxoanions. The tetrahedral geometry directs four such π-acidic faces outward, allowing them to dimerize or assemble into larger capsules through complementary anion-π interactions with templating anions. This synthon combines metal coordination (Sn–O), electrostatic interactions, and directional anion-π contacts, and is chemically robust due to the high stability of Sn(IV) complexes. It maps to primitives as: (1) tetrahedral node (Sn center), (2) planar connectors (catecholate ligands), (3) electrostatic attractors (π-acidic surfaces), (4) directional interactions (anion-π), (5) self-assembly via anion templating, (6) reversible capsule formation, and (7) potential for redox-switching via catecholate redox states.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organoselenonium cations (R3Se+) that engage in dual anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming capsule-like architectures. The synthon features: (1) tetrahedral selenonium cation as a strong electrostatic anchor point, (2) electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or nitroaromatic panels) as π-acidic surfaces, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the cation-bound anion (Cl-, Br-, BF4-, etc.) and the electron-deficient π-systems, and (4) preorganized geometry from rigid spacers connecting the π-panels to the central selenonium hub. The system can be mapped to primitives: positive charge (selenonium), negative charge (anion), π-system (electron-deficient arene), tetrahedral geometry, directional non-covalent interaction (anion-π), preorganization (rigid linkers), and encapsulation (capsule formation).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organoselenonium cations (R3Se+) that engage in simultaneous anion binding through electrostatic interactions and π-stacking interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon features: (1) a positively charged selenium(IV) center with tetrahedral geometry, (2) three organic substituents (typically aryl or alkyl groups) providing structural definition, (3) a directional anion binding site at the selenium center (Se+···X- interaction), and (4) extended aromatic arms capable of parallel-displaced π-stacking with complementary electron-rich or electron-deficient aromatics. This creates a dual-interaction motif where the anion binding organizes the cationic centers, while the π-stacking between the aromatic substituents drives capsule formation. The system is chemically realistic as organoselenonium salts are known stable compounds, and their anion binding properties combined with aromatic stacking offer a route to self-assembled capsules. This maps to primitives: positive charge (Se+), directional interaction (anion binding), aromatic surface (π-stacking), tetrahedral geometry, and reversible assembly (supramolecular capsule formation).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organoselenonium cations (R3Se+) that engage in dual non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction between the positively charged selenium center and electron-rich aromatic systems (anion-π interaction in reverse polarity), and (2) secondary Se···O/N chalcogen bonding between the σ-hole on selenium and lone pairs of adjacent carbonyl or nitro groups. The tetrahedral geometry of R3Se+ creates a directional binding pocket that can encapsulate planar anions like tetrafluoroborate or perchlorate through a combination of anion-π and weak chalcogen bonds. The system features phenyl or naphthyl substituents on selenium to provide extended π-surfaces for stacking interactions, while electron-withdrawing substituents on these aromatics enhance the σ-hole on selenium. This creates a reversible, stimuli-responsive capsule that can be disassembled by redox changes (reduction of Se(IV) to Se(II)) or competitive solvents.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organoselenonium cations (R3Se+) that engage in dual anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon consists of a central selenonium cation (e.g., trimethylselenonium or triarylselenonium) with three substituents creating a tetrahedral geometry. The positively charged selenium center coordinates an anion (Cl-, Br-, NO3-) through electrostatic interaction, while the electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., perfluorinated benzene, cyanobenzene, or nitrobenzene derivatives) on the substituents provide complementary anion-π binding sites. This creates a 'capsule-like' recognition motif where the anion is partially encapsulated between the cationic selenium center and the electron-poor π-systems. The interaction combines electrostatic, anion-π, and potentially weak chalcogen bonding components, making it suitable for constructing supramolecular cages, ion-pair receptors, or crystalline frameworks with anion-templated assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral telluronium cations (R3Te+) that engage in simultaneous anion binding through electrostatic interactions and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) telluronium centers as strong cationic recognition elements for anions (halides, carboxylates), (2) electron-deficient arenes (e.g., perfluorinated benzene, triazine rings) positioned ortho or para to the telluronium that provide complementary anion-π binding sites, (3) a tetrahedral arrangement of four telluronium-arene units that can converge to form a capsule-like cavity capable of encapsulating an anion cluster or solvent-separated ion pair. The telluronium's polarizability and relatively soft character compared to lighter chalcogen analogs enable tunable binding strength. This synthon maps to primitives: positive charge (telluronium), negative charge (anion), π-system (electron-deficient arene), tetrahedral geometry, directional electrostatic interactions, and reversible assembly/disassembly (temporal domain).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(III) catecholate complexes that function as anion-π receptors. The system features an Sb(III) center coordinated to three catecholate ligands in a propeller-like arrangement, creating a tetrahedral geometry with an electron-deficient cavity. The three catecholate oxygen atoms form a convergent binding pocket with partial negative charge, while the aromatic rings of the catecholates are electron-deficient due to coordination to the Lewis acidic antimony center, creating favorable anion-π interactions. This creates a synergistic binding environment where anions can interact simultaneously with the partial negative charges on oxygen and the electron-deficient π-surfaces. The tetrahedral geometry allows for encapsulation of spherical anions like chloride or bromide, while the propeller arrangement provides chiral discrimination potential. The system can be mapped to primitives: (1) Sb(III) as electrophilic center, (2) catecholate oxygens as nucleophilic sites, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings as π-acceptors, (4) tetrahedral geometry as structural constraint, (5) anion binding as recognition event, (6) potential for chiral induction, and (7) reversible coordination chemistry at Sb center.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(III) catecholate complexes that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. The system features antimony(III) centers chelated by two catecholate ligands in a distorted tetrahedral geometry, creating an electron-deficient cavity with Lewis acidic character. The catecholate oxygen atoms provide hydrogen bond acceptor sites, while the antimony center offers a region of positive electrostatic potential. This synthon can encapsulate anions through a combination of anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic rings of adjacent catecholates, electrostatic attraction to the antimony center, and hydrogen bonding to the oxygen atoms. The tetrahedral arrangement allows for directional assembly into larger capsule structures through π-π stacking between catecholate rings and coordination of additional ligands to the antimony centers. This represents a novel extension of main-group element supramolecular chemistry into the pnictogen bond domain with unique geometric constraints.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral stibonium cations (R₄Sb⁺) that engage in dual anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming capsule-like architectures. The synthon features: (1) a central tetrahedral stibonium cation (e.g., tetraphenylstibonium or functionalized derivatives) as a strong, directional cationic node; (2) electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., tetrafluoropyrazine, s-tetrazine, or perfluorinated benzene derivatives) that accept electron density from anions via anion-π interactions; (3) complementary anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or BArF⁻) that sit above the electron-deficient π-systems while being electrostatically attracted to the cationic antimony center; and (4) peripheral functionalization allowing for covalent linkage or secondary interactions (halogen bonding, hydrogen bonding) to extend the assembly. This system combines underutilized pnictogen (Sb) cationic chemistry with anion-π recognition, creating a charge-assisted, shape-persistent capsule synthon suitable for host-guest chemistry, selective anion recognition, or as a building block for porous materials.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(III) centers coordinated by two catecholate ligands, creating an electron-rich anionic complex with exposed π-surfaces. The antimony center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with two bidentate catecholate ligands, resulting in a dianionic [Sb(cat)₂]⁻ species. This anionic complex features extended aromatic surfaces from the catecholate rings that participate in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The combination of the tetrahedral metal center geometry, anionic charge, and exposed π-electron density creates a directional building block for self-assembly into capsule-like structures through complementary anion-π interactions with cationic or neutral electron-deficient aromatic panels. This represents an underexplored combination of pnictogen (antimony) coordination chemistry with supramolecular anion-π interactions, distinct from previously proposed boron, silicon, or gallium analogs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(V) cations (e.g., [SbR4]+ where R = aryl or alkyl) that function as anion-π acceptors. The synthon features a cationic antimony center with a σ-hole along each Sb–C bond axis, creating four convergent, electropositive regions ideal for binding electron-rich anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-) via pnictogen bonding. The aryl substituents on antimony are π-deficient (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl) and are oriented to provide additional anion-π interaction surfaces. This creates a convergent, tetrahedrally symmetric binding pocket that can encapsulate a single anion or pair of anions in a sandwich-like fashion. The synthon is chemically realistic, known in antimony(V) onium chemistry, and offers a heavier pnictogen analog to phosphonium/arsonium systems with potentially stronger, more directional pnictogen bonds due to antimony's larger size and polarizability.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_dithiolene_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(III) centers coordinated by dithiolene ligands, forming anionic complexes that engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features Sb(III) with a stereochemically active lone pair, creating a distorted tetrahedral geometry when bound to two bidentate dithiolene ligands (e.g., maleonitriledithiolate). The resulting anionic complex [Sb(dithiolene)₂]⁻ possesses a delocalized π-system on the dithiolene ligands and a localized negative charge, enabling it to act as an anion-π donor to complementary electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or pyrazine panels). This creates a reversible, directional assembly motif for constructing supramolecular capsules or cages through multiple convergent anion-π interactions, with potential for redox-switching due to the non-innocent nature of dithiolene ligands. The synthon maps to primitives: (1) Sb as tetrahedral node, (2) dithiolene as planar connector, (3) anion as charge carrier, (4) π-system as recognition surface, (5) anion-π as directional interaction, (6) capsule as assembly geometry, and (7) redox-activity as temporal dimension.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8

The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral phosphazenium core with four cationic nitrogen centers providing strong electrostatic recognition for anions, (2) four extended arms terminating in perfluorinated aromatic rings (e.g., hexafluorobenzene or pentafluoropyridine) that create electron-deficient π-surfaces, (3) these π-surfaces engage in multiple anion-π interactions with the encapsulated anion (e.g., Cl-, BF4-, PF6-), and (4) the overall assembly forms a capsule-like structure where the anion is sandwiched between two facing phosphazenium units. The recognition elements include electrostatic attraction, anion-π interactions, and shape complementarity. This system maps to primitives: positive charge (phosphazenium cation), negative charge (anion), π-system (electron-deficient aromatics), tetrahedral geometry, and directional non-covalent interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_cage_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a cationic tetrahedral core with four positively charged nitrogen vertices, each bearing organic substituents (methyl, ethyl, or aryl groups). This core is encapsulated by four electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-tetrazine derivatives) positioned above each face of the tetrahedron. The primary recognition elements are: (1) electrostatic anion-π interactions between the cationic nitrogen centers and the π-acidic aromatic surfaces, (2) complementary shape matching between the tetrahedral cation and the inwardly-directed aromatic panels forming a cage-like architecture, and (3) potential secondary C–H···π or edge-to-face interactions from the ammonium substituents. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through: shape complementarity (tetrahedral), electrostatic attraction (cation–π-acidic surface), directional preorganization (rigid aromatic panels), and reversible assembly (non-covalent encapsulation). The system is chemically realistic, inspired by known quaternary ammonium structures and anion-π active aromatics, and represents a distinct variation from the listed iodonium, phosphonium, and selenonium examples by employing ubiquitous ammonium chemistry with different electronic and steric properties.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9

The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral phosphazenium core with strong positive charge delocalization through P=N⁺ bonds, (2) four extended aromatic arms (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, trinitrobenzene, or cyanophenyl groups) that provide multiple electron-deficient π-surfaces, (3) cooperative anion binding where the central cation electrostatically pre-organizes anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻) while the surrounding aromatic panels engage in directional anion-π interactions, and (4) self-assembly into dimeric capsules through complementary electrostatic and dispersion interactions. This system combines pnictogen-bond-like character (from P=N⁺), electrostatic interactions, and multi-point anion-π recognition in a geometrically defined tetrahedral architecture suitable for selective anion encapsulation and transport applications.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphazenium cations (R3P=N+=PR3) that form anion-binding capsules through cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral phosphazenium core with four cationic nitrogen centers providing electrostatic complementarity to anions, (2) four electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) positioned at the vertices to create anion-π binding sites, and (3) flexible aliphatic linkers enabling capsule self-assembly. Recognition elements include: strong electrostatic interactions between phosphazenium cations and anions, multiple anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes, and hydrophobic effects from the capsule interior. This system can encapsulate tetrahedral anions (ClO4-, BF4-) or spherical halides through multivalent binding, with potential temporal control via pH-responsive protonation of the phosphazenium centers or redox-switching of the aromatic panels' electron deficiency.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphazenium cation [P(NR₂)₄]⁺ (where R = alkyl or aryl groups) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon features: (1) a large, stable tetrahedral cation with four electron-donating NR₂ groups that enhance the cation's polarizability and size, (2) four electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or pyrazine) positioned at the vertices of a tetrahedron, creating an anion-binding pocket via cooperative anion-π interactions, and (3) the ability to encapsulate anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻) within the cavity formed by the four π-acidic faces. This system combines electrostatic attraction from the cationic phosphorus center with directional anion-π interactions from the aromatic panels, creating a well-defined, preorganized capsule-like architecture for anion recognition and encapsulation. The synthon maps to primitives: positive charge (cation), π-system (aromatic panels), directional non-covalent interactions (anion-π), tetrahedral geometry, and encapsulation space.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral telluronium cations (R₄Te⁺) that form capsule-like structures through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels and electrostatic anion binding. The telluronium center provides strong electrostatic attraction for anions, while the attached aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) create electron-deficient π-surfaces that engage in complementary anion-π interactions with the same anion, creating a three-dimensional encapsulation motif. This system combines pnictogen-bond-like character from the heavy tellurium center with anion-π interactions and electrostatic forces, enabling the formation of discrete capsules or extended networks depending on ligand design. The telluronium cation's polarizability and size enhance both electrostatic and dispersion contributions, making it particularly effective for binding larger anions like BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or carboxylates.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) centers coordinated to dipyrromethene (BODIPY-like) ligands with pendant anionic groups, forming anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) tetrahedral boron centers with B-N coordination bonds to two pyrrole nitrogens, (2) anionic sulfonate or carboxylate groups attached to the ligand periphery, (3) electron-deficient fluorinated or nitro-substituted aromatic panels on adjacent synthons, (4) directional anion-π interactions between anionic groups and electron-poor π-systems, (5) complementary hydrogen bonding via amide or urea linkers, (6) hydrophobic packing of the BODIPY cores, and (7) potential for photophysical modulation via the BODIPY chromophore. This creates a self-assembling capsule where tetrahedral nodes direct geometry, anionic groups provide recognition sites, and π-systems mediate panel alignment, enabling temporal control through light or redox stimuli.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within a π-electron-rich aromatic cage formed by four electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-trinitrobenzene or tetrafluoroterephthalonitrile derivatives). The synthon features: (1) electrostatic cation-π interactions between the positively charged nitrogen and the π-faces of the arenes; (2) anion-π interactions between a complementary anionic species (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or ClO4-) and the same electron-deficient arenes, creating a synergistic binding pocket; (3) hydrogen bonding between the anion and peripheral functional groups on the arene edges; (4) van der Waals contacts between alkyl/aryl substituents on the ammonium cation and the cage interior; (5) geometric complementarity enforcing a tetrahedral encapsulation geometry; (6) reversible assembly/disassembly via solvent competition; (7) potential for temporal control via pH- or redox-switching of the ammonium cation or anion. This system represents a charge-assisted, multi-point recognition motif for constructing dynamic capsules and porous frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O+) core that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) a positively charged oxygen center with three organic substituents (alkyl/aryl) forming the tetrahedral cation, (2) four electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or pyrazine derivatives) positioned as faces of a capsule-like structure, (3) directional electrostatic anion-π interactions between the oxonium cation and the π-faces, stabilized by (4) complementary C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from methyl/aryl substituents, (5) edge-to-face aromatic interactions between panels, and (6) potential for encapsulation of small anions or neutral molecules within the cavity. The oxonium cation's high charge density and well-defined geometry provide a strong electrostatic anchor, while the tunable electron deficiency of the aromatic panels allows modulation of interaction strength. This represents a novel, charge-assisted supramolecular assembly motif with potential in molecular recognition and encapsulation chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_pyrazolylborate_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular tetrahedral synthon based on a zinc(II) cation coordinated to three facially arranged tris(pyrazolyl)borate ligands, creating a cationic tetrahedral metal center with π-rich pyrazole faces. This cationic capsule can encapsulate anionic guests through a combination of (1) electrostatic cation-anion attraction, (2) anion-π interactions between the guest anion and the electron-deficient faces of the coordinated pyrazoles, and (3) potential hydrogen bonding from B-H groups on the borate backbone. The system exhibits temporal control through reversible guest exchange modulated by solvent or redox changes at the zinc center. Recognition elements include the tetrahedral Zn(II) coordination geometry, the π-acidic aromatic faces of the pyrazoles, and the overall cationic charge. This maps to the seven primitives through: (1) Zn(II) as a metal node, (2) pyrazolylborate as a directional ligand, (3) anion as the guest, (4) electrostatic and anion-π as interaction types, (5) tetrahedral capsule as the assembly, (6) solvent/redox as external stimuli, and (7) guest encapsulation as the function.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation [R₃B-L]⁺ (where L is a neutral two-electron donor ligand like pyridine or THF) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine derivatives) and electrostatic anion binding to a complementary anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻). The synthon combines: (1) a cationic tetrahedral boron center (boronium) as an electrostatic anchor, (2) directional anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-poor arenes, (3) potential C-H···anion or halogen···anion contacts, and (4) π-π stacking between the arene panels to form a capsule-like architecture. This represents a novel combination of p-block cation, anion-π, and π-π interactions for programmable self-assembly, distinct from previously proposed iodonium, phosphonium, or silane-based capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation [R₃B-L]⁺ (where L is a neutral Lewis base like pyridine or THF) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-tetrazine derivatives) and electrostatic anion binding. The cationic boron center, with its empty p-orbital character partially satisfied by the Lewis base, creates a strong electrostatic field that attracts anions (Cl⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) while the electron-deficient aromatic rings, often integrated into a rigid scaffold like a calix[4]arene or resorcinarene, provide complementary anion-π recognition sites. This combination yields a tetrahedral 'capsule' synthon where the boronium cation sits at the vertex, anions are bound at the faces via anion-π contacts, and the overall assembly is stabilized by additional dispersion forces and edge-to-face aromatic interactions. The synthon is chemically realistic, drawing from known boronium cation chemistry and robust anion-π interactions, and can be mapped to primitives: attraction (electrostatic, anion-π), repulsion (steric, electrostatic shielding), linkage (covalent boron-Lewis base, coordinative), protection (encapsulation of anion), and transformation (anion exchange, redox activity at boron).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O+) as the central core, where three organic arms extend from the oxygen center, each terminated with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or triazine). These electron-deficient π-surfaces engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with a complementary tetrahedral anion (e.g., ClO4-, BF4-, or PF6-) positioned at the center of the cavity formed by the three aromatic panels. The oxonium cation provides strong electrostatic directionality, while the preorganized aromatic arms create a convergent binding pocket for anion encapsulation via multiple simultaneous anion-π contacts. This system combines cation-anion electrostatic attraction with geometrically matched multivalent anion-π recognition, suitable for constructing self-assembled capsules or cages in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral telluronium cation (R4Te+) that engages in simultaneous anion binding through electrostatic interactions and π-capsule formation through extended aromatic surfaces. The telluronium center, with its large, polarizable electron cloud and formal positive charge, acts as a strong anion binder. Four extended aromatic arms (e.g., pyrene or perylene derivatives) attached to tellurium provide large, curved π-surfaces. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) cation-π between R4N+ and electron-poor π-systems, (2) anion-π between anions and the same π-systems, and (3) electrostatic stabilization between the ions. The tetrahedral symmetry matches the guest geometry, enabling predictable self-assembly into capsule-like structures. This synthon is chemically realistic, exploits underutilized combined anion-π/cation-π cooperativity, and is distinct from previously proposed halogen-bonding or heavier pnictogen-based capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O+) core that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system consists of a positively charged oxygen center with three organic substituents (alkyl/aryl groups) forming a pyramidal geometry, paired with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanobenzene, or s-triazine derivatives) that create anion-π binding sites. The oxonium cation's positive charge is stabilized by inductive effects from electron-withdrawing substituents, while the electron-deficient π-systems attract anions (e.g., halides, BF4-, PF6-) that are in turn coordinated by the oxonium center. This creates a reversible, electrostatic capsule-like environment suitable for anion encapsulation and transport. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral oxonium cation as an anion-binding motif, (2) electron-deficient arenes for anion-π interactions, (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from substituents, and (4) tunable cavity size via substituent bulk. Mapped to primitives: positive charge (oxonium), negative charge (anion), π-system (electron-deficient arene), tetrahedral geometry, electrostatic attraction, directional H-bond-like O+···anion interaction, and reversible assembly/disassembly (temporal control).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin complex that functions as an anion-π capsule. The system features a Zn(II) center coordinated to four nitrogen atoms of a porphyrin macrocycle, creating a planar, electron-deficient π-surface. The porphyrin is further functionalized with four peripheral pyridyl groups at the meso positions, which coordinate to additional metal centers or form hydrogen bonds, enforcing a tetrahedral arrangement of multiple porphyrin units around a central cavity. This assembly creates a three-dimensional electron-deficient pocket capable of binding anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through cooperative anion-π interactions with the porphyrin π-systems. The recognition elements include: (1) the electron-deficient porphyrin π-system for anion-π interactions, (2) zinc coordination site for axial ligand binding, (3) peripheral pyridyl groups for directional assembly, and (4) the tetrahedral geometry creating a defined cavity. This maps to primitives as: electron-deficient surface (π-acceptor), tetrahedral node (connector), anion (guest), coordination bonds (linker), directional pyridyl groups (vector), and the assembled capsule (container).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7

The cationic charge is stabilized by through-space electrostatic attraction to the π-face, while the tetrahedral geometry directs three substituents to preorganize a capsule-like environment. This creates a reversible, electrostatically-driven assembly motif suitable for encapsulation of small anions or polar molecules, with potential applications in selective anion recognition, supramolecular catalysis, or stimuli-responsive materials. synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9
