This cavity can encapsulate an anion (e.g., Cl-, Br-, BF4-) via multiple anion-π interactions, with the oxonium's positive charge enhancing the anion affinity. The system can be realized using rigid scaffolds like adamantane or calixarene derivatives functionalized with both oxonium-forming groups (ethers that can be protonated or alkylated) and electron-deficient arenes. Recognition elements include: (1) the oxonium cation (electrostatic, hydrogen-bond donor), (2) electron-deficient π-systems (anion-π), and (3) the preorganized tetrahedral geometry (shape complementarity). This synthon is novel relative to the listed iodonium, selenonium, etc., analogs because oxonium cations are less common in supramolecular chemistry and offer distinct reactivity and stability profiles.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The oxonium center (O+) provides strong electrostatic complementarity to anions, while the three aromatic arms (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) attached to the oxygen create electron-deficient π-surfaces. These surfaces engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with halide or tetrafluoroborate anions, while also potentially participating in C–H···anion contacts from alkyl/aryl substituents on the oxonium. The tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the π-systems to form a three-walled partial capsule around the anion, with the oxonium's positive charge enhancing anion binding affinity. This system combines cationic charge, anion-π interactions, and geometric preorganization—mapping to primitives: positive charge (oxonium), π-system (electron-deficient aromatics), anion, tetrahedral geometry, and directional non-covalent interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (H₃O⁺ or substituted R₃O⁺) encapsulated within a crown ether host via multiple directional hydrogen bonds and ion-dipole interactions. The oxonium cation serves as a trigonal pyramidal hydrogen bond donor with three acidic protons oriented toward the crown ether oxygen atoms. The crown ether (typically 18-crown-6 or derivatives) provides a complementary array of Lewis basic oxygen atoms that accept hydrogen bonds, creating a highly directional and electrostatically stabilized host-guest complex. This system exemplifies a reversible, tunable supramolecular interaction where oxonium cation size, substitution (primary, secondary, tertiary oxonium), and crown ether cavity size can be modulated. The seven primitives map clearly: the oxonium cation is the electrophilic core (positive charge concentration), the crown ether oxygens are nucleophilic sites, hydrogen bonds are the directional interactions, the tetrahedral geometry provides spatial organization, the ion-dipole forces provide the energetic drive, the reversible binding offers temporal control, and the entire assembly represents a functional supramolecular unit.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) centers chelated by β-diketonate ligands, forming anionic complexes with extended π-conjugated systems. The boron atom adopts a tetrahedral geometry with two oxygen atoms from the β-diketonate ligand and two additional anionic or neutral ligands (e.g., fluoride, hydroxide, or alkoxide). The resulting anionic complex features a delocalized negative charge across the diketonate π-system, creating a strong anion-π recognition site. This synthon can self-assemble into dimeric capsules via complementary anion-π interactions between the electron-rich π-surface of one complex and the anionic character of another, or form heteromeric capsules with cationic π-systems. The tetrahedral geometry directs assembly into well-defined cavities suitable for guest encapsulation. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral boron coordination sphere, (2) anionic β-diketonate π-system for anion-π interactions, (3) directional hydrogen-bonding capability from ligand substituents, and (4) tunable cavity size via ligand substitution. Mappable to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), anion (charge), π-system (polarizability), directional H-bonding (directionality), self-assembly (reversibility), encapsulation (containment), and tunable electronics (modulation).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_crown_ether_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O+) encapsulated within a crown ether macrocycle, which in turn engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) oxonium cation (O+) as the central electrophilic core, (2) crown ether (e.g., 18-crown-6) as the first-shell host via multiple O···O+ dipole-dipole and ion-dipole interactions, (3) electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluoropyrazine or s-tetrazine) as π-acidic panels positioned above and below the crown ether plane, creating an anion-π binding site for an anionic guest (e.g., Cl⁻, BF₄⁻). This creates a hierarchical capsule-like environment: oxonium ⊂ crown ether ⊂ π-acidic panels ⊂ anion. The synthon demonstrates orthogonal recognition elements: ion-dipole (crown-oxonium), anion-π (arene-anion), and π-π stacking between panels if dimerized. It maps to primitives: charge (oxonium +, anion -), polarity (crown ether dipoles), polarizability (π-systems), H-bond capacity (crown ether oxygens can also interact with outer-shell protons), shape (tetrahedral cation, planar arenes, spherical anion), topology (encapsulation hierarchy), and reactivity (oxonium as strong electrophile, anion as nucleophile).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage. The cationic nitrogen center (formally N⁺ with four substituents) engages in electrostatic and cation-π interactions with multiple electron-poor arene panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or nitrobenzene derivatives) arranged in a tetrahedral or octahedral coordination geometry around the cation. The arene panels are linked through rigid organic spacers or metal-coordination vertices to form a three-dimensional cage that selectively binds the ammonium ion via synergistic cation-π and hydrogen-bonding interactions (C–H···π and N⁺–H···π). This system represents a synthetic host-guest motif for molecular recognition of quaternary ammonium species, with potential applications in sensing, separation, and catalysis. The interaction primitives include: (1) electrostatic attraction (cation-anion/π), (2) dispersion (π-π stacking), (3) polarization (cation-π), (4) hydrogen bonding (C–H···π), (5) shape complementarity (cavity encapsulation), (6) rigidity (scaffold preorganization), and (7) cooperativity (multi-point binding).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) centers chelated by β-diketonate ligands (such as acetylacetonate derivatives) that form anionic complexes with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with two oxygen atoms from the β-diketonate and two additional anionic or neutral ligands (e.g., fluoride, hydroxide, or alkoxide). The resulting anionic complex features a delocalized negative charge across the diketonate π-system and exhibits strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzenes, triazines, or nitroaromatics). This creates a directional, charge-assisted recognition motif where the anionic boron complex acts as a 'guest' that can be encapsulated within π-acidic aromatic 'host' cages or frameworks. The system is chemically realistic, known in coordination chemistry (boron β-diketonates are stable and synthetically accessible), and offers tunability via substituents on the diketonate and the π-acidic arena.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O⁺) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic cage. The oxonium center (O⁺) forms strong electrostatic interactions with four surrounding electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetrafluoropyridine, or s-triazine rings) arranged in a tetrahedral geometry. This creates a stable cation-π capsule where the positively charged oxygen is centered within a π-basic cavity. The oxonium cation can be generated from ether protonation or as a stable species with electron-withdrawing substituents (e.g., perfluorinated alkyl groups). The outer shell can be functionalized with hydrogen-bond acceptors or donors to enable hierarchical assembly into extended frameworks. Recognition elements include: (1) strong cation-π interactions between O⁺ and electron-deficient arenes, (2) potential C–H···O hydrogen bonds from cage methylene groups to oxonium, (3) peripheral halogen/hydrogen bonding for secondary assembly, and (4) shape-complementary encapsulation. This synthon maps to primitives: electrostatics (cation-π), shape (tetrahedral), dynamics (oxonium formation/reversion), hierarchy (capsule → framework), and information (defined stoichiometry and geometry).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O+) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system consists of a central oxonium ion (e.g., trialkyloxonium or triaryloxonium) with three organic arms terminating in electron-deficient aromatic systems (such as tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or nitrobenzene derivatives). These aromatic panels create a partial capsule-like environment that can encapsulate anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-, etc.) through a combination of electrostatic attraction to the positively charged oxygen center and anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient π-surfaces. The tetrahedral geometry of the oxonium cation directs the three aromatic panels into a convergent arrangement, while the fourth position (the lone pair site converted to positive charge) provides the primary electrostatic recognition site. This creates a multi-point recognition system for anions that combines charge-charge, anion-π, and potentially C-H···anion interactions from the aromatic panel edges. The synthon is chemically reasonable as oxonium ions are known stable species (e.g., Meerwein's salt derivatives), and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatics are well-documented in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1

The interaction pattern combines: 1) electrostatic attraction between the anionic boron center and cationic guests, 2) anion-π interactions between electron-deficient arenes and anionic/electron-rich species, 3) potential C-H···O hydrogen bonds from the β-diketonate oxygen atoms, and 4) shape complementarity from the preorganized tetrahedral geometry. This system maps to primitives as: electron-deficient π-systems (acceptor), anionic charge (donor/acceptor), preorganized cavity (scaffold), and coordinatively saturated boron (node).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_13

synthons.name: tetrahedral_beryllium_β-diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon

The planar, conjugated β-diketonate rings provide extended π-surfaces that engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, trinitrobenzene units) from a complementary cationic or neutral receptor. The tetrahedral geometry of the beryllium center creates a well-defined, directional scaffold, while the anionic charge and π-surface enable dual electrostatic and dispersion-driven encapsulation within π-acidic aromatic cages. This represents a rare example of beryllium coordination chemistry applied to supramolecular assembly, combining metal-ligand coordination, anion-π interactions, and geometric preorganization to form discrete capsular structures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boroxine anions (B₃O₃ rings) that engage in synergistic anion-π and lone pair-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The boroxine anion, formed by deprotonation of boronic acids or hydrolysis of boroxines, presents a planar, trigonal arrangement of oxygen atoms with a delocalized negative charge across the B₃O₃ ring. This anion acts as a recognition element that binds inside pre-organized π-acidic aromatic cages (e.g., tetrahedral frameworks built from triazine or tetrazine panels). The interaction combines: (1) anion-π interactions between the electron-rich boroxine oxygen atoms and the electron-deficient aromatic panels, and (2) lone pair-π contributions from oxygen lone pairs into the π* orbitals of the arenes. The tetrahedral geometry of the capsule provides a complementary cavity for the planar boroxine anion, enabling selective encapsulation and stabilization. This system is chemically realistic, as boroxine anions are known in coordination chemistry and supramolecular anion recognition, while electron-deficient aromatic cages are established in host-guest chemistry. The synthon maps to primitives: electrostatics (anion-π), dispersion (π-stacking), directional H-bond-like geometry (lone pair orientation), and can exhibit dynamic exchange (temporal domain) under stimuli like pH or competing anions.

Four electron-deficient arenes (such as 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or cyanophenyl derivatives) are arranged in a tetrahedral geometry around the oxonium-anion pair, engaging in directional anion-π interactions that encapsulate the anion. synthons.name: tetrahedral_beryllium_crown_ether_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon

The beryllium center adopts tetrahedral geometry with four oxygen donors from the crown ether, creating a compact, highly charged cation with significant electrostatic potential. This cation can engage in: (1) strong electrostatic interactions with anions (anion recognition), (2) cation-π interactions with electron-rich arenes due to the exposed Be²⁺ center, (3) hydrogen bonding via crown ether oxygen atoms, and (4) π-π stacking of the crown ether's ethylene bridges with aromatic systems. The synthon is chemically realistic as beryllium forms stable tetrahedral complexes with oxygen donors, and crown ether complexes of group 2 metals are known. This represents a novel combination of hard Lewis acid metal coordination, macrocyclic encapsulation, and supramolecular recognition elements.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_18

This creates a dynamic capsule-like environment suitable for anion encapsulation through combined electrostatic and π-system interactions. The synthon demonstrates reversible anion binding with potential for temporal control through pH or solvent modulation, bridging molecular cation-anion pairing with supramolecular assembly principles.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin cation coordinated to an axial anionic ligand, which simultaneously engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels of a complementary capsule-forming partner. The system features: (1) a Zn²⁺ center in a porphyrin macrocycle (molecular recognition via metal coordination), (2) an axial anionic ligand (e.g., carboxylate, phenolate, or halide) providing charge-assisted coordination, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or pyrazine) on the capsule walls that accept anion-π interactions with the coordinated anion, and (4) additional van der Waals/π-π contacts between porphyrin and capsule aryl groups. This creates a hierarchical assembly: metal-ligand coordination directs primary binding, while synergistic anion-π and π-π interactions stabilize the encapsulation geometry. The tetrahedral zinc center ensures directional fidelity, and the anionic ligand bridges coordination and supramolecular interaction domains. This synthon is novel relative to prior tetrahedral cation/anion-π capsules by employing a metalloporphyrin core (instead of main-group or onium ions) and leveraging both coordination chemistry and multi-point supramolecular recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin complexes that function as cationic π-capsules for anion recognition. The system features a zinc(II) center coordinated to a porphyrin macrocycle with axial ligands (typically pyridine derivatives) creating a tetrahedral geometry. The porphyrin's extended π-system provides a cationic surface (due to the +2 metal charge partially delocalized) that engages in anion-π interactions with halide or oxoanions. The tetrahedral arrangement of substituents at the porphyrin periphery (meso-positions) creates a bowl-shaped cavity ideal for encapsulating spherical anions like chloride or tetrahedral anions like perchlorate. Recognition elements include: (1) metal-anion electrostatic attraction, (2) porphyrin π-system anion-π interactions, (3) hydrogen bonding from peripheral functional groups, and (4) shape complementarity from the tetrahedral distortion. This maps to primitives as: tetrahedral geometry (shape), cationic metal center (charge), porphyrin π-system (surface), anion binding site (pocket), axial ligand exchange (hinge), redox-active porphyrin (state changer), and tunable periphery (connector).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming a capsule-like structure. The iodonium center features three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl or fluorinated aryl groups) creating a pyramidal cationic charge, while the fourth coordination site is occupied by a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., BF4- or PF6-). The electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or tetrafluoropyridine derivatives) are arranged around the cation, engaging in cooperative anion-π interactions with the iodonium-bound anion. This creates a three-dimensional capsule where the anion is encapsulated within a π-acidic aromatic cavity, stabilized by electrostatic and dispersion forces. The system demonstrates halogen bonding character from the hypervalent iodine center, combined with supramolecular anion-π recognition, offering a novel route to charged capsule assemblies with potential applications in anion sensing or selective encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that engages in simultaneous anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels and halogen bonding with anions, forming a capsule-like structure. The iodonium center features three aromatic substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenyl groups) that create electron-deficient π-surfaces, while the positively charged iodine acts as a halogen bond donor. This synthon combines (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-deficient arenes, and (3) halogen bonding (I⁺···anion) in a convergent geometry. The tetrahedral arrangement directs four interactions (three anion-π + one halogen bond) toward a central anion binding site, mimicking a supramolecular capsule. It maps to primitives: positive charge (iodonium), polarizable π-system (electron-deficient arenes), directional halogen bond donor (I⁺), and convergent geometry enabling encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming a capsule-like assembly. The iodonium center provides a strong, directional positive electrostatic potential, while the three aryl substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenyl groups) create electron-deficient π-surfaces. These surfaces attract anions (e.g., Cl-, BF4-) via anion-π interactions, while the tetrahedral geometry of the iodonium cation organizes three such panels into a convergent, bowl-shaped cavity. This preorganizes the system to encapsulate an anion, acting as a synthon for constructing larger supramolecular capsules or frameworks through combination with complementary anion-binding or π-donor units. The synthon maps to the seven primitives via: (1) iodonium as a charged, tetrahedral core (shape/charge), (2) electron-deficient aryl panels (surface), (3) convergent anion-π interaction sites (pattern), (4) directional electrostatic complementarity (complement), (5) preorganized cavity (assembly), (6) potential for redox activity at iodine (transformation), and (7) defined spatial arrangement for hierarchical assembly (hierarchy).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin complex that functions as an anion-π capsule building block. The system features a Zn(II) center coordinated to a porphyrin macrocycle with four peripheral electron-deficient aromatic substituents (e.g., tetrafluorophenyl or trinitrophenyl groups). The tetrahedral geometry around zinc creates a concave, bowl-shaped electron-deficient π-surface. This surface acts as a selective receptor for anions (e.g., chloride, nitrate, or carboxylates) through cooperative anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic rings. The synthon's recognition elements include: (1) the metal coordination site (Lewis acidic Zn²⁺), (2) the electron-deficient π-systems for anion binding, and (3) the rigid tetrahedral scaffold that preorganizes the binding pocket. This synthon can dimerize or assemble into larger capsules through complementary interactions (e.g., metal-ligand coordination with added pyridyl ligands or hydrogen bonding via appended groups), creating enclosed spaces for anion encapsulation. It maps to the seven primitives through: shape (tetrahedral concave), electrostatics (anion-π attraction), coordination (Zn-Nporphyrin), and assembly into higher-order structures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin complex with axial pyridine ligands, where the electron-deficient porphyrin π-system acts as an anion-π acceptor. The tetrahedral geometry is achieved through coordination of two axial pyridine ligands to the zinc center, creating a directional scaffold. The porphyrin macrocycle's large, planar, electron-deficient π-surface provides a recognition site for anions (e.g., chloride, nitrate) via anion-π interactions. The axial pyridine ligands can be functionalized with hydrogen-bond donors or additional coordination sites to enable hierarchical assembly into capsule-like structures. This system combines metal coordination (Zn-N), anion-π interactions, and potential hydrogen bonding or additional π-stacking, mapping to primitives of geometry (tetrahedral node), electrostatics (anion-π), coordination, and directional bonding for predictable self-assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron center coordinated to a β-diketonate anion, where the boron atom adopts a tetrahedral geometry with the β-diketonate occupying three coordination sites via its oxygen atoms, and the fourth site occupied by a variable organic substituent. The planar, conjugated β-diketonate ligand presents an electron-rich π-surface suitable for anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. This creates a dual-function synthon: (1) a well-defined tetrahedral metal-ligand coordination motif, and (2) a directional π-recognition surface. The synthon can self-assemble into capsule-like structures through complementary anion-π interactions between the electron-rich β-diketonate π-system of one unit and an electron-deficient arene (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, s-triazine) attached to the boron's fourth position on another unit. This represents a novel combination of coordination chemistry (B-O chelation) and supramolecular anion-π recognition in a single, programmable building block.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin complex with axial coordination of an anionic ligand (such as chloride or phenolate) that simultaneously engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels of a complementary capsule component. The system features: (1) a Zn(II) center in a distorted tetrahedral geometry (N₄ from porphyrin, one axial anion), (2) an anionic axial ligand that acts as both a coordination partner and an anion-π donor, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine) on the capsule walls as anion-π acceptors, and (4) additional van der Waals and shape complementarity between the porphyrin plane and the curved capsule surface. This creates a hierarchical assembly where metal coordination directs the primary binding, while anion-π interactions and geometric fitting provide secondary stabilization for capsule formation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin complexes that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. The system features a Zn(II) center coordinated to a porphyrin macrocycle with one axial coordination site occupied by a pyridine ligand, creating a tetrahedral geometry. The porphyrin's electron-deficient π-surface (enhanced by electron-withdrawing substituents like pentafluorophenyl groups at the meso-positions) provides strong anion-π recognition sites. Two such tetrahedral zinc porphyrin units can assemble into a capsule through cooperative interactions: (1) anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient porphyrin surface and an encapsulated anion (e.g., chloride, nitrate), (2) π-π stacking between the porphyrin rings of adjacent units, and (3) hydrogen bonding between peripheral functional groups. This creates a well-defined supramolecular capsule capable of anion recognition and encapsulation, with the tetrahedral geometry directing assembly into discrete dimeric structures rather than extended networks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_cobalt_corrin_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral cobalt(III) center coordinated within a corrin macrocycle (vitamin B12 analog), where the axial ligand positions are occupied by an anionic cyanide ligand and a labile water molecule. The hydrophobic corrin ring system creates a concave π-surface that can encapsulate planar anions (like nitrate, perchlorate, or tetrafluoroborate) through anion-π interactions within the bowl-shaped cavity. The cobalt center provides both structural rigidity (tetrahedral coordination geometry) and potential redox activity (Co(III)/Co(II) couple), while the cyanide ligand offers hydrogen-bond acceptance. This system combines metal coordination geometry, hydrophobic π-cavity formation, anion recognition, and potential temporal redox switching in a single supramolecular entity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R-I⁺-R') where the iodine center adopts a T-shaped geometry with two organic substituents and an empty coordination site. The positively charged iodine(III) center engages in strong anion binding through electrostatic and halogen-bonding interactions. The organic substituents (typically aromatic groups like phenyl or naphthyl) provide π-rich surfaces that can engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with the bound anion, while also enabling π-π stacking with complementary synthons. This creates a three-dimensional capsule-like assembly where the iodonium centers act as vertices, anions occupy the edges through halogen bonding, and aromatic panels form the faces through π-stacking. The system exhibits directional, tunable interactions: iodine(III) halogen bond strength can be modulated by substituent electronics, anion selectivity follows the halogen-bond acceptor scale, and π-surface dimensions control capsule size. This represents an underexplored combination of hypervalent iodine chemistry with supramolecular capsule design.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that forms a capsule-like structure through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The iodonium center (hypervalent iodine(III)) adopts a T-shaped geometry with three organic substituents (typically aryl groups with electron-withdrawing substituents like -CF3 or -NO2) and one vacant coordination site occupied by a counteranion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-). The electron-deficient aromatic rings on the substituents create multiple anion-binding pockets via anion-π interactions, while the overall tetrahedral arrangement of the aryl groups forms a semi-enclosed cavity that can encapsulate an anion through cooperative interactions. This system combines pnictogen-bond-like character from the hypervalent iodine center with directional anion-π interactions, creating a unique supramolecular recognition motif for anion binding and encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that engages in simultaneous anion binding through electrostatic interaction and π-capsule formation through orthogonal cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels. The iodonium center adopts a T-shaped geometry with three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, mesityl, or pyridyl groups) and a formally vacant coordination site that strongly attracts anions (Cl-, Br-, PF6-). Surrounding the cation are four curved, electron-rich aromatics (e.g., naphthalene diimide derivatives or corannulene bowls) arranged in a tetrahedral fashion, creating a π-basic capsule that encapsulates the iodonium core through multipoint cation-π contacts. This creates a stable, charge-assisted supramolecular assembly with dual recognition: (1) anion binding to the hypervalent iodine center and (2) three-dimensional encapsulation via aromatic panels. The synthon maps to primitives: electrostatic (cation-anion), dispersion (π-π/cation-π), shape (tetrahedral cavity), and polarity (charge separation).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with salicylaldiminate ligands that forms anion-binding capsules through cooperative anion-π and CH-π interactions. The system features: (1) a Ga³⁺ center coordinated by three bidentate salicylaldiminate ligands (N,O-donors from Schiff base derivatives of salicylaldehyde), creating a tetrahedral metal complex with a vacant coordination site occupied by a labile solvent molecule; (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings on the ligands (with electron-withdrawing substituents like -NO₂ or -CF₃) positioned to create convergent anion-π binding pockets; (3) preorganized C-H groups adjacent to the aromatic rings for cooperative CH-π interactions with anions; (4) labile coordination at Ga allowing for anion exchange and temporal control; (5) self-assembly into dimeric capsules via complementary π-stacking of ligand aromatics, encapsulating anions like Cl⁻, Br⁻, or NO₃⁻; (6) redox-active potential through the imine linkage; (7) modularity through variation of aromatic substituents and imine substituents. This combines metal coordination, anion-π, CH-π, and π-stacking interactions in a single programmable supramolecular architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_cobalt_diimine_dioxolene_redox_switchable_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral cobalt(III) complex with mixed diimine (bipyridine-type) and dioxolene (catecholate/semiquinone) ligands that exhibits redox-switchable anion-π and cation-π interactions. The neutral complex features a Co(III) center coordinated to two diimine N-donors and two dioxolene O-donors. Upon one-electron reduction to Co(II), the dioxolene ligand undergoes valence tautomerism to a semiquinone radical form, creating a redox-switchable π-system. In the reduced state, the electron-deficient semiquinone moiety acts as an anion-π acceptor for halides or oxoanions, while the diimine π-system serves as a cation-π donor for alkali metals. This creates a dual recognition site where redox state controls binding preference and affinity. The tetrahedral geometry provides directional control over interaction vectors, making it suitable for constructing redox-responsive capsules or frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral iodonium cations (R3I+) that function as anion-binding capsules through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features three electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or nitrobenzene derivatives) arranged around a central iodine(III) atom, creating a pyramidal cationic host with a σ-hole at the iodine apex. The electron-deficient aromatic faces create a convergent anion-binding pocket through cooperative anion-π interactions, while the iodonium center provides additional electrostatic stabilization. This synthon demonstrates halogen bonding (type I/II), anion-π interactions, and electrostatic complementarity, mapping to primitives: electrostatics (cation-anion), dispersion (π-π), directionality (halogen bond), complementarity (shape/charge), cooperativity (multiple weak interactions), preorganization (rigid tetrahedral geometry), and reversibility (dynamic anion binding).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with salicylaldiminate ligands that forms an anion-binding capsule through cooperative anion-π and hydrogen bonding interactions. The system features: (1) a Ga(III) center coordinated by three bidentate salicylaldiminate ligands (N,O-donors from Schiff base derivatives of salicylaldehyde), creating a tetrahedral metal complex with a vacant coordination site occupied by a labile solvent molecule; (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (pyridine or triazine substituents) introduced at the imine nitrogen para-positions, creating strong anion-π recognition surfaces; (3) phenolic OH groups positioned to form complementary hydrogen bonds with anions. The assembly forms dimeric capsules in solution where two tetrahedral complexes face each other, encapsulating anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through a combination of anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatics and hydrogen bonding with phenolic OH groups. This represents a novel metal-organic capsule system distinct from previously proposed boron, zinc, or silicon analogs, exploiting gallium's hard Lewis acidity and the versatile coordination chemistry of Schiff base ligands.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) core that engages in simultaneous anion binding through electrostatic interaction and π-capsule formation through cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels. The iodonium center, with its strong σ-hole character, provides directional anion binding to halides or carboxylates, while the three aromatic arms (e.g., pyrene or perylene derivatives) arranged in a tetrahedral geometry create a concave, electron-rich surface that can encapsulate small cationic or neutral guests via π-stacking and van der Waals interactions. This system combines pnictogen-bond-like anion recognition (via the iodonium σ-hole) with a π-basic cavity, enabling dual-site recognition and potential use in selective anion sensing or as a building block for self-assembled coordination cages.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_13
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) where three aromatic arms with electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or 1,3,5-triazine) are arranged around a central iodine(III) atom. The cationic iodine center acts as a strong halogen bond donor, while the electron-deficient aromatic arms provide multiple anion-π recognition sites. This creates a convergent, cage-like binding pocket capable of encapsulating polyatomic anions (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or carboxylates) through a combination of halogen bonding (I+···anion) and cooperative anion-π interactions (electron-deficient arene···anion). The tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the recognition elements for selective anion encapsulation, making it a versatile synthon for constructing anion-templated supramolecular capsules or frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate salen-type ligand (N₂O₂ donor set) bearing extended aromatic arms. The cationic [Ga(salen-Ar)₂]⁺ complex features a tetrahedral geometry with two bidentate salen ligands, creating a positively charged metal center. The aromatic arms (e.g., naphthyl or phenanthryl substituents) project outward, forming a curved, electron-deficient π-surface suitable for anion-π interactions. This synthon is designed to encapsulate polyatomic anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or carboxylates) through a combination of (1) electrostatic attraction to the Ga³⁺ center, (2) directional anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic panels, and (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from ligand methylene or methyl groups. The tetrahedral geometry enforces a bowl-like cavity, making it a pre-organized 'π-capsule' for anion recognition. This system explores the underexplored combination of metal-templated cation formation, tetrahedral geometry, and multi-point anion-π recognition within the supramolecular domain.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) core, where three aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups) are arranged around the central iodine(III) atom. The cationic iodine center acts as a strong halogen bond donor, while the three extended aromatic arms create a concave, bowl-shaped cavity lined with π-electron density. This cavity is designed to selectively bind complementary anionic guests (e.g., halides, BF4-, PF6-) via synergistic anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient faces of the aromatic rings. The overall tetrahedral geometry and the combination of directional halogen bonding (I+···anion) and multi-point anion-π interactions create a well-defined, three-dimensional recognition motif capable of forming capsular assemblies or serving as a building block for larger supramolecular frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salen-type Schiff base ligand (N,N'-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine) that forms a cationic metal center. This positively charged tetrahedral complex acts as a structural building block that can encapsulate an anion through electrostatic attraction while simultaneously engaging in π-π stacking interactions with electron-rich aromatic systems on adjacent synthons. The salen ligand provides extended aromatic surfaces for face-to-face stacking, while the tetrahedral geometry creates directional constraints. The gallium(III) center offers strong Lewis acidity and stable coordination geometry. This synthon enables the construction of supramolecular capsules or extended frameworks through a combination of: (1) metal-ligand coordination (primitives: bond, angle), (2) electrostatic anion binding (primitive: charge), (3) aromatic π-π stacking between salen phenyl rings (primitive: plane), and (4) directional assembly into 3D structures (primitives: torsion, conformation, chirality). The system is chemically realistic as gallium(III) readily forms stable complexes with salen ligands, and such complexes are known to participate in supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_15
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that forms a capsule-like structure through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The iodonium center (hypervalent iodine(III)) provides a strong cationic charge (+1) distributed over three organic substituents (typically aryl groups), creating a tetrahedral geometry. Electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, cyanophenyl, or triazine rings) are positioned around the cation to engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with a complementary anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or ClO4-). The assembly creates a capsule-like environment where the anion is encapsulated by the electron-deficient π-systems, stabilized by electrostatic and orbital interactions. Recognition elements include: (1) the iodonium cation as a tetrahedral cationic hub, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels as anion-binding sites, (3) complementary anions as guests, and (4) potential secondary interactions (C–H···anion, halogen bonding from iodine). This system maps to primitives: positive charge (iodonium), negative charge (anion), π-system (electron-deficient arenes), tetrahedral geometry, directional interactions (anion-π), electrostatic complementarity, and encapsulation motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the specific recognition between a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) and a crown ether host. The ammonium center features four alkyl/aryl substituents arranged tetrahedrally, creating a complementary size and shape match for crown ether cavities (typically 18-crown-6 for NH₄⁺ analogs). Primary recognition occurs through multiple C–H···O hydrogen bonds between the ammonium methylene/methyl protons and the crown ether oxygen atoms, supplemented by electrostatic attraction between the positive nitrogen and electron-rich oxygens. This synthon demonstrates high binding selectivity based on cation size and crown ether cavity diameter, with potential for temporal control through competitive binding or pH-switchable ammonium formation. The system maps to primitives through: (1) tetrahedral geometry at nitrogen, (2) electrostatic + hydrogen bonding interactions, (3) host-guest complementarity, (4) size-dependent selectivity, (5) potential for kinetic trapping, (6) modular substituent variation, and (7) applications in molecular machines, sensors, and switchable supramolecular assemblies.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate salen-type Schiff base ligand (N₂O₂ donor set) that forms a cationic metal center. This synthon features: (1) a positively charged Ga³⁺ center creating a strong electrostatic potential, (2) a rigid, bowl-shaped aromatic cavity formed by the phenyl rings of the salen ligand, (3) directional anion-π interactions between electron-deficient aromatic surfaces and complementary anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, ClO₄⁻), and (4) potential secondary interactions via the ligand's phenolic oxygen atoms. The tetrahedral geometry prevents planar stacking, instead creating a three-dimensional 'capsule' pocket that can selectively encapsulate anions through combined electrostatic and π-acidic interactions. This system maps to primitives: electrostatic (cation-anion), π-system (aromatic cavity), shape (tetrahedral constraint), polarity (polarized Ga-O/N bonds), connectivity (coordination bonds), dynamics (anion exchange), and function (anion recognition/transport).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_16
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) core that engages in simultaneous anion binding and electron-deficient arene π-acceptor interactions. The iodonium center, with its strong σ-hole along each I-C bond, acts as a potent halogen bond donor to anions (Cl-, Br-, I-, BF4-, PF6-). Simultaneously, the three aromatic substituents (typically pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) are oriented in a propeller-like tetrahedral geometry, creating a concave, electron-deficient aromatic surface that can engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with the same bound anion, as well as edge-to-face or offset π-π stacking with complementary electron-rich arenes from a second, identical unit. This dual interaction mode (R3I+···X- halogen bonding + ArF···X- anion-π) enables the self-assembly of dimeric or higher-order capsules where two tetrahedral iodonium cations encapsulate an anion pair, stabilized by peripheral π-stacking. The system is chemically realistic, with known stable iodonium salts (e.g., triphenyliodonium) and well-documented halogen bonding/anion-π cooperativity in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_17
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) where three aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups) are arranged around a central iodine(I) atom, creating a pyramidal cationic core. The fourth coordination site is occupied by a counter-anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or BArF-). Each aromatic arm is functionalized with electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, 1,3,5-triazine, or tetracyanobenzene) at its distal end. These electron-deficient arenes engage in strong, directional anion-π interactions with the encapsulated anion, while the cationic iodonium center provides additional electrostatic stabilization. The combination of (1) tetrahedral cation geometry, (2) electrostatic attraction, and (3) multiple convergent anion-π interactions creates a well-defined, three-dimensional 'capsule-like' binding pocket for anions. This synthon is chemically realistic, as iodonium salts are known stable species, and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatics are well-established in supramolecular chemistry. It maps to the seven primitives through its defined molecular recognition elements (anion-π, electrostatics), directional interactions, and potential for modular assembly into larger supramolecular architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_boronate_ester_cage_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the reversible covalent assembly of boroxine (B₃O₃) rings and boronate esters, forming a tetrahedral coordination cage. The system features a central tetrahedral boron atom (sp³ hybridized) coordinated to three oxygen atoms from a cyclic boroxine unit and one oxygen from a pendant boronate ester linker. This creates a rigid, three-dimensional scaffold with: (1) B–O covalent bonds as strong recognition elements, (2) reversible boronate ester/boroxine formation enabling temporal control (dynamic covalent chemistry), (3) exposed π-surfaces on aromatic substituents attached to boron for guest encapsulation via π-stacking or cation-π interactions, and (4) potential for anion binding via Lewis acidic boron centers. The tetrahedral geometry directs assembly into porous organic cages or coordination networks, suitable for molecular recognition, separation, or catalysis. This synthon maps to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), boron (element), oxygen (ligand), reversible covalent bond (interaction), π-surface (property), cage (assembly), and dynamic exchange (temporal behavior).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_18
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that engages in simultaneous anion binding via electrostatic interaction and π-capsule formation through face-to-face stacking with electron-rich aromatic panels. The iodonium center (hypervalent iodine(III)) provides a strong cationic charge localized in a tetrahedral geometry, while four extended aromatic arms (e.g., pyrene or perylene derivatives) attached via flexible linkers create a π-rich cavity. The system exhibits three interaction primitives: (1) electrostatic anion recognition by the positively charged iodine, (2) π-π stacking between the aromatic panels of adjacent synthons to form a capsule-like enclosure, and (3) potential halogen-bonding-like character from the σ-hole on iodine orthogonal to the I–C bonds. This synthon is chemically realistic, known in iodonium salt chemistry, and extends supramolecular design into hypervalent main-group cation-π-anion ternary recognition motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_cobalt_bis(dioxolene)_redox_switchable_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral cobalt(III) complex with two redox-active catecholate/dioxolene ligands arranged in a divergent geometry. The metal center coordinates two bidentate 3,5-di-tert-butylcatecholate ligands, creating a tetrahedral geometry with the ligands oriented to form two concave π-surfaces. These π-surfaces can engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with oxoanions (sulfate, phosphate) or carboxylates. The key innovation is the redox-switchable nature: reduction to cobalt(II) with concomitant oxidation of catecholate to semiquinone radicals alters both the charge state and π-electron density of the ligand surfaces, modulating binding affinity. This creates a temporal dimension where redox potential controls capsule assembly/disassembly. Recognition elements: (1) tetrahedral metal geometry directing ligand orientation, (2) electron-rich π-surfaces from catecholate aryl rings, (3) redox-active metal-ligand combination, (4) anion-binding pockets. Interaction patterns: metal-ligand coordination (primary), anion-π interactions (recognition), π-π stacking (capsule closure), and redox-switching (temporal control). Mappable to primitives: donor/acceptor (metal-ligand, anion-π), connector (tetrahedral geometry), director (redox state), protector (tert-butyl groups), container (concave surfaces), regulator (redox potential), transformer (catecholate↔semiquinone).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_19
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that acts as a cationic π-acidic capsule for anion binding. The system features: (1) a central iodine(III) atom with three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, pentafluorophenyl, or mesityl groups) arranged in a distorted tetrahedral geometry, (2) the positively charged iodine center creating a σ-hole along each I–C bond axis, enabling halogen bonding, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings on the substituents providing anion-π interactions, and (4) the overall tetrahedral architecture creating a preorganized cavity suitable for encapsulating tetrahedral anions (e.g., ClO4−, BF4−) or spherical halides via synergistic halogen bonding and anion-π contacts. This represents an underexplored class of hypervalent iodine-based supramolecular hosts with dual recognition modes.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_8_hydroxyquinolinate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated to three 8-hydroxyquinolinate ligands, creating a facially polarized metal complex with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The three planar quinoline rings are arranged in a propeller-like geometry around the gallium center, creating a concave, bowl-shaped electron-deficient cavity. This synthon functions as an anion-π capsule building block through: (1) strong anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient quinoline rings and anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻), (2) electrostatic complementarity from the overall +1 charge of the complex after accounting for the anionic ligands, (3) directional hydrogen bonding from the phenolic oxygen atoms at the 8-position, and (4) π-π stacking with complementary electron-rich aromatic systems. The tetrahedral geometry creates a well-defined three-fold symmetric recognition pocket that can encapsulate spherical anions or serve as a convergent binding site for larger anionic guests. This represents a novel metallosupramolecular synthon combining metal coordination geometry, polarized π-surfaces, and electrostatic complementarity for anion recognition and capsule assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salicylaldiminate Schiff base ligand. The complex features a central Ga(III) ion coordinated by two bidentate salicylaldiminate ligands, each providing an O,N-donor set, resulting in a distorted tetrahedral geometry with a formal negative charge. The synthon's recognition elements include: (1) the exposed, electron-deficient gallium center as a Lewis acidic site for anion binding or coordination expansion, (2) the planar, electron-rich aromatic rings of the salicylaldiminate ligands for parallel-displaced π-stacking with complementary electron-deficient arenes, and (3) the imine nitrogen atoms as weak hydrogen bond acceptors. The tetrahedral shape and directional π-surfaces enable it to act as a corner unit in self-assembled capsule frameworks through synergistic anion-π interactions (where the complex's anion interacts with electron-deficient cavity walls) and π-π stacking. This system maps to the seven primitives as: SHAPE (tetrahedral), CHARGE (anionic), POLARITY (polar ligand environment), SIZE (∼8-10 Å span), CONNECTIVITY (4 potential interaction faces), FLEXIBILITY (semi-rigid), and FUNCTION (anion binding/π-acceptor recognition).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salen-type Schiff base ligand (N,N'-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine) that forms an anion-binding pocket. The gallium center coordinates to the tetradentate salen ligand, leaving one axial site occupied by a labile ligand (chloride or solvent) that can be displaced by an anionic guest. The salen ligand's aromatic rings create a π-rich cavity suitable for anion-π interactions with oxoanions like nitrate, perchlorate, or tetrafluoroborate. The tetrahedral geometry directs the anion into the π-capsule, while the gallium's Lewis acidity provides additional electrostatic stabilization. This system combines metal-ligand coordination, anion-π interactions, and geometric preorganization to create a selective supramolecular recognition motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boroxine anion (B₃O₃ ring) that forms a π-acidic capsule through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The core consists of a cyclic trimeric boroxine [(RBO)₃]⁻ anion, where R is an electron-withdrawing substituent (e.g., pentafluorophenyl), creating a planar, highly π-acidic B₃O₃ ring with a delocalized negative charge. This anion acts as a tetrahedral face, engaging in three simultaneous anion-π interactions with the faces of three separate electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or s-tetrazine derivatives) arranged in a trigonal pyramid. The panels are functionalized with peripheral hydrogen-bond acceptors (e.g., pyridyl groups) to enable secondary assembly into a tetrahedral capsule. The synthon exhibits clear recognition elements: (1) the planar, charged boroxine ring as an anion-π donor, (2) electron-deficient aromatics as π-acidic surfaces, and (3) directional hydrogen-bonding motifs at the vertices for capsule closure. It maps to the seven primitives via: shape (tetrahedral), electrostatics (anion-π), dynamics (reversible capsule formation), information (complementary π-surfaces), energy (anion-π binding ~20–40 kJ/mol), matter (B, O, N, C, F), and time (kinetically labile boroxine formation).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_20
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels to form capsule-like architectures. The iodonium center features three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) creating a tetrahedral cationic charge center with significant σ-hole character on iodine, enabling strong anion binding. The synthon incorporates four electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or nitrobenzene derivatives) positioned as faces of a tetrahedron, each capable of engaging in cooperative anion-π interactions with halide or oxoanion guests. The combination of electrostatic attraction from the iodonium cation and directional anion-π interactions from the aromatic panels creates a well-defined, three-dimensional recognition pocket suitable for encapsulating anions. This system demonstrates halogen bonding (from iodonium), anion-π interactions, electrostatic forces, and hydrophobic effects, mapping to primitives including charged species, π-systems, and directional non-covalent interactions for programmable self-assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center chelated by two β-diketonate ligands, creating a facially exposed metal center with a net negative charge. The synthon features two distinct recognition elements: (1) the anionic metal complex can engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, cyanuric acid derivatives) through its π-delocalized β-diketonate rings, and (2) the tetrahedral geometry and Lewis acidic gallium center can participate in weak directional coordination with additional Lewis bases (e.g., ether oxygens, pyridine nitrogens) to guide assembly. This combination enables the formation of dimeric or higher-order capsule-like structures when paired with complementary π-acidic panels and/or coordinating linkers. The system is chemically realistic as gallium(III) readily forms stable, air- and moisture-resistant β-diketonate complexes (e.g., Ga(acac)₃ derivatives), and anion-π interactions with such complexes are documented. The synthon maps to primitives: anion (charged metal complex), π-system (diketonate rings), tetrahedron (metal coordination geometry), hydrogen bond acceptor (ketone oxygens), dipole (polar metal-ligand bonds), and can exhibit temporal behavior through ligand exchange dynamics at the gallium center.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate salen-type Schiff base ligand (N₂O₂ donor set) that forms a cationic metal center. The synthon features: (1) a positively charged Ga³⁺ center with tetrahedral geometry, (2) two axial aromatic rings from the salen ligand oriented perpendicular to the coordination plane, creating a π-rich cavity, (3) electrostatic attraction for anions (Cl⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) positioned within the π-cavity via anion-π interactions, and (4) peripheral substituents (e.g., tert-butyl groups) on the aromatic rings that enable secondary van der Waals contacts. This system combines metal coordination (primitive: bond), electrostatic attraction (primitive: charge), anion-π interactions (primitive: orbital), and shape complementarity (primitive: shape) to create a directional, pre-organized capsule-like building block for supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_21
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) where three aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups) are arranged around a central iodine(I) atom, creating a pyramidal cationic core. The fourth coordination site on iodine is occupied by a weak axial ligand (e.g., solvent or a labile anion). This cationic structure acts as a convergent, three-fold symmetric host that can encapsulate a complementary polyatomic anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or a carboxylate) through a combination of anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic arms and electrostatic attraction to the central positive charge. The three aromatic arms are often substituted with electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., -CF3, -NO2) to enhance both the stability of the hypervalent iodonium center and the anion-π binding affinity. This creates a well-defined, charge-assisted supramolecular capsule motif driven by multivalent anion recognition, suitable for constructing porous ionic crystals or supramolecular assemblies.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_cobalt_diimine_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral cobalt(III) complexes with diimine ligands (e.g., 2,2'-bipyridine or 1,10-phenanthroline derivatives) that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. The synthon features: (1) a positively charged tetrahedral [Co(diimine)₂X₂]⁺ core (X = halide or pseudohalide) with exposed cationic metal center, (2) extended aromatic surfaces on the diimine ligands providing π-acidic recognition sites, and (3) oriented halide ligands that can participate in halogen bonding. These complexes can dimerize through complementary anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient aromatic rings of one complex and the anionic ligands (X⁻) of another, forming capsule-like structures with internal cavities suitable for guest encapsulation. The system combines metal coordination geometry, electrostatic attraction, anion-π interactions, and π-π stacking in a hierarchical assembly pattern that maps to all seven supramolecular primitives.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_boronate_ester_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boroxine core (B₃O₃) functionalized with three boronate ester groups, creating an electron-deficient cavity that exhibits strong anion-π interactions with halide anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻). The boroxine ring provides a rigid, planar, π-acidic surface, while the boronate esters extend outward to form a tetrahedral coordination environment. This system combines (1) covalent B-O bonds in the boroxine core, (2) dynamic covalent B-O bonds in the boronate esters, (3) anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient boroxine ring and the anion, (4) potential C-H···anion interactions from ester alkyl groups, (5) π-stacking between adjacent boroxine planes in extended assemblies, (6) Lewis acid-base interactions at boron centers, and (7) hydrogen bonding involving ester oxygen atoms. The synthon is chemically realistic, inspired by known boroxine and boronate ester chemistry, and represents a novel entry in supramolecular anion recognition with potential for capsule formation through self-assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salicylaldiminate Schiff base ligand that forms an anion-binding capsule through cooperative anion-π interactions. The system features: (1) a Ga(III) center with +3 charge, (2) two bidentate salicylaldiminate ligands (N,O-donors) forming a distorted tetrahedral geometry, (3) an overall anionic complex [Ga(salicylaldiminate)₂]⁻, (4) electron-deficient aromatic rings on the ligand periphery (nitro-substituted phenyl groups) creating multiple anion-π recognition sites, (5) self-assembly into dimeric capsules that encapsulate spherical anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻) through convergent anion-π interactions from four ligand faces. The recognition involves synergistic electrostatic attraction (anion to Ga center) and directional anion-π contacts (anion to electron-deficient arenes), creating a well-defined supramolecular cavity with size selectivity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_22
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) interacting with an electron-rich aromatic anion through anion-π interactions, forming a capsule-like assembly. The iodonium center features three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, mesityl, or electron-withdrawing aryl groups) creating a pyramidal cationic charge. This cation engages with planar, polycyclic aromatic anions (e.g., tetracyanoquinodimethane anion radical, TCNQ•−, or a perfluorinated anthracene carboxylate) via strong anion-π interactions where the anion's π-cloud interacts with the positively charged iodine center. Additional secondary interactions include C–H···π contacts from cation substituents to the anion periphery and potential halogen bonding from iodine to counteranions or solvent molecules. The tetrahedral geometry directs assembly into discrete dimeric or tetrameric capsules that can encapsulate small solvent molecules or ions. This system combines hypervalent iodine chemistry with supramolecular anion-π recognition, offering a novel route to charged, self-assembled architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_23
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that acts as a cationic π-acidic capsule for anion binding. The system features: (1) a central iodine(III) atom with three aryl substituents arranged in a propeller-like tetrahedral geometry, creating a cationic cavity; (2) electron-deficient arenes (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) on the aryl rings that provide strong anion-π interactions; (3) a halide or tetrafluoroborate anion encapsulated within the π-acidic cavity via multipoint anion-π contacts; (4) potential for secondary C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from the aryl C–H groups; (5) tunable cavity size via substituent bulk; (6) redox-active iodine center enabling temporal control through electrochemical switching between I(III) and I(I) states; (7) halogen-bond donor capability from the iodine σ-hole orthogonal to the anion-binding site. This synthon combines pnictogen bonding (hypervalent iodine), anion-π interactions, and electrostatic forces in a well-defined 3D assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_24
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) interacting with electron-rich aromatic panels through anion-π interactions. The system features a central hypervalent iodine(III) cation with three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl groups) arranged in a distorted tetrahedral geometry. This cationic core is encapsulated by four electron-rich, concave aromatic panels (e.g., hexaalkoxytriphenylenes or curved nanographenes) that form a capsule-like structure through anion-π interactions—where the cationic iodine center acts as an 'anion' analog due to its partial positive charge delocalization. The recognition elements include: (1) the tetrahedral iodonium cation as an electrostatic and shape-complementary hub, (2) electron-rich arene panels with preorganized curvature, (3) stabilizing anion-π interactions between the cationic center and π-systems, and (4) peripheral alkoxy chains that provide solubility and additional van der Waals contacts. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through: shape (tetrahedral), electrostatics (cation-π-like attraction), connectivity (multi-point recognition), dynamics (reversible encapsulation), polarity (polar cation with polarizable arenes), charge (formal +1 on iodine), and sterics (complementary curvature).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salicylaldiminate Schiff base ligand that forms an anion-binding capsule through synergistic anion-π and hydrogen bonding interactions. The system features: (1) a Ga³⁺ center coordinated by two oxygen and two nitrogen donors from the salicylaldiminate ligand, creating a rigid tetrahedral geometry; (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (pyridine or phenyl with electron-withdrawing substituents) positioned above and below the metal center, creating π-acidic surfaces; (3) strategically placed hydrogen bond donors (NH groups from the imine moiety) adjacent to the π-surfaces. This arrangement creates a three-dimensional binding pocket capable of encapsulating spherical anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻) through simultaneous anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatics and hydrogen bonding with the NH donors. The tetrahedral geometry enforces a well-defined cavity size, while the metal coordination provides stability and directionality. This synthon represents a novel metal-organic capsule system distinct from previously proposed boron, zinc, or silicon analogs through its specific Ga³⁺ coordination chemistry and salicylaldiminate ligand framework.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with salicylaldiminate ligands that forms an anion-binding capsule through cooperative anion-π interactions. The system features a Ga(III) center coordinated by three bidentate salicylaldiminate ligands (N,O-donors from Schiff bases of salicylaldehyde and primary amines), creating a facially polarized tetrahedral complex with electron-deficient aromatic rings positioned to form a convergent binding pocket. The electron-deficient nature of the aromatic rings (enhanced by the electron-withdrawing imine groups and metal coordination) creates strong anion-π interaction sites. Three such complexes can assemble into a trigonal prismatic capsule through complementary π-π stacking of peripheral aromatic groups, creating an enclosed cavity suitable for binding spherical anions like chloride or bromide. The recognition elements include: (1) metal-ligand coordination (Ga-N and Ga-O bonds), (2) directional anion-π interactions between electron-deficient aromatics and anions, (3) π-π stacking between peripheral aromatic rings of adjacent complexes, and (4) geometric complementarity of the tetrahedral complexes to form a capsule. This represents a novel metallosupramolecular anion receptor system distinct from previously proposed tetrahedral capsules by using gallium(III) with Schiff base ligands rather than porphyrins, catecholates, or dithiolenes.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate salen-type ligand (N,N'-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine derivative) that functions as a cationic capsule. The gallium center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with two phenolate oxygen and two imine nitrogen donors. The cationic complex features: (1) a permanent positive charge on the gallium center, (2) aromatic walls from the salicylidene phenyl rings that create an electron-deficient cavity suitable for anion-π interactions, and (3) preorganized geometry that can encapsulate complementary anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, ClO₄⁻) through a combination of electrostatic attraction and anion-π contacts with the electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon demonstrates a metal-coordination-driven assembly where the tetrahedral geometry enforces a well-defined cavity, and the π-acidic aromatic surfaces provide secondary recognition sites for anions, creating a hierarchical binding motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_cobalt_corrinoid_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral cobalt(III) center within a corrinoid macrocycle (similar to vitamin B12 derivatives) that forms a π-capsule through synergistic interactions. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral Co(III) center with axial ligands (typically cyanide or methyl groups) providing directional coordination geometry, (2) a corrin macrocycle with extended π-conjugation that creates a curved, bowl-shaped hydrophobic cavity, (3) peripheral amide/carboxylate groups on the corrin side chains for hydrogen bonding, and (4) the ability to bind anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, CN⁻) within the π-bowl through anion-π interactions enhanced by the cobalt center's positive charge. The recognition elements include: metal coordination (Co-N₄ from corrin), axial ligand binding sites, curved π-surface for concave-convex stacking, hydrogen bonding from side chains, and electrostatic complementarity. This synthon can self-assemble into dimeric capsules or host-guest complexes with complementary anions, mapping to all seven primitives through its combination of covalent (Co-ligand bonds), coordination (axial sites), electrostatic (charged metal center), van der Waals (π-surface), and directional hydrogen bonding interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_25
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) core where three aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups) are arranged in a propeller-like geometry around the central iodine(III). The fourth ligand is a halide or pseudohalide anion (Cl-, Br-, or BF4-) completing the tetrahedral coordination. The aromatic arms feature electron-deficient arenes (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl) that create strong anion-π interaction sites. This synthon self-assembles into dimeric capsules via complementary interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction between the cationic iodonium center of one monomer and the anion bound to another, (2) cooperative anion-π interactions between electron-deficient aryl faces and the anions, and (3) edge-to-face or offset π-π stacking between the aromatic arms of adjacent monomers. The system represents a rare example of hypervalent iodine(III) cations serving as both electrostatic organizers and structural nodes in supramolecular assembly, combining pnictogen bonding (from iodine(III)), anion-π, and π-π interactions in a single, well-defined recognition motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_26
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that acts as a cationic π-acidic capsule for anion binding. The iodonium center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with three aromatic substituents (e.g., phenyl or pyridyl groups) and a formal positive charge on iodine. The three aromatic arms create a π-acidic cavity through arene-arene interactions, while the central iodonium provides a strong electrostatic binding site for anions (e.g., halides, tetrafluoroborate). This system combines cation-anion electrostatic attraction with anion-π interactions and potential halogen bonding (via the σ-hole on iodine). The tetrahedral geometry enforces a three-dimensional capsule-like structure that can selectively encapsulate anions of complementary size and shape. Recognition elements include: (1) the iodonium cation as an electrophilic center, (2) π-acidic aromatic surfaces for anion-π interactions, (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from ortho-hydrogens, and (4) shape-persistent tetrahedral architecture. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through its defined geometry (shape), electrostatic and dispersion interactions (binding), and directional preferences (orientation).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_crown_ether_cation_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within a crown ether macrocycle, with additional anion-π interactions from electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral ammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium or tetraethylammonium) as the cationic recognition element, (2) a crown ether (e.g., 18-crown-6 or 15-crown-5) that selectively binds the ammonium cation through multiple C–H···O hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) positioned above and below the crown ether plane to engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with an accompanying anion (e.g., chloride or nitrate). This creates a three-dimensional 'capsule-like' environment where the cation is encapsulated by the crown ether, and the anion is held by the π-acidic surfaces, resulting in a stable ion-paired assembly. The synthon can be mapped to the seven primitives through its directional non-covalent interactions, complementary electrostatic surfaces, and preorganized binding sites.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_27
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that forms a capsule-like structure through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The iodonium center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl groups) and a formal positive charge on iodine, creating a strong electrostatic field. This cationic core is surrounded by four electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or s-triazine rings) arranged in a tetrahedral fashion, each engaging in anion-π interactions with halide or pseudohalide anions (Cl-, Br-, I-, or BF4-). The combination of the bulky, charge-dense iodonium cation and the directional anion-π contacts creates a well-defined, three-dimensional recognition motif that can encapsulate anions within a π-rich cavity. This synthon exploits hypervalent iodine chemistry and emerging anion-π interactions, offering a novel entry into charge-assisted supramolecular assembly with potential for chiral induction if asymmetric substituents are used on the iodonium center.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate salen-type Schiff base ligand (N₂O₂ donor set) that forms a cationic metal center.
