This cation engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., s-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives) to form a capsule-like assembly. The synthon combines: (1) metal coordination (Ga³⁺ with imine N and phenolate O), (2) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the anion and the π-acidic panels of the capsule, (4) potential CH-π or van der Waals contacts for capsule closure, (5) geometric preorganization from the rigid salen scaffold enforcing a tetrahedral distortion, (6) reversible assembly/disassembly (temporal aspect) via anion exchange or pH modulation of the Schiff base, and (7) modularity through variation of the salen backbone and π-acidic aromatic units.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_28
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The iodonium center provides a strong cationic charge (+1 formal charge on iodine in hypervalent III oxidation state) that attracts anions, while the three aromatic arms (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) are oriented in a tetrahedral geometry around iodine. These electron-deficient π-systems simultaneously engage in anion-π interactions with the same anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or ClO4-), creating a three-point recognition motif that encapsulates the anion within a π-rich pocket. The system exhibits clear recognition elements: (1) the iodonium cation as an electrophilic/anion-binding site, (2) electron-deficient arenes as anion-π donors, and (3) geometric preorganization for encapsulation. It maps to the seven primitives through: atoms (I, C, F/N, anion atoms), bonds (covalent I-C bonds, ionic/electrostatic interactions, anion-π noncovalent bonds), rings (aromatic rings), cages (encapsulation motif), chains (aryl substituents), intermolecular interactions (anion-π, electrostatic), and functional groups (iodonium, electron-deficient arenes, anions). This represents a novel extension of halogen-based supramolecular chemistry beyond common halogen bonding, utilizing hypervalent iodine's unique geometry and charge.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salicylaldiminate Schiff base ligand that forms an anion-binding capsule through synergistic anion-π and CH-π interactions. The system features a Ga(III) center coordinated by two bidentate salicylaldiminate ligands (N,O-donors from salicylaldehyde-derived Schiff bases), creating a tetrahedral geometry with a formal negative charge. The electron-deficient aromatic rings of the salicylaldiminate ligands are oriented to create a π-acidic cavity capable of binding anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through anion-π interactions. Peripheral tert-butyl groups provide solubility and preorganize the cavity, while methyl groups on the imine nitrogen donors engage in additional CH-π interactions with the bound anion, enhancing binding affinity. This synthon demonstrates a rare combination of metal coordination geometry, anion binding through π-acidic surfaces, and preorganized cavity formation suitable for supramolecular assembly and anion recognition applications.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_29
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) core that engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming a capsule-like structure. The iodonium center provides a strong cationic charge (+1 formal charge on iodine) with tetrahedral geometry enforced by three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and one coordination site occupied by a weakly coordinating anion or solvent. Electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or nitrobenzene derivatives) positioned around the iodonium center create convergent anion-binding pockets via anion-π interactions. This system combines (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) anion-π interactions with polarized arenes, (3) potential halogen bonding from the iodonium iodine, (4) shape complementarity from the tetrahedral arrangement, and (5) solvophobic effects that drive capsule assembly. The synthon can be mapped to the seven primitives: atoms (I, C, N, O, F), bonds (covalent C-I, potential I···anion contacts), angles (tetrahedral ~109.5°), dihedrals (aryl ring orientations), charges (+1 on I), polarity (polarized I⁺-arene systems), and sterics (substituent bulk controlling cavity size).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_boronate_ester_cage_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the dynamic covalent assembly of boroxine (B₃O₃) rings and boronate esters. The system features a tetrahedral boroxine core formed by three boron atoms and three oxygen atoms in a six-membered ring, with each boron atom further functionalized with an aryl group bearing ortho-diol or ortho-diamine substituents. These substituents enable the formation of boronate esters with complementary dialcohols or diamines, creating a 3D tetrahedral cage through reversible B–O or B–N bond formation. Recognition elements include: (1) the planar, electron-deficient boroxine ring acting as a π-acceptor for arene stacking, (2) the tetrahedral boron centers as Lewis acids for dative O→B or N→B coordination, and (3) the reversible covalent boronate ester linkages enabling self-correction and error-checking. This maps to the seven primitives as: atoms (B, O, C, H), bonds (covalent B–O, dative O/N→B), angles (tetrahedral at B, trigonal planar in boroxine ring), dihedrals (conformation of aryl linkers), charges (partial δ+ on B, δ− on O), rings (boroxine 6-membered ring, boronate ester 5-membered chelates), and cages (3D tetrahedral assembly). The system is chemically realistic, inspired by covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and dynamic combinatorial chemistry, and explores underexplored supramolecular domain through reversible covalent bonding and cage formation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_salen_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral germanium(IV) center coordinated to a salen-type (N₂O₂) Schiff base ligand, where the germanium atom bears a formal positive charge and is further coordinated to an anionic axial ligand (e.g., chloride or phenolate). This cationic complex is designed to act as a 'cap' for an electron-rich aromatic cavity. The key recognition elements are: 1) The tetrahedral germanium cation serves as a strong anion-binding site via electrostatic and coordinative interactions with the axial anion. 2) The planar, electron-deficient π-surface of the salen ligand's aromatic rings (often with electron-withdrawing substituents) engages in complementary anion-π interactions with the bound anion. 3) The overall wedge-shaped geometry of the complex, with the germanium at the apex and the salen ligand forming a broad base, allows it to function as one hemisphere of a molecular capsule when paired with an identical or complementary counterpart. The interaction patterns map to the seven primitives as: AFFINITY (Ge⁺-anion coordination), SHAPE (tetrahedral metal center + planar aromatic panel), POLARITY (cationic metal, anionic guest, polarized π-system), SIZE (defined by salen ligand span), DIRECTIONALITY (tetrahedral coordination geometry), COOPERATIVITY (combined electrostatic and anion-π binding), and ADAPTABILITY (axial ligand exchangeability). This system explores the underexplored combination of germanium coordination chemistry, salen ligands, and anion-π interactions within a supramolecular capsule architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_30
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that engages in simultaneous anion binding and electron-deficient arene π-interactions to form capsule-like architectures. The iodonium center features three bulky aryl substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenyl groups) creating a pyramidal cation with a σ-hole along the I–C bond axis. This σ-hole interacts strongly with anions (Cl–, Br–, PF6–) via halogen bonding, while the electron-deficient fluorinated arene faces engage in anion–π interactions with the same or additional anions, and parallel-displaced π–π stacking with other electron-rich arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene). The combination of directional halogen bonds and multi-point π-interpositions leads to predictable, capsule-like dimeric or tetrameric assemblies in the solid state. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through: (1) halogen bond donor (I+), (2) anion acceptor, (3) electron-deficient π-surface, (4) electron-rich π-donor partner, (5) tetrahedral node, (6) self-complementary interaction set, and (7) encapsulation geometry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salicylaldiminate ligand system, where the electron-deficient metal center (Ga³⁺) coordinates to three anionic oxygen/nitrogen donors from the Schiff base ligand, creating a facially polarized complex. The fourth coordination site is occupied by a labile solvent molecule or weakly coordinating anion. The planar aromatic portions of the salicylaldiminate ligands present extended π-deficient surfaces that can engage in complementary anion-π interactions with electron-rich anions (e.g., halides, tetrafluoroborate). Simultaneously, the overall tetrahedral geometry and hydrophobic exterior allow for capsule formation through van der Waals contacts and CH-π interactions with other identical units or complementary partners. This system combines metal-ligand coordination (primitive: bond), directional electrostatic/anion-π interactions (primitive: columb), aromatic surface complementarity (primitive: surface), and three-dimensional shape matching (primitive: shape) to create programmable self-assembling architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated by two β-diketonate ligands, creating a neutral complex with a pronounced electron-deficient region above the metal center. The β-diketonate ligands provide a rigid, planar, and π-conjugated surface with partial negative charge on the oxygen atoms. The overall complex adopts a tetrahedral geometry where the two chelating ligands occupy four coordination sites, leaving the gallium center with a formal positive charge. This creates a strong, localized electrophilic region (the metal center and its coordination sphere) capable of engaging in anion-π interactions with electron-rich arenes or anions, and simultaneously, the π-conjugated diketonate arms can participate in conventional π-π stacking or hydrogen bonding via their carbonyl oxygens. This synthon is designed to act as a 'capsule corner' in coordination-driven self-assembly, where multiple such units can link via bridging ligands or direct metal-metal interactions to form hollow 3D structures capable of guest encapsulation. The gallium(III) oxidation state ensures kinetic inertness and thermodynamic stability, while the β-diketonate provides synthetic tunability of electronic and steric properties.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with salicylaldiminate ligands that creates an electron-deficient cavity capable of anion-π interactions. The gallium center coordinates to three bidentate salicylaldiminate ligands (N,O-donors derived from salicylaldehyde and primary amines), forming a facially polarized complex with a partial positive charge on the metal center and electron-deficient aromatic rings oriented toward a central cavity. The three planar aromatic systems create a trigonal pyramidal electron-deficient pocket that can bind anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through cooperative anion-π interactions. The salicylaldiminate ligands provide additional hydrogen-bond acceptor sites (imine nitrogen and phenolate oxygen) at the periphery for secondary assembly into larger capsules or frameworks. This system combines metal coordination geometry, directional anion-π recognition, and peripheral hydrogen-bonding sites for hierarchical supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center chelated by two β-diketonate ligands (e.g., acetylacetonate derivatives), creating a neutral, hydrophobic complex with a net negative charge localized on the oxygen atoms. The planar, conjugated β-diketonate arms present extended π-surfaces. These π-surfaces are designed to engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with suitable tetraalkylammonium or phosphonium cations, while the overall tetrahedral shape and hydrophobic exterior promote assembly into dimeric or higher-order capsule-like structures in non-polar solvents. The recognition elements are: (1) the anionic, chelated metal center (electrostatic/coordination primitive), (2) the extended, electron-deficient π-systems of the diketonates (anion-π/π-π primitive), and (3) the complementary shape and hydrophobicity of the tetrahedral complex (shape/solvophobic primitive). This system explores the underexplored combination of a neutral metal complex acting as an anion-π donor for cationic guests within a supramolecular assembly framework.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_cobalt_corrinoid_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral cobalt(III) center coordinated within a corrinoid macrocycle (similar to vitamin B12 derivatives), where the axial ligand is an anionic group (e.g., cyanide, thiolate, or carboxylate) that participates in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels of a capsule-forming host. The equatorial corrin ring provides a hydrophobic, shape-persistent platform for additional van der Waals contacts and directional hydrogen bonding via peripheral amide/carboxyl substituents. This system combines metal coordination geometry, macrocyclic preorganization, and anion-π recognition to direct capsule assembly, with potential redox-switchable behavior via Co(III)/Co(II) couples (temporal domain). Recognition elements: (1) tetrahedral metal center with anionic axial ligand, (2) electron-deficient aromatic surfaces on capsule panels, (3) peripheral H-bond donors/acceptors on corrin periphery, (4) hydrophobic corrin surface for dispersion interactions. Mappable to primitives: contact (Co–ligand bonds, anion-π), complementarity (shape-matched capsule panels), constraint (macrocyclic and tetrahedral geometry), change (redox switching), conduit (charge transfer upon anion-π interaction), concentration (capsule cavity encloses guest), and context (solvent-dependent assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with salicylaldiminate ligands that forms a directional anion-π capsule assembly. The system features: (1) a Ga(III) center in tetrahedral coordination geometry with two bidentate salicylaldiminate ligands (N,O-donors), creating a monoanionic complex; (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (pyridine or triazine substituents) incorporated into the ligand framework that provide strong anion-π recognition sites; (3) complementary hydrogen bond donors/acceptors on ligand periphery for secondary stabilization; (4) the anionic metal complex acts as a 'guest' that is encapsulated by electron-deficient aromatic 'host' panels through cooperative anion-π interactions; (5) the tetrahedral geometry enforces a specific orientation of recognition elements, enabling predictable self-assembly into capsule-like architectures; (6) tunable through substituents on both the imine and aromatic components; (7) applicable in molecular recognition, supramolecular catalysis, and anion-responsive materials.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_31
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that forms a capsule-like structure through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The iodonium center adopts a T-shaped geometry with three organic substituents (typically aryl groups with electron-withdrawing substituents like -CF3 or -NO2) that create a cationic, electron-deficient cavity. This cavity selectively binds anions (Cl-, Br-, PF6-) through cooperative anion-π interactions with the π-faces of the aryl groups. The tetrahedral arrangement of the three aryl arms creates a pre-organized, bowl-shaped recognition site that encapsulates anions via multiple simultaneous anion-π contacts. This represents a rare example of a hypervalent iodine-based supramolecular host with potential applications in anion sensing and transport.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldimine_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with salicylaldimine ligands that forms an anion-binding capsule through synergistic anion-π interactions. The system features: (1) a Ga³⁺ center coordinated by three bidentate salicylaldimine ligands (N,O-donors), creating a tetrahedral metal complex with a +1 formal charge; (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings on the ligand periphery (fluorinated phenyl or pyridine substituents) that create multiple anion-π recognition sites; (3) a convergent arrangement of these π-deficient surfaces that collectively encapsulates spherical or tetrahedral anions (Cl⁻, BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻) through multipoint anion-π interactions. The recognition involves simultaneous electrostatic attraction between the cationic metal center and anion, plus directional anion-π contacts with the electron-poor aromatic rings. This represents a hybrid metal-organic supramolecular synthon combining coordination chemistry with anion-π interactions for selective anion recognition and encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_32
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) that forms a capsule-like structure through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The iodonium center provides a strong cationic charge (+1 formal charge on iodine) with tetrahedral geometry enforced by three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl or 2,4,6-triisopropylphenyl groups) and one labile ligand (often solvent or weakly coordinating anion). This cationic core is surrounded by four electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or perfluorinated naphthalene units) arranged in a tetrahedral fashion, creating a cavity that binds anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-) through cooperative anion-π interactions. The system exhibits strong directionality due to the σ-hole on iodine (pnictogen bond donor) and the polarized π-systems, enabling predictable self-assembly into larger capsules or frameworks. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral iodonium cation (electrophilic center), (2) electron-deficient π-panels (anion-binding sites), (3) anion guests, and (4) potential secondary interactions (C–H···anion, halogen–halogen). This synthon maps to primitives: A (iodonium as electrophile), B (anion as nucleophile), C (anion-π as attractive interaction), D (steric bulk of substituents as repulsive element), E (tetrahedral geometry as constraint), F (assembly into capsule as higher-order structure), and G (anion binding/release as reversible process).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_cobalt_bis(dioximato)_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral cobalt(III) complex with two bridging dioximato ligands (dimethylglyoximate or similar), forming an anionic metal complex [Co(dmgH)₂]⁻. The planar, electron-rich π-surfaces of the dioximato ligands create concave aromatic faces that can engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The tetrahedral geometry positions these π-surfaces in a convergent arrangement, creating a 'capsule-like' recognition pocket. This synthon can form supramolecular assemblies through: (1) anion-π interactions between the electron-rich dioximato ligands and electron-deficient arenes (e.g., nitroaromatics, cyanobenzenes), (2) hydrogen bonding via the oxime N-OH groups, (3) metal coordination to additional ligands, and (4) electrostatic interactions with cations. The cobalt(III) center provides redox stability and potential for chirality when using asymmetric dioximato ligands. This system maps to primitives through its convergent geometry (shape), electron-rich π-surfaces (property), anion-π recognition (interaction), and potential for hierarchical assembly (hierarchy).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_33
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R-I⁺-R') where the iodine(III) center adopts a T-shaped geometry with two organic substituents and a lone pair. The cationic iodine center engages in strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) that form the walls of a self-assembled capsule. The iodonium's σ-hole along the C-I⁺-C axis provides directional halogen bonding to encapsulated anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻), while the cationic charge enhances anion binding. The tetrahedral arrangement of the iodonium within the capsule creates a polarized microenvironment suitable for stabilizing reactive intermediates or facilitating selective reactions. This system combines pnictogen/halogen bonding (iodonium as hypervalent iodine), anion-π interactions, and electrostatic complementarity in a well-defined supramolecular architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salicylaldiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salicylaldiminate Schiff base ligand that creates a concave, electron-deficient cavity. The gallium center coordinates to the tridentate ONO-donor ligand, forming a rigid tetrahedral geometry with one coordination site occupied by a labile ligand (chloride or solvent). The planar aromatic portion of the salicylaldiminate ligand presents an electron-deficient π-surface due to the electron-withdrawing imine group and coordination to the Lewis acidic gallium. This creates a convergent anion-π binding site capable of encapsulating anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through a combination of electrostatic attraction and π-hole interactions. The system functions as a 'capsule' synthon because the tetrahedral arrangement positions three additional substituents (typically alkyl or aryl groups on the imine nitrogen) to create a partial enclosure around the bound anion. Recognition elements include: (1) Lewis acidic metal center (Ga³⁺), (2) electron-deficient aromatic π-system, (3) convergent electrostatic field from the tetrahedral geometry, and (4) secondary C-H···anion interactions from the substituents. This represents a novel metal-organic capsule synthon distinct from previously proposed boron, zinc, or silicon systems, exploring gallium's intermediate Lewis acidity and the versatile salicylaldiminate ligand scaffold.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_β_diketiminate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron center coordinated to a β-diketiminate ligand, forming an anionic complex with extended π-surface. The boron atom adopts tetrahedral geometry with one coordination site occupied by a halide or pseudohalide, while the remaining three sites are bound to the nitrogen atoms of the β-diketiminate scaffold. This creates a rigid, planar π-conjugated system with electron-rich character, enabling multiple interaction modes: (1) anion-π interactions between the boron-centered anion and electron-deficient aromatic systems, (2) π-π stacking of the extended diketiminate aromatic wings, (3) potential halogen bonding via the coordinated halide, and (4) metal coordination through the nitrogen lone pairs. The synthon can serve as a building block for self-assembled capsules through complementary anion-π and π-π interactions, with the tetrahedral geometry directing assembly toward three-dimensional architectures. This system explores underexplored boron-anion supramolecular chemistry distinct from the catalog's existing metal-centered tetrahedral anions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral anionic boron(III) complexes of dipyrromethene (BODIPY-like) ligands that function as anion-π recognition units for encapsulation chemistry. The system features a tetrahedral boron center coordinated to two dipyrromethene ligands, creating a rigid, planar π-electron deficient cavity with four fluorine substituents at the boron center. The anionic character arises from the formal negative charge on the tetrahedral boron center, while the extended π-system of the dipyrromethene ligands creates electron-deficient surfaces suitable for anion-π interactions with cationic or neutral electron-rich guests. The fluorine substituents provide additional halogen bonding sites for orthogonal recognition. This synthon can self-assemble into dimeric capsules through complementary anion-π and π-π stacking interactions, creating confined spaces for guest encapsulation with potential applications in molecular sensing and catalysis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boronate anions formed from catechol derivatives and boronic acids, creating an anionic tetrahedral boron center with extended aromatic systems. The catecholate ligand provides a rigid, planar π-surface that can participate in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules or receptors. The boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with one vacant coordination site occupied by a hydroxyl or alkoxy group, making it anionic. This creates a dual recognition motif: (1) the anionic charge allows electrostatic interactions with cationic hosts, and (2) the extended catechol π-system enables stacking interactions with complementary π-surfaces in capsule architectures. The system is chemically realistic, drawing from known boronate ester chemistry and anion-π recognition principles, and can be mapped to primitives through its geometric constraints, charge distribution, and directional non-covalent interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boronate anions formed from catechol derivatives and boronic acids, creating an anionic tetrahedral boron center with extended π-systems. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral boron(III) center coordinated by two catecholate oxygen donors and two additional substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups), forming a stable boronate anion; (2) extended aromatic surfaces (e.g., naphthalene- or pyrene-substituted catechols) that provide large, planar π-surfaces for anion-π interactions; (3) these anionic, π-rich assemblies can serve as recognition elements for complementary cationic or π-deficient hosts, enabling capsule formation through synergistic electrostatic and stacking interactions. The boronate anion is chemically robust, tunable via substituent choice, and offers directional recognition through both its negative charge distribution and planar aromatic wings. This synthon maps to primitives: charge (anionic center), shape (tetrahedral core with planar extensions), polarity (polar B-O bonds with delocalized π-systems), hydrogen bonding capability (through catechol OH groups if not fully deprotonated), aromaticity (extended π-systems), conformational flexibility (substituent rotation), and redox activity (catechol/quinone redox couple if accessible).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boronate anions formed from boron(III) complexed with catechol derivatives, creating an electron-rich anionic center that engages in synergistic anion-π and π-π stacking interactions with complementary electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral boron center with formal negative charge delocalized over the catecholate oxygen atoms, (2) extended aromatic substituents on the catechol rings providing large π-surfaces for stacking, (3) electron-deficient pyridinium- or triazine-based capsule components that create complementary electrostatic and π-stacking recognition, and (4) tunable cavity size through catechol substituent modification. Recognition elements include: anion-π interactions between the boronate anion and electron-deficient aromatics, offset π-π stacking between catechol aromatics and capsule walls, and potential weak C-H···O hydrogen bonds. This represents a novel entry in the under-explored supramolecular domain, combining organoboron chemistry with host-guest recognition principles.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral borate anions derived from BODIPY (boron-dipyrromethene) fluorophores, where the anionic boron center (BF₂⁻ or B(OR)₂⁻ variant) engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels of a self-assembled capsule. The tetrahedral geometry of the borate anion (sp³ boron with two fluorides/alkoxides and two nitrogen donors from the dipyrromethene core) provides directional recognition, while the extended π-surface of the BODIPY ligand enables additional π-π stacking or edge-to-face interactions with capsule walls. This system combines anion-π recognition (borate anion to electron-poor arene), metal-free coordination geometry, and fluorescent reporting capability within a self-assembled encapsulation motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) complexed with dipyrromethene (BODIPY-like) ligands bearing anionic substituents, designed to form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral boron center with three anionic oxygen donors from β-diketonate-type chelates and one axial anionic group (e.g., phenolate or carboxylate), (2) extended π-conjugated dipyrromethene frameworks that provide large, polarized aromatic surfaces, (3) electron-deficient tetrafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl substituents on the boron periphery to enhance anion binding affinity, and (4) pre-organized geometry that fits within complementary π-acidic molecular capsules (e.g., tetrahedral perfluorinated arene-based cages). Recognition elements include: anion-π interactions between the anionic oxygen donors and electron-deficient capsule walls, π-π stacking between conjugated ligands and aromatic panels, and shape complementarity with tetrahedral capsule cavities. This synthon enables programmable assembly of photoactive supramolecular structures with potential applications in sensing and light-harvesting systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boronate anions formed from catechol derivatives and boronic acids, creating an anionic tetrahedral boron center with extended π-conjugated aromatic systems. The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral boron(III) center coordinated by two catecholate oxygen donors and two additional substituents (typically aryl groups), forming a negatively charged boronate anion; (2) extended aromatic surfaces from the catechol and boron-bound aryl groups that enable π-π stacking and anion-π interactions; (3) oxygen atoms from the catecholate moiety that can participate in hydrogen bonding or Lewis acid-base interactions; (4) a well-defined tetrahedral geometry that directs the orientation of the π-systems for capsule-like assembly. This system combines the directionality of tetrahedral coordination with the versatility of boronate ester chemistry and the rich non-covalent interactions of extended π-systems, making it suitable for constructing supramolecular capsules through complementary electrostatic and π-based interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) complexed with catecholate ligands, forming an anionic species with extended aromatic surfaces that can engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with two oxygen donors from the catecholate and two additional anionic or neutral ligands (e.g., fluoride or hydroxide), creating a rigid, negatively charged core. The planar, electron-rich catecholate π-systems provide recognition surfaces for complementary electron-deficient aromatic panels in capsule assemblies. This synthon combines coordination chemistry (B–O bonds), electrostatic interactions (anion charge), and π-based recognition (anion-π to electron-deficient arenes) to direct the assembly of well-defined supramolecular capsules or frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron(III) center coordinated to two β-diketonate ligands, forming a monoanionic complex with extended aromatic substituents. The boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with two oxygen atoms from each β-diketonate and one additional anionic site (e.g., fluoride or hydroxide) completing the coordination sphere. The β-diketonate ligands are functionalized with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) that create strong anion-π recognition surfaces. This anionic boron complex acts as a guest that can be encapsulated within π-basic aromatic capsule hosts (e.g., resorcinarene or pyrogallolarene-based cavitands) through complementary anion-π interactions. The synthon combines metal-like coordination geometry (boron as a Lewis acid), anionic charge, and programmed π-surfaces for directed assembly into larger supramolecular architectures or capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6

The electron-deficient boron center creates a region of positive electrostatic potential, enabling anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic systems. The planar, conjugated dipyrromethene ligand provides extended π-surface for stacking interactions, while the tetrahedral geometry creates directional recognition elements. This system can form self-assembled capsules through complementary anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient boron center of one complex and the π-system of another, combined with π-π stacking of the dipyrromethene planes. The synthon maps to primitives through: (1) tetrahedral geometry (shape), (2) boron(III) center (element), (3) dipyrromethene ligand (scaffold), (4) anion-π interactions (recognition), (5) π-π stacking (secondary interaction), (6) tunable axial substituents (modulation), and (7) reversible capsule formation (dynamics).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_boronate_ester_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronate anion encapsulated within a boroxine-based π-acidic aromatic capsule. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral boronate anion [B(OR)₄]⁻ with electron-withdrawing substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenoxy groups) that enhances its stability and Lewis acidity; (2) a self-assembled boroxine trimer (B₃O₃) ring functionalized with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or cyanophenyl groups) that create a π-acidic cavity; (3) synergistic anion-π interactions between the boronate anion and the electron-deficient aromatic walls of the capsule; (4) additional C–H···O hydrogen bonds between boronate alkoxy groups and boroxine oxygen atoms; (5) potential for dynamic covalent exchange at both boronate and boroxine sites, enabling temporal control over capsule formation and guest encapsulation. This system combines dynamic covalent chemistry (boronate/boroxine equilibria) with supramolecular anion-π recognition in a single, tunable assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_34
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) where three aromatic arms with electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or 1,3,5-triazine rings) are arranged around a central iodine(III) atom. The cationic iodine center acts as a strong halogen bond donor, while the electron-deficient aromatic arms create convergent anion-π binding pockets. This creates a three-dimensional, cage-like recognition site capable of encapsulating an anionic guest (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or a carboxylate) through a combination of electrostatic attraction, halogen bonding (I+···anion), and multiple cooperative anion-π interactions. The synthon maps to the seven primitives via: (1) I+ as an electrophilic site (Electrophile), (2) anion as a nucleophile (Nucleophile), (3) aromatic rings as π-acceptors (π-system), (4) halogen bond as a directional interaction (Polar Attraction), (5) tetrahedral geometry defining a cavity (Container), (6) cooperative binding for high affinity (Amplifier), and (7) potential for redox-active iodine centers (Redox).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) centers chelated by catecholate ligands, forming an anionic complex with extended aromatic surfaces. The system features: (1) a rigid tetrahedral boron center providing directional geometry, (2) catecholate ligands with extended π-conjugation creating large, planar aromatic surfaces, (3) a formal negative charge on the boron-catecholate complex enabling anion-π interactions, and (4) peripheral substituents (e.g., tert-butyl groups) providing solubility and preventing aggregation. This synthon can serve as a building block for self-assembled capsules through complementary anion-π interactions between the electron-rich aromatic surfaces of one complex and electron-deficient aromatic panels of another, or through coordination with cationic metal centers. The boron-catecholate unit is chemically robust, synthetically accessible, and offers tunable electronic properties through substituent variation on the catechol ring.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_boronate_ester_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronate anion (formed from boronic acid and catechol) encapsulated within a cyclic boroxine trimer (B₃O₃) π-bowl. The boroxine ring acts as an electron-deficient π-acidic host through its empty p-orbitals on boron, engaging in anion-π interactions with the tetrahedral boronate anion positioned above its centroid. The system features: (1) covalent B-O bonds forming the boronate ester anion, (2) directional O→B dative bonds in the boroxine ring, (3) strong anion-π interactions between the anionic boronate and the electron-deficient boroxine π-surface, (4) potential C-H···O hydrogen bonds from aromatic substituents on the catechol to boroxine oxygen atoms, (5) π-π stacking between aromatic substituents on both components, (6) electrostatic complementarity between anion and electron-deficient host, and (7) well-defined three-dimensional geometry enabling predictable self-assembly into capsule-like structures. This represents a novel boron-based supramolecular system combining Lewis acid/base chemistry with anion-π recognition in an underexplored structural motif.

The catecholate provides redox activity and strong chelation, while the tetrahedral geometry enforces directional assembly. Recognition elements include: (1) the anionic charge localized on the boron-catecholate core, (2) the curved π-surface of the catecholate aryl ring, (3) potential hydrogen-bond acceptor sites at the oxygen atoms, and (4) the tetrahedral geometry directing outward-facing substituents. This maps to primitives as: electron-rich/electron-deficient (anion-π), concave/convex (curved π-surface), charged/neutral, redox-active, directional (tetrahedral), chelating, and self-assembling.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2

The boroxine ring (formed from three boronic acid units via dehydration) carries a negative charge delocalized over the B-O framework, making it an excellent anion-π donor. Recognition elements: (1) tetrahedral geometry of both anion and receptor, (2) charge-complementarity (anion-π), (3) shape matching of concave boroxine with convex aromatic panels, (4) directional B-O dipole alignment with π-system quadrupole.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6

This represents a metallosupramolecular anion-π capsule system distinct from purely organic or main-group element capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10

This represents an underexplored combination of coordination chemistry (boron-catecholate), supramolecular anion-π interactions, and directional assembly toward capsules rather than extended networks.

The system can be mapped to the seven primitives: atoms (Zn, N, O), bonds (coordinate, covalent), motifs (tetrahedral metal center, macrocyclic ring), interactions (coordination, electrostatic, π-stacking, anion-π), roles (host, guest), rules (coordination geometry, charge complementarity), and contexts (supramolecular assembly, host-guest chemistry).

This synthon can function as a building block for self-assembled capsules through complementary anion-π interactions between the electron-rich ligand π-surface of one complex and an electron-deficient aromatic cavity (e.g., nitroarenes, cyanopyridiniums) of another. The system exhibits clear recognition via (1) metal-ligand coordination (B–N, B–O), (2) π-conjugation across the chelate ring, (3) electrostatic anion-π attraction, and (4) shape complementarity from tetrahedral geometry directing capsule assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_bis(dipicolylamine)_anion_π_capsule_synthon
