Two such anions orient with their electron-deficient aromatic faces parallel, creating a concave π-surface that encapsulates small cationic or neutral guests through anion-π interactions with the boronate oxyanions and complementary π-π stacking between the fluorinated aryl rings. The recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral geometry enforcing directional interactions, (2) electron-deficient π-surfaces for anion-π binding, (3) exposed anionic oxygen lone pairs for secondary hydrogen bonding or electrostatic interactions, and (4) fluorinated aromatic rings for orthogonal C–F···π contacts. This synthon maps to primitives: SHAPE (tetrahedral), CHARGE (anionic), POLARITY (polar electron-deficient π-system), TOPOLOGY (concave binding pocket), ENERGY (moderate anion-π binding ~20-40 kJ/mol), TIME (reversible capsule formation), and INFORMATION (complementary electrostatic and geometric recognition).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_dithiolene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(III) complexed with two aromatic dithiolene ligands, forming an anionic [Sb(dithiolene)₂]⁻ species that acts as a π-rich capsule. The antimony center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with two bidentate dithiolene ligands, each featuring extended aromatic systems (e.g., benzene-1,2-dithiolate derivatives). The resulting anion possesses a concave, electron-rich π-surface capable of encapsulating small cationic or neutral guests via anion-π interactions, cation-π interactions, and van der Waals contacts. The sulfur atoms provide additional Lewis basic sites for secondary coordination or hydrogen bonding. This synthon combines metal coordination geometry, redox-active dithiolene ligands, and supramolecular encapsulation in a single entity, mapping to primitives of shape (tetrahedral core), charge (anionic), π-system (extended conjugation), and recognition (concave binding pocket).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholboronate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron center chelated by a catecholboronate anion, designed to form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels in self-assembled capsules. The boron atom is sp³-hybridized and bears a formal negative charge, balanced by an external cation (e.g., tetraalkylammonium). The catecholboronate unit provides a rigid, planar, and highly polarized anionic face that can act as a strong anion-π donor to complementary electron-poor arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or pyrazine panels) in coordination cages or hydrogen-bonded capsules. The system exploits the synergy between the Lewis acidic boron, the chelate effect of catechol, and the directionality of anion-π contacts to drive selective encapsulation or framework formation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on cyclic boroxine (B₃O₃) anions that form tetrahedral coordination environments through B-O-B bridging, creating electron-deficient boron centers that engage in strong anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives). The system self-assembles into capsule-like structures where four boroxine rings occupy tetrahedral vertices, connected by π-acidic aromatic spacers. Each boroxine unit acts as a Lewis acidic anion receptor, while the aromatic panels provide complementary π-surfaces for encapsulation of small cationic or neutral guests. Recognition elements include: (1) B-O σ* orbitals as electron acceptors for anion binding, (2) planar boroxine rings as structural directors, (3) aromatic π-systems for stacking interactions, and (4) tetrahedral symmetry enabling 3D capsule formation. Mapped to primitives: Contact (B-O bonds, π-stacking), Polarity (polar B-O vs. aromatic regions), Shape (tetrahedral capsule), Charge (anionic boroxine, cationic guests), Flexibility (conformational adaptation of spacers), Reactivity (Lewis acid-base interactions), and Information (directional assembly via symmetry).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(III) catecholate anions that form self-assembled π-capsules through anion-π interactions. The system features Sb(III) centers chelated by two catecholate ligands (1,2-dihydroxybenzene derivatives) with a lone pair, creating a distorted tetrahedral geometry with overall negative charge. The electron-rich catecholate aromatic rings engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or triazine derivatives) on adjacent synthons, directing assembly into dimeric or oligomeric capsules. The Sb(III) lone pair provides additional Lewis basic character for potential secondary interactions, while the catecholate hydroxyl groups can participate in hydrogen bonding networks. This synthon combines metal-organic coordination geometry, redox-active ligands, and directional supramolecular interactions for programmable self-assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_15
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron center coordinated by two catecholate ligands, forming a rigid, bowl-shaped anion with electron-rich aromatic surfaces. The boron atom (B³⁺) is chelated by two ortho-dihydroxybenzene (catechol) derivatives, creating a stable anionic complex [B(cat)₂]⁻. This anion features four electron-rich π-surfaces (two from each catecholate) arranged in a tetrahedral-like geometry around the central boron. The synthon functions as a π-basic capsule component that can encapsulate cationic or electron-deficient species through anion-π interactions, complemented by potential C–H···π and lone pair-π interactions. The catecholate oxygens provide additional hydrogen-bond acceptor sites at the periphery. This system combines metal-like coordination geometry (tetrahedral) with organic π-surfaces, creating a versatile building block for supramolecular capsules, anion-responsive hosts, or frameworks with tunable electronics via catecholate substituents.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_dithiolene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(III) complexed with a dithiolene ligand framework, forming an anionic [Sb(dithiolene)₂]⁻ species that acts as a π-acidic capsule component. The antimony center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with two bidentate dithiolene ligands, creating an electron-deficient cavity with significant π-acidity on the ligand periphery. This anion can engage in complementary anion-π interactions with cationic arenes or electron-rich π-systems, while the sulfur atoms of the dithiolene ligands provide additional chalcogen bonding sites. The system exhibits dual recognition: (1) electrostatic and anion-π interactions between the anionic antimony complex and cationic/π-basic partners, and (2) chalcogen bonding from sulfur to electron donors. This represents a novel metal-organic capsule synthon combining pnictogen (Sb) coordination chemistry with dithiolene redox activity and supramolecular recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_36
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral iodonium cations (R3I+) interacting with electron-rich aromatic anions through anion-π interactions, forming capsule-like assemblies. The iodonium center features three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) creating a tetrahedral cationic geometry, while the fourth position is occupied by a positive charge. This cation interacts with planar, electron-rich aromatic anions (e.g., tetraphenylborate, BArF4-, or carboxylate-substituted polyaromatic anions) through directional anion-π interactions where the anion sits above the π-face of one aromatic substituent. Additional secondary interactions include C-H···anion contacts and potential halogen bonding from the iodonium center to counteranions. The system exhibits reversible assembly/disassembly under electrochemical or chemical redox control (temporal domain), with the iodonium's oxidation state and geometry directing capsule formation. Recognition elements: (1) tetrahedral cationic iodonium center, (2) planar aromatic anions with extended π-systems, (3) complementary electrostatic and dispersion-driven anion-π interactions, (4) tunable substituents for cavity size control.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_37
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) interacting with electron-rich aromatic anions via anion-π interactions to form capsule-like structures. The iodonium center features three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) creating a pyramidal cationic charge center with significant σ-hole character on iodine. This engages with planar, electron-rich aromatic anions (e.g., tetraphenylborate, BAr4-, or carboxylate-substituted polyaromatic anions) through directional anion-π interactions. The tetrahedral geometry of the cation and planar geometry of the anions enable assembly into dimeric or higher-order capsule architectures through complementary electrostatic and dispersion forces. Recognition elements include: (1) the σ-hole on iodine for anion binding, (2) electron-deficient regions on the iodonium substituents for additional π-π or C-H···π contacts, and (3) tunable anion aromatic systems for geometric matching. This system explores underutilized hypervalent iodine supramolecular chemistry and expands anion-π motifs beyond typical nitroaromatic or triazine acceptors.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_38
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) core, where three aryl substituents are functionalized with electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl) to create convergent anion-π binding sites. The fourth ligand is a labile group (e.g., OH, OTs) that can be displaced, allowing the cation to act as an electrophilic capsule precursor. The electron-deficient aryl faces attract anions (Cl-, BF4-, etc.) via anion-π interactions, while the overall tetrahedral geometry preorganizes these faces to form a partial capsule or cage when combined with complementary anionic components. This system combines hypervalent iodine chemistry (iodonium cations) with supramolecular anion-π recognition and preorganized tetrahedral geometry, enabling the construction of charged capsule architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_16
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) complexed with catecholate ligands, forming an anionic tetrahedral core [B(cat)₂]⁻. The catecholate aromatic rings provide extended π-surfaces for anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine rings) from complementary synthons. The anionic charge is delocalized over the oxygen atoms and the aromatic system, enabling both electrostatic and π-stacking recognition. This synthon can dimerize with cationic tetrahedral species via charge-assisted anion-cation pairing, or form extended capsules with π-acidic aromatic hosts through multi-point anion-π contacts. The boron center offers tunability via substituents on the catecholate rings (electron-withdrawing groups enhance anion-π donor strength; electron-donating groups modulate solubility and stacking geometry). This system combines metal-like coordination geometry (tetrahedral) with organic π-functionality, bridging molecular and supramolecular domains.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin complex where the central zinc coordinates to a porphyrin macrocycle and an axial anionic ligand (typically carboxylate or phenolate). The porphyrin's extended π-system engages in complementary anion-π interactions with tetrahedral anions like perchlorate (ClO₄⁻) or tetrafluoroborate (BF₄⁻). The overall tetrahedral geometry of the metal center combined with the planar π-surface creates a directional, three-dimensional recognition motif capable of assembling into capsule-like structures through synergistic metal coordination, anion-π, and π-π stacking interactions. This represents a metallo-supramolecular building block with orthogonal interaction vectors.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_39
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral iodonium cations (R3I+) that form charge-assisted anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like assembly. The iodonium center features three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, mesityl, or electron-withdrawing aryl groups) and a positive charge localized on iodine, making it a strong electrophile. The anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or BArF-) interacts with the electron-deficient π-system of adjacent panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or perfluorinated arenes) integrated into the ligand framework. This combination of cation-anion electrostatic forces, directional anion-π contacts, and shape-persistent tetrahedral geometry enables predictable self-assembly into discrete, hollow architectures capable of guest encapsulation. The synthon maps to primitives: electrostatic (iodonium-anion), anion-π (anion-electron-deficient arene), dispersion (aryl stacking), shape (tetrahedral), and valence (covalent I-C bonds).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_40
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) core, where three aryl substituents create a pyramidal, electron-deficient cavity. The cationic iodine center engages in strong anion binding (halogen bonding via σ-hole), while the surrounding electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) provide multiple anion-π interaction sites. The overall tetrahedral geometry and complementary electrostatic surfaces enable it to act as a 'capsule' synthon that can selectively encapsulate polyatomic anions (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or carboxylates) through a combination of halogen bonding and cooperative anion-π interactions. This system is chemically realistic, with known stable iodonium salts, and maps clearly to primitives: shape (tetrahedral), charge (cation/anion), polarity, H-bond-like (halogen bond), π-system (anion-π), and metal-free Lewis acid behavior.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_17
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron center chelated by two catecholate oxygen donors, forming a rigid, anionic, bowl-shaped complex with electron-rich aromatic surfaces. The catecholate ligands provide extended π-systems that can engage in anion-π interactions with cationic guests or complementary π-π stacking with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The overall tetrahedral geometry and anionic charge create a well-defined, three-dimensional binding pocket suitable for encapsulation of small cations or polar molecules. The boron-catecholate unit is chemically robust, synthetically accessible, and offers tunability through substitution on the catechol rings. Recognition elements include: (1) the anionic charge center (B-O⁻), (2) the concave π-surface of the catecholate aromatics, (3) potential CH-π interactions from ligand substituents, and (4) the defined tetrahedral cavity shape. This system maps to primitives: AFFORDANCE (defined cavity), RECOGNITION (anion-π/π-π), CONSTITUTION (tetrahedral B center), CONFIGURATION (rigid chelate), CONFORMATION (bowl shape), COMPOSITION (B, O, C, H), and BEHAVIOR (host-guest binding).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_41
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (R3I+) where three aromatic arms with electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) are arranged around a central iodine(I) atom. The cationic iodine center acts as a strong halogen bond donor, while the electron-deficient aromatic arms provide complementary anion-π and cation-π interaction surfaces. This creates a 3D recognition pocket capable of encapsulating anions (Cl-, Br-, BF4-) through a combination of: (1) strong halogen bonding from I+ to the anion, (2) anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient arenes, and (3) potential cation-π stabilization from counter-cations. The tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the system for capsule-like assembly with complementary anionic guests, making it a building block for supramolecular cages or frameworks. Mappable to primitives: contact (halogen bond, anion-π), polarity (charged I+, polarized arenes), valency (tetrahedral coordination), topology (3D capsule), dynamics (guest exchange), energy (strong halogen bond ~20-40 kJ/mol), and information (shape-selective anion recognition).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boroxine_anion_π_crown_ether_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boroxine anion [B₃O₃]³⁻ core stabilized by three aromatic substituents (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups). The planar, electron-rich boroxine ring acts as a potent anion-π donor, while the oxygen atoms of the boroxine ring can engage in cooperative interactions with crown ether hosts (e.g., 18-crown-6) via dipole-dipole and weak B-O···H-C hydrogen bonding. The three aromatic wings provide additional π-π stacking surfaces and cation-π sites for alkali metals (e.g., K⁺) coordinated by the crown ether, creating a three-level recognition system: (1) anion-π between boroxine and electron-deficient arenes, (2) crown ether–cation coordination, and (3) cation-π between the metal and boroxine's aromatic substituents. This system enables programmable assembly of 2D sheets or capsules via orthogonal interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_zinc_porphyrin_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral zinc(II) porphyrin complex where the zinc center coordinates to a pyridine-functionalized anion (e.g., pyridine-4-carboxylate). The cationic zinc porphyrin core engages in anion-π interactions with the carboxylate group of the anion, while the porphyrin's extended π-system provides a curved, bowl-shaped cavity suitable for capsule formation through complementary π-stacking with another identical unit. The tetrahedral geometry arises from the zinc coordination sphere (porphyrin N4 plane + axial pyridine ligand), creating a directional building block for self-assembled capsules. Recognition elements include: (1) metal-ligand coordination (Zn-Npyridine), (2) anion-π interaction between porphyrin π-system and carboxylate, (3) π-π stacking between porphyrin macrocycles, and (4) shape complementarity of curved surfaces. This system maps to primitives: contact (coordination bond), enclosure (capsule formation), orientation (tetrahedral geometry), and can exhibit temporal behavior through ligand exchange dynamics.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenium_selenoxide_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arrangement of four selenium-containing aromatic units where each selenium atom is oxidized to selenoxide (Se=O). The selenoxide groups serve dual functions: (1) their polarized Se=O bonds create σ-holes on selenium atoms for chalcogen bonding interactions with anions, and (2) the electron-deficient selenium centers enhance the π-acidity of the adjacent aromatic rings for anion-π interactions. The four units assemble via Se···O chalcogen bonds between selenoxide groups, forming a tetrahedral capsule with convergent anion-binding pockets. This system combines chalcogen bonding (Se···anion), anion-π interactions (aromatic ring···anion), and dipole-dipole interactions (Se=O···Se=O) to create a selective anion receptor. The selenium oxidation state can be reversibly modulated (Se(II)/Se(IV)), introducing redox-responsive temporal control over capsule formation and anion binding affinity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenazole_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arrangement of four selenazole units connected through selenium-nitrogen coordination bonds, forming a cationic capsule with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. Each selenazole unit contains a cationic selenium center (Se⁺) with σ-hole regions for anion binding, while the extended π-conjugated system creates electron-deficient surfaces for anion-π interactions. The tetrahedral architecture creates an enclosed cavity suitable for anion encapsulation through synergistic Se···anion σ-hole interactions and anion-π contacts with the electron-poor selenazole rings. This system combines pnictogen bonding (from selenium) with anion-π interactions in a three-dimensional capsule framework, offering orthogonal recognition elements for anion binding and potential applications in anion sensing and transport.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenium_selenoxide_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenium(IV) center bearing three aromatic arms and one selenoxide oxygen. The system features: (1) a central selenium atom with tetrahedral geometry, (2) three electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., perfluorinated phenyl or naphthalene) extending from the selenium to create an anion-binding π-cavity, (3) a selenoxide group (Se=O) that provides a strong dipole and hydrogen-bond acceptor site, and (4) charge-assisted anion-π interactions between electron-deficient aromatic surfaces and an encapsulated anion (e.g., chloride, nitrate). The selenoxide oxygen can further engage in hydrogen bonding or dipole-dipole interactions with complementary partners, while the tetrahedral arrangement pre-organizes the aromatic panels into a convergent capsule-like geometry. This synthon combines pnictogen/chalcogen bonding (from Se), anion-π interactions, and dipole interactions in a single, pre-organized supramolecular building block.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenium_selenoxide_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral selenium(IV) centers bearing selenoxide groups (R-Se(=O)-R') that function as anion-π acceptors. Each selenium atom adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with two organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups), one oxygen atom from the selenoxide, and a lone pair. The electron-deficient π-surfaces of aromatic substituents (e.g., perfluorinated phenyl or electron-poor heterocycles) create anion-binding pockets via anion-π interactions. Four such units can self-assemble through Se=O···Se=O dipole-dipole interactions and/or Se···O chalcogen bonding into a tetrahedral capsule that encapsulates an anionic guest (e.g., chloride, nitrate) via cooperative anion-π interactions. The system combines chalcogen bonding (Se···O), dipole-dipole interactions, and anion-π interactions in a single, redox-active scaffold where the selenium oxidation state (IV) is stable yet tunable.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_halogen_bond_donor_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on antimony(V) as a strong halogen bond donor, featuring four identical organic arms terminating in electron-deficient aromatic rings. Each arm contains a para-substituted pyridine-N-oxide moiety with adjacent halogen atoms (iodine or bromine) positioned to act as halogen bond donors. The central antimony atom provides tetrahedral geometry, while the electron-deficient aromatic systems create anion-π interaction sites. The combination of directional halogen bonding (Sb-X···anion) and anion-π interactions from the electron-deficient rings enables encapsulation of anions within a tetrahedral cage structure. This synthon is particularly effective for binding oxyanions (sulfate, phosphate) and halides through multivalent interactions, with potential applications in anion sensing and separation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gold_phosphine_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular tetrahedral capsule synthon based on a gold(I) phosphine cationic complex that engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral Au(I) center coordinated by three monodentate phosphine ligands and one labile solvent molecule, creating a cationic [Au(PR₃)₃]⁺ core; (2) three electron-deficient hexafluorobenzene or s-tetrazine aromatic panels attached via flexible linkers to the phosphine ligands, positioned to form the faces of a tetrahedron; (3) anion binding through cooperative anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient aromatic panels and an encapsulated anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻); (4) weak autophilic Au···Au interactions that can stabilize capsule dimerization; (5) labile coordination at the fourth site allowing for dynamic guest exchange; (6) tunable cavity size via phosphine substituents and linker length; (7) potential for redox-switching via Au(I)/Au(III) chemistry. This system combines metal coordination, electrostatic, anion-π, and weak autophilic interactions to create a reversible, stimuli-responsive supramolecular capsule for anion recognition and encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_oxide_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arrangement of four phosphine oxide groups (R₃P=O) positioned at the vertices of a tetrahedron, with their oxygen atoms oriented inward to create an electron-rich cavity capable of anion binding through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The phosphine oxide groups serve as both structural elements and hydrogen bond acceptors, while the electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives) positioned between the vertices provide complementary anion-π recognition sites. This creates a neutral, tetrahedral capsule-like scaffold that can encapsulate anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through a combination of anion-π interactions and dipole-anion electrostatic stabilization from the P=O groups. The system is chemically realistic, synthetically accessible via Sonogashira or Suzuki coupling to connect phosphine oxide vertices with π-acidic aromatic spacers, and represents a novel entry in supramolecular anion recognition chemistry distinct from metal-based or charged capsule systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_halogen_bond_donor_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(V) centers with halogen bond donor capabilities, designed to form anion-π capsules. The system features antimony atoms coordinated to three aromatic electron-deficient pyrazine rings (providing anion-π interaction surfaces) and one halogen bond donor group (iodine or bromine substituent). The tetrahedral geometry directs three π-deficient faces and one halogen bond donor toward a common point, enabling encapsulation of anions through simultaneous anion-π interactions with the three electron-poor aromatic systems and halogen bonding with the fourth arm. This creates a 3D recognition pocket for anions like tetrafluoroborate or hexafluorophosphate. The antimony center's +V oxidation state and electron-withdrawing substituents enhance both the π-acidity of the aromatic rings and the σ-hole on the halogen bond donor. This represents a novel combination of pnictogen (antimony) coordination geometry, halogen bonding, and anion-π interactions in a supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_argentophilic_cage_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular tetrahedral cage formed through argentophilic interactions (d¹⁰-d¹⁰ Ag···Ag contacts) between four silver(I) centers coordinated to N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligands with appended pyrene or perylene panels. The cage creates a hydrophobic cavity with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces that engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with polyatomic anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, ClO₄⁻). The tetrahedral geometry arises from the linear coordination of each silver(I) ion to two NHC donors and the directional argentophilic interactions (≈3.0–3.5 Å) between adjacent metal centers. The system combines metal-metal bonding, coordination chemistry, and supramolecular anion recognition in a single, structurally well-defined synthon.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_halogen_bond_donor_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on antimony(V) as a strong halogen bond donor, featuring four identical arms each terminating in an iodotriazole halogen bond donor group. The central antimony atom provides tetrahedral geometry, while each arm contains an electron-deficient aromatic system (trifluoromethyl-substituted pyridine) positioned to engage in anion-π interactions with encapsulated anions. The iodotriazole groups act as strong halogen bond donors (σ-hole on iodine) to coordinate anions, while the electron-deficient π-systems provide additional stabilization through anion-π interactions. This creates a tetrahedral capsule-like environment suitable for anion recognition and encapsulation, with potential applications in anion transport and sensing. The system combines halogen bonding (I···anion), anion-π interactions (electron-deficient arene···anion), and tetrahedral preorganization—all mapped to the seven primitives through directional interactions, geometric constraints, and complementary electronic properties.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stiborane_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(V) stiborane anions (R₄Sb⁻) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating capsule-like assemblies. The synthon features: (1) tetrahedral antimony centers with four organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, pentafluorophenyl, or alkyl groups) and a formal negative charge, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or tetrafluoropyridine derivatives) that serve as π-acidic surfaces, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the Sb⁻ center and the arene π-system, (4) complementary van der Waals and dispersion forces between organic substituents, and (5) geometric preorganization for capsule formation through multiple convergent anion-π contacts. This system explores underexplored pnictogen-based anions in supramolecular chemistry and leverages the relatively large, polarizable antimony center for strong noncovalent interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stiborane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(V) stiborane anions [SbR4]⁻ (where R = aryl or perfluorinated aryl groups) that function as anion-π acceptors within a capsule framework. The electron-deficient antimony center, enhanced by electron-withdrawing substituents on the aryl rings, creates a region of positive electrostatic potential suitable for anion binding. The tetrahedral geometry directs four π-acidic aromatic faces outward, enabling them to interact with cationic or electron-rich guests through anion-π interactions. The synthon can be incorporated into larger frameworks via coordination of the antimony to Lewis basic sites or through the organic substituents, creating a well-defined cavity. Recognition elements include the σ-hole on antimony (for pnictogen bonding), the electron-deficient π-systems of the aryl rings, and the overall tetrahedral symmetry that predisposes capsule formation. This represents an underexplored combination of pnictogen chemistry (antimony) with anion-π interactions in a supramolecular assembly context.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stiborane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(V) stiborane complexes (R₃SbX₂) that form anion-binding capsules through synergistic anion-π and halogen bonding interactions. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral Sb(V) center with two labile halogen ligands (X = Cl, Br) that serve as halogen bond donors, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or triazine rings) attached to the organic substituents (R) to provide anion-π recognition surfaces, and (3) a preorganized geometry where four such units self-assemble into a capsule through complementary interactions. The labile halogens on Sb coordinate to anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) via halogen bonding, while the electron-deficient π-systems provide additional stabilization through anion-π interactions. This creates a tetrahedral capsule capable of encapsulating anions with size selectivity. The system maps to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), antimony center (element), halogen bonds and anion-π interactions (noncovalent forces), labile ligands (exchange), electron-deficient aromatics (redox/electronic), and self-assembly into a capsule (higher-order structure).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stiborane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on antimony(V) stiborane complexes (R₃SbX₂) that form anion-binding capsules through synergistic anion-π interactions and electrostatic complementarity. The system features: 1) A central tetrahedral antimony(V) atom with three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, pentafluorophenyl) and two halide ligands (Cl⁻, Br⁻) that can be displaced by anions, 2) Electron-deficient aromatic faces on the substituents (particularly pentafluorophenyl groups) providing multiple anion-π recognition sites, 3) Preorganized tetrahedral geometry directing four such units to assemble into a capsule through complementary electrostatic interactions between the partially positive antimony centers and encapsulated anions, 4) Tunable cavity size via substituent bulk, and 5) Reversible anion binding with potential for temporal control via redox switching between Sb(V) and Sb(III) oxidation states. This combines pnictogen bonding (Sb···anion), anion-π interactions, and electrostatic complementarity in a structurally defined supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stiborane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(V) stiborane complexes (R₃SbX₂) that form anion-binding capsules through synergistic anion-π and halogen bonding interactions. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral Sb(V) center with two axial halogens (Cl, Br) that act as halogen bond donors, (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, s-triazine) attached to the Sb center that provide anion-π binding surfaces, and (3) a preorganized geometry where three such units self-assemble into a trigonal capsule that encapsulates spherical anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻) through convergent interactions. The recognition elements include: σ-hole interactions from the Sb-bound halogens (halogen bonding), electrostatic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes, and geometric complementarity from the tetrahedral coordination. This represents an underexplored combination of pnictogen (Sb) and halogen bonding with anion-π interactions in a supramolecular capsule architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stiborane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral antimony(V) stiborane compounds (R₃SbX₂ type) that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. The synthon features: (1) A central antimony(V) atom with tetrahedral geometry, (2) Three aromatic substituents (e.g., phenyl, naphthyl, or pyridyl groups) providing electron-deficient π-surfaces, (3) Two anionic ligands (typically halides, carboxylates, or sulfonates) that can be displaced or participate in anion binding, (4) The electron-deficient aromatic rings create strong anion-π interaction sites, while the tetrahedral geometry directs four such faces toward a common cavity, (5) The Lewis acidic antimony center can further coordinate anions or polarize nearby π-systems, enhancing binding, (6) This creates a pre-organized capsule-like structure capable of encapsulating anions through multipoint anion-π interactions, (7) The system exhibits temporal behavior through reversible anion exchange at the antimony center and modulation of π-acidity via redox changes at antimony. Recognition elements include: σ-hole interactions from antimony, anion-π interactions from electron-deficient aromatics, and potential halogen/chalcogen bonds from substituents. This represents an underexplored pnictogen-based supramolecular architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_halogen_bond_donor_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on antimony(V) centers with halogen bond donor capabilities and anion-π interactions. The system features four antimony atoms at the vertices of a tetrahedron, each coordinated to three organic ligands containing electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or tetracyanobenzene groups) that create anion-binding π-surfaces. Each antimony center bears a σ-hole positive region on its axial halogen substituent (Cl, Br, or I) oriented inward toward the tetrahedron's center, enabling strong halogen bonding interactions with encapsulated anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻, BF₄⁻, etc.). The combination of directional halogen bonds from the four antimony vertices and multiple anion-π interactions from the electron-deficient aromatic panels creates a well-defined tetrahedral capsule capable of selectively binding anions through complementary electrostatic and orbital interactions. This represents a novel integration of pnictogen-based halogen bonding with anion-π recognition in a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_calixarene_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on gallium(III)-calix[4]arene complexes that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. Each vertex consists of a gallium(III) center coordinated to a calix[4]arene lower rim through two phenoxide oxygens, with the remaining coordination sites occupied by labile ligands (e.g., water or acetonitrile). The calixarene's electron-deficient aromatic cavity (often fluorinated or nitrated at upper rim) provides strong anion-π recognition sites. When four such units converge tetrahedrally via appropriate bridging ligands or through self-assembly with complementary anions, they form a capsule capable of encapsulating anions via synergistic anion-π interactions from all four inwardly-directed calixarene cavities. The gallium(III) centers provide structural rigidity and potential for further coordination expansion, while the calixarene scaffolds offer tunable π-acidity and preorganized geometry. This system combines metal coordination, anion-π interactions, and supramolecular self-assembly into a novel tetrahedral capsule former.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_halogen_bond_acceptor_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A tetrahedral arsenic(V) center functionalized with three halogen-bond accepting groups (iodo- or bromo-substituted aromatic rings) and one electron-deficient π-system (e.g., tetrafluoropyridinium or cyanophenyl). The arsenic center adopts a +V oxidation state with four substituents arranged tetrahedrally. The halogen-bond accepting groups (C–I···X⁻ or C–Br···X⁻) provide directional recognition sites for anions, while the electron-deficient π-face engages in complementary anion–π interactions with the same anion, creating a convergent binding pocket. This dual interaction mode (halogen bonding + anion–π) stabilizes anion encapsulation within a supramolecular capsule formed by multiple such synthons. The system is chemically realistic using known arsenic(V) aryl compounds and can be mapped to primitives: (1) tetrahedral node, (2) halogen-bond acceptor, (3) anion–π acceptor, (4) convergent binding site, (5) supramolecular capsule geometry, (6) anion recognition, (7) modular substitution for tuning affinity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organometallic_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on mercury(II) organometallic complexes that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. The system features a central mercury(II) atom coordinated to four aromatic ligands containing electron-deficient π-systems (such as perfluorinated phenyl or naphthalene groups). The tetrahedral geometry creates a convergent arrangement of four electron-deficient aromatic faces that can cooperatively bind anions through anion-π interactions. The mercury center provides structural rigidity through strong covalent Hg-C bonds while allowing for electronic tuning of the π-acidity through substituent effects. The system can encapsulate spherical anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻) or oxoanions within the tetrahedral cavity formed by the four aromatic panels. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral mercury(II) coordination geometry, (2) electron-deficient aromatic surfaces for anion-π interactions, (3) potential for secondary Hg···anion interactions, and (4) peripheral functionalization for hierarchical assembly. This represents a novel combination of organometallic chemistry with supramolecular anion recognition in a tetrahedral capsule architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_arene_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on mercury(II) centers coordinated to electron-deficient arenes, creating a cationic capsule framework with strong anion-π interactions. Each mercury center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with two coordination sites occupied by nitrogen donors from pyridine ligands and two sites occupied by σ-bonded aryl groups containing electron-deficient trifluoromethyl substituents. The electron-deficient arene faces project inward, forming a tetrahedral cavity with four convergent anion-π recognition sites. This creates a selective capsule for polyatomic anions (ClO₄⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) through cooperative anion-π interactions. The system exhibits reversible anion binding with tunable affinity via arene substitution, and the tetrahedral symmetry enables self-assembly into larger supramolecular architectures. Recognition elements include: Hg-N coordination bonds, Hg-C σ-bonds, electron-deficient arene π-systems, and convergent electrostatic fields for anion capture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on a gallium(III) complex with a salen-type Schiff base ligand (N,N'-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine). The gallium center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with one labile coordination site occupied by a weakly-bound anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻). The synthon features two distinct recognition elements: (1) strong directional anion binding to the Lewis acidic Ga(III) center, and (2) extended aromatic surfaces from the salen phenyl rings that participate in cooperative anion-π interactions with the bound anion. The tetrahedral arrangement positions four aromatic panels (two from each salen ligand in a dinuclear or extended assembly) to form the walls of a potential capsule or cage when combined with complementary units. The labile anion can be exchanged, making this a temporal synthon with dynamic character. Recognition primitives include: metal coordination (Ga-anion), anion-π (aromatic ring-anion), π-π stacking (between aromatic panels of adjacent units), and hydrogen bonding (from residual phenolic OH or imine CH groups).

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_spiropyran_merocyanine_zwitterion_synthon
synthons.description: A temporally-controlled molecular synthon based on the reversible photoisomerization of spiropyran to merocyanine. The neutral, closed spiropyran form (spiro C-O bond intact) undergoes UV-induced cleavage to form the open merocyanine zwitterion, which features a phenolate anion and an indolinium cation within the same conjugated π-system. This transformation creates a transient zwitterionic recognition element capable of both anion-π interactions (via the electron-deficient indolinium moiety) and cation-π interactions (via the electron-rich phenolate), alongside hydrogen bonding from the indolinium N-H. The system reverts thermally or with visible light to the closed form, erasing the recognition sites. This provides a time- and light-gated molecular synthon where recognition (supramolecular assembly) is activated only during the merocyanine lifetime, enabling dynamic, temporally-programmed binding events for substrates like carboxylates (via indolinium) or metal cations (via phenolate).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand (salophen-type N₂O₂ donor set) that functions as a supramolecular synthon through two complementary interactions: (1) the Lewis acidic gallium center coordinates anionic guests (halides, carboxylates, or sulfonates) via strong electrostatic and dative bonds, and (2) the extended planar aromatic wings of the Schiff base ligand provide concave π-surfaces for anion-π interactions with the bound anion, as well as additional π-π stacking surfaces for capsule assembly with complementary aromatic units. The rigid tetrahedral geometry directs the formation of well-defined cavities when combined with appropriate linker units, creating a versatile building block for anion-responsive supramolecular capsules. This system combines metal-ligand coordination (primitive: bond), electrostatic attraction (primitive: coulomb), anion-π interactions (primitive: dispersion/polarization), and directional aromatic stacking (primitive: shape) to achieve programmable self-assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand (salicylaldimine type) that creates a cationic metal center with Lewis acidic character. The complex features four aromatic walls arranged in a tetrahedral geometry, creating a cavity with electron-deficient π-surfaces suitable for anion-π interactions. The gallium center's positive charge enhances the electron deficiency of the aromatic rings, while the Schiff base nitrogen donors provide additional hydrogen bond acceptor sites. This synthon can form supramolecular capsules through complementary anion-π interactions with tetrahedral anions (e.g., perchlorate, tetrafluoroborate) or through combination with π-rich aromatic systems. The system exhibits temporal control through pH-dependent Schiff base formation/reversibility and potential redox activity at the gallium center (GaIII/GaI). Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral cationic metal center, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels, (3) imine hydrogen bond acceptors, (4) phenolic oxygen donors, and (5) coordinatively unsaturated sites for additional ligand exchange.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_calixarene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular tetrahedral capsule formed by four gallium(III)-calix[4]arene units arranged at the vertices of a tetrahedron. Each gallium center coordinates to the phenolic oxygens of the calixarene and bears a labile axial ligand (e.g., triflate) that can be displaced. The assembly creates a convergent, electron-deficient cavity lined with the π-surfaces of the calixarene aromatic rings, enabling strong cooperative anion-π interactions with encapsulated anions (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻). The tetrahedral geometry is enforced by bridging ditopic linkers (e.g., bipyridine or carboxylate spacers) connecting the gallium centers. Recognition elements include: (1) Lewis acidic gallium(III) centers for anion coordination, (2) electron-deficient calixarene cavities for anion-π binding, (3) bridging ligands for structural integrity, and (4) labile sites for guest exchange. This system maps to the seven primitives via: vertices (Ga centers), edges (bridging linkers), faces (calixarene panels), container (tetrahedral capsule), recognition (anion-π + coordination), transformation (anion exchange), and temporal control (guest release triggered by competitive ligands or pH changes).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organometallic_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on mercury(II) organometallic complexes with electron-deficient aromatic panels that form anion-π interactions. The system features Hg(II) centers coordinated to four pyridyl or carbene ligands arranged tetrahedrally, with each face of the tetrahedron capped by a perfluorinated aromatic panel (e.g., hexafluorobenzene or decafluorobiphenyl). These electron-deficient panels create strong anion-binding pockets through anion-π interactions, while the tetrahedral geometry directs the assembly of capsule-like structures. The mercury centers provide additional Lewis acidic character and potential for secondary coordination with anions. This synthon combines metal coordination (Hg-N or Hg-C bonds), anion-π interactions, and tetrahedral symmetry to create a directional, three-dimensional recognition motif for anions, suitable for constructing supramolecular capsules or cages with anion-templated assembly.

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_spiropyran_merocyanine_zwitterion_synthon_1
synthons.description: A light-responsive molecular synthon based on spiropyran-merocyanine interconversion that creates temporally controlled zwitterionic recognition sites. The closed spiropyran form is neutral and lipophilic, while UV irradiation (365 nm) opens the C-O bond to form the planar merocyanine zwitterion with a phenolate anion and indolinium cation. This creates multiple simultaneous interaction sites: (1) phenolate anion acts as hydrogen bond acceptor and anion-π donor, (2) indolinium cation serves as hydrogen bond donor and cation-π acceptor, (3) planar conjugated π-system enables π-π stacking, and (4) the zwitterion can undergo reversible metal coordination at the phenolate oxygen. Visible light (>550 nm) or thermal relaxation returns the system to the closed form, erasing recognition sites. This temporal control allows sequential binding of different partners: the merocyanine form can recognize carboxylic acids via dual hydrogen bonding (phenolate∙∙∙H-O and N⁺-H∙∙∙O=C) and aromatic compounds via π-stacking, while the spiropyran form recognizes only lipophilic guests. The system maps to all seven primitives: atoms (O, N), bonds (C-O, C=C), angles (planar vs. tetrahedral), torsion (ring-opening rotation), non-covalent interactions (H-bonds, π-effects), charges (zwitterionic), and dynamics (photoisomerization kinetics).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_calixarene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated to four pyridyl-functionalized calix[4]arene ligands, creating a cationic metal-organic capsule. The system features: (1) strong directional Ga(III)-N coordination bonds as the primary structural element; (2) four pre-organized, electron-deficient calixarene cavities that serve as potent anion-π recognition sites; (3) the tetrahedral geometry directing the calixarenes outward to form a three-dimensional capsule capable of encapsulating tetrahedral anions (e.g., ClO₄⁻, BF₄⁻) or spherical halides via cooperative anion-π interactions; (4) additional secondary interactions including C-H···anion hydrogen bonds from the calixarene methylene bridges and potential π-π stacking between adjacent aromatic rings of neighboring capsules. This synthon combines hard acid (Ga³⁺) coordination chemistry with soft supramolecular anion-π recognition, creating a unique hierarchical assembly motif for anion encapsulation and transport.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_calixarene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on gallium(III) ions coordinated to calix[4]arene derivatives, forming a cationic metal-organic capsule that selectively encapsulates anions via synergistic anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic walls of the calixarene. Each gallium center adopts a tetrahedral geometry through coordination to two phenolic oxygens from the calixarene and two ancillary ligands (e.g., β-diketonates or halides). The four calixarene units are arranged at the vertices of a tetrahedron, creating a cavity lined with π-deficient arenes that engage in multiple directional anion-π contacts with encapsulated anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻, NO₃⁻). The system exhibits reversible anion binding with allosteric regulation through metal coordination dynamics, enabling temporal control over anion encapsulation and release via redox or pH stimuli.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand (salophen-type N₂O₂ donor set) that functions as a supramolecular synthon through two complementary interactions: (1) the Lewis acidic gallium center acts as an anion binding site via coordinative interaction with anionic guests (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻), and (2) the extended aromatic surfaces of the Schiff base ligand provide curved π-surfaces for anion-π interactions with the bound anion. The tetrahedral geometry creates a directional, three-dimensional binding pocket where the anion sits at the intersection of electrostatic coordination to the metal and parallel-displaced π-stacking with the electron-deficient aromatic rings. This system combines metal-ligand coordination (primitive: metal coordination) with anion-π interactions (primitive: anion-π) and directional geometric constraints (primitive: tetrahedral geometry) to create a self-assembling capsule when combined with complementary π-donor or cation-containing partners.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_calixarene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on gallium(III) ions coordinated to calix[4]arene derivatives, forming a cationic tetrahedral core that engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. Each gallium center is chelated by a lower-rim functionalized calix[4]arene bearing two phenolate donors, creating a +1 charge per vertex. The four calixarenes are oriented such that their electron-poor upper-rim tetrafluorophenyl groups point inward, creating a convergent anion-binding pocket through cooperative anion-π interactions. The system self-assembles into a tetrahedral capsule capable of encapsulating a spherical anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻) or an anionic guest. Recognition elements include: (1) metal-ligand coordination (Ga–O bonds), (2) anion-π interactions between the encapsulated anion and fluorinated arenes, (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from methylene bridges, and (4) π-stacking between adjacent calixarene aromatic rings. This synthon maps to primitives: vertices (Ga centers), edges (calixarene linkers), faces (triangular panels of fluorinated aromatics), containers (tetrahedral capsule), gates (anion ingress/egress), clocks (kinetic stability of Ga–O bonds), and roles (anion receptor).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand (salicylaldimine type) that creates a cationic metal center with accessible coordination sites. The complex features: (1) a positively charged Ga(III) center that can engage in anion binding through electrostatic and coordinative interactions, (2) aromatic panels from the Schiff base ligand that provide extensive π-surfaces for anion-π interactions with electron-deficient anions (NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻), (3) preorganized tetrahedral geometry that enables self-assembly into dimeric capsule structures via complementary π-π stacking of the aromatic panels, and (4) tunable electronic properties through substituents on the aromatic rings to modulate anion binding affinity. This system combines metal coordination, anion-π interactions, and π-π stacking to create a hierarchical supramolecular assembly capable of selective anion encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silver_pyrazolate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on silver(I)-pyrazolate coordination cages that function as anion-π receptors. The system consists of four silver(I) centers coordinated by three bridging pyrazolate ligands each, forming a tetrahedral [Ag₄(L)₆]⁴⁺ cage where L is a pyrazolate derivative with electron-deficient aromatic extensions (e.g., tetrafluorophenyl or trifluoromethylphenyl substituents). The tetrahedral cationic cage creates four electron-deficient π-surfaces at its faces that can simultaneously engage anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.) through cooperative anion-π interactions. The recognition elements include: (1) Ag-N coordination bonds (primitive: bond), (2) tetrahedral geometry (primitive: shape), (3) electron-deficient π-systems (primitive: charge/polarization), (4) anion-π interactions (primitive: non-covalent interaction), (5) cationic charge (primitive: charge), (6) preorganized cavity (primitive: shape/space), and (7) dynamic ligand exchange at silver centers (primitive: transformation). This represents a novel metallosupramolecular approach to anion encapsulation combining coordination chemistry with anion-π interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_calixarene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on gallium(III) centers coordinated to calix[4]arene scaffolds, forming an anion-binding capsule through synergistic anion-π and coordination interactions. Each gallium center is bound to the lower rim phenolic oxygens of a calix[4]arene, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped electron-deficient cavity with a partial positive charge. Four such units assemble via metal-ligand coordination to bridging pyridine-dicarboxylate linkers at the gallium axial sites, forming a tetrahedral cage. The electron-deficient, cation-decorated (Ga³⁺) aromatic surfaces of the calixarenes create strong anion-π recognition sites, while the tetrahedral architecture encapsulates an anionic guest (e.g., Cl⁻, NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻) at the cage center through multipoint interactions. This system combines metal coordination (primitive: bond), directional anion-π interactions (primitive: attraction), shape-defined cavity (primitive: container), tetrahedral symmetry (primitive: pattern), reversible assembly (primitive: transformation), charge complementarity (primitive: property), and guest encapsulation dynamics (primitive: change over time).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand (salophen-type N₂O₂ donor set) that functions as a supramolecular synthon. The electron-deficient gallium center creates a Lewis acidic cavity that can bind anions through coordination, while the planar aromatic wings of the Schiff base ligand provide extended π-deficient surfaces for anion-π interactions with electron-rich anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻). The tetrahedral geometry allows for directional assembly into capsule-like structures when combined with complementary π-donor components. The system exhibits dual recognition: (1) metal-anion coordination bond (Ga←X⁻), and (2) anion-π interactions between the electron-poor aromatic rings and anions. This synthon can be mapped to the seven primitives through its geometric constraints (tetrahedral node), directional interactions (coordination and π-stacking), and dynamic exchange (labile Ga-anion bonds enabling temporal control).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_organotin_halide_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A tetrahedral organotin(IV) halide complex (R₃SnX, where R = aromatic group like phenyl or naphthyl, X = Cl, Br, I) that functions as a supramolecular synthon through dual interaction modes: (1) the tin center acts as a Lewis acidic halogen bond acceptor via the σ-hole on the halide ligand (Sn–X⋯anion interaction), and (2) the aromatic R groups provide electron-deficient π-surfaces for anion–π interactions. This creates a convergent, tetrahedrally-oriented recognition motif capable of encapsulating anions within a π-rich cavity. The system exhibits temporal control through reversible Sn–X bond formation/cleavage under redox or photochemical stimuli, enabling dynamic capsule assembly/disassembly. Recognition elements include the polarized Sn–X bond (σ-hole), electron-deficient arenes, and the tetrahedral geometry directing multiple interactions toward a central binding site.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on a gallium(III) salen complex that functions as an anion-π capsule building block. The system features a square-planar salen ligand (N,N'-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine) coordinated to Ga(III) with an axial site occupied by a labile ligand (chloride or triflate). The electron-deficient aromatic rings of the salen ligand create π-acidic surfaces for anion binding, while the tetrahedral geometry of the Ga center (with one labile site) enables directional assembly into capsule structures through anion-π interactions with tetrahedral anions like [BF4]⁻ or [ClO4]⁻. The metal center provides additional Lewis acidity for anion coordination, creating a synergistic anion-binding pocket. Recognition elements include: (1) π-acidic aromatic surfaces (anion-π), (2) Lewis acidic Ga(III) center, (3) directional tetrahedral geometry, and (4) labile coordination site for exchange. This synthon maps to primitives through its tetrahedral symmetry (shape), electron-deficient π-systems (polarization), directional anion binding (recognition), and dynamic ligand exchange at the metal center (lability).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A tetrahedral supramolecular synthon based on gallium(III) salen complexes that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. The system features: (1) a Ga(III) center in a distorted tetrahedral geometry coordinated by a tetradentate salen ligand (N₂O₂ donor set), (2) a labile axial site occupied by a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) that can be exchanged, (3) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) incorporated into the salen ligand framework, creating convergent anion-π binding pockets, and (4) peripheral functionalization (alkyl chains, hydrogen bond donors/acceptors) to control self-assembly into dimeric capsules. The recognition elements include: metal-anion coordination (Ga···anion electrostatic interaction), anion-π interactions between the encapsulated anion and electron-deficient arenes, and secondary interactions (C–H···anion, π-π stacking between panels of adjacent complexes). This synthon maps to the seven primitives through: (1) Ga as a tetrahedral node, (2) salen as a rigid connector, (3) anion as a guest/template, (4) electron-deficient arenes as interaction surfaces, (5) labile coordination for temporal control, (6) peripheral groups for solubility/assembly, and (7) overall capsule geometry for encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand (salicylaldimine type) that forms a cationic metal center with a vacant coordination site oriented toward the center of a supramolecular capsule. The complex features: (1) a Ga³⁺ center with strong Lewis acidity, (2) a rigid tetrahedral geometry enforced by the Schiff base ligand with phenyl substituents, (3) exposed π-surfaces on the ligand aromatic rings for capsule wall assembly via π-π stacking, and (4) a directional electrostatic potential suitable for anion-π interactions with encapsulated anions. The system combines metal coordination (primitive: bond), electrostatic complementarity (primitive: charge), directional π-stacking (primitive: surface), and geometric preorganization (primitive: shape) to create a supramolecular capsule that selectively binds anions like Cl⁻ or NO₃⁻ through synergistic anion-π and electrostatic interactions at the capsule interior.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand (salophen-type N₂O₂ donor set) that functions as a supramolecular synthon. The electron-deficient gallium center creates a Lewis acidic cavity with a partial positive charge, enabling anion binding through electrostatic and coordinative interactions. The planar aromatic wings of the Schiff base ligand provide extended π-deficient surfaces for complementary anion-π interactions with oxoanions (e.g., nitrate, sulfate) or halides. The tetrahedral geometry directs four convergent recognition elements (two from metal Lewis acidity, two from aromatic faces) toward a central binding pocket, enabling encapsulation of anionic guests. This synthon can self-assemble into larger capsules through π-π stacking of aromatic panels and/or metal-anion coordination bridges, creating hierarchical supramolecular architectures with temporal control possible through pH-modulated Schiff base formation/dissociation or redox-active metal centers.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand (salicylaldimine type) that creates a cationic metal center with Lewis acidic character. The complex features four aromatic walls from the ligand's phenyl rings that form an electron-deficient cavity capable of anion-π interactions. The gallium center provides additional electrostatic attraction for anions, while the tetrahedral geometry creates a well-defined binding pocket. This synthon can self-assemble into capsule-like structures through complementary anion-π interactions between electron-deficient aromatic surfaces and halide or oxoanions, with the gallium centers providing directional coordination preferences.
