synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) cages with tetrahedral silicon centers. The system features a rigid, cubic Si₈O₁₂ inorganic core functionalized with organic substituents containing electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl groups). The electron-deficient π-surfaces create multiple, geometrically precise anion-π recognition sites. The tetrahedral silicon vertices provide structural rigidity and directionality, while the siloxane (Si-O-Si) linkages offer polarizable oxygen atoms for additional electrostatic interactions. This synthon enables the programmable assembly of anion-binding capsules or extended frameworks through cooperative anion-π interactions and siloxane coordination, mapping to primitives of shape, charge, polarity, and spatial arrangement.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organometallic_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organomercury(II) complexes with electron-deficient aromatic caps that engage in simultaneous anion binding and anion-π interactions. The system features a mercury(II) center coordinated to three organic ligands (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and one anionic ligand (e.g., halide, carboxylate, or pseudohalide), creating a tetrahedral geometry with a localized negative charge. This anionic complex is encapsulated within a π-acidic aromatic cavity formed by electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanobenzene, or nitroaromatic panels) arranged in a bowl-shaped or cage-like architecture. Recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions between the anion and the cavity walls, (2) anion-π interactions between the anionic ligand and electron-deficient π-systems, (3) potential C–Hg···π interactions with the aromatic panels, and (4) van der Waals complementarity. The synthon enables the design of self-assembled capsules, selective anion receptors, and stimuli-responsive supramolecular materials. It maps to the seven primitives through geometric constraints (tetrahedral metal center), electrostatic complementarity (anion within electron-deficient cavity), directional interactions, and dynamic exchange (labile Hg–anion bond).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_mercaptide_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral mercury(II) centers coordinated to thiolate (mercaptide) anions, forming an anionic metal-organic capsule stabilized by anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features Hg(II) in a tetrahedral geometry bound to four thiolate ligands from aromatic thiols (e.g., benzene-1,3,5-trithiol derivatives), creating a negatively charged cage. This anionic capsule engages in strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, cyanobenzene, or nitrobenzene units) on complementary synthons. The recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral Hg-S4 coordination centers, (2) anionic charge delocalized over the thiolate ligands, (3) π-acidic aromatic surfaces for anion-π binding, and (4) preorganized cavity for guest encapsulation. This represents a novel combination of heavy metal coordination chemistry, anionic supramolecular assemblies, and anion-π interactions—an underexplored area in supramolecular synthon design.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanediol_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) centers bearing two hydroxyl groups (silanediol motif) that can deprotonate to form silanolate anions. These anionic oxygen atoms engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or triazine rings) that form the walls of a self-assembled capsule. The tetrahedral geometry of silicon directs two silanolate arms inward for anion-π binding to the aromatic surfaces, while the other two substituents (typically inert alkyl or aryl groups) point outward, defining the capsule's exterior. This creates a reversible, charge-assisted recognition motif where the silanolate's negative charge enhances the anion-π interaction with the π-acidic cavity, enabling the assembly of well-defined supramolecular containers for small molecule encapsulation. The system is chemically realistic, with silanediols known for their hydrogen-bonding and anion-binding capabilities, and perfluorinated aromatics established as strong π-acceptors.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanolate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers bearing silanolate anions (R₃SiO⁻) that engage in dual interaction modes: (1) electrostatic anion-π interactions between the electron-rich silanolate oxygen and electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or cyanuric acid derivatives) forming the walls of a self-assembled capsule, and (2) directional Si-O⁻···H-N hydrogen bonds or Si-O⁻···M⁺ coordination (with alkali/alkaline earth metals) that reinforce capsule assembly. The tetrahedral geometry at silicon preorganizes three organic arms (aryl or alkyl) to create a concave, bowl-shaped environment that templates capsule formation. This system combines the stability of silicate-like anions with the programmability of supramolecular architectures, enabling encapsulation of small polar guests via synergistic anion-π and hydrogen-bonding interactions within the cavity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) complexed with anionic dipyrromethene (BODIPY-like) ligands, forming an electron-rich π-surface that engages in anion-π interactions with complementary cationic guests. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral boron center with three anionic nitrogen donors from dipyrromethene ligands and one labile site for dynamic exchange, (2) extended planar π-conjugated systems on each ligand creating a trigonal pyramidal electron-rich cavity, (3) peripheral fluorine substituents enabling additional halogen bonding interactions, (4) tunable electronic properties through substituent variation on the dipyrromethene core, (5) dynamic reversibility of boron-ligand coordination allowing temporal control, (6) complementary electrostatic interactions between the anionic boron complex and cationic guests (e.g., quaternary ammonium, phosphonium, or metallocenium species), and (7) potential for hierarchical assembly into larger capsules via π-stacking of the planar ligands. This system combines coordination chemistry, anion-π interactions, and dynamic covalent chemistry across molecular, supramolecular, and temporal domains.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silsesquioxane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon center in a silsesquioxane cage (RSiO₁.₅)₈ framework, where one silicon vertex is functionalized with an anionic group (e.g., -O⁻, -S⁻, or -N⁻-R). This anionic site is positioned at the apex of a cubic-like polyhedral cage. The electron-rich, polarizable siloxane (Si-O-Si) framework of the cage creates a concave, partially shielded pocket lined with oxygen atoms. This pocket can engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, trinitrobenzene) or cation-π interactions if the cage interior is modified with arene groups. The rigid silsesquioxane scaffold provides a pre-organized, three-dimensional recognition site, enabling the encapsulation of planar π-systems via a combination of electrostatic (anion-π), van der Waals, and dipole-induced dipole interactions. This system maps to the primitives as: (1) tetrahedral geometry at Si, (2) anionic charge center, (3) π-system as guest/partner, (4) capsule-like cavity from the cage, (5) directional non-covalent interactions, (6) pre-organization from the rigid scaffold, and (7) potential for dynamic guest exchange (temporal domain).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_oxide_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphorus(V) centers where phosphine oxide groups (R3P=O) serve as anion-binding sites through P=O→anion interactions, while aromatic extensions from the phosphorus substituents create curved π-surfaces that self-assemble into dimeric capsules. The system features: (1) tetrahedral phosphorus centers with three aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl, naphthyl, or pyridyl groups) and one P=O group pointing inward; (2) anion binding to the polarized P=O oxygen (σ-hole-like interaction); (3) curved π-surfaces from the aromatic arms that engage in complementary π-π stacking and edge-to-face interactions; (4) self-assembly into dimeric capsules that encapsulate anions via convergent P=O groups; (5) tunable cavity size via aromatic arm length and substitution; (6) potential for chiral capsules with asymmetric phosphorus centers; (7) mapping to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), P=O→anion (electrostatic), π-π stacking (dispersion), aromatic curvature (topology), capsule formation (assembly), anion encapsulation (recognition), and tunable binding (adaptability). This synthon combines pnictogen bonding (P=O as acceptor) with π-based assembly in the underexplored supramolecular domain.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organometallic_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organomercury(II) complexes with π-acidic cavity-forming ligands. The system features a mercury(II) center coordinated to three anionic ligands (e.g., thiolates or aryl anions) and one neutral pyridine-type donor, creating a tetrahedral geometry with a net negative charge. This anionic complex is encapsulated within a π-acidic aromatic cage (e.g., hexafluorobenzene-based cyclophane or perfluorinated arene macrocycle) via synergistic anion-π interactions between the anionic mercury complex and the electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The recognition elements include: (1) the tetrahedral shape of the mercury complex providing directional constraints, (2) the localized negative charge on mercury-ligand bonds, (3) the π-deficient cavity of the macrocycle, and (4) secondary C–H···F or C–H···π contacts. This represents a novel metallosupramolecular anion-π capsule system distinct from previously proposed pnictogen or chalcogen-based capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanolate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers with silanolate anions (R₃SiO⁻) that engage in dual interaction modes: (1) electrostatic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or cyanuric acid derivatives) forming the walls of a self-assembled capsule, and (2) coordinative Si–O⁻···M⁺ interactions with alkali metal cations (Na⁺, K⁺) that template capsule assembly. The silanolate anion provides a strong anionic recognition site, while the tetrahedral silicon geometry directs three organic arms (aryl or alkyl) to create a curved, bowl-shaped cavity suitable for encapsulation. This system combines anion-π, cation-dipole, and van der Waals interactions, mapping to primitives: anion (silanolate), π-system (electron-deficient arene), metal cation (template), tetrahedral geometry (silicon center), capsule (assembly), electrostatic (anion-π), and directional (Si–O⁻ coordination).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_borane_adduct_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphorus center in a phosphine-borane adduct (R3P→BH3) that acts as an anion-binding site through the electron-deficient boron atom, while the phosphine's aromatic substituents (e.g., phenyl, pyridyl) provide π-surfaces for complementary cation-π or anion-π interactions with counterions or additional guests. The tetrahedral geometry of the P→B bond creates a directional, Lewis acidic pocket for anions (F-, Cl-, CN-) via σ-hole interactions from boron, while the aryl groups can engage in parallel-displaced π-stacking or T-shaped interactions to form dimeric or capsule-like assemblies. This system combines pnictogen-bonding (from P) and boron-centered electrophilicity with aromatic recognition, enabling the formation of chiral capsules if asymmetric phosphines are used, and can be mapped to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (P center), anion binding (B site), π-system (aryl groups), directional interaction (P→B bond), complementarity (anion-π pairing), self-assembly (capsule formation), and potential temporal control via borane dissociation/reassociation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silsesquioxane_cage_anion_π_synthon_1_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) cages with tetrahedral silicon centers at the vertices. Each silicon atom bears one organic substituent (typically phenyl, vinyl, or other π-rich groups) and three oxygen bridges connecting to adjacent silicon atoms, forming a rigid cage structure (commonly T8, T10, or T12 architectures). The synthon exploits two complementary interactions: (1) anion-π interactions between electron-deficient regions of the cage's organic substituents and anionic guests (e.g., halides, carboxylates, or tetrafluoroborate), and (2) the well-defined, rigid tetrahedral geometry of silicon centers that preorganizes multiple π-systems into a convergent binding pocket. The oxygen bridges provide additional weak hydrogen bond acceptor sites. This system is chemically realistic, with POSS cages being commercially available and extensively studied in hybrid materials. It maps to primitives through: shape (tetrahedral vertices), electrostatics (anion-π), connectivity (Si-O-Si bridges), dynamics (rigid yet tunable via substituents), energy (moderate binding ~10-50 kJ/mol), information (geometric recognition of anions), and time (stable cage persists across synthetic steps).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphazenium cation [P(NR₂)₄]⁺ (where R = alkyl or aryl groups) that forms a capsule-like assembly through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels and electrostatic interactions with encapsulated anions. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral cationic core with four positively charged nitrogen atoms surrounding phosphorus, creating a strong electrostatic field; (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, trinitrobenzene derivatives) attached via the R groups that participate in anion-π interactions; (3) encapsulation of halide or oxoanions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.) within the cavity formed by the aromatic panels; (4) tunable cavity size via R-group modification; (5) directional N⁺...anion electrostatic interactions; (6) π-system geometry optimized for concave anion binding; and (7) potential for temporal control via pH- or redox-responsive R groups. This represents an underexplored combination of phosphazenium chemistry with supramolecular anion recognition motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers with positively charged silylium cations (R3Si+) that engage in dual interaction modes: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the cationic silicon center, and (2) parallel anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or triazine rings) arranged in a capsule-like geometry. The system features a rigid tetrahedral scaffold (such as tetraphenylsilane derivatives) where three arms bear electron-deficient π-systems and the fourth arm terminates in a silylium cation. This creates a convergent binding pocket that can encapsulate anions (Cl-, BF4-, PF6-) through cooperative cation-anion and anion-π interactions. The synthon demonstrates reversible anion binding with potential for temporal control via redox or photochemical modulation of the silylium stability or π-acidity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_borane_adduct_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphorus center in a phosphine-borane adduct (R3P→BH3) that functions as an anion-binding capsule through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral phosphorus atom with three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and a dative bond to BH3, creating a zwitterionic P⁺–B⁻ character; (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl) as π-acidic panels attached to the phosphine substituents; (3) a preorganized cavity formed by convergent arrangement of these aromatic panels that selectively binds anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) via cooperative anion-π interactions; (4) tunable cavity size and electronics via substituent modification on both phosphorus and aromatic rings; (5) potential for temporal control through reversible dissociation of the P→B dative bond under stimuli (heat, light). This system combines pnictogen bonding (from P⁺), dative bonding, anion-π interactions, and supramolecular encapsulation in a single modular framework.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silsesquioxane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on cubic silsesquioxane (POSS) frameworks functionalized with electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., pentafluorophenyl groups) at the silicon vertices. The tetrahedral silicon centers in the cage structure create a rigid, three-dimensional scaffold. The electron-deficient arenes provide multiple, spatially oriented anion-π interaction sites, capable of encapsulating small anions (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) within the cage's interior cavity. The synthon combines the structural robustness and synthetic tunability of organosilicon chemistry with the directional, attractive forces of anion-π interactions. It can be mapped to the seven primitives: (1) Tetrahedral Si nodes as structural hubs, (2) Electron-deficient π-systems as recognition surfaces, (3) Anions as guests, (4) Anion-π interactions as the primary binding force, (5) The cubic cage as a pre-organized 3D container (capsule), (6) Functional group substitution on the arenes for tuning affinity, and (7) Potential for temporal control via anion exchange or redox-active pendant groups.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphazenium cation [P(NR₂)₄]⁺ (where R = alkyl/aryl) that forms a charge-assisted anion-π interaction capsule with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon features: (1) a central tetrahedral phosphorus(V) with four amino substituents creating a bulky, stable cation; (2) four electron-deficient 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene panels attached via flexible linkers to the nitrogen atoms, creating a preorganized cavity; (3) strong electrostatic anion-π interactions between the cationic center and encapsulated anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.); (4) secondary C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from the linker methylene groups; (5) tunable cavity size via linker length and panel electron deficiency; (6) potential for temporal control via pH- or redox-responsive amino groups; (7) orthogonal interaction sites for hierarchical assembly. This system combines pnictogen-based cationic centers, anion-π interactions, and preorganized cavity effects—an underexplored combination in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_borane_adduct_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphorus center in a phosphine-borane adduct (R₃P→BH₃) that acts as an anion-binding site through its electron-deficient borane moiety, while being encapsulated within an electron-rich aromatic π-capsule. The synthon combines: (1) a directional P→B dative bond creating a polarized tetrahedral P center, (2) the Lewis acidic BH₃ unit that can bind anions (F⁻, Cl⁻, CN⁻) via B–anion coordination, (3) peripheral aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene or naphthalene diimide derivatives) that form an electron-deficient or electron-rich π-cavity via stacking interactions, (4) the overall tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the system for encapsulation. Recognition elements include: anion–borane Lewis acid–base interaction, π–π stacking of the capsule walls, and potential C–H⋯anion contacts. This integrates pnictogen bonding (from P), Lewis acid binding, and π-based encapsulation in a single supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_borane_frustrated_lewis_pair_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) system featuring a sterically hindered tetrahedral phosphorus(III) center (tertiary phosphine) and a complementary Lewis acidic borane (B(C₆F₅)₃ or similar perfluorinated arylborane). The synthon exploits the non-quenching, cooperative interaction where the phosphine lone pair and the boron empty p-orbital are held in proximity by a rigid organic scaffold (e.g., a xanthene or triptycene backbone) but prevented from forming a classical dative bond by steric bulk. This creates a polarized pocket capable of reversibly binding and activating small molecules (H₂, CO₂, olefins) via heterolytic cleavage or polarization. Recognition elements include the frustrated P···B interaction, secondary dispersion forces from the fluorinated aryl groups, and shape complementarity of the scaffold. It maps to primitives: (1) Lewis basic site (P lone pair), (2) Lewis acidic site (B center), (3) steric repulsion elements (bulky substituents), (4) π-system of the backbone, (5) dipole from polarized P-B space, (6) hydrophobic perfluoroaryl regions, and (7) reversible binding site for substrates.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanolate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers bearing silanolate anions (R₃SiO⁻) that participate in dual interaction modes: (1) electrostatic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, cyanuric acid derivatives, or nitroaromatics) and (2) coordinative Si-O⁻···M⁺ interactions with alkali or alkaline earth metal cations. The tetrahedral geometry directs three organic substituents (alkyl, aryl, or fluorinated groups) to form a concave, capsule-like exterior, while the exposed silanolate anion sits at the apex, poised for recognition. This system enables programmable assembly via orthogonal interactions—anion-π for aromatic panel binding and metal coordination for linking multiple units or templating capsule formation. Chemically robust, synthetically accessible via silyl chloride hydrolysis or silane oxidation, and tunable in electronics (via R-groups) and binding affinity (via aromatic π-acidity and metal choice). Mappable to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), silanolate anion (charge), anion-π and metal coordination (interactions), reversible assembly (dynamics), and programmable stoichiometry (information).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanediol_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers bearing two hydroxyl groups (silanediol motif) that can deprotonate to form silanolate anions. These anionic oxygen atoms engage in strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or s-triazine rings) arranged in a capsule-like architecture. The tetrahedral geometry of silicon directs two silanolate groups outward for anion-π binding while the remaining two substituents (typically aryl or alkyl groups) provide structural rigidity and solubility. The system can be mapped to the seven primitives through: (1) tetrahedral silicon as core, (2) silanolate as anionic donor, (3) electron-deficient arene as π-acceptor, (4) directional anion-π interaction as recognition element, (5) capsule-like assembly through multiple such interactions, (6) pH-dependent deprotonation for temporal control, and (7) potential for encapsulation of small neutral guests within the cavity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organometallic_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organomercury(II) complexes with electron-deficient aromatic caps that engage in simultaneous anion binding and anion-π interactions. The system features a mercury(II) center coordinated to three carbon-based ligands (alkyl/aryl groups) and one anionic ligand (halide, carboxylate, or pseudohalide), creating a tetrahedral geometry with a permanent negative charge. This anionic complex is encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, nitroaromatics, or cyanostar macrocycles) that provides multiple anion-π interactions with the bound anion. The mercury center's high polarizability enhances both the strength of the anion binding and the subsequent anion-π recognition. This creates a hierarchical assembly: (1) molecular recognition at the mercury center (anion binding), (2) supramolecular recognition via anion-π interactions with the aromatic capsule, and (3) potential temporal control through redox-active ligands or photoresponsive aromatic panels. The seven primitives map clearly: atoms (Hg, C, N/O/F), bonds (Hg-C covalent, Hg-anion coordinate, anion-π noncovalent), motifs (tetrahedral metal center, aromatic panels), interactions (coordination, anion-π, hydrophobic), assemblies (capsule encapsulation), functions (anion recognition/sensing), and systems (redox/photoresponsive control).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanediol_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_5

These anionic oxygen atoms engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., triazine or tetrazine rings) on adjacent building blocks, directing assembly into capsule-like structures. The tetrahedral geometry at silicon provides three-dimensional directionality, while the remaining two substituents on silicon (typically aryl or alkyl groups) control solubility and steric bulk. The system combines covalent siloxane bond potential (Si-O-Si) with non-covalent anion-π and hydrogen bonding interactions, enabling hierarchical assembly from discrete molecular units to defined supramolecular capsules capable of guest encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_lead_plumbylene_crown_ether_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon featuring a tetravalent lead(II) center in a distorted tetrahedral geometry coordinated to a crown ether macrocycle through Pb-O interactions, with the plumbylene (PbR₂) moiety positioned to engage in simultaneous anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic rings and secondary Pb···X (X = halogen) pnictogen bonding. The system combines: (1) strong Pb-O coordination bonds from the crown ether (18-crown-6 or derivatives), (2) directional anion binding to the electron-deficient π-system (e.g., perfluorinated arene or triazine), (3) secondary Pb···X interactions with halogenated substituents, and (4) potential for temporal control via redox switching between Pb(II) and Pb(IV) states. This integrates metal coordination, anion-π, pnictogen bonding, and redox-active temporal domains into a single modular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organometallic_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organomercury(II) complexes that function as anion-binding capsules through anion-π interactions. The system features a mercury(II) center coordinated to three aromatic ligands (such as phenyl or pyridyl groups) and one anionic site (chloride or acetate), creating a tetrahedral geometry. The electron-deficient aromatic rings (substituted with nitro or cyano groups) are positioned to form a convergent anion-binding pocket through cooperative anion-π interactions. The mercury center provides both structural rigidity (due to its preference for tetrahedral coordination in organomercury compounds) and potential for secondary Hg···anion interactions. This creates a preorganized capsule-like structure capable of selectively binding anions like nitrate, perchlorate, or tetrafluoroborate through a combination of anion-π and weak coordinative interactions. The system can be mapped to the seven primitives through its defined geometry (tetrahedral mercury center), recognition elements (electron-deficient aromatics), and reversible anion binding suitable for supramolecular assembly and temporal control through anion exchange.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanolate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers with silanolate anions (R3SiO-) that engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming capsule-like architectures. The silicon centers provide tetrahedral geometry for directional assembly, while the silanolate anions (strong hydrogen bond acceptors/nucleophiles) interact with π-acidic aromatic surfaces (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, cyanurated benzenes) through anion-π contacts. Additional stabilization comes from dispersion forces between the organic substituents on silicon (e.g., phenyl, naphthyl groups) and the aromatic panels. This system combines s-block-like anion behavior (from silicon) with supramolecular anion-π recognition, enabling the construction of charged capsules or cages that can encapsulate small molecules or ions. The seven primitives map clearly: tetrahedral geometry (shape), silanolate anion (charge/polarization), aromatic π-system (polarization), anion-π interaction (recognition), dispersion (organic shell), directional assembly (connectivity), and potential for dynamic exchange (temporal behavior).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_oxide_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphine oxide derivatives that form anion-binding capsules through synergistic anion-π interactions and hydrogen bonding. The system features a tris(2-pyridyl)phosphine oxide core where the phosphoryl oxygen serves as a strong hydrogen bond acceptor, while the three pyridyl arms provide π-acidic surfaces for anion binding. When protonated at the pyridyl nitrogens, the structure forms a cationic cage with convergent anion-π sites that selectively encapsulate tetrahedral anions (e.g., ClO₄⁻, BF₄⁻) through multipoint interactions. The tetrahedral geometry of the phosphine oxide center directs the three pyridyl arms into a tripodal arrangement, creating a preorganized cavity. This synthon demonstrates: 1) hydrogen bonding (P=O···H-N⁺), 2) anion-π interactions (pyridinium rings with anions), 3) electrostatic complementarity, 4) geometric preorganization, 5) cavity-based recognition, 6) charge-assisted binding, and 7) tunable selectivity through pyridyl substitution. The system bridges molecular and supramolecular domains through its programmable self-assembly into higher-order capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silsesquioxane_cage_anion_π_synthon_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) cages with tetrahedral silicon centers functionalized with electron-deficient aromatic groups (e.g., pentafluorophenyl substituents) that create multiple anion-π interaction sites. The rigid, cubic T8 cage structure (Si₈O₁₂ core) provides a three-dimensional scaffold with precisely positioned arene faces that can cooperatively bind anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through electrostatic and polarization interactions. The synthon combines: (1) tetrahedral silicon coordination geometry, (2) siloxane bridging oxygen atoms as weak hydrogen bond acceptors, (3) electron-deficient π-systems for anion recognition, (4) cage confinement effects, (5) preorganized multivalency, (6) hydrophobic exterior for solubility control, and (7) synthetic tunability via substituent variation. This system enables the construction of extended supramolecular architectures through programmed anion-directed assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silsesquioxane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on cubic silsesquioxane (POSS) cages functionalized with electron-deficient arenes at the silicon vertices, creating a tetrahedral arrangement of anion-binding π-acidic surfaces. Each silicon center in the R₈Si₈O₁₂ cage is substituted with a pentafluorophenyl or tetracyanobenzene group, positioning four electron-deficient aromatic faces at the corners of a tetrahedron. This creates a well-defined, rigid cavity capable of encapsulating spherical anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻) via cooperative anion-π interactions. The synthon exhibits: (1) tetrahedral symmetry from the POSS core, (2) multiple anion-π recognition sites, (3) preorganized cavity geometry, (4) tunable electron deficiency via substituent choice, (5) potential for hierarchical assembly into larger capsules, (6) orthogonal interaction sites for additional supramolecular connections, and (7) robust thermal/chemical stability. This represents a novel inorganic-organic hybrid synthon bridging molecular silicon chemistry with supramolecular anion recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silsesquioxane_cage_anion_π_synthon_12

The rigid, cubic or prismatic POSS cage provides a precise three-dimensional scaffold that presents multiple convergent anion-binding sites via anion-π interactions. The synthon's recognition pattern involves cooperative binding of a single anion (e.g., chloride, nitrate) within the electron-deficient aromatic 'pocket' formed by multiple faces of the cage. The tetrahedral geometry of the silicon nodes directs the aromatic panels into a complementary arrangement for encapsulating anions, while the siloxane (Si-O-Si) framework provides structural integrity and potential for further functionalization. This system combines covalent molecular architecture (the POSS cage) with supramolecular anion recognition, mapping to primitives of shape, charge, and spatial arrangement.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_borane_adduct_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4

This system combines pnictogen bonding (from P), dative bonding (P→B), anion-π interactions, and weak hydrogen bonding in a single supramolecular entity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanediol_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) centers bearing two hydroxyl groups (silanediol motif) that can deprotonate to form silanolate anions. These anionic oxygen atoms engage in strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or triazine rings) that form the walls of a self-assembled capsule. The tetrahedral geometry directs two organic substituents (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups) outward to participate in additional π-π stacking or hydrophobic interactions, while the two anionic oxygen atoms point inward toward the π-acidic surfaces. This creates a reversible, charge-assisted recognition motif where the silanolate anion acts as both a hydrogen bond acceptor (from residual silanol OH) and an anion-π donor, enabling the formation of dimeric capsules or higher-order assemblies through complementary electrostatic and dispersion interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_4

The tetrahedral geometry arises from boron coordination to two nitrogen atoms of the dipyrromethene core and two anionic oxygen donors from either solvent or additional ligands. The planar, electron-deficient π-surface of the dipyrromethene acts as an anion-π acceptor site. In the supramolecular assembly, these units dimerize or oligomerize via synergistic interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction between the anionic groups on one unit and the tetrahedral boron center (Lewis acidic site) of another, (2) anion-π interactions between anionic groups and the electron-deficient dipyrromethene π-system, and (3) possible π-π stacking of the planar aromatic cores. This creates a reversible, capsule-like framework capable of encapsulating small cations or polar molecules. The system maps to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), boron (element), anion (charge), π-system (surface), and capsule (assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silanolate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers with silanolate anions (R3SiO-) that engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming capsule-like architectures. synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silsesquioxane_cage_anion_π_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on cubic T8 silsesquioxane cages with pendant ammonium groups that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The synthon exhibits three key recognition elements: 1) the rigid, shape-persistent siloxane scaffold providing spatial directionality, 2) the cationic ammonium groups for electrostatic complementarity, and 3) the electron-deficient siloxane rings (Si-O-Si) serving as anion-π acceptors. This represents a hybrid inorganic-organic supramolecular motif combining electrostatic, anion-π, and van der Waals interactions, suitable for constructing porous frameworks or molecular capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silsesquioxane_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_5

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_borane_frustrated_lewis_pair_synthon_2

This cation engages in cooperative interactions with anions (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) that are simultaneously involved in anion-π bonding with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine derivatives). The resulting ternary complex exhibits directional recognition: the oxonium cation's positive charge enhances anion binding, and the anion bridges to π-acidic aromatic panels, enabling the assembly of dimeric or higher-order capsule architectures. This system utilizes electrostatic, anion-π, and van der Waals interactions, and can be mapped to primitives such as charge, polarity, and spatial arrangement for programmable supramolecular design.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_borane_adduct_anion_π_capsule_synthon_13
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphorus center in a phosphine-borane adduct (R3P-BH3) that undergoes deprotonation to form an anionic phosphido-borane complex [R2P-BH3]⁻. This anion features a localized negative charge on phosphorus with significant lone pair character, enabling strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or cyanuric acid derivatives) in a capsule assembly. The tetrahedral geometry at phosphorus is maintained by the borane moiety, while the anionic charge and directional lone pair create a predictable interaction vector. Recognition elements include: (1) the anionic phosphido center as an electron-rich site, (2) the borane group providing structural rigidity and weak Lewis acidity for secondary interactions, (3) electron-deficient π-systems as complementary receptors. This system maps to primitives as: electron density (anion), directionality (tetrahedral P center), polarity (charge-separated P⁻-BH3), complementarity (anion-π pairing), rigidity (constrained tetrahedral geometry), cooperativity (secondary B-H...X contacts), and reversibility (dynamic anion-π association).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organometallic_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organomercury anions (R-Hg⁻) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The mercury center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with one anionic lone pair, one covalent carbon bond (typically from an aryl or alkyl group), and two coordination sites occupied by weakly-bound solvent or counterions. The anionic mercury center acts as an anion-π donor to π-acidic aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or pyrazine rings) in self-assembled coordination cages or covalent organic capsules. This creates a directional, charge-assisted supramolecular recognition motif where the soft, polarizable mercury anion selectively binds to electron-deficient aromatic surfaces, enabling the construction of metallo-supramolecular architectures with tunable host-guest properties. The system exhibits clear mapping to primitives: atoms (Hg, C, N/O donors), bonds (covalent Hg-C, dative bonds, anion-π interactions), rings (aromatic panels), cages (self-assembled capsule), intermolecular interactions (anion-π, van der Waals), and dynamic exchange (ligand substitution at Hg).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O+) that forms a complementary anion-π interaction capsule with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The oxonium center (O+) acts as a strong hydrogen bond acceptor at its three vertices while maintaining a positive charge that enhances anion binding. This creates a three-fold symmetric recognition motif where three electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanopyrazine, or s-tetrazine derivatives) arrange around the oxonium cation via anion-π interactions with the partially negative faces of the π-systems oriented toward the central O+. The system exhibits directional hydrogen bonding from the oxonium to anion donors (if present) and cooperative electrostatic stabilization. This represents an underexplored cationic analogue to silanediol/anion capsules, with potential in supramolecular assembly, ion-pair recognition, and dynamic covalent systems via oxonium stability in non-aqueous or acidic environments.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphazene anion (hexachlorocyclotriphosphazene derivative with one chloride replaced by a phenolate anion) that acts as an anion-π donor to electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: 1) A P₃N₃ core with alternating P and N atoms forming a six-membered ring, 2) Five remaining chlorides providing halogen-bond acceptor sites, 3) One phenolate anion (deprotonated phenol substituent) extending from a phosphorus center, creating a tetrahedral anion geometry, 4) Electron-deficient triazine or tetrazine panels as π-acceptors that form anion-π interactions with the phenolate oxygen's electron density, 5) Complementary halogen bonds between P-Cl groups and electron donors on the aromatic panels. This creates a self-assembling capsule where multiple phosphazene anions interact with multiple aromatic panels through synergistic anion-π and halogen-bonding interactions, suitable for encapsulation of small neutral molecules or cations.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_15
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O+) that forms a directional electrostatic interaction with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces (anion-π interaction), creating a capsule-like assembly motif. The oxonium center (typically from protonated ethers, epoxides, or crown ether derivatives) carries a formal positive charge distributed across the oxygen and three substituents (alkyl, aryl, or heterocyclic). This cation engages in a strong, oriented anion-π interaction with electron-poor arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanopyrazine, or nitroaromatics) where the cationic oxygen sits above the π-face. Additional secondary interactions (C–H···O, C–H···F, or weak hydrogen bonds) from the substituents help preorganize the assembly. The synthon is dynamic and can be tuned by varying the oxonium substituents and the electron deficiency of the arene, making it suitable for stimuli-responsive capsules or ion-pair recognition in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenium_selenoxide_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral selenium(IV) centers in selenoxide anions (R-Se(=O)-R') that function as anion-π donors to electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The system features: (1) tetrahedral selenium with stereogenic lone pair, (2) negatively charged oxygen (selenoxide anion, pKa ~8-10), (3) directional Se-O⁻···π interactions with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., perfluorinated pyrazine or triazine rings in capsule walls), (4) additional C-H···O hydrogen bonds from capsule methylene bridges to selenoxide oxygen, (5) chiral recognition capability due to pyramidal selenium stereochemistry, (6) redox-active selenium center enabling temporal switching between oxidation states, and (7) tunable lipophilicity via organic substituents (R/R') for phase-transfer applications. This represents an underexplored chalcogen-bonding anion-π hybrid interaction motif with potential for enantioselective encapsulation and redox-responsive host-guest systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenium_selenoxide_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral selenium(IV) centers in selenoxide anions (R-Se(=O)-R') that function as anion-π interaction donors. The selenium atom adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with two organic substituents, one oxygen atom (forming the Se=O bond with significant polarity), and a lone pair. The electron-deficient π-system of the Se=O bond, combined with the partial positive charge on selenium due to the electronegative oxygen, creates a region of positive electrostatic potential that can engage in anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic systems or anions. This synthon is particularly effective in forming capsular assemblies when combined with complementary π-basic aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives, tetrazine rings) that provide the anion-binding sites. The tetrahedral geometry directs the substituents outward, allowing for peripheral functionalization to control capsule assembly and stability. Recognition elements include: (1) the polarized Se=O bond as an electrostatic interaction donor, (2) the tetrahedral selenium center providing directional control, and (3) the organic substituents (alkyl/aryl) that can be tuned for solubility and additional weak interactions (C-H···π, van der Waals). This represents an underexplored chalcogen-bonding variant in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_16
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral oxonium cations (R3O+) that engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The oxonium center (O+) adopts a tetrahedral geometry with three organic substituents (alkyl/aryl) and a positive charge, creating a strong electrostatic field. This cationic center interacts with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., perfluorinated benzene, triazine, or tetrazine rings) that form capsule-like structures through π-stacking or edge-to-face interactions. The anion-π interaction between the positively charged oxygen and the π-acidic surface is complemented by C-H···O hydrogen bonds from capsule methylene/methine groups to oxonium oxygen, and potential weak C-F···H-C contacts if perfluoroarenes are used. This system maps to primitives as: (1) tetrahedral geometry at oxygen, (2) electrostatic (+/-) recognition, (3) π-system as receptor, (4) capsule confinement, (5) directional H-bonding, (6) hydrophobic filling, and (7) charge-transfer character. The oxonium cation is chemically stable with non-nucleophilic counterions (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, BArF-), and the capsule can be tailored via substituents on both oxonium and arene components.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_12_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium cation [R3Se]+ where R are electron-withdrawing aryl groups (e.g., pentafluorophenyl) that enhance the Lewis acidity of selenium. The synthon exploits two orthogonal interaction patterns: (1) anion binding via the σ-hole on selenium along the extension of one R-Se bond (pnictogen-type chalcogen bonding), and (2) parallel engagement of one electron-deficient aryl ring in anion-π interactions with the same anion, creating a chelate-like motif. The remaining two aryl groups provide steric bulk and additional π-surfaces for secondary stacking interactions with other synthons or capsule walls. This combination creates a directional, charge-assisted recognition element suitable for constructing self-assembled capsules or cages through convergent anion binding sites. The system is chemically realistic, with known stable selenonium salts, and maps cleanly to primitives: atoms (Se, C, F), bonds (covalent Se-C, non-covalent Se···anion, π-anion), angles (tetrahedral around Se), dihedrals (aryl ring orientations), rings (aromatic), and surfaces (anion-binding σ-hole and π-face).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organomercurate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organomercurate anions (R-HgX₃⁻) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating self-assembled capsule architectures. The mercury center adopts tetrahedral geometry with one organic substituent (alkyl or aryl) and three halide or pseudohalide ligands, creating a negatively charged tetrahedral anion. This anion interacts through its electron-rich halide ligands with electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, trinitrobenzene, or pyrazine panels) in a complementary fashion. The synthon exhibits directional Hg-X···π interactions (X = Cl, Br, I, CN, SCN) with well-defined geometries, enabling predictable assembly into dimeric or oligomeric capsules through multiple simultaneous anion-π contacts. The mercury center's relativistic effects enhance the polarizability of the Hg-X bonds, strengthening the non-covalent interactions. This system combines metalloorganic chemistry with supramolecular anion recognition, offering tunability through variation of the organic substituent, halide ligands, and electron-deficient aromatic panels.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) centers chelated by β-diketonate ligands, forming anionic complexes with extended π-surfaces. The boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with two oxygen atoms from the β-diketonate and two additional anionic or neutral ligands (e.g., fluoride, hydroxide, or aryl groups). The planar, conjugated β-diketonate backbone provides an electron-deficient π-surface capable of engaging in anion-π interactions with complementary cationic or electron-rich partners. The overall assembly features: (1) tetrahedral boron as a geometric constraint element, (2) anionic charge for electrostatic recognition, (3) extended aromatic surfaces for π-stacking and anion-π interactions, (4) chelate ring rigidity for preorganization, and (5) tunable substituents on the β-diketonate for modulating electronic properties and solubility. This system can form dimeric capsules via complementary anion-π interactions between electron-deficient boron chelates and cationic or electron-rich aromatic units, or serve as a building block for larger coordination frameworks through metal binding to the diketonate oxygen lone pairs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the oxonium cation (H₃O⁺) encapsulated within a crown ether host. The tetrahedral oxonium ion (O⁺ with three hydrogens) forms strong hydrogen bonds with the ether oxygen atoms of the crown (e.g., 18-crown-6), creating a stable host-guest complex. Recognition elements include: (1) the positively charged oxonium center acting as a hydrogen bond donor, (2) the crown ether's oxygen lone pairs as hydrogen bond acceptors in a preorganized cavity, and (3) size-complementarity between the oxonium ion and the crown cavity. This system maps to primitives as: donor (oxonium H), acceptor (crown ether O), charged (positive oxonium), hydrophobic (crown ether alkyl chains), shape (tetrahedral guest in circular host), backbone (polyether macrocycle), and stereochemistry (conformationally locked crown). The interaction is reversible and tunable by crown ether size and solvent, making it valuable for proton transport systems, switchable catalysis, and temporal control in dynamic covalent chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_lead_plumbylene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedrally coordinated lead(II) center in a plumbylene anion framework (R₂Pb⁻) that acts as an anion-π donor to electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a formally anionic lead center with a stereochemically active lone pair, coordinated by two bulky organic substituents (e.g., terphenyl or silyl groups) and stabilized by intramolecular donor ligands (e.g., N-heterocyclic carbene or phosphine). This anionic metalloid complex engages in strong, directional anion-π interactions with the faces of electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanopyrazine, or s-tetrazine derivatives) arranged in a capsule-like geometry. The recognition elements include: (1) the localized negative charge and lone pair on lead, (2) the steric profile of the organic substituents directing capsule assembly, and (3) the complementary electrostatic and polarization effects between the anion and π-acidic surfaces. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through: shape (tetrahedral metal center), charge (anionic), polarity (polarizable Pb center), H-bonding (not primary), aromaticity (π-acidic panels), hydrophobicity (organic substituents), and conformational flexibility (adjustable capsule panels).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_crown_ether_cation_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (H₃O⁺) encapsulated within a crown ether host, which then engages in cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral H₃O⁺ core with three hydrogen-bond donor sites, (2) 18-crown-6 ether as the primary host via multiple O···H–O hydrogen bonds, (3) electron-deficient hexafluorobenzene or s-tetrazine π-surfaces positioned above and below the crown-ether complex, creating a sandwich-like capsule through anion-π interactions (where the oxonium cation acts as the 'anion' counterpart in this non-covalent interaction). Recognition elements include crown ether-oxonium ion-dipole/hydrogen bonding, tetrahedral geometry of the cation, and complementary electrostatic surfaces for π-system engagement. This represents a rare example of a cationic species participating in anion-π interactions within a pre-organized host-guest framework.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O⁺) that forms a complementary anion-π interaction with electron-deficient aromatic systems, creating a capsule-like assembly motif. The oxonium center (typically from protonated ethers or epoxides) serves as a strong hydrogen bond donor through its three equivalent O-H⁺ bonds, while its positive charge enhances anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes like hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ), or nitroaromatics. This creates a three-fold symmetric recognition element where the oxonium cation sits above an electron-deficient aromatic plane, with additional secondary interactions (C-H···π, dipole-dipole) stabilizing the assembly. The system can be extended to form dimeric capsules through complementary pairing of multiple oxonium cations and anion-π acceptors, relevant to supramolecular container chemistry and selective anion recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) β-diketonate anions that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The boron center adopts tetrahedral geometry with two oxygen atoms from the β-diketone ligand and two additional anionic or neutral ligands (typically halides, alkoxides, or solvent molecules). The β-diketonate moiety provides extended π-conjugation and delocalized negative charge, enhancing both the anion-π interaction strength and the synthon's directionality. The tetrahedral geometry creates a well-defined spatial arrangement of recognition elements: (1) the anionic charge center for electrostatic complementarity, (2) the π-face of the β-diketonate for secondary stacking interactions, and (3) the ligand periphery for steric modulation. This system can be mapped to the seven primitives through its charge distribution (primitive 1), tetrahedral geometry (primitive 2), directional anion-π interactions (primitive 3), tunable electronic properties via β-diketone substitution (primitive 4), reversible capsule formation (primitive 5), potential for multi-component assembly (primitive 6), and responsiveness to pH or counterion exchange (primitive 7).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) complexed with anionic dipyrromethene (BODIPY-like) ligands, where the boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with two anionic nitrogen donors from the dipyrromethene core and two additional anionic or neutral axial ligands (typically fluoride or aryloxide). The planar, electron-deficient π-surface of the dipyrromethene chromophore acts as an anion-π recognition site, while the tetrahedral boron center provides directional hydrogen-bond acceptor capability via its axial ligands. This creates a dual-mode supramolecular building block: (1) the electron-deficient aromatic plane can engage in anion-π interactions with anions or electron-rich guests, and (2) the tetrahedral boron-fluoride or boron-oxygen bonds can act as hydrogen-bond acceptors for NH or OH donors. When combined with complementary cationic or hydrogen-bond donor species, this synthon can form self-assembled capsules or cages via a combination of anion-π, hydrogen-bonding, and electrostatic interactions. The system is chemically realistic, inspired by known tetrahedral boron BODIPY complexes and their supramolecular applications in sensing and host-guest chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on oxonium ion (H₃O⁺) encapsulated within a crown ether host through multiple hydrogen bonds and ion-dipole interactions. The tetrahedral oxonium cation (H₃O⁺) acts as a guest with three directional hydrogen bond donor sites, while crown ethers like 18-crown-6 provide complementary oxygen lone pairs as acceptors. This creates a stable host-guest complex with C₃ₖ symmetry, where the oxonium ion sits at the center of the crown ether cavity. The interaction pattern involves three strong O–H···O hydrogen bonds (2.6-2.8 Å) supplemented by electrostatic ion-dipole stabilization. This synthon is chemically realistic, observed in crystal structures of acid-crown ether complexes, and can serve as a building block for proton-conducting materials or pH-responsive supramolecular assemblies. It maps to primitives through: (1) hydrogen bond donors (oxonium protons), (2) hydrogen bond acceptors (crown ether oxygens), (3) electrostatic complementarity, (4) directional preferences, (5) size/shape matching, (6) cooperative binding, and (7) reversible association dynamics.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) complexed with a β-diketonate ligand (e.g., acetylacetonate derivative) bearing an extended aromatic substituent. The boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with the β-diketonate occupying two coordination sites via its oxygen atoms, while the remaining two sites are occupied by anionic or neutral ligands (e.g., fluoride, hydroxide, or a phenolate). The extended aromatic system on the β-diketonate backbone provides a concave, electron-deficient π-surface. This synthon is designed to engage in dual interaction modes: (1) anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient aromatic cavity and an anionic guest (e.g., chloride, nitrate), and (2) coordinative encapsulation via the Lewis acidic boron center, which can further bind a small anion or neutral Lewis base. The combination creates a synergistic 'capsule-like' binding environment suitable for selective anion recognition and encapsulation. Recognition elements include the Lewis acidic boron, the pre-organized β-diketonate chelate, the electron-deficient π-system, and potential hydrogen-bond donors/acceptors on ligand substituents. This system maps to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), anion binding (electrostatic), π-system (surface), chelate ring (cycle), Lewis acid-base interaction (link), pre-organized cavity (pocket), and tunable electronics (state).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphonate anions [R-PO3]²⁻ that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The phosphonate group provides three oxygen atoms for hydrogen bonding or metal coordination, while the tetrahedral geometry creates directional recognition elements. The negatively charged oxygen atoms engage in anion-π interactions with cationic or electron-deficient π-systems of capsule frameworks, particularly with tetrafluorinated or trinitro-substituted aromatic panels. This creates a dual recognition motif: (1) directional hydrogen bonds from the phosphonate oxygens to complementary donors on the capsule, and (2) electrostatic anion-π interactions between the anionic phosphonate and electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The system is chemically realistic as phosphonates are stable anions in aqueous and organic media, and their anion-π interactions have been documented in crystal engineering. This synthon maps to primitives through: 1) tetrahedral geometry (shape), 2) anionic charge (electrostatics), 3) oxygen lone pairs (donor), 4) π-acceptor surfaces (acceptor), 5) directional H-bonds (vectorial), 6) encapsulation (spatial), and 7) pH-dependent formation (temporal).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_imidazolium_zwitterion_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron center bearing an imidazolium substituent, creating a zwitterionic structure with both cationic and anionic character. The boron atom is coordinated to three electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., trifluoromethyl or pentafluorophenyl substituents) and one imidazolium group via a B-N bond. This creates a unique recognition pattern: (1) the tetrahedral boron anion (B⁻ center) can engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems, (2) the cationic imidazolium moiety can participate in cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatics or hydrogen bonding, and (3) the peripheral fluorinated groups enable additional halogen bonding or hydrophobic interactions. This synthon is chemically realistic, drawing from known tetrahedral borate anions and N-heterocyclic carbene-borane adducts, but combines them in a zwitterionic architecture that provides multiple orthogonal interaction sites for supramolecular assembly or temporal control through pH or redox modulation of the imidazolium group.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_lead_plumbate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetravalent lead (Pb⁴⁺) in a distorted tetrahedral coordination environment, forming a plumbate anion [PbR₄]²⁻ where R are electron-withdrawing aryl groups with extended π-systems. The synthon features: (1) a central Pb(IV) anion with high formal negative charge, (2) four aromatic arms arranged tetrahedrally, creating a concave, bowl-shaped electron-rich surface, (3) strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes or cationic π-systems, (4) potential for encapsulation of small cationic or polar guests within the tetrahedral cavity, (5) halogen-bond acceptor capability via the plumbate lone pairs, (6) redox-active behavior with accessible Pb(IV)/Pb(II) couple for temporal control, and (7) directional coordination sites for metal ions at the oxygen atoms of substituted aryloxy ligands. This system combines heavy p-block element chemistry with supramolecular anion-π recognition and encapsulation motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral boron(III) complexed with anionic dipyrromethene (BODIPY-like) ligands, where the boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with two anionic nitrogen donors from the dipyrromethene core and two additional anionic or neutral axial ligands (typically halides or alkoxides). The electron-deficient boron center and the extended π-system of the dipyrromethene create a dual recognition motif: (1) anion-π interactions between the electron-rich faces of aromatic guest molecules and the electron-deficient BODIPY π-system, and (2) electrostatic stabilization of cationic or dipole-containing guests by the tetrahedral borate anion. The planar, rigid dipyrromethene scaffold promotes self-assembly into dimeric or capsule-like structures through complementary π-π stacking and edge-to-face interactions, while the tetrahedral boron center provides directional control. This synthon is chemically realistic, known in coordination chemistry and materials science, and offers programmable assembly via ligand exchange at boron and substitution on the dipyrromethene periphery.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphine_borane_adduct_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphorus center in a phosphine-borane adduct (R3P→BH3) where the borane moiety can be deprotonated to form an anionic borohydride-like species [R3P→BH2]⁻. This anion engages in dual interaction modes: (1) anion-π interactions between the electron-rich borohydride fragment and electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or nitroaromatics), and (2) directional C–H···π interactions from alkyl/aryl groups on phosphorus to complementary π-systems. The tetrahedral geometry at phosphorus, combined with the directional P→B dative bond and the anionic BH2 unit, creates a well-defined, three-dimensional recognition element. This synthon can self-assemble into capsule-like structures through complementary anion-π and π-π stacking interactions, with potential for encapsulation of small guests. The system is chemically realistic, with phosphine-borane adducts being well-known and their deprotonation chemistry established in frustrated Lewis pair chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_17
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral oxonium cation (R3O⁺) stabilized by anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming a capsule-like assembly. The oxonium center (O⁺ with three organic substituents, typically alkyl or aryl groups) acts as a strong hydrogen bond donor through its three O–H⁺-like polarized bonds. These interact with anionic species (Cl⁻, Br⁻, PF₆⁻, etc.) that are simultaneously engaged in anion-π interactions with adjacent arenes bearing electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, trinitrophenyl, or cyanophenyl rings). The combination creates a three-dimensional recognition motif where the oxonium cation sits at the center of a tetrahedral arrangement, with anions occupying vertices and π-acidic aromatic panels providing additional directional stabilization. This synthon is chemically realistic in superacidic or stabilized ionic environments and maps to primitives: (1) tetrahedral geometry at oxygen, (2) cationic charge, (3) anion binding, (4) π-acidic surface, (5) directional O⁺···anion hydrogen bonds, (6) electrostatic complementarity, and (7) encapsulation propensity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_mercury_organomercurial_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organomercurial anions that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The system features R-Hg-L₃⁻ tetrahedral anions (where R = organic substituent, L = thiolate or carboxylate ligands) with a formal negative charge on mercury. These anions interact with π-acidic aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, triazine rings, or nitroaromatics) in self-assembled coordination cages or covalent organic cages. The mercury center's high polarizability enhances dispersion forces, while the anionic charge creates strong electrostatic complementarity with electron-deficient π-systems. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral Hg(II) geometry with anionic character, (2) electron-deficient aromatic surfaces in the host framework, (3) secondary Hg···π interactions with adjacent arenes, and (4) potential auxiliary hydrogen bonds from ligand periphery. This represents a novel combination of heavy-metal coordination chemistry, anion-π interactions, and supramolecular encapsulation motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_oxonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral oxonium cations (R3O⁺) interacting with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces via anion-π interactions within a capsule-like architecture. The oxonium center (O⁺) adopts a tetrahedral geometry with three organic substituents (alkyl/aryl groups) and a positive charge, creating a strong electrostatic field. This cationic center is positioned above electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or tetracyanobenzene derivatives) that serve as anion-π acceptors. The system forms through complementary electrostatic and dispersion interactions: (1) the positively charged oxonium acts as an 'anion surrogate' for the electron-deficient π-system, (2) the tetrahedral geometry provides directional control, and (3) surrounding hydrogen-bond acceptors (e.g., carbonyl groups on the aromatic periphery) can further stabilize the oxonium via weak C–H···O interactions. This represents a rare example of using oxonium cations (rather than metal cations or ammonium) in anion-π contexts, with potential for temporal control via oxonium formation/dissociation under acidic conditions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_iminomethyl_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_diarylethene_anion_π_switch_synthon

The system maps to primitives through: electron-deficient arenes (π-acidic surface), photochromic switching (temporal control element), anion recognition (electrostatic complementarity), and reversible covalent bond formation/breaking in the photocyclization process.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_calixarene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1

The overall tetrahedral geometry of the silicon center orients the calixarene cavity for encapsulation of tetrahedral or spherical anions (e.g., Cl⁻, BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻). This system combines covalent (Si–O, Si–X), coordinative (Si←anion, if anion acts as ligand), and non-covalent (anion-π, C–H···anion, van der Waals) interactions, making it a versatile building block for self-assembled capsules or extended frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stibonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_31

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stibine_anion_π_capsule_synthon_15

The electron-deficient aromatic rings provide multiple anion-π binding sites, while the antimony center acts as a pnictogen bond donor through its σ-hole along the Sb-ligand axis. The synthon demonstrates chelate cooperativity where anion binding to Sb enhances the electron deficiency of the aromatic rings, strengthening the anion-π contacts. This represents an underexplored combination of heavy pnictogen chemistry with supramolecular anion recognition motifs.

This represents an underexplored pnictogen-bonding system with heavier group 15 elements, offering tunable cavity sizes through aromatic substituent modification and potential for selective anion recognition in competitive media.
