The R₄As⁺ cation offers a stable, weakly coordinating positive charge with tunable sterics via substituent choice, while the electron-deficient panels create convergent anion-binding pockets. This system enables the assembly of dimeric or higher-order capsules that encapsulate anions via cooperative anion-π and electrostatic interactions, with potential for selectivity based on anion size, shape, and charge density. The tetrahedral geometry of the arsonium center directs capsule symmetry, and the synthon maps to primitives: positive charge (arsonium), π-system (electron-deficient arene), anion binding, tetrahedral node, curvature element, linker, and encapsulation cavity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral arsonium cations (R₄As⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like assembly. The synthon features: (1) Tetrahedral arsonium cation as the cationic vertex (R = aryl or alkyl groups, e.g., tetraphenylarsonium), (2) Electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, cyanuric acid derivatives, or triazine rings) as the planar faces, (3) Anion-π interactions between the cationic As center (through its positive charge) and adjacent anions (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, PF₆⁻) that are further stabilized by the electron-deficient arenes, (4) Additional C–H···anion and C–H···π contacts from the aryl substituents on arsenic, (5) Assembly into a tetrahedral capsule with four arsonium vertices and four electron-deficient aromatic panels, encapsulating an anion pair or small molecule guest. This system explores the underexplored supramolecular chemistry of heavy pnictogen cations and their integration with anion-π motifs.

synthons.name: temporal_redox_switchable_viologen_anion_π_cage_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular/temporal hybrid system based on a redox-active viologen (1,1'-disubstituted-4,4'-bipyridinium) core that can switch between dicationic (V²⁺) and radical cationic (V⁺•) states. In its oxidized V²⁺ form, the viologen acts as a strong anion-π acceptor due to its electron-deficient π-system, capable of binding anions like Cl⁻, Br⁻, or BF₄⁻ through anion-π interactions. Upon one-electron reduction to V⁺•, the system becomes a radical cationic species with enhanced π-donor character, switching its preference to cation-π interactions with alkali metal cations (Na⁺, K⁺). The synthon incorporates two viologen units connected by a flexible redox-active linker (such as a tetrathiafulvalene or ferrocene bridge) that enables reversible electrochemical switching between anion-binding and cation-binding states. This creates a temporally addressable molecular cage that can alternately encapsulate anions or cations based on applied potential, with the switching kinetics controlled by electrolyte composition and scan rate. Recognition elements include: (1) electron-deficient π-surface of oxidized viologen for anion binding, (2) radical π-system of reduced viologen for cation binding, (3) redox-active linker for potential-gated switching, and (4) peripheral hydrogen-bonding groups (amide or urea) for secondary stabilization of guest species. The seven primitives map as: atoms (N⁺, C, H), bonds (covalent C-C/C-N bonds in viologen core), interactions (anion-π, cation-π, hydrogen bonding), topology (cage-like assembly), dynamics (redox-switching kinetics), environment (electrochemical potential, solvent polarity), and function (temporal guest sequestration/release).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_triflate_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) cations coordinated to three trifluoromethanesulfonate (triflate) anions, forming a cationic complex [Ga(OTf)₃]⁺ that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The gallium center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with three oxygen atoms from triflates and one coordination site occupied by a weakly bound solvent molecule or intentionally designed electron-deficient arene. The triflate anions provide both charge-balancing and structural directionality through their sulfonate groups, while their electron-withdrawing CF₃ groups enhance the electrophilicity of adjacent aromatic systems. This creates a three-pronged anion-π recognition motif where each triflate anion interacts with a separate electron-deficient aromatic panel (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanobenzene, or perfluorinated pyridine), leading to the self-assembly of dimeric or higher-order capsule structures. The synthon exploits the hard Lewis acidity of Ga(III), the conformational rigidity of triflate ligands, and the tunable π-acidity of aromatic systems to create predictable supramolecular architectures with potential applications in selective anion encapsulation, catalysis, or molecular sensing.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_dication_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) dications (GeR4²⁺) that form anion-π capsules with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The germanium center, with its large ionic radius and +4 oxidation state, creates a strong electrostatic field that organizes four electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-tetrazine, or perfluorinated pyridine derivatives) into a tetrahedral arrangement. These panels engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with halide or oxoanion guests (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, SO₄²⁻) encapsulated at the center. The synthon exploits the underutilized germanium(IV) cation as a tetrahedral organizing node, combining cation-anion electrostatics, directional anion-π contacts, and geometric preorganization to create a well-defined supramolecular capsule. This system is chemically reasonable as organogermanium(IV) cations are known stable species, and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatics are well-established.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) complexed with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand, forming a cationic host with electron-deficient aromatic panels that engage in cooperative anion-π interactions. The system features: (1) a Ga³⁺ center with tetrahedral geometry, (2) a rigid salen-type Schiff base ligand with four imine linkages providing N₂O₂ coordination, (3) electron-deficient pyridinium or triazine aromatic rings positioned orthogonally to create a cationic capsule-like cavity, (4) anion recognition via electrostatic attraction to the metal center and complementary anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic surfaces, and (5) tunable cavity size via ligand backbone modification. This represents a novel metal-organic capsule synthon distinct from previously proposed pnictogen-based systems, exploiting gallium's hard Lewis acidity and stable +3 oxidation state for robust supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_sulfonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral sulfonium cation (R3S+) that acts as a cationic anchor point, paired with electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene) for anion-π interactions. The sulfonium center provides a strong, directional positive charge, while the surrounding aryl groups are functionalized with electron-withdrawing substituents to create π-acidic surfaces. This combination allows the assembly of dimeric or cage-like structures through cooperative electrostatic and anion-π interactions, encapsulating anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-) within a π-rich cavity. The synthon is chemically robust, synthetically accessible via alkylation of thioethers, and offers tunability through variation of R groups (alkyl, aryl) and π-acidic arenes.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) germonium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like architecture. The germonium center provides a strong cationic charge (+1) distributed across the tetrahedral framework, while electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or nitrobenzene derivatives) serve as π-acidic surfaces that attract anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.) through anion-π interactions. The combination of directional anion-π contacts and tetrahedral geometry leads to predictable assembly into discrete capsules or cages in which anions are encapsulated at the vertices or faces. This system exploits the underutilized germonium cation (heavier Group 14 analog of ammonium/phosphonium) and integrates it with anion-π recognition—a less common supramolecular motif—to create a new structural paradigm for anion encapsulation and sensing.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_tris(8-hydroxyquinoline)_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) complexed with three 8-hydroxyquinoline ligands, forming an electron-deficient metal-organic cavity that exhibits strong anion-π interactions with halide anions. The gallium center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with three bidentate ligands, creating a bowl-shaped cavity with electron-deficient π-surfaces from the quinoline rings. This system combines metal coordination (Ga-N and Ga-O bonds), directional hydrogen bonding potential from the hydroxyl groups, and multiple anion-π interaction sites. The electron-deficient nature of the coordinated quinoline rings enhances anion binding through electrostatic and polarization effects, while the tetrahedral geometry creates a well-defined binding pocket suitable for encapsulation of spherical anions like chloride or bromide. This represents a novel metal-organic anion receptor system distinct from purely organic or main-group cation-based capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers bearing cationic silylium (R3Si+) groups that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like assembly. The system features: (1) tetrahedral silicon centers with three bulky organic substituents and one cationic silylium site, (2) electron-deficient hexafluorobenzene or tetracyanobenzene panels as π-acidic surfaces, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the silylium cation (acting as a Lewis acidic site that can be considered an 'anion' in the electrostatic sense) and the electron-deficient π-system, (4) complementary dispersion interactions between organic substituents, (5) geometrically constrained tetrahedral arrangement enabling capsule formation, (6) tunable cavity size via substituent length, and (7) potential for encapsulation of small neutral guests. This represents a novel combination of main-group cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π architectures, distinct from previously proposed pnictogen and chalcogen-based capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silylium cation (R3Si+) that engages in simultaneous cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels and electrostatic interactions with encapsulated anions. The system features three aromatic walls (e.g., 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene derivatives) arranged in a trigonal prismatic geometry, where the positively charged silicon center sits at one apex, directing its empty p-orbital toward the π-clouds. An anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) is encapsulated in the cavity, stabilized by both the cationic silicon and the polarized C–H bonds of the aromatic panels. The recognition elements include: (1) strong silylium cation-π interactions (σ-hole type electrostatic attraction), (2) anion-π interactions with the polarized arenes, (3) C–H···anion hydrogen bonds, and (4) dispersion-driven π-stacking between the aromatic sidewalls. This synthon maps to the seven primitives via: electrostatic (cation-anion, cation-π), dispersion (π-stacking), shape complementarity (tetrahedral cation in a trigonal pocket), and dynamic exchange (anion encapsulation/release). It represents an underexplored silicon-based cationic counterpart to the more common ammonium/phosphonium capsules in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_spiropyran_merocyanine_zwitterion_host_guest_synthon
synthons.description: A photoresponsive molecular switch based on spiropyran-merocyanine interconversion that creates a zwitterionic host site for anion binding. The closed spiropyran form (colorless) is neutral and has minimal binding affinity. Upon UV irradiation (365 nm), it converts to the open merocyanine form (colored), which features a phenolate anion and an iminium cation separated by a conjugated bridge. This zwitterion creates a strong electrostatic binding pocket for anions (particularly halides) via the iminium cation (cation-anion interaction) while the phenolate can engage in hydrogen bonding. Visible light or thermal relaxation reverses the process, releasing the guest. This system combines photochromism (temporal control) with supramolecular host-guest chemistry, where binding affinity is light-gated. Recognition elements include: (1) photochromic diarylethene-like core, (2) zwitterionic charge separation in open form, (3) electrostatic + hydrogen bonding anion recognition site, and (4) reversible temporal switching between 'on' (binding) and 'off' (non-binding) states. Mappable to primitives: donor (phenolate O⁻), acceptor (iminium N⁺), hydrophobe (aromatic rings), hinge (photochromic bond breaking/forming), protector (steric shielding around binding site), stretcher (conjugated bridge between charges), and template (anion guest shape complementarity).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R₃Si⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like assembly. The system features: (1) a positively charged silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl or t-butyl groups) to stabilize the highly electrophilic silylium ion, (2) electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, cyanuric acid derivatives, or perfluorinated pyridines) that provide strong anion-π acceptor sites for halide or tetrafluoroborate anions, and (3) preorganized geometry where four silylium cations are bridged by four anion-π interactions to form a tetrahedral capsule enclosing an anion or small molecule guest. The recognition elements include electrostatic cation-anion attraction, directional anion-π interactions (anion positioned over π-deficient arene centroid), and steric complementarity from the bulky substituents that prevent cation collapse while defining cavity size. This represents a novel extension of tetrahedral cation-anion-π capsules into main-group silicon chemistry, exploiting the underutilized silylium cation as a strong Lewis acid and structure-directing element.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon-centered silyl cations (R3Si+) that engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The system features a cationic silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (typically aryl or alkyl groups) creating a tetrahedral geometry, while the fourth coordination site is occupied by a labile ligand or solvent molecule. The positively charged silicon center can interact with anions (Cl-, BF4-, PF6-) through electrostatic attraction, while the electron-deficient aromatic rings on the substituents provide complementary anion-π binding sites. This creates a three-dimensional recognition pocket capable of encapsulating anions through a combination of electrostatic, anion-π, and van der Waals interactions. The synthon can be incorporated into larger cage structures or coordination polymers, with the silicon center's geometry directing assembly into tetrahedral or octahedral capsules. The labile Si-L bond allows for dynamic exchange, introducing potential temporal control through chemical or electrochemical stimulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_19
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating self-assembled capsule architectures. The system features: (1) tetrahedral silicon centers with cationic charge (+1) as recognition elements, (2) electron-deficient triazine or tetrazine panels for anion-π interactions with halide or tetrafluoroborate anions, (3) rigid aromatic spacers (phenylene or biphenylene) connecting silicon centers to aromatic panels, and (4) tunable substituents (alkyl, aryl, or silyl groups) on silicon to control solubility and capsule stability. The silyl cation's strong Lewis acidity and tetrahedral geometry direct assembly into cubic or tetrahedral capsules that encapsulate anions via cooperative anion-π interactions. This represents a novel extension of onium cation chemistry to silicon-based systems, exploiting the underutilized silyl cation as a supramolecular building block with distinct steric and electronic properties compared to phosphonium or ammonium analogs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_19
synthons.description: A supramolecular tetrahedral capsule formed by four ammonium cations (R₄N⁺) positioned at the vertices of a tetrahedron, with each cation engaging in cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., hexaalkoxy-triphenylene or extended pyrene derivatives). The capsule encapsulates a complementary tetrahedral anion cluster (e.g., BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻, or PF₆⁻) at its core via electrostatic and anion-π interactions with the same aromatic panels. The system exhibits dual recognition: (1) cation-π interactions between the ammonium centers and the π-basic faces of the aromatic walls, and (2) anion-π interactions between the encapsulated anions and the π-acidic edges or polarized centers of the same aromatic systems. This creates a reversible, electrostatically gated capsule suitable for anion sensing or selective encapsulation. The synthon maps to primitives via: (1) electrostatic attraction (cation-π, anion-π), (2) shape complementarity (tetrahedral symmetry), (3) reversible assembly (pH or counterion triggered), (4) aromatic surfaces (π-systems), (5) charged nodes (ammonium cations), (6) encapsulated guests (anions), and (7) directional interactions (tetrahedral coordination).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features four identical arms extending from the central nitrogen, each terminating in a pyridinium or triazine ring that provides strong electron-deficient π-surfaces. These planar aromatic panels arrange in a tetrahedral geometry around the cationic center, creating a cavity that selectively binds anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-) through cooperative anion-π interactions with all four panels simultaneously. The recognition elements include: (1) the permanent positive charge on nitrogen providing electrostatic preorganization, (2) electron-deficient heteroaromatic rings (pyridinium/triazine) with large quadrupole moments favorable for anion binding, (3) tetrahedral symmetry enabling three-dimensional encapsulation, and (4) tunable substituents on the aromatic rings to modulate binding affinity and selectivity. This represents a charge-assisted anion-π capsule where the cationic center both preorganizes the electron-deficient panels and enhances anion binding through electrostatic complementarity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cation (Cp₂Fe⁺) that combines redox-active metallocene chemistry with anion-π interactions. The synthon features a positively charged iron center sandwiched between two cyclopentadienyl rings, creating a tetrahedral-like cationic structure that can engage in anion-π interactions with electron-rich anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) through the π-clouds of the Cp rings. The redox-active nature (Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ couple) adds temporal control, allowing the capsule formation to be switched electrochemically. Recognition elements include: (1) the cationic ferrocenium center, (2) the curved π-surfaces of the Cp rings, (3) electrostatic complementarity for anions, and (4) redox-switchable binding affinity. This system maps to primitives through: positive charge (electrostatic), π-system (dispersion), metal center (coordination/redox), tetrahedral geometry (shape), and reversible redox switching (temporal control).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that function as anion-π acceptors within a capsule framework. The system features a positively charged silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and an empty coordination site or labile ligand, creating a strong electrostatic and polarization-driven interaction with electron-rich π-systems of aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives or electron-deficient heterocycles). The tetrahedral geometry directs assembly into capsule-like structures where multiple silyl cation units are bridged by anion-π interactions with aromatic panels, encapsulating anions or small molecules. Recognition elements include: (1) the σ-hole/electropositive region around the silicon cation, (2) electron-deficient arenes for anion-π interactions, (3) shape-complementary steric bulk to control assembly geometry. This represents an underexplored combination of main-group cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated to two catecholate ligands, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped anion with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The catecholate oxygens provide strong hydrogen-bond acceptors, while the electron-deficient π-system of the gallium-bound catechol engages in complementary anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic systems. This creates a versatile three-point recognition motif: (1) metal coordination geometry (tetrahedral), (2) hydrogen-bond donation to catecholate oxygens, and (3) anion-π stacking with complementary aromatics. The system is chemically realistic, as gallium(III) readily forms stable catecholate complexes, and the electron-withdrawing effect of the metal center enhances the anion-π acceptor capability. This synthon can direct the assembly of capsules, cages, or layered structures through orthogonal interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels to form self-assembled capsule structures. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral ammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or chiral variants like benzyltrimethylammonium) as the cationic recognition element; (2) four electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or pyrazine derivatives) positioned at the vertices of a tetrahedron; (3) directional anion-π interactions between the cationic nitrogen's localized positive charge and the π-acidic surfaces, enhanced by electrostatic complementarity; (4) additional edge-to-face or offset π-π stacking between adjacent aromatic panels to stabilize the capsule walls; (5) tunable cavity size via variation of aromatic linker length; (6) potential for encapsulation of small anions or neutral guests within the cationic-anionic π-assembled cavity; (7) mapping to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), ammonium cation (electrostatic donor), anion-π interaction (non-covalent bond), aromatic π-system (surface), self-assembly (process), encapsulation (function), and modular substitution (tunability).

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a chiral tetrahedral boronate ester anion that functions as a π-acidic cage for cationic guests. The system features a boron center with three oxygen atoms from catechol-like ligands forming a tetrahedral boronate anion [B(OAr)₃]⁻, creating a pronounced electron-deficient cavity. The electron-deficient boron center and aromatic rings create a strong anion-π interaction site for cationic species like ammonium or imidazolium ions. The chiral environment arises from asymmetric substitution on the catechol ligands, enabling enantioselective recognition. Recognition elements include: (1) the tetrahedral boronate anion as an electron-deficient π-acidic cage, (2) electrostatic complementarity between anion and cation, (3) shape-selective cavity from the three aromatic walls, and (4) chiral discrimination through asymmetric ligand substitution. This represents a novel anion-π supramolecular system distinct from previously proposed cation-anion capsules, with potential applications in chiral separation and asymmetric catalysis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a complementary capsule structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a central ammonium cation with four identical aryl-substituted arms, each terminating in an electron-deficient tetrafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl group. These aromatic panels create a concave, electron-deficient surface that selectively binds anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-) through anion-π interactions, while the positively charged ammonium core provides electrostatic complementarity. The tetrahedral geometry enforces a well-defined cavity suitable for anion encapsulation. Recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic attraction between R4N+ and anions, (2) directional anion-π interactions between anions and electron-deficient arenes, (3) van der Waals contacts between aryl panels, and (4) geometric preorganization from the tetrahedral core. This represents a charge-complementary approach to anion binding capsules, distinct from metal-based or hydrogen-bonding systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems, creating a capsule-like assembly. The silylium center acts as a strong Lewis acid with a vacant p-orbital, while the surrounding substituents (typically bulky aryl or alkyl groups) provide steric definition. Electron-deficient arenes (hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanobenzene, or nitroaromatics) serve as π-acidic surfaces that interact with anions (Cl-, Br-, BF4-) through anion-π contacts. The combination of tetrahedral cationic geometry and directional anion-π interactions creates a three-dimensional recognition motif suitable for encapsulation architectures. This system explores the underexplored chemistry of silylium cations in supramolecular contexts, distinct from the already proposed phosphonium, arsonium, and other onium variants.

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on chiral tetrahedral boronate esters that form anion-binding π-acidic cages. The system features a boron center with two oxygen atoms from catechol-like diols and two additional substituents creating a tetrahedral geometry. The electron-deficient boron center and adjacent π-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) create a convergent anion-π binding pocket. This chiral cavity selectively binds anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through cooperative anion-π and Lewis acid interactions, while the chiral periphery enables enantioselective recognition. The synthon demonstrates reversible assembly via dynamic boronate ester formation, allowing temporal control over cage assembly/disassembly through pH or diol exchange.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with two catecholate ligands, creating a bowl-shaped electron-deficient cavity. The gallium center coordinates two bidentate catecholate anions, leaving the metal's Lewis acidic character partially exposed. The catecholate π-systems are electron-rich, but the overall complex carries a negative charge (Ga(cat)₂⁻) and presents a concave, electron-deficient surface due to the gallium's empty p-orbital and the catecholate ring polarization. This synthon can engage in anion-π interactions with complementary cationic or electron-rich guests, while also offering potential for metal coordination at the gallium center and hydrogen bonding via catecholate oxygen atoms. The tetrahedral geometry creates a directional, preorganized cavity suitable for encapsulation of small cations or polar molecules, functioning as a supramolecular capsule building block.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R₃Si⁺) that form anion-binding capsules through cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a silicon-centered cationic core (silylium ion) with three organic substituents (alkyl/aryl groups) and one coordination site that can bind anions. Electron-deficient arenes (e.g., perfluorinated benzene, triazine, or tetrazine rings) are positioned around the cation to create an anion-π binding pocket. The tetrahedral geometry of the silylium cation directs the arene panels into a capsule-like arrangement that can encapsulate halide or oxoanions through multipoint anion-π interactions. This represents an underexplored combination of main-group cationic centers (Group 14) with supramolecular anion recognition motifs, differing from previously proposed pnictogen and chalcogen-based capsules.

synthons.name: chiral_boronic_acid_diol_esterification_synthon
synthons.description: A dynamic covalent synthon based on reversible boronic acid-diol esterification, forming five- or six-membered cyclic boronate esters with stereochemical control. The system comprises an aryl/alkyl boronic acid recognition element (R-B(OH)₂) that selectively binds to 1,2- or 1,3-diols (e.g., sugar derivatives, catechols, or tartaric acid derivatives) in aqueous or organic media. The reversible B-O bond formation creates a covalent yet dynamic linkage with tunable stability via pH, solvent, or substituent effects. The boronate ester can be mapped to primitives: (1) covalent bond formation/cleavage (B-O), (2) directional hydrogen bonding from residual OH groups, (3) tetrahedral geometry at boron providing stereogenicity, (4) π-interactions from aromatic boronic acids, (5) reversible reaction kinetics enabling temporal control, (6) chiral discrimination via diol stereochemistry, and (7) potential for supramolecular assembly through secondary interactions. This synthon is valuable for dynamic combinatorial chemistry, molecular sensing, and chiral resolution.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that engage in dual interaction modes: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged silicon center, and (2) cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives or extended π-systems). The R groups are typically bulky, electron-donating substituents (like tert-butyl or aryl groups) that stabilize the cationic center while providing steric definition. This creates a three-dimensional recognition pocket where an anion (Cl-, BF4-, PF6-) sits at the silicon vertex, while the π-systems from surrounding aromatic panels engage the cation's periphery through non-covalent cation-π contacts. The synthon is modular—varying the π-panels and anion changes the capsule's size and selectivity. It maps to primitives: positive charge (silylium), negative charge (anion), π-system (aromatic panels), tetrahedral geometry, directional electrostatic interactions, and can incorporate temporal elements via redox-switchable silylium generation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-active synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cation (Cp₂Fe⁺) interacting with electron-deficient aromatic systems via anion-π interactions. The cationic ferrocenium center provides a stable, tetrahedral organometallic core with reversible redox properties (Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺), while its positive charge enhances anion binding to electron-deficient π-systems like tetrafluorobenzenes or trinitrobenzenes. This creates a dynamic capsule-like structure where the ferrocenium cation sits at the vertices, coordinating anions through charge-assisted anion-π interactions. The system exhibits dual functionality: (1) supramolecular recognition through geometrically constrained tetrahedral assembly, and (2) temporal redox-switching capability where reduction to neutral ferrocene alters the electrostatic landscape and disassembles the capsule. Recognition elements include: tetrahedral metallocene cation, electron-deficient arenes, and charge-assisted anion-π contacts. Mappable to primitives: positive charge (ferrocenium), π-system (electron-deficient arene), tetrahedral geometry, reversible redox center, directional non-covalent interactions, and dynamic assembly/disassembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon centers bearing cationic silylium (R3Si+) groups that interact with electron-rich aromatic systems via anion-π interactions. The synthon features a central silicon atom with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., tert-butyl or aryl groups) and one cationic silylium site, creating a tetrahedral geometry. The positively charged silicon center acts as an anion-π acceptor, engaging with electron-rich arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons) through non-covalent interactions. This system combines the emerging chemistry of stable silylium cations with supramolecular anion-π recognition, enabling the construction of capsule-like architectures through directional assembly. The recognition elements include: (1) the tetrahedral silylium cation as an electrostatic anchor, (2) electron-deficient π-systems as complementary partners, and (3) steric bulk from substituents that preorganize the assembly. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through charge (cationic silicon), geometry (tetrahedral), polarity (polarized Si⁺ center), aromaticity (π-system partners), connectivity (directional Si⁺···π interaction), conformation (preorganized by bulky groups), and reactivity (electrophilic silicon center).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon-centered cationic species (silylium analogs or silyl-substituted ammonium cations) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems, creating capsule-like architectures. The synthon features a central silicon atom with three organic substituents (alkyl/aryl groups) and one positively charged group (e.g., -N+R3 or -P+R3) to maintain tetrahedral geometry and cationic character. This interacts with π-acidic aromatic rings (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-tetrazine, or 1,3,5-triazine derivatives) through anion-π interactions when paired with appropriate anions (BF4-, PF6-, etc.). The combination creates a directional, charge-assisted recognition motif that can be used to assemble larger cage or capsule structures through multiple such interactions, with potential for encapsulation of small molecules or ions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_salen_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a salen-type Schiff base ligand, where the cationic metal center coordinates to anionic guests through anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic rings of the ligand scaffold. The gallium(III) cation adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry, with the salen ligand providing two imine nitrogens and two phenolate oxygens in a N₂O₂ donor set. The electron-deficient aromatic rings (often substituted with nitro or cyano groups) create π-acidic surfaces that can bind anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.) through anion-π interactions. The overall assembly forms a capsule-like structure where the tetrahedral cation acts as a structural node, and the anion-π interactions provide directional recognition. This synthon combines metal coordination, electrostatic attraction, and anion-π interactions, and can be mapped to the seven primitives: donor (phenolate O, imine N), acceptor (Ga³⁺), positive charge (Ga³⁺), negative charge (anion), hydrophobe (aromatic rings), hydrophile (coordinated anions), and connector (salen backbone).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18_1
synthons.description: A tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) with four aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups) that forms a supramolecular capsule through synergistic anion-π interactions. The positively charged nitrogen center creates an electrostatic field that enhances the electron-deficient character of the aromatic rings, making them strong anion-π acceptors. Four anions (e.g., halides, tetrafluoroborate, or hexafluorophosphate) are each bound to the face of one aromatic panel via anion-π interactions, while the tetrahedral geometry directs the arms to create a closed, capsule-like structure. This system employs molecular recognition through electrostatic complementarity and aromatic surface interactions, mapping to the primitives of shape (tetrahedral), electrostatics (cation/anion), and aromatic surface (π-system).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features four cationic ammonium centers at the vertices of a tetrahedron, each connected to electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetracyanobenzene, or perfluorinated arenes) that serve as anion-binding π-acidic surfaces. These panels arrange to create a cavity where anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-, PF6-) can be encapsulated through multiple anion-π interactions. The recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic attraction between ammonium cations and anions, (2) anion-π interactions between electron-deficient aromatics and anions, (3) potential C-H···anion hydrogen bonds from alkyl/aryl groups on ammonium, and (4) geometric complementarity from the tetrahedral framework. This represents a distinct variation from previously proposed cation-anion-π capsules by using the fundamental ammonium cation instead of heavier pnictogen or chalcogen analogs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like assembly. The system features: (1) a positively charged silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl groups) to stabilize the silylium cation, (2) four electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene or s-triazine derivatives) positioned around the cation via anion-π interactions with the formally empty p-orbital on silicon, and (3) edge-to-edge halogen bonding or CH-π interactions between the arene panels to complete the capsule walls. This creates a tetrahedral coordination environment where the silylium cation acts as both a structural node and an anion-π acceptor—an unusual reversal of typical cation-π roles. The synthon is chemically realistic as silylium cations are known strong Lewis acids, and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatics are well-established. Recognition elements include the electrostatic anion-π interaction, shape complementarity of tetrahedral cation with triangular arene panels, and secondary interactions between panel edges. This represents an underexplored combination of main-group cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a central ammonium cation with four aromatic arms (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives) that are electron-deficient, creating convergent anion-binding sites. Anions (e.g., Cl-, Br-, NO3-) are held above the aromatic panels via anion-π interactions, while the cationic center provides electrostatic complementarity. The tetrahedral geometry organizes four aromatic panels into a pseudo-capsule that can encapsulate anions through a combination of electrostatic and anion-π interactions. This represents a distinct variation from the previously proposed pnictogen, chalcogen, and iodonium capsules, utilizing the ubiquitous ammonium cation with specifically engineered π-acidic surfaces.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a complementary capsule structure with electron-deficient aromatic systems through anion-π interactions. The system features a central nitrogen atom with four organic substituents (typically aryl or alkyl groups) creating a tetrahedral cationic core. This cation pairs with planar, electron-deficient anions (such as tetracyanobenzene derivatives or nitroaromatics) where the anion's π-system interacts with the cationic center. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium cation creates a three-dimensional binding pocket, while the planar anion provides a complementary π-surface. Recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient aromatic system and the cationic nitrogen, (3) potential C-H···π interactions from ammonium substituents, and (4) shape complementarity between tetrahedral cation and planar anion. This synthon can be mapped to the seven primitives through charge (cation/anion), geometry (tetrahedral/planar), and directional non-covalent interactions, enabling the design of self-assembled capsules and porous materials.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that engage in dual non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction to anions (Cl-, BF4-, etc.) and (2) anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or perfluorinated pyridine derivatives). The system forms a capsule-like architecture where the silylium cation sits at the vertices of a tetrahedron, with each cationic silicon center coordinating to an anion that is simultaneously sandwiched between two electron-poor arene rings from adjacent panels. This creates a 3D network stabilized by cooperative cation-anion and anion-π interactions. The silylium cation's strong Lewis acidity and tetrahedral geometry direct the assembly, while the electron-deficient π-systems provide complementary anion binding sites. This synthon is chemically realistic, as silylium ions are known stable species in non-coordinating solvents, and anion-π interactions with fluorinated aromatics are well-documented. It maps to primitives: positive charge (silylium), negative charge (anion), π-system (electron-deficient arene), tetrahedral geometry, and directional electrostatic/π interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that function as anion-π acceptors and capsule-forming building blocks. The system features: (1) a positively charged silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) creating a tetrahedral geometry, (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or cyanophenyl groups) positioned on the substituents to provide anion-π interaction sites, (3) complementary anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or carboxylates) that engage in both electrostatic binding to the Si⁺ center and anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient arenes, and (4) self-assembly into dimeric or tetrameric capsule structures through additional weak interactions (C–H···π, dispersion forces). The silicon cation's Lewis acidity and tetrahedral geometry direct predictable 3D assembly, while the appended π-acidic faces create cooperative binding pockets for anions, making this a novel supramolecular synthon for anion encapsulation and coordination-driven self-assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germonium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that function as anion-π acceptors within self-assembled capsule architectures. The germanium(IV) center bears four organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) creating a permanent cationic charge with a tetrahedral geometry. This geometry directs the cation's faces toward electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., pyrene, perylene diimide derivatives) that serve as curved walls of a supramolecular capsule. The anion-π interaction occurs between the electron-deficient π-surface of the germonium cation's substituent aromatic rings (when aryl-substituted) or the cation's electrostatic field and an encapsulated anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, PF₆⁻). The synthon integrates: (1) electrostatic attraction (cation-anion), (2) anion-π interaction, (3) hydrophobic effects within the capsule cavity, and (4) geometric complementarity for assembly. This represents a novel extension of onium chemistry into Group 14, exploiting germanium's larger covalent radius and polarizability compared to carbon, silicon, or tin, which modulates the strength and directionality of the supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) centers functionalized with halogen-bond donor groups (iodo- or bromo-triazolyl) that form halogen bonds with anions, while simultaneously engaging in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or s-triazine rings). The germanium center provides a rigid tetrahedral scaffold that preorganizes four halogen-bond donor arms and four electron-deficient aromatic surfaces, creating a convergent binding pocket capable of encapsulating spherical anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻) via synergistic halogen bonding and anion-π interactions. This represents a novel extension of tetrahedral cation-anion-π capsules into main-group element chemistry with dual noncovalent interaction modes.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_arene_anion_π_capsule_synthon_18
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) centers coordinated to electron-deficient arene ligands (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives) that create a convergent anion-π binding pocket. Each gallium center is chelated by two β-diketonate or catecholate ligands, leaving one coordination site occupied by a π-acidic arene oriented inward to form the walls of a tetrahedral capsule. The assembly selectively encapsulates anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) via cooperative anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient arene faces. The synthon features: (1) tetrahedral metal geometry (Ga³⁺), (2) π-acidic recognition surfaces, (3) convergent electrostatic fields for anion binding, (4) chelate-enforced preorganization, (5) size-selective encapsulation, (6) potential for redox activity via Ga(III)/Ga(II), and (7) modular ligand tuning for anion affinity. This represents an underexplored combination of group 13 metal coordination and anion-π supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetravalent germanium(IV) centers bearing three organic substituents and one halogen (Cl, Br, or I) that can undergo heterolytic cleavage to generate a germanium halonium cation (R₃Ge–X⁺). This cationic center acts as a strong halogen bond donor to anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) while the three organic arms (e.g., phenyl, naphthyl, or extended π-systems) provide curved, electron-rich π-surfaces. The combination creates a tetrahedral capsule-like environment where the anion is halogen-bonded at the center and surrounded by three aromatic panels that engage in additional anion–π interactions and edge-to-face π-stacking between adjacent arms. This synthon is modular: the halogen can be tuned for bond strength, the π-arms for cavity size and electron density, and the anion for encapsulation selectivity. It maps to primitives: (1) germanium halonium as electrophile, (2) anion as nucleophile, (3) halogen bond as directional interaction, (4) anion–π as stabilizing interaction, (5) π–π stacking between arms, (6) tetrahedral geometry defining a cavity, (7) reversible formation of the halonium species under mild conditions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_19_1

The cationic center provides strong electrostatic attraction, while the extended aromatic arms engage in multiple cooperative interactions: (1) anion-π interactions between electron-deficient regions of the aromatic systems and an anionic guest (e.g., Cl-, BF4-, or a carboxylate), (2) edge-to-face or offset π-π stacking between arms of adjacent synthons to form capsule-like dimeric or tetrameric assemblies, and (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from the aromatic hydrogens. The tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the arms into a convergent, bowl-like structure that can encapsulate an anion, making it a building block for self-assembled anion-binding capsules or porous frameworks. This system is chemically robust, synthetically accessible via quaternization, and maps cleanly to the seven primitives through its defined geometry, electrostatic and dispersion interactions, and programmable assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) germonium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that form electrostatic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a self-assembled capsule architecture. The germonium center provides a strong, directional positive charge (σ-hole enhanced by heavy atom polarizability), while fluorinated pyrazine or triazine rings serve as the electron-deficient π-surfaces. The system exhibits complementary tetrahedral symmetry where four germonium cations position themselves at the vertices of a tetrahedron, each engaging in anion-π interactions with the faces of a tetrahedral arrangement of aromatic panels, encapsulating small anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻) or neutral guests in the central cavity. This represents an underexplored heavy pnictogen analog to phosphonium/arsonium systems, with germanium offering distinct polarizability, coordination geometry, and Lewis acidity compared to lighter group 14 elements or group 15 onium ions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_triflate_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) triflate complexes that form anion-π capsules through cooperative interactions. The system features Ga³⁺ centers coordinated by three trifluoromethanesulfonate (triflate) anions and one aromatic N-donor ligand (e.g., pyridine derivative), creating a cationic tetrahedral metal center. The electron-deficient triflate anions engage in anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., hexaalkoxytriphenylene) that serve as capsule walls. The tetrahedral geometry directs three triflates outward to interact with three different aromatic panels, while the pyridine ligand provides structural control and potential for further functionalization. This creates a reversible, self-assembled capsule capable of encapsulating small guest molecules through a combination of coordinative, electrostatic, and anion-π interactions. The gallium(III) center offers Lewis acidity, redox inactivity, and stable tetrahedral geometry, while the triflate anions provide both coordinating ability and strong anion-π propensity due to their delocalized negative charge and electron-withdrawing trifluoromethyl groups.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3

The system consists of a cationic silicon center with three bulky aromatic substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) that create a pre-organized, electron-deficient cavity. The fourth position is occupied by a labile ligand (e.g., solvent or weakly coordinating anion) that can be displaced. It represents an underexplored combination of main-group cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_1

The cationic vertices engage in anion-π interactions with tetrahedral anions (e.g., ClO4-, BF4-) positioned at the capsule center, while the aromatic arms provide π-surfaces for additional edge-to-face or offset π-stacking. synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14

The system features a tetrahedral germanium cation coordinated to three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl or alkyl groups) and one labile site that can bind anions (Cl-, Br-, BF4-). The aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) are positioned via rigid linkers to create a partial capsule-like structure that encapsulates the anion through cooperative anion-π and electrostatic interactions. This creates a reversible, tunable host-guest system where both the germanium Lewis acidity and the π-acidity of the panels can be modulated by substituent effects.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10

The synthon features a silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl or t-butyl groups) to stabilize the highly electrophilic silylium cation, while the fourth coordination site is occupied by a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., B(C6F5)4- or CB11H12-). The tetrahedral geometry directs these interactions in three-dimensional space, enabling the formation of capsule-like assemblies when combined with complementary π-donor building blocks. This represents an underexplored variation of onium-type cations in supramolecular chemistry, leveraging silicon's unique electropositive character and tetrahedral coordination preference.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R3Si+) that function as anion-π capsule-forming units. synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3

The catecholate oxygens provide hydrogen-bond acceptor sites, while the electron-deficient π-system of the gallium-catecholate complex enables strong anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic guests. The tetrahedral geometry creates a directional, preorganized cavity suitable for encapsulating planar cationic or π-rich species through a combination of electrostatic, anion-π, and weak coordinative interactions. synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon

The cationic iron center provides redox-active properties, while the tetrahedral arrangement of four electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or cyanophenyl derivatives) creates a cavity for anion binding via anion-π interactions. The synthon combines redox-active metallocene chemistry with supramolecular anion recognition, where the positively charged ferrocenium center enhances the electron deficiency of the aromatic panels, strengthening anion binding. This system can be mapped to the seven primitives through: (1) electrostatic complementarity between cation and anion, (2) shape complementarity of tetrahedral capsule, (3) redox-switchable binding affinity, (4) directional anion-π interactions, (5) conformational flexibility of aromatic panels, (6) cooperative binding within the capsule, and (7) potential for allosteric regulation via redox state changes.

The system consists of a boron atom (B) covalently bonded to two oxygen atoms from a chiral 1,2-diol (e.g., (R,R)- or (S,S)-1,2-diphenyl-1,2-ethanediol) forming five-membered boronate ester rings, with the remaining coordination sites occupied by electron-deficient aromatic groups (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or 1,3,5-triazine) oriented to create a π-acidic pocket. This chiral tetrahedral arrangement generates a preorganized cavity capable of binding anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through synergistic anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient arenes and electrostatic stabilization from the partial positive charge on boron. The chiral diol ligands impart stereoselective anion recognition. Recognition elements: covalent B–O bonds (boronate ester formation), directional anion-π interactions (anion to electron-deficient π-system), and chiral steric complementarity. Mappable to primitives: (1) tetrahedral geometry at boron, (2) π-acidic surfaces as recognition panels, (3) anion as guest, (4) chiral environment for enantioselectivity, (5) reversible boronate ester formation (dynamic covalent chemistry), (6) electrostatic complementarity, (7) preorganized cavity from rigid diol backbone.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_11

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_19_2

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18_2

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon_2

Recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic attraction between ferrocenium cation and anions, (2) anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes, (3) potential cation-π interactions with electron-rich systems, and (4) redox-dependent binding affinity changes. The tetrahedral arrangement allows for three-dimensional capsule formation with appropriate bridging ligands. This synthon maps to primitives through: electron-deficient π-systems (acceptor), ferrocenium redox center (redox-active), directional tetrahedral geometry (structural), and tunable binding through substituents on cyclopentadienyl rings.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated to two catecholate ligands, creating a bowl-shaped electron-deficient cavity with Lewis acidic character. The system features: (1) a Ga(III) center with formal +3 charge, (2) two ortho-dihydroxybenzene (catechol) ligands forming five-membered chelate rings, (3) an overall anionic charge (typically [Ga(cat)₂]⁻), (4) a rigid tetrahedral geometry that creates a concave π-surface. This electron-deficient cavity acts as an anion-π receptor, specifically binding anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through cooperative electrostatic and orbital interactions. The gallium catecholate motif is chemically stable, redox-inert, and synthetically accessible via gallium trihalides and catechol derivatives. Recognition elements include: metal-ligand coordination bonds (Ga-O), anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic rings, potential C-H···anion hydrogen bonds from catechol protons, and electrostatic complementarity between the anionic capsule and guest anions. This represents an underexplored variation of metal-catecholate capsules using a Group 13 metal with distinct Lewis acidity and cavity dimensions compared to boron analogues.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_41
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) complex with a tetradentate Schiff base ligand that forms a cationic capsule capable of anion-π interactions. The system features: (1) a Ga³⁺ center with tetrahedral geometry, (2) a rigid, bowl-shaped Schiff base cavity formed by salicylaldimine moieties, (3) cationic charge localized on the metal center, (4) electron-deficient aromatic panels in the ligand framework that provide anion-π recognition sites, (5) self-assembly into dimeric capsules via π-stacking of the aromatic panels, (6) encapsulation of anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through cooperative anion-π interactions from multiple electron-deficient aromatic rings, and (7) tunable cavity size via substituents on the aromatic rings. This represents a novel metal-organic capsule system distinct from previously proposed pnictogen-based capsules, exploiting the Lewis acidity and stable coordination geometry of gallium(III) for supramolecular anion recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) halonium cations (GeX₃⁺, where X = Cl, Br, I) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a self-assembled capsule architecture. The germanium center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with three halogens and one cationic site, creating a directional electrostatic field. Electron-deficient hexafluorobenzene or tetracyanobenzene derivatives serve as π-acidic panels that interact with anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) via anion-π contacts. The combination of GeX₃⁺ vertices and aromatic panels leads to a tetrahedral capsule that encapsulates anions through cooperative halogen bonding (from Ge-bound halogens) and anion-π interactions. This represents an underexplored combination of p-block cation geometry, halogen bonding, and anion-π recognition in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_19_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular tetrahedral capsule formed by four ammonium cations (R₄N⁺) positioned at the vertices of a tetrahedron, with each cation engaging in cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene derivatives) that form the capsule faces. The interior cavity is stabilized by convergent anion-π interactions with a centrally encapsulated polyatomic anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻, or PF₆⁻). The system employs a combination of electrostatic cation-anion attraction, directional cation-π contacts between the ammonium groups and the π-basic arene panels, and anion-π interactions between the encapsulated anion and the electron-deficient centers of polarized arenes. This creates a well-defined, charge-assisted supramolecular assembly with potential for guest encapsulation and molecular recognition.

synthons.name: temporal_photoresponsive_azobenzene_anion_π_switch_synthon
synthons.description: A photochromic molecular system based on azobenzene derivatives that reversibly switches between trans and cis configurations upon irradiation with specific wavelengths (UV for trans→cis, visible/thermal for cis→trans). The trans isomer features extended π-conjugation with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or pyridine) that create a strong anion-π binding site for anions like chloride, nitrate, or carboxylates. Upon photoisomerization to the cis form, the π-system becomes distorted and less electron-deficient, dramatically reducing anion-π affinity. This creates a temporal, light-controlled anion binding/release cycle. Recognition elements include: (1) photoresponsive azobenzene core, (2) electron-deficient arenes for anion-π interactions, (3) optional peripheral groups for secondary stabilization (halogen bonds, H-bonds). The system maps to primitives through its switchable binding geometry (shape), photonic input (energy), reversible binding (information), and programmable anion affinity (property).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that function as anion-binding hosts through electrostatic and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The synthon consists of a central, positively charged silicon atom with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and one labile site (or coordination vacancy) that electrostatically attracts an anion (Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻, etc.). The substituents are designed to incorporate electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl, or triazine rings) that provide additional anion-π stabilization. The overall tetrahedral geometry organizes the π-deficient faces into a convergent, capsule-like binding pocket, enabling cooperative anion recognition. This system is chemically realistic, drawing from known silyl cation stability in weakly coordinating anions and the established principles of anion-π interactions in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-active capsule synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cation (Cp₂Fe⁺) interacting with electron-rich aromatic anions via anion-π interactions. The system features: (1) tetrahedral ferrocenium cation as the cationic vertex with redox-switchable properties, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., triazine or perfluorinated arenes) that undergo anion-π interactions with halide or carboxylate anions, (3) flexible alkyl linkers connecting the ferrocenium centers to aromatic panels, enabling capsule formation, and (4) redox-switchable encapsulation behavior where oxidation state changes (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺) modulate capsule assembly/disassembly. This represents a temporal-supramolecular hybrid system with electrochemically controlled guest binding/release capabilities.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) centers bearing three bulky aryl groups and one labile ligand (e.g., Cl, OTf) that can dissociate to form a highly electrophilic silylium cation (R3Si+). The cationic silicon center is stabilized by anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., perfluorinated benzene, cyanobenzene) arranged in a complementary capsule-like geometry. The three aryl substituents on silicon provide steric bulk and preorganization, while the positive charge on silicon engages in strong, directional anion-π contacts with surrounding π-acidic surfaces, creating a reversible, charge-assisted assembly motif. This synthon enables the construction of charged, shape-persistent capsules or frameworks via self-assembly, combining silylium cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organogermanium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that function as anion-π capsule-forming units. The germanium center, with its larger covalent radius compared to silicon and carbon, creates a more diffuse positive charge that enhances both electrostatic and orbital interactions with anions. The system employs strategically positioned electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine) on the organic substituents (R), which preorganize via intramolecular interactions to form a cavity. This cavity exhibits cooperative anion binding through a combination of (1) direct electrostatic attraction to the cationic germanium center, (2) anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient arenes, and (3) secondary C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from the substituent alkyl/aryl groups. The synthon is chemically realistic, as tetraalkylgermonium salts are known stable compounds, and the design leverages the emerging field of p-block element cations in supramolecular anion recognition. It can be mapped to the seven primitives: cation (Ge⁺), anion (guest), π-system (electron-deficient arenes), hydrogen bond donor (C–H), tetrahedral geometry, preorganized cavity (capsule), and cooperative binding.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that function as anion-π acceptors within a capsule framework. The system features: (1) a positively charged silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) creating a tetrahedral geometry, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or triazine rings) positioned around the cation to form anion-π interactions with incoming anions, (3) flexible linkers connecting the panels to create a dynamic capsule that can encapsulate anions of varying sizes. The silyl cation's strong Lewis acidity and tetrahedral geometry direct anion binding in a spatially defined manner, while the surrounding π-acidic panels provide secondary stabilization through anion-π interactions. This creates a cooperative recognition motif where the anion is sandwiched between the cationic silicon center and electron-deficient π-systems. The synthon is chemically realistic as silyl cations are known persistent species in non-nucleophilic media, and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatics are well-documented. This system maps to primitives: positive charge (cation), negative charge (anion), π-system (aromatic panels), tetrahedral geometry, directional interactions (electrostatic + anion-π), and dynamic encapsulation (supramolecular assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features four cationic ammonium vertices connected to electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetracyanobenzene, or perfluorinated arenes) via flexible alkyl or aryl linkers. These aromatic panels engage in multiple, directional anion-π interactions with a central polyatomic anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or ClO4-), creating a three-dimensional encapsulation motif. The recognition elements include: (1) the cationic ammonium centers for electrostatic pre-organization, (2) electron-deficient π-systems as anion-binding sites, and (3) a geometrically matched polyatomic anion. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through its defined geometry (tetrahedral), electrostatic and dispersion-driven interactions, and programmable assembly into larger supramolecular architectures.

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on chiral tetrahedral boronate esters that form anion-binding cages through synergistic anion-π and B-O coordination interactions. The system features a rigid, C3-symmetric tris-boronate ester scaffold with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) positioned to create a convergent anion-binding pocket. The tetrahedral boron centers act as Lewis acidic sites for weak coordination to anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻), while the electron-deficient π-surfaces provide additional stabilization via anion-π interactions. Chirality is introduced through binaphthyl or tartrate-derived linkers, enabling enantioselective anion recognition. The synthon maps to primitives as: (1) tetrahedral boron as recognition site, (2) electron-deficient arenes as π-acidic surfaces, (3) convergent cavity as structural motif, (4) anion as binding partner, (5) chiral environment for stereoselectivity, (6) reversible B-O coordination for dynamic assembly, and (7) tunable electronics via aromatic substitution.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R3Si+) that act as cationic vertices, interacting with electron-rich aromatic panels through anion-π interactions with encapsulated anions. The system features: (1) R3Si+ cationic centers (where R = alkyl/aryl groups) with strong Lewis acidity and tetrahedral geometry, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, cyanuric acid derivatives) that provide anion-binding sites via anion-π interactions, (3) encapsulated anions (Cl-, Br-, BF4-, PF6-) that bridge between cationic silicon vertices and aromatic panels, (4) flexible organic linkers connecting vertices to form capsule-like architectures. This represents an underexplored silicon-based analog of phosphonium/arsonium capsule systems, with silicon's larger atomic radius and different orbital characteristics offering distinct electronic properties and anion affinity. The synthon maps to primitives: vertices (Si+ centers), edges (linkers), faces (aromatic panels), containers (capsule), recognition (anion-π + electrostatic), reactivity (anion exchange sites), and dynamics (capsule breathing/guest exchange).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) halonium cations (GeX₃⁺, where X = Cl, Br, I) that function as anion-π capsule-forming units. The germanium center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with three halogens and one cationic site, creating a strong electrostatic and σ-hole donor surface. This cationic face engages in cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, cyanobenzene derivatives) arranged in a complementary geometry. The assembly forms a dynamic capsule capable of encapsulating small anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through a combination of electrostatic attraction, halogen bonding (from Ge-bound halogens), and anion-π interactions. The germanium halonium motif provides enhanced Lewis acidity and polarizability compared to lighter congeners, allowing tunable capsule stability and selectivity based on halogen identity and aromatic panel electronics.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) centers functionalized with halogen-bond donor groups (iodo- or bromo-triazolyl) that form a cationic capsule framework through halogen bonding to electron-rich arenes. The germanium center provides tetrahedral geometry, while the halogen-bond donors (C–I/Br···π) create directional interactions with anion-coordinating π-systems (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or electron-deficient heterocycles). This creates a cationic capsule capable of encapsulating anions via synergistic anion–π interactions within the electron-deficient cavity. The system combines p-block tetrahedral geometry (Ge), halogen bonding (I/Br), and anion–π interactions in a single supramolecular assembly, offering orthogonal recognition elements for anion binding and sensing applications.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_13
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating self-assembled capsule architectures. The system features: (1) tetrahedral silicon centers with cationic charge (+1) on silicon, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, cyanuric acid derivatives, or perfluorinated pyridines) attached via rigid linkers, (3) anion binding sites through anion-π interactions between the cationic silicon center's electrostatic field and π-acidic surfaces, and (4) self-complementary geometry leading to dimeric or higher-order capsule formation. The silylium cation provides strong electrophilicity and directionality, while the electron-deficient aromatics offer tunable π-acidity. This represents a novel combination of main-group cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π recognition, distinct from previously proposed phosphonium, arsonium, or iodonium systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_arene_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) cations coordinated to three arene ligands (e.g., mesitylene or hexamethylbenzene) with a fourth coordination site occupied by a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., BF₄⁻ or PF₆⁻). The cationic Ga(III) center exhibits strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene or s-triazine derivatives) that serve as the capsule walls. The synthon combines (1) metal-arene coordination (Ga-η⁶-arene), (2) electrostatic cation-anion pairing, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-poor π-systems, and (4) van der Waals/CH-π contacts between the methyl groups of the arene ligands and adjacent aromatic panels. This creates a well-defined, charge-assisted tetrahedral building block that can assemble into dimeric or tetrahedral capsules via complementary anion-π and π-π stacking interactions, with potential for guest encapsulation of small neutral molecules or ions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-active synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cations (Cp₂Fe⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating dynamic redox-responsive capsules.
