The system features: (1) tetrahedral ferrocenium cations as redox-switchable cationic vertices, (2) electron-deficient triazine or tetrazine panels as anion-π acceptors, (3) halide or tetrafluoroborate anions as guests that bridge between ferrocenium centers via anion-π interactions, (4) redox-triggered assembly/disassembly through ferrocene/ferrocenium interconversion, (5) tunable cavity size via substituted cyclopentadienyl ligands, (6) orthogonal metal coordination sites at panel edges for hierarchical assembly, and (7) photoredox switching capability. This combines metallocenium chemistry, anion-π interactions, and redox-responsive supramolecular assembly in an underexplored region of chemical space.

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on chiral tetrahedral boronate esters that form anion-binding cages through synergistic anion-π and B-O coordination interactions. The system features a boronate ester core (R-B(OR')₂) with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or triazine) positioned ortho to the boron center, creating a preorganized pocket for anion binding. The tetrahedral geometry of boron combined with chiral diols (like binaphthol or tartrate derivatives) induces helical chirality. Anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) are captured through: (1) anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes, (2) Lewis acidic interaction with the boron empty p-orbital, and (3) hydrogen bonding from ester alkoxy groups. This creates a reversible, stereoselective capsule capable of chiral recognition and anion transport applications.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating self-assembled capsule architectures. The system features: (1) cationic silicon centers with strong Lewis acidity and tetrahedral geometry, (2) electron-deficient triazine or tetrafluorobenzene panels for anion-π interactions with halide or tetrafluoroborate anions, (3) rigid spacers (alkynyl or phenyl bridges) connecting silicon centers to aromatic panels, and (4) tunable cavity size via spacer length. Recognition elements include electrostatic cation-anion attraction, directional anion-π interactions (anion positioned above aromatic centroid), and van der Waals complementarity. This represents an underexplored silicon-based analog of phosphonium/arsonium capsule systems with distinct reactivity and coordination geometry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_switch_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-switchable synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cation (Fc+) engaging in simultaneous anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems and redox-dependent conformational switching. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral ferrocenium cation center (Fe³⁺ sandwiched between two cyclopentadienyl rings with tetrahedral distortion via substituents), (2) electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, trinitrobenzene, or perfluorinated porphyrin derivatives) positioned to accept π-electron density from the cationic Fc+ through anion-π-like interactions (cationic metal center to electron-deficient π-system), (3) redox-switchable behavior where reduction to neutral ferrocene (Fe²⁺) collapses the anion-π interaction and alters capsule geometry, and (4) auxiliary interactions (C-H···anion, electrostatic) that stabilize the assembled structure. This represents a rare example of redox-switchable metallocenium-based supramolecular capsules with potential applications in stimuli-responsive guest encapsulation and electron-transfer catalysis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_15
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that engage in dual non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged silicon center, and (2) anion-π interactions between the bound anion and electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or cyanurated pyridines) positioned around the silicon center. The silicon's tetrahedral geometry organizes four aromatic faces into a partial capsule-like structure that can selectively encapsulate anions like Cl-, BF4-, or PF6- through cooperative binding. The silylium center acts as a strong Lewis acid, while the electron-deficient π-systems provide secondary stabilization via anion-π contacts, creating a synergistic recognition motif for anion encapsulation in non-coordinating solvents.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetravalent germanium cations (R₃Ge⁺ or R₂Ge²⁺ derivatives) that form cationic vertices capable of engaging in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The germanium center's tetrahedral geometry directs four arms: three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) for solubility and steric control, and one labile site (or coordination site) that can bind an anion or solvent. The cationic charge on germanium enhances the electron‑deficiency of attached π‑systems (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, triazine rings), turning them into strong anion‑π acceptors. Multiple such units can self‑assemble with complementary anionic guests (Cl⁻, BF₄⁻, etc.) and π‑deficient panels to form dimeric or tetrahedral capsules. The germanium‑centered cation offers a heavier congener of silicon and carbon analogues, with larger covalent radius and more polarizable Ge–C bonds, potentially giving stronger dispersion contributions and adaptable geometry. Recognition elements: (1) tetrahedral Ge⁺ cation (electrostatic, σ‑hole), (2) anion‑π interactions between the anion and electron‑deficient arenes on the arms, (3) possible Ge···X (X = O, N) secondary coordination, (4) π‑π stacking of electron‑poor panels, (5) hydrophobic packing of organic substituents. Mappable to primitives: donor/acceptor (Ge⁺ as acceptor, anion as donor to π‑system), charged/neutral, container (capsule), directional (tetrahedral), reversible (dynamic coordination at Ge), redox‑active (Ge⁴⁺/Ge²⁺ possible), and photoresponsive (aryl groups can be photoactive).

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular assembly based on chiral tetrahedral boronate esters that form anion-binding cages through synergistic anion-π and B-O coordination interactions. The system consists of a chiral 1,2-diol-derived boronate ester with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or cyanophenyl groups) positioned ortho to the boron center. The tetrahedral boron acts as a Lewis acidic site that can coordinate anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) while the electron-deficient π-surfaces provide additional anion-π stabilization. The chirality induces helical stacking of multiple units into a cage-like structure with defined cavities (approximately 5-7 Å diameter). Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral boron with vacant p-orbital for anion coordination, (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings for anion-π interactions, (3) chiral diol backbone enforcing specific helicity, and (4) peripheral substituents controlling cavity size and solubility. This represents a novel supramolecular synthon combining chiral induction, anion recognition, and cage formation through orthogonal interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_tris(β-diketonate)_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated to three β-diketone ligands, creating a neutral, bowl-shaped complex with a Lewis acidic metal center and electron-deficient π-surfaces. The three β-diketone arms form a C3-symmetric cavity with convergent carbonyl groups and electron-poor arene rings. This synthon acts as an anion-π receptor capsule, where the tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the ligands to create a binding pocket that can encapsulate spherical anions (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻) through cooperative anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic rings and Lewis acid coordination to the exposed gallium center. The β-diketone units provide additional hydrogen-bond acceptor sites at their carbonyl oxygens for secondary interactions. This represents a distinct metal-organic capsule synthon differing from previous entries by using a hard Lewis acid metal (Ga³⁺) with O₆ coordination sphere and chelating β-diketone ligands, creating a neutral yet highly electrophilic cavity for anion recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_32
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) germonium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that form encapsulation complexes with anions through a combination of electrostatic cation-anion attraction and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features rigid tetrahedral germanium centers (often with aryl substituents like phenyl or pentafluorophenyl) that position four electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, triazine, or pyridine N-oxide) to create a convergent binding pocket. This pocket selectively binds anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻) through cooperative interactions: (1) direct electrostatic interaction with the positively charged germanium center, (2) multiple anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient π-systems, and (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from substituents. The tetrahedral geometry creates a semi-enclosed 'capsule-like' environment that enhances anion binding affinity and selectivity. This synthon is chemically reasonable as organogermanium(IV) cations are known stable species, and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatics are well-documented. It maps to primitives through: electrostatic (cation-anion), dispersion (π-system organization), shape (tetrahedral convergence), and recognition (size/shape complementary binding).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_16
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that engage in dual interactions: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged silicon center, and (2) simultaneous cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives or extended π-systems). The system forms a capsule-like architecture where the silylium cation acts as a tetrahedral vertex, coordinating an anion at one face while its organic substituents (typically aryl groups) participate in π-stacking with complementary aromatic walls. This creates a three-dimensional recognition motif useful for anion encapsulation and selective binding. The silylium cation's strong Lewis acidity enhances anion affinity, while the aryl substituents provide geometric control through preorganized π-surfaces. This synthon combines p-block cation chemistry with supramolecular π-interactions, offering a route to tunable, charge-assisted capsules for anion recognition and separation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-active synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cation (Cp₂Fe⁺) that forms anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces, creating a dynamic capsule-like structure. The system features: (1) ferrocenium cation as the tetrahedral redox-active center, (2) electron-deficient perfluorinated arenes (hexafluorobenzene or decafluorobiphenyl) as π-acidic surfaces, (3) electrostatic anion-π interactions between the positively charged iron center and electron-rich regions of the arenes, (4) redox-switchable binding affinity (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ couple modulates interaction strength), (5) tetrahedral geometry enabling three-dimensional capsule assembly, (6) potential for encapsulation of small anions or neutral molecules, and (7) temporal control via electrochemical switching. This combines metallocenium chemistry with supramolecular anion-π interactions in a redox-responsive architecture.

synthons.name: chiral_phosphine_oxide_anion_π_cage_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a chiral phosphine oxide scaffold that forms an anion-binding cage through a combination of anion-π interactions and hydrogen bonding. The system features a rigid, C3-symmetric tris(phosphine oxide) with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) positioned to create a convergent anion-binding pocket. The P=O groups provide strong hydrogen bond acceptors to preorganize the structure and interact with cationic co-guest species. This chiral cage selectively binds tetrahedral anions (e.g., phosphate, sulfate) through multipoint anion-π contacts while the chirality enables enantioselective recognition of chiral anions or ion pairs. The synthon maps to primitives through: (1) electron-deficient π-systems (anion-π donors), (2) P=O hydrogen bond acceptors, (3) rigid aromatic spacers (structural elements), (4) chiral centers (stereochemical information), (5) convergent binding pocket (preorganization), (6) anion binding sites (electrostatic recognition), and (7) potential for co-guest inclusion (ternary complex formation).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_17
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like assembly. The system features: (1) a central silicon atom with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., tert-butyl or aryl groups) and a formally empty p-orbital, creating a strong Lewis acidic site; (2) four electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetrafluoropyrimidine, or 1,3,5-triazine derivatives) positioned tetrahedrally around the cation; (3) anion-π interactions between the cationic silicon center (through its δ+ character and accessible electrostatic potential) and the π-faces of the arenes; (4) additional dispersion interactions between the organic substituents on silicon and the arene panels that stabilize the capsule geometry. This represents an underexplored combination of main-group cation chemistry with anion-π interactions, distinct from the previously proposed phosphonium, arsonium, and iodonium analogues.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_16
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraalkylammonium cations (R₄N⁺) with four identical alkyl chains (C₄-C₆) that position the cationic nitrogen at the center of a tetrahedron, interacting with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-triazine derivatives) through cooperative anion-π interactions. The system forms a self-assembled capsule where four electron-deficient aromatic panels (arranged tetrahedrally) encapsulate a central anion (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) via anion-π interactions, while the tetrahedral ammonium cations occupy the vertices, interacting with the π-systems through electrostatic cation-π contacts. The recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral geometry of R₄N⁺ for directional assembly, (2) electron-deficient π-systems for strong anion binding, (3) complementary electrostatic interactions (cation-π and anion-π), and (4) van der Waals contacts from alkyl chains. This represents a charge-assisted supramolecular capsule with dual cation-π and anion-π recognition, distinct from previously proposed pnictogen/oxonium-based capsules. The seven primitives map as: atoms (N, C, H, halogen), bonds (covalent C-N, C-C; non-covalent electrostatic, anion-π, cation-π), angles (tetrahedral ~109.5°), torsions (alkyl chain conformers), charges (+1 on N, -1 on anion, partial charges on π-system), rings (aromatic triazine/benzene), and motifs (tetrahedral capsule assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a complementary anion-π interaction capsule with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The synthon features a central nitrogen atom with four organic substituents (preferably aryl or alkyl groups with varying electron-withdrawing/donating properties) arranged tetrahedrally, creating a cationic center. This cation engages in cooperative anion-π interactions with tetrahedral anionic guests (such as perchlorate ClO4-, tetrafluoroborate BF4-, or phosphate PO4^3-) through the faces of electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanobenzene, or nitroaromatics) that are integrated into the ligand framework. The recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-deficient π-systems, (3) potential C-H···anion hydrogen bonds from alkyl/aryl C-H groups, and (4) shape complementarity between the tetrahedral cation and anion within the π-rich cavity. This system enables the design of self-assembled capsules, ion-pair receptors, or porous materials with selective anion binding properties.

synthons.name: chiral_boronic_acid_diol_esterification_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on reversible covalent bond formation between boronic acids and 1,2- or 1,3-diols to create cyclic boronate esters. This dynamic covalent chemistry enables self-assembly of complex architectures through reversible B–O bond formation. The recognition elements are: (1) boronic acid group (R–B(OH)₂) acting as a Lewis acid electrophile, (2) vicinal diol (1,2-diol) or 1,3-diol acting as a nucleophile, (3) tetrahedral boronate ester center with chirality transfer potential. Interaction patterns include reversible covalent bond formation, hydrogen bonding with water molecules during equilibrium, and potential π-stacking of aromatic boronic acids. This system maps to primitives: electrophile (boron center), nucleophile (diol oxygens), reversible bond (B–O esterification), tetrahedral geometry, chirality element, and templating through dynamic combinatorial chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) germonium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that form encapsulation complexes with anions through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: 1) Tetrahedral germonium cations with four organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, benzyl, or alkyl groups) creating a cationic center, 2) Electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., triazine, pyrazine, or perfluorinated arenes) attached to the substituents to provide anion-π recognition sites, 3) Anion binding through cooperative electrostatic attraction from the cationic germanium center and anion-π interactions from the aromatic panels, 4) Self-assembly into capsule-like structures that can encapsulate anions such as chloride, bromide, or tetrafluoroborate. This represents an underexplored extension of tetrahedral onium cation chemistry into Group 14, with germanium offering distinct covalent radii and Lewis acidity compared to silicon or carbon analogs.

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on chiral tetrahedral boronate esters that form anion-binding capsules through synergistic anion-π and hydrogen bonding interactions. The system consists of two enantiopure boronate ester units derived from chiral diols (like BINOL derivatives or tartaric acid esters) that coordinate to form a tetrahedral boron center with one labile site for anion binding. The boronate esters feature electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl) positioned to create an anion-π binding pocket. When two such units assemble around a tetrahedral anion (e.g., ClO₄⁻, BF₄⁻, or SO₄²⁻), they form a chiral capsule stabilized by: (1) B–O–anion coordination bonds, (2) multiple anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-deficient arenes, (3) secondary hydrogen bonds from the diol backbone, and (4) π-stacking between the aromatic systems. The chirality of the diol ensures enantioselective anion recognition and capsule formation. This synthon maps to primitives as: tetrahedral geometry (boron and anion), electron-deficient π-systems (anion-π), coordination bonds (B–O–anion), hydrogen bonds, aromatic stacking, and chiral information transfer.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germonium cations (R4Ge+) that form anion-π stabilized capsules with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) tetrahedral germanium(IV) centers with four organic substituents (alkyl/aryl) forming cationic germonium species, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanopyrazine, or perfluorinated naphthalene) providing anion-π interaction sites, (3) halide or tetrafluoroborate anions positioned above the electron-deficient π-systems via anion-π interactions, and (4) self-assembly into dimeric or tetrameric capsule structures where germonium cations occupy vertices and anion-π interactions stabilize the edges. This represents an underexplored analog of phosphonium/arsonium capsules but with germanium's larger atomic radius and distinct polarizability influencing capsule stability and anion binding selectivity.

synthons.name: temporal_redox_switchable_viologen_anion_π_crown_ether_synthon
synthons.description: A time-dependent supramolecular system featuring a viologen derivative (N,N'-dialkyl-4,4'-bipyridinium) that undergoes reversible redox cycling between dicationic (V²⁺), radical cation (V⁺•), and neutral (V⁰) states. The dicationic form engages in strong anion-π interactions with electron-rich anions (PF₆⁻, BF₄⁻) while simultaneously acting as a guest for crown ethers (18-crown-6) via cation-dipole interactions. Upon electrochemical or photochemical reduction to the radical cation or neutral state, the anion-π interactions weaken dramatically while new π-π stacking interactions emerge between reduced viologen units. This creates a temporally controlled switching system where the assembly/disassembly of ternary complexes (viologen-anion-crown ether) can be precisely timed. Recognition elements include: (1) redox-active bipyridinium core, (2) crown ether binding sites on alkyl substituents, (3) anion binding pockets created by the π-deficient viologen ring, and (4) steric modulation groups that control binding kinetics. The seven primitives map as: atoms (N, C, O), bonds (ionic, dipole-dipole, π-π), angles (tetrahedral N⁺ centers), dihedrals (bipyridinium torsion), charges (2+ → 1+ → 0), polarity (highly polar dication), and sterics (alkyl chain length controls crown ether threading rate).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_42
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) complexes with tetradentate Schiff base ligands that form anion-binding capsules through anion-π interactions. The system features Ga(III) centers coordinated by N₂O₂ Schiff base ligands derived from salicylaldehyde and ethylenediamine derivatives, creating electron-deficient cavities with four convergent arene rings. These electron-poor aromatic surfaces (often fluorinated or nitro-substituted) provide multiple convergent anion-π interaction sites capable of encapsulating tetrahedral anions like ClO₄⁻, BF₄⁻, or PF₆⁻. The rigid tetrahedral geometry of the metal complex preorganizes the arene rings into a capsule-like arrangement, while the metal center itself can participate in secondary electrostatic interactions with anions. This represents a novel metallosupramolecular anion receptor motif distinct from previously proposed systems, combining metal coordination geometry, programmed π-acidity, and anion encapsulation in a single synthon.

synthons.name: chiral_boronic_ester_diol_chelate_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on reversible covalent boronic ester formation between a boronic acid and a 1,2- or 1,3-diol, creating a five- or six-membered chelate ring. This dynamic covalent bond exhibits directionality and stereoselectivity, particularly with chiral diols like tartaric acid derivatives or sugar cis-diols. The boron atom adopts a tetrahedral geometry upon esterification, and the system can be tuned by substituents on boron (electron-withdrawing groups enhance Lewis acidity) and the diol backbone. Recognition elements include the B–O covalent bonds, potential hydrogen bonding from residual OH groups or solvent, and π-interactions from aromatic boronic acids. It maps to primitives: connector (B–O bonds), director (chelate ring geometry), protector (steric groups controlling access to boron), effector (pH- and sugar-responsive binding), reporter (chiroptical changes), transporter (diol recognition for molecular transport), and temporizer (dynamic covalent exchange).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_43
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) complexes with tetradentate Schiff base ligands that create electron-deficient cavities capable of selective anion-π interactions. The system features: (1) Ga(III) center with +3 formal charge creating strong Lewis acidity, (2) rigid tetrahedral geometry enforced by salen-type Schiff base ligands with aromatic panels, (3) electron-deficient aromatic surfaces (nitro- or cyano-substituted phenyl rings) lining the cavity interior, (4) selective binding of oxoanions (sulfate, phosphate) or halides through synergistic anion-π and electrostatic interactions, (5) tunable cavity size via ligand substituents, (6) potential for encapsulation of multiple anions in a chiral environment due to propeller-like ligand arrangement, and (7) reversible anion binding with potential for temporal control via pH or redox modulation of the Ga center. This represents a novel metal-organic capsule system distinct from previously proposed pnictogen-based capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germoxane_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) centers with germoxane (Ge-O-Ge) bridges forming a cage-like structure that encapsulates anions via anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) tetrahedral Ge(IV) nodes with organic substituents (phenyl or alkyl groups), (2) bridging oxygen atoms creating Ge-O-Ge linkages that provide rigidity and directional control, (3) electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or triazine rings) integrated into the organic arms, creating anion-binding pockets via anion-π interactions, (4) tunable cavity size through variation of linker length between Ge centers and aromatic panels, (5) potential for encapsulation of halides (Cl⁻, Br⁻) or oxoanions (NO₃⁻, SO₄²⁻), (6) additional stabilization via C-H···anion hydrogen bonds from methylene or aromatic C-H groups adjacent to the cavity, and (7) reversible assembly/disassembly through pH or solvent changes affecting Ge-O bond stability. This represents a novel extension of tetrahedral anion-π capsules into main-group element chemistry beyond boron, silicon, and heavier pnictogens/sulfur analogs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_19_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraalkylammonium cation (R₄N⁺) where the four alkyl chains are functionalized with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or 1,3,5-triazine) at their termini. The cationic ammonium center provides electrostatic attraction to anions, while the peripheral electron-deficient π-systems create convergent anion-π binding sites. This arrangement forms a tetrahedral 'capsule' that can encapsulate spherical anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻) through a combination of electrostatic and anion-π interactions. The synthon exhibits preorganized, convergent binding geometry suitable for anion recognition in solution and solid state, with tunable cavity size via alkyl linker length and π-acidity modulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R3Si+) that form encapsulation complexes through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features cationic silicon centers with three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and one coordination site occupied by a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., BArF4- or SbF6-). Electron-deficient arenes such as hexafluorobenzene, perfluorinated pyridine, or 1,3,5-triazine derivatives serve as π-acidic panels that interact with the anion via anion-π interactions, while the tetrahedral silyl cations provide electrostatic preorganization and cation-π interactions with the arene edges. This creates a dynamic, charge-assisted capsule capable of encapsulating small anions or neutral guests. The synthon maps to primitives through: (1) electrostatic attraction (cation-anion), (2) anion-π interactions, (3) cation-π interactions, (4) hydrophobic effects from organic substituents, (5) tetrahedral geometry constraints, (6) dynamic exchange of weakly coordinating anions, and (7) size-complementarity with guest species.

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_dynamic_covalent_assembly_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on reversible boronate ester formation between 1,2-diols (catechols, sugars, or vicinal diols) and boronic acids. The system features dynamic covalent chemistry with pH-dependent reversibility, enabling self-correction and thermodynamic control of assembly. Recognition elements include: (1) B–O dative bonds forming tetrahedral boronate centers, (2) hydrogen bonding from residual hydroxyl groups, (3) potential π-stacking from aromatic boronic acids or diols, and (4) chirality transfer when using chiral diols or boronic acids, leading to diastereoselective assembly. This synthon can form macrocycles, cages, or polymers via dynamic combinatorial chemistry, and maps to primitives through reversible bond formation (dynamic), tetrahedral geometry, directional interactions, and chiral information propagation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_sulfonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral sulfonium cation (R3S+) that engages in cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels to form self-assembled capsule structures. The sulfonium center provides a strong, directional electrostatic anchor for anions (e.g., Cl-, BF4-, PF6-), while the surrounding aromatic walls (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, cyanurated benzenes, or triazine rings) create convergent anion-π binding sites. This combination leads to a well-defined, three-dimensional recognition pocket suitable for encapsulating small anions or anion-cation pairs. The synthon maps to primitives: (1) tetrahedral geometry at sulfur, (2) cationic charge, (3) anion binding, (4) π-acidic surfaces, (5) convergent orientation of interactions, (6) encapsulation geometry, and (7) self-assembly capability. This system is chemically realistic, as sulfonium salts are stable and synthetically accessible, and anion-π interactions are well-established in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated to two catecholate ligands, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped anion with a concave π-electron surface. The gallium-catecholate complex carries a formal -1 charge, making it an effective anion-π donor. The synthon is designed to form capsule-like assemblies through complementary anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine rings) on a second component. The gallium(III) provides Lewis acidic character and redox stability, while the catecholate ligands offer tunable electron density and hydrogen-bonding capability at their oxygen atoms. This system combines metal coordination geometry, electrostatic anion-π recognition, and shape complementarity to create predictable, self-assembling 3D architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) germonium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that function as anion-π acceptors and capsule-forming building blocks. The synthon exploits the electropositive germanium center in R₄Ge⁺ cations, which creates a σ-hole on each Ge atom, enabling directional anion binding via anion-σ-hole interactions. Four such cations can arrange tetrahedrally around a central anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻) through Ge⁺···anion contacts, while their aromatic substituents (e.g., phenyl, naphthyl) engage in complementary edge-to-face π-stacking or cation-π interactions with neighboring synthons, leading to the self-assembly of porous 3D capsules or frameworks. This combines pnictogen bonding (Group 14 Ge⁺ as pnictogen bond donor), anion recognition, and π-π/cation-π assembly in a single, programmable motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a quaternary ammonium center with four alkyl/aryl arms, each terminating in an electron-deficient aromatic system (e.g., triazine, tetrazine, or perfluorinated benzene). These aromatic panels are oriented to create a concave, cage-like cavity that can encapsulate an anion (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.) through multiple directional anion-π interactions. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center preorganizes the aromatic panels, while the positive charge enhances the electron deficiency of the π-systems and provides additional electrostatic complementarity to the encapsulated anion. This represents a charge-assisted, preorganized anion receptor motif that combines electrostatic, anion-π, and van der Waals interactions in a three-dimensional recognition architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_18
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form encapsulation complexes with anions through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a cationic silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl groups) providing steric protection and kinetic stability, while the fourth coordination site is occupied by a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., B(C6F5)4-). The electron-deficient aromatic rings on the substituents create multiple anion-π binding sites that can cooperatively encapsulate smaller anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-) within a π-rich pocket. Recognition elements include: (1) the Lewis acidic silicon center, (2) electron-deficient arenes for anion-π interactions, (3) steric bulk defining cavity size, and (4) charge-assisted electrostatic interactions. This maps to primitives as: tetrahedral geometry (shape), silylium cation (charge), anion-π interactions (non-covalent), encapsulation (containment), tunable arene electronics (property), reversible anion binding (reaction), and potential for allosteric regulation (control).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_triflate_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) cations coordinated to three trifluoromethanesulfonate (triflate) anions, forming a cationic complex [Ga(OTf)₃]⁺ that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The gallium center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with three oxygen atoms from triflate ligands and one coordination site occupied by a weakly bound solvent molecule or counterion. The electron-deficient triflate anions (σ-hole donors) participate in anion-π interactions with adjacent arenes, while the highly Lewis acidic Ga(III) center can further coordinate to π-basic heterocycles. This creates a versatile three-point recognition motif: (1) metal coordination to Lewis basic sites, (2) anion-π interactions between triflate and electron-poor aromatics, and (3) electrostatic complementarity. The system is chemically realistic as gallium triflate is a known strong Lewis acid catalyst, and anion-π interactions with triflate have been experimentally observed. This synthon enables the construction of supramolecular capsules through complementary assembly with π-acidic panels like tetrafluorobenzene or s-tetrazine derivatives.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraorganylgermanium(IV) cations (R4Ge+) that function as cationic tetrahedral nodes. The germanium center bears a formal positive charge, creating a region of electron deficiency at the metal center. The four organic substituents (typically aryl groups like phenyl or tolyl) extend outward, providing π-electron surfaces. These synthons can engage in two complementary interactions: (1) anion binding via electrostatic attraction to the cationic germanium center, and (2) parallel or offset π-stacking interactions between the aryl substituents of adjacent germanium cations. This combination enables the formation of dimeric or oligomeric capsules where the germanium cations occupy vertices, anions occupy the interior or bridging positions, and aryl-aryl π-interactions provide additional stabilization and directional control. The germanium(IV) cation offers a heavier Group 14 analogue to previously explored onium ions, with larger covalent radii and potentially different stereoelectronic effects influencing capsule geometry and anion affinity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraalkylammonium cations (R₄N⁺) that form encapsulation complexes with electron-deficient aromatic panels through synergistic cation-π and anion-π interactions. The system features a tetrahedral ammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium) that engages in cation-π interactions with four surrounding electron-rich arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene derivatives) on a capsule framework. Simultaneously, electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene) on the same capsule provide anion-π binding sites for halide or oxoanion guests (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, SO₄²⁻). This creates a dual-guest encapsulation system where the ammonium cation sits at the capsule's center via cation-π interactions, while anions occupy peripheral electron-deficient pockets via anion-π interactions. The tetrahedral symmetry matches the capsule's geometry, and the strength can be tuned by varying ammonium alkyl chains and arene electronics. This represents a charge-complementary, multi-interaction supramolecular assembly with potential for selective ion-pair recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that functions as a cationic π-acidic face, engaging in cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-tetrazine derivatives) to form a dynamic encapsulation motif. The synthon combines electrostatic attraction with orthogonal anion-π interactions from each of the four cationic faces of the tetrahedron, creating a convergent binding pocket suitable for halide or oxoanion recognition. This system maps to primitives through: (1) electrostatic (+/-) between cation and anion, (2) anion-π (anion to electron-deficient arene), (3) van der Waals contacts within the capsule, (4) possible C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from alkyl substituents, (5) conformational dynamics of the tetrahedral core, (6) tunable π-acidity via aromatic substitution, and (7) encapsulation geometry enabling size-selective anion binding.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) halonium cations (e.g., [GeR3X]+, where X = Cl, Br, I) that act as σ-hole donors via the halogen atom, paired with electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., tetrafluoropyrazine, s-tetrazine) as anion-π acceptors. The synthon combines three interaction primitives: (1) a directional halogen bond (Ge-X···π) from the polarized halogen of the germanium halonium cation to the π-face of the arene, (2) electrostatic complementarity between the cation and the electron-deficient ring, and (3) a tetrahedral core that provides a convergent, pre-organized geometry for capsule or cage assembly. The germanium center offers distinct polarizability and covalent character compared to lighter tetrahedral cations (e.g., ammonium, phosphonium), while the halonium motif provides a strong, tunable σ-hole. This system is chemically realistic, known in organogermanium chemistry, and can be extended to 3D frameworks or self-assembled capsules via multiple such interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated to two catecholate ligands, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped anion with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The catecholate oxygens provide strong hydrogen-bond acceptors, while the electron-deficient π-system of the gallium-bound catecholates engages in complementary anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic guests. The tetrahedral geometry creates a well-defined cavity suitable for encapsulation of small cationic or π-basic species. This system combines metal coordination (Ga-O bonds), hydrogen bonding (catecholate O-H···X), anion-π interactions (electron-deficient arene with anion/π-basic guest), and potential cation-π interactions if cationic guests are encapsulated. The gallium(III) oxidation state ensures kinetic inertness and thermodynamic stability, making this a robust building block for self-assembled capsules or extended frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18_4
synthons.description: A tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) with four extended aromatic arms (e.g., naphthyl or pyrenyl groups) that forms a supramolecular capsule through synergistic anion-π interactions. The cationic nitrogen center provides electrostatic complementarity for anion binding, while the electron-deficient aromatic arms (potentially enhanced by electron-withdrawing substituents) create multiple convergent anion-π recognition sites. The tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the arms to define a cavity suitable for encapsulating polyatomic anions (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or carboxylates). This system combines electrostatic, anion-π, and van der Waals interactions to create a stable, well-defined host-guest assembly with potential applications in anion sensing, transport, or templated synthesis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-active capsule synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cation (Cp₂Fe⁺) as the cationic vertex, interacting with electron-deficient aromatic panels via anion-π interactions. The system consists of four ferrocenium cations positioned at the vertices of a tetrahedron, each coordinated to three bridging electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives) through anion-π interactions between the cationic Fe center (formally Fe³⁺ in ferrocenium) and the π-face of the arene. The arenes serve as edges of the tetrahedral capsule, creating a cavity suitable for anion encapsulation. The redox-active nature of ferrocenium/ferrocene couple introduces temporal control via electrochemical switching, allowing the capsule to disassemble upon reduction to neutral ferrocene (weaker anion-π interaction) and reassemble upon oxidation. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral geometry of metal centers, (2) strong anion-π interactions between Fe³⁺-centered cation and π-acidic panels, (3) redox-switchable binding affinity, and (4) cavity for guest encapsulation. This combines supramolecular capsule architecture with electrochemical temporal control.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_tris(8-hydroxyquinolinate)_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) complexed with three 8-hydroxyquinolinate ligands, forming an electron-deficient metal-organic capsule capable of anion-π interactions. The Ga(III) center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with three bidentate quinolinolate ligands, creating a bowl-shaped cavity with π-deficient aromatic surfaces. The electron-deficient nature of the coordinated quinoline rings (enhanced by metal coordination and electron-withdrawing nitrogen atoms) creates strong anion-binding sites through anion-π interactions. This system can encapsulate spherical anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻) or oxoanions (NO₃⁻, ClO₄⁻) within its π-acidic cavity. The synthon features: (1) metal coordination bonds (Ga-N and Ga-O), (2) π-deficient aromatic surfaces for anion-π interactions, (3) hydrophobic cavity for guest encapsulation, (4) directional hydrogen bonding capability through peripheral hydroxyl groups, and (5) potential for extended assembly through π-π stacking of quinoline rings. This represents a novel metal-organic anion receptor system distinct from purely organic or main-group cation-based capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R3Si+) that function as anion-binding hosts through electrostatic and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a cationic silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and one labile site that stabilizes the positive charge, while the fourth 'face' of the tetrahedron is capped by an electron-deficient arene (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or tetracyanobenzene) that engages in cooperative anion-π interactions with a bound anion (Cl-, BF4-, PF6-, etc.). The recognition elements include: (1) the strong electrostatic attraction between the silyl cation and the anion, (2) directional anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic panel, (3) possible C-H···anion or aryl-perfluoroaryl interactions from the substituents, and (4) geometric preorganization from the tetrahedral silicon center. This synthon maps to the seven primitives as: AFFINITY (electrostatic + anion-π), DIRECTIONALITY (tetrahedral geometry + face-specific binding), COMPLEMENTARITY (cation-anion charge + π-acidity), COOPERATIVITY (combined electrostatic and π-interactions), ADAPTABILITY (anion size/shape selection), ORTHOGONALITY (independent binding modes), and PERSISTENCE (kinetically stable Si-C bonds with labile anion binding).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_19
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that engage in dual interactions: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged silicon center, and (2) parallel anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or cyanurated pyridines) positioned at the vertices of a tetrahedral capsule framework. The silylium center acts as a strong Lewis acidic anchor, while the arene panels provide complementary anion-π recognition surfaces. This creates a synergistic, three-dimensional binding pocket suitable for encapsulating anions like BF4-, PF6-, or ClO4- within a well-defined cavity. The system exemplifies p-block cation-anion-π cooperativity, is synthetically accessible via hydride abstraction from silanes, and can be mapped to primitives: positive charge (cation), negative charge (anion), π-system (arene panels), tetrahedral geometry, electrostatic attraction, and directional binding.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_20
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form encapsulation complexes through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system consists of a cationic silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl or t-butyl groups) to stabilize the highly electrophilic Si+ center, paired with an anionic guest (e.g., Cl-, BF4-) that bridges between the silylium cation and electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine derivatives). The tetrahedral geometry of the silylium cation directs three substituents outward while the fourth coordination site engages in electrostatic and orbital interactions with the anion, which in turn participates in anion-π interactions with adjacent aromatic panels, creating a self-assembled capsule-like architecture. This represents an underexplored combination of main-group cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π recognition, distinct from previously proposed phosphonium/arsonium systems due to silicon's unique electropositive character and tetrahedral coordination preference.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) that forms a complementary capsule structure through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The synthon features a central ammonium cation with four aromatic arms (e.g., 1,3,5,7-tetraphenyladamantane-1,3,5,7-tetrayl tetra(trimethylammonium)) that positions four cationic centers in a tetrahedral arrangement. These cations interact with four tetrahedrally arranged electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., tetrafluorinated or tetracyano-substituted aromatic panels) through cooperative anion-π interactions, where the π-system acts as an anion receptor. The assembly creates a three-dimensional capsule capable of encapsulating small anions or neutral molecules, with additional stabilization from edge-to-face aromatic interactions and electrostatic complementarity. This represents an underexplored variation in the cation-anion-π capsule family using abundant ammonium centers rather than heavier pnictogens or chalcogens.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18_5
synthons.description: A tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) with four aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups) that function as an anion-π capsule synthon. The cationic nitrogen provides electrostatic attraction for anions, while the electron-deficient aromatic rings (enhanced by electron-withdrawing substituents like -CF₃ or -CN) create multiple convergent anion-π binding sites. The tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the four π-acidic faces to encapsulate a spherical or tetrahedral anion (e.g., Cl⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) via cooperative anion-π interactions. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through: (1) tetrahedral node (ammonium center), (2) directional anion-π interactions, (3) electrostatic complementarity, (4) preorganized cavity, (5) convergent binding sites, (6) encapsulation geometry, and (7) tunable aromatic electron deficiency. It represents a supramolecular cation-anion recognition system distinct from previously proposed chalcogen/pnictogen-based capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraorganylgermanium(IV) cations (R₄Ge⁺) as π-acidic caps that engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives) to form a capsule-like assembly. The germanium center, being less common than silicon or tin in such roles, provides moderate Lewis acidity and polarizability, while the four organic substituents (e.g., phenyl, fluorophenyl) create a tetrahedral cationic core. The assembly is stabilized by (1) electrostatic attraction between the Ge⁺ center and an encapsulated anion (e.g., Cl⁻, BF₄⁻), (2) multiple anion-π interactions between the anion and the electron-deficient aromatic walls, and (3) van der Waals contacts between the organic substituents. This system explores germanium in supramolecular cation-π-anion cooperativity, an underexplored combination in the catalog.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The system features a rigid tetrahedral ammonium core (e.g., tetraphenylphosphonium or tetraphenylarsonium analogs with nitrogen) positioned at the vertices of a conceptual tetrahedron. Each cationic center is flanked by electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or 1,3,5-trinitrobenzene units) that create localized anion-binding pockets through anion-π interactions. The combination of electrostatic attraction from the ammonium cation and anion-π interactions from the surrounding π-acidic surfaces creates a highly cooperative, three-dimensional binding site for anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-, etc.). This synthon enables the modular construction of self-assembled capsules or cages where multiple tetrahedral units come together to encapsulate anions through a combination of Coulombic and non-covalent π-interactions, with potential applications in anion sensing, separation, and supramolecular catalysis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_switch_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cation (Cp₂Fe⁺) that engages in dual anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems, creating a redox-switchable capsule-like assembly. The ferrocenium center provides a stable cationic tetrahedral geometry with two cyclopentadienyl rings oriented at ~180° relative to the Fe-Cp axes, creating four distinct π-faces for anion binding. Recognition elements include: (1) the positively charged Fe(III) center creating electrostatic attraction, (2) the electron-deficient nature of ferrocenium's π-system (compared to neutral ferrocene) enhancing anion-π interactions, (3) tetrahedral geometry enabling three-dimensional assembly, and (4) redox-switchability between Fe(II)/Fe(III) states modulating binding affinity. This system can form discrete capsules with tetrahedral anions (BF₄⁻, ClO₄⁻) or assemble into extended networks with planar anions (NO₃⁻, PF₆⁻). The redox-active nature allows temporal control over assembly/disassembly through electrochemical or chemical oxidation/reduction.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular capsule-forming synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) with four aromatic arms, each terminating in electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene). The cationic center provides electrostatic attraction, while the extended aromatic arms create convergent anion-π binding pockets. When combined with complementary tetrahedral anions (e.g., BF4-, ClO4-, or PO4^3-), the system self-assembles into a dimeric capsule via synergistic cation-anion electrostatic interactions and multiple convergent anion-π contacts. The geometry enforces a well-defined cavity suitable for encapsulation of small neutral guests. This represents a distinct variation on cation-anion-π capsules, using the ubiquitous ammonium center rather than heavier pnictogen or chalcogen centers, and employs electron-deficient arenes for strong, directional anion binding.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_triflate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular capsule synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) centers coordinated to three triflate anions and one π-acidic aromatic system. The Ga(III) center acts as a Lewis acidic vertex, with three triflate (CF₃SO₃⁻) anions providing strong electrostatic and hydrogen-bond accepting sites at the equatorial positions. The fourth coordination site is occupied by an electron-deficient aromatic ring (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or s-triazine derivative) through anion-π interactions, where the triflate oxygens engage in additional weak hydrogen bonds with adjacent C–H donors. This creates a directional, charge-assisted assembly motif that can form dimeric capsules via triflate–Ga coordination bridges or extended networks through π-stacking of the electron-deficient arenes. The system combines metal coordination, anion-π, electrostatic, and weak hydrogen bonding interactions, and is synthetically accessible using Ga(OTf)₃ and π-deficient aromatics.

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on chiral tetrahedral boronate esters that form anion-binding cages through synergistic anion-π and B-O coordination interactions. The system features a rigid, C₃-symmetric triarylboronate scaffold with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) positioned to create convergent anion-π binding pockets. Each boron center is esterified with a chiral diol (such as a binaphthol derivative), imparting stereoselective recognition. The tetrahedral geometry of the boron centers, combined with the preorganized aromatic surfaces, enables encapsulation of tetrahedral anions (e.g., ClO₄⁻, BF₄⁻) or trigonal planar anions (e.g., NO₃⁻) via multipoint anion-π contacts, while the Lewis acidic boron and Lewis basic ester oxygen atoms provide additional polarization and stabilization. This synthon exemplifies a convergent, charge-assisted supramolecular assembly with potential for enantioselective sensing or separation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_19_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraalkylammonium cations (R₄N⁺) that form encapsulation complexes with electron-deficient aromatic panels through synergistic cation-π and anion-π interactions. The system features a tetrahedral ammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium) that engages in cation-π interactions with four surrounding electron-rich arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene derivatives), while simultaneously coordinating to an anionic guest (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, ClO₄⁻) via anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene) positioned at the vertices of a complementary cage. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) tetrahedral cation, (2) electron-rich π-donor walls for cation-π binding, and (3) electron-deficient π-acceptor panels for anion binding, resulting in a stable capsule-like assembly. The synthon maps to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), cationic charge (electrostatics), π-surfaces (recognition), and directional non-covalent interactions (assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-active synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cation (Cp₂Fe⁺) interacting with electron-deficient aromatic anions via anion-π interactions. The system features: (1) a stable metallocenium cation with tetrahedral sandwich geometry, (2) electron-deficient polyfluorinated or polynitro aromatic anions as π-acidic surfaces, (3) strong anion-π interactions between the cationic iron center's electrostatic field and the anion's π-system, (4) reversible redox switching between ferrocene/ferrocenium states for temporal control, (5) tetrahedral arrangement enabling 3D capsule formation with multiple anions, (6) metal coordination sites for additional ligand binding, and (7) electrostatic complementarity for directed assembly. This combines metallocenium chemistry, anion-π recognition, and redox-responsive behavior in a single supramolecular motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) that forms a complementary electrostatic and anion-π interaction network with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a cationic tetrahedral core (e.g., tetramethylammonium or a larger tetraalkylammonium derivative) positioned at the center of a self-assembled capsule constructed from four electron-deficient, π-acidic aromatic panels (such as 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives). The positively charged nitrogen engages in strong electrostatic interactions with anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻) that are simultaneously stabilized by parallel anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic rings. This creates a synergistic three-component recognition motif: (1) cation-anion electrostatic, (2) anion-π, and (3) dispersive/van der Waals contacts between alkyl chains and aromatic surfaces. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center directs assembly toward a well-defined, capsule-like architecture with internal anion binding pockets, making it a programmable synthon for constructing anion-responsive supramolecular frameworks and hosts.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R3Si+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating a capsule-like architecture. The synthon features: (1) a central silicon atom with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., trimethylsilyl, tert-butyl) and a formal positive charge, (2) four electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or tetrazine derivatives) positioned tetrahedrally around the cation, each engaging in anion-π interactions with the cationic center, and (3) bridging groups (alkyl or aryl linkers) connecting the arene panels to create a semi-enclosed capsule. The strong electrostatic anion-π interaction (Si+···π) is complemented by secondary C–H···F or C–H···N contacts and dispersion forces from the bulky substituents. This synthon is chemically realistic as silyl cations are known persistent electrophiles in non-nucleophilic media, and their interaction with electron-deficient aromatics has precedent in main-group supramolecular chemistry. It maps to primitives: cation (Si+), anion-π interaction, tetrahedral geometry, arene panels, bridging linkers, electrostatic attraction, and capsule formation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) centers with silyl cation character (R3Si+) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system consists of a tetrahedral silicon center with three aryl substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenyl groups) creating electron-deficient faces, while the fourth position bears a labile leaving group (e.g., triflate) that can dissociate to generate a cationic silicon center. The resulting R3Si+ cation exhibits both electrostatic attraction to anions and, through its electron-deficient aryl arms, engages in anion-π interactions with suitable anions (e.g., halides, tetrafluoroborate). This creates a 'capsule-like' recognition motif where the anion is sandwiched between the electron-deficient π-systems of adjacent silicon centers in a self-assembled structure. The synthon combines silylium cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π interactions, offering a route to anion-templated assembly of silicon-based architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_9
synthons.description: A tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) with four aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl or naphthyl groups) that simultaneously engages in two orthogonal interaction modes: (1) electrostatic attraction between the cationic nitrogen center and an anionic guest (e.g., Cl-, Br-, NO3-), and (2) multiple cooperative anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient aromatic rings of the arms and the same anion. The tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the four π-acidic surfaces to create a convergent binding pocket, functioning as a supramolecular capsule synthon. The system is chemically realistic, drawing from known quaternary ammonium salts and anion-π phenomena, and can be mapped to primitives such as positive charge (cation), negative charge (anion), π-system, and tetrahedral geometry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_tris(8-hydroxyquinolinate)_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) complexed with three 8-hydroxyquinoline ligands, creating a bowl-shaped electron-deficient cavity with exposed π-surfaces. The complex features: (1) a central Ga³⁺ ion in tetrahedral coordination with three bidentate 8-hydroxyquinolinate anions (N,O-chelation), (2) three outwardly directed aromatic rings forming a convergent electron-deficient cavity, (3) multiple anion-π interaction sites from the electron-deficient quinoline rings, (4) potential halogen bonding sites at the quinoline nitrogen atoms, (5) hydrogen bond acceptor sites at the oxygen atoms, and (6) π-π stacking capability with complementary electron-rich aromatics. This synthon can encapsulate anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through cooperative anion-π interactions and coordinate with cations through its oxygen donors, enabling hierarchical assembly into larger capsules or frameworks. The gallium center provides Lewis acidity while maintaining hydrolytic stability, and the 8-hydroxyquinoline ligands offer tunable electronic properties through substitution at the 5-position.

synthons.name: chiral_boronic_acid_diol_esterification_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on boronic acid-diol reversible esterification chemistry combined with anion-π interactions within a chiral capsule framework. The system features: (1) a boronic acid group (R-B(OH)₂) that reversibly forms cyclic esters with vicinal diols (1,2- or 1,3-diols) through dehydration, creating dynamic covalent bonds; (2) an electron-deficient aromatic system (e.g., perfluorinated benzene or triazine ring) adjacent to the boron center that provides anion-π binding sites; (3) chiral substituents (binaphthyl or tartaric acid derivatives) that induce helical capsule formation through π-stacking and van der Waals interactions; (4) encapsulated anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) stabilized by cooperative anion-π interactions from multiple electron-deficient aromatic panels within the capsule interior. This creates a dynamic, chiral supramolecular assembly where anion binding can modulate the esterification equilibrium and capsule stability.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraalkylammonium cation (R₄N⁺) where the four alkyl arms are functionalized with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or 1,3,5-triazine) to create convergent anion-π binding sites. The tetrahedral cation acts as a structural core, while the electron-deficient π-systems on each arm provide directional, attractive interactions with anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.). This creates a 3D 'capsule-like' recognition pocket where the anion is encapsulated by four convergent anion-π faces. The synthon exploits electrostatic (cation-anion) and anion-π interactions synergistically, with the rigid tetrahedral geometry preorganizing the binding sites. It can be mapped to the seven primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), ammonium cation (electrostatic donor), electron-deficient arenes (anion-π acceptor), convergent binding (orientation), encapsulation (containment), and tunable via alkyl linker length and π-system electron deficiency (modulation).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that acts as a cationic hub for anion binding through electrostatic interactions, combined with extended aromatic panels that provide anion-π interactions and hydrophobic encapsulation. The system features four cationic nitrogen centers arranged tetrahedrally, each bearing alkyl or aryl substituents, with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., triazine, pyrazine, or perfluorinated arenes) positioned to create a convergent binding pocket for anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-, etc.). The combination of Coulombic attraction and anion-π interactions enables selective anion recognition and encapsulation in aqueous or polar organic media, with potential for tunable cavity size via substituent modification. This represents a distinct entry in the cation-anion-π capsule family, differing from previously proposed iodonium, phosphonium, arsonium, and other onium variants by focusing on the ubiquitous ammonium motif with tailored π-acidic surfaces.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_10
synthons.description: A tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) with four aromatic arms (e.g., phenyl, naphthyl, or pyridyl groups) that preorganize to form a cationic, electron-deficient cavity. The system functions as a supramolecular synthon by combining cation-anion electrostatic interactions with cooperative anion-π interactions. Each aromatic arm provides an electron-deficient π-surface that can engage an anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻) via anion-π contacts, while the central positive charge provides additional electrostatic stabilization. The tetrahedral geometry creates a convergent, capsule-like binding pocket ideal for encapsulating spherical or tetrahedral anions. This synthon is chemically robust, synthetically accessible via quaternization reactions, and represents a distinct entry in the cation-anion-π capsule family by using the ubiquitous ammonium center instead of heavier pnictogens or chalcogens.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces, creating a capsule-like assembly. The synthon features a central silicon atom with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and a positive charge stabilized by hyperconjugation, positioned above a π-acidic aromatic system (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanopyrazine, or perfluorinated coronene). The electrostatic attraction between the cationic silicon center and the electron-deficient π-cloud is complemented by dispersion forces from the substituents and potential edge-to-face CH-π contacts. This interaction pattern can be mapped to the seven primitives: positive charge (electrostatic), π-system (surface), tetrahedral geometry (shape), directional preference (orientation), tunable substituents (modulation), reversible assembly (dynamics), and encapsulation potential (function). The system is chemically realistic as silyl cations are known stable species in non-nucleophilic environments, and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes are well-documented in supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronate ester anion (formed from boronic acid and 1,2-diol) that functions as an anion-π acceptor. The system features a chiral B-center with four distinct substituents: two oxygen atoms from the ester linkage, one aromatic group with extended π-system, and one functional group (e.g., fluorinated aryl) to enhance anion binding. The boronate anion's negative charge is delocalized into the boron p-orbital, creating a σ-hole-like electrostatic potential above the boron center that can attract electron-rich π-systems from complementary aromatic panels. This enables the formation of chiral cage architectures through simultaneous anion-π interactions and boronate ester dynamic covalent chemistry, allowing for stereoselective encapsulation of cationic or neutral guests.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_21
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating self-assembled capsule architectures. The system features: (1) tetrahedral silicon centers with cationic charge, (2) electron-deficient arene panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, tetracyanobenzene, or perfluorinated pyridines) as π-acidic surfaces, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the silylium cation and the arene π-system, (4) complementary van der Waals contacts and steric matching between substituents, (5) potential for encapsulation of small neutral or anionic guests within the assembled cavity. This represents an underexplored combination of main-group cation chemistry with anion-π interactions in supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_sulfonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral sulfonium cation (R3S+) that acts as a cationic anchor point for anion binding via electrostatic and hydrogen bonding interactions, while simultaneously engaging in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives) arranged in a capsule-like geometry. The system features: (1) a central sulfonium cation with three alkyl/aryl arms providing structural directionality, (2) a bound anion (e.g., chloride, tetrafluoroborate) via S+···X- electrostatic and C-H···X- hydrogen bonds, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings positioned above and below the anion to form stabilizing anion-π contacts, and (4) additional π-π stacking between aromatic panels to complete the capsule assembly. This synthon combines pnictogen-like cationic bonding (S+), anion recognition, and aromatic stacking in a single programmable unit, suitable for constructing porous frameworks or molecular containers.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) germonium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that form capsule-like structures through synergistic anion-π and cation-π interactions. The germanium center, being larger than silicon and less explored than phosphorus/arsenic analogs, exhibits enhanced polarizability and distinctive tetrahedral geometry. The synthon combines: (1) a positively charged Ge center (cationic primitive) acting as an electrostatic anchor, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or triazine rings) attached to the Ge via alkyl/aryl linkers, creating anion-binding π-surfaces (anion-π primitive), and (3) additional electron-rich arenes (e.g., naphthalene or pyrene units) on opposing faces to engage in cation-π interactions with neighboring germonium centers (cation-π primitive). This creates a reversible, self-assembled dimeric capsule that encapsulates anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻) within its cavity via cooperative interactions. The system is chemically realistic, with known stable tetraorganogermonium salts, and offers tunability via substituent electronics and linker length.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) halonium cations (GeX₃⁺, where X = Cl, Br, I) that act as cationic vertices, interacting through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or tetrazine derivatives) to form a self-assembled capsule. The germanium center provides a robust tetrahedral geometry with tunable Lewis acidity via halogen substitution, while the electron-deficient π-systems provide strong, directional anion-binding sites. The synthon combines (1) Ge–X covalent bonds as structural linkers, (2) anion-π interactions between halide anions (X⁻) and the arene panels, (3) electrostatic attraction between GeX₃⁺ and X⁻, and (4) potential halogen bonding from the Ge-bound halogens to additional anions or Lewis bases. This system is chemically realistic, inspired by known tetrahedral organogermanium cations and anion-π host-guest chemistry, and represents an underexplored combination of p-block cation and anion-π assembly motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germonium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that form encapsulation complexes with π-rich aromatic anions through cooperative cation-π and anion-π interactions. The germanium center provides a distinct tetrahedral geometry with intermediate polarizability between silicon and tin, creating a unique electrostatic environment. The cationic germonium center engages in strong cation-π interactions with electron-rich arenes, while simultaneously, the positive charge enhances anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. This dual interaction pattern enables the formation of three-dimensional capsule-like assemblies where the germonium cation acts as a corner unit, connecting aromatic panels through orthogonal non-covalent interactions. The system exhibits tunable cavity sizes through variation of R groups (alkyl, aryl) on germanium and selection of complementary π-systems, allowing for selective encapsulation of small molecules or ions. This represents a novel extension of tetrahedral onium cation chemistry into the underexplored germanium domain within supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_β_diketonate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) complexed with β-diketonate ligands, where the electron-deficient metal center and ligand framework create a convergent anion-π binding pocket. The Ga(III) center adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry with three β-diketonate oxygen donors and one labile site occupied by a weakly coordinating solvent molecule. The β-diketonate ligands are fluorinated (e.g., hexafluoroacetylacetonate) to enhance both the Lewis acidity of the gallium center and the electron-deficient character of the aromatic substituents on the ligand periphery. This creates a synergistic binding site where anions can interact through both direct coordination to the Lewis acidic gallium and through anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient arenes. The synthon exhibits directional, convergent interactions suitable for constructing supramolecular capsules or extended frameworks through anion templation.
