synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_19_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The cation features four identical aromatic arms (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) extending from the central nitrogen, creating a tetrahedral geometry. Each arm engages in simultaneous anion-π interactions with a halide or tetrafluoroborate anion positioned above its electron-deficient π-surface. The anions act as 'caps' that are held in place by these interactions, while the tetrahedral arrangement of the arms creates a defined cavity. This system demonstrates a rare example of using purely organic cation-anion-π networks to preorganize a capsule-like architecture without metal coordination, suitable for host-guest chemistry or as a building block for porous organic salts.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ferrocenium_cation_anion_π_redox_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-active capsule synthon based on tetrahedral ferrocenium cations (Cp₂Fe⁺) that engage in dual anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) tetrahedral ferrocenium cations as redox-active cationic vertices, (2) electron-deficient hexafluorobenzene or tetrafluoropyrazine panels as π-acidic surfaces, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the cationic iron center's partial positive charge and electron-rich anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻), (4) complementary electrostatic and van der Waals interactions stabilizing the capsule assembly. This creates a dynamic, redox-responsive capsule where oxidation state (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺) modulates capsule stability and anion binding affinity. The synthon maps to primitives: positive charge (ferrocenium), negative charge (anion), π-system (electron-deficient arene), directional interaction (anion-π), tetrahedral geometry, redox activity (temporal dimension), and self-assembly (supramolecular domain).

synthons.name: directional_selenium_selenoxide_chalcogen_bonding_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on directional Se···O chalcogen bonding between an electron-deficient selenium center (in selenoxide or selenonium derivatives) and an electron-rich oxygen atom (carbonyl, ether, or hydroxyl oxygen). The synthon features a σ-hole on selenium along the extension of the R-Se bond axis, creating a highly directional interaction (150-180°). Recognition elements include: (1) electron-deficient selenium atom with σ-hole, (2) electron-rich oxygen lone pairs, (3) appropriate substituents on selenium to enhance σ-hole potential (electron-withdrawing groups or positive charge). Interaction patterns include linear Se···O contacts (2.5-3.2 Å) with binding energies of 10-40 kJ/mol. This synthon can be mapped to primitives: donor (oxygen lone pair), acceptor (selenium σ-hole), directionality (linear geometry), polarity (polarized Seδ+···Oδ- interaction), complementarity (electron deficiency/richness matching), cooperativity (works alongside hydrogen bonds or π-interactions), and reversibility (moderate strength, dynamic in solution).

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_diol_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron center forming a chiral boronate ester with a 1,2-diol (catechol or sugar derivative), creating an electron-deficient cavity that engages in simultaneous anion-π interactions with halide anions and π-stacking with electron-rich aromatic systems. The boron atom adopts sp³ hybridization with two oxygen atoms from the diol and two additional substituents (aryl or alkyl groups) that project outward, creating a bowl-shaped electron-deficient region above the boron center. This synthon features: (1) covalent B-O bonds forming the boronate ester core, (2) electrostatic anion-π interactions between halide anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻) and the electron-deficient boron-aryl π-system, (3) directional π-π stacking with complementary electron-rich aromatics, (4) potential hydrogen bonding from residual hydroxyl groups, (5) chirality transfer from the diol to the entire assembly, (6) reversible boronate ester formation enabling temporal control, and (7) metal-coordination capability through peripheral functional groups. This represents a multifunctional supramolecular building block for chiral sensing and anion encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) halonium cations (GeX₃⁺, where X = Cl, Br, I) that act as anion-π acceptors when paired with electron-rich aromatic panels. The synthon features: (1) a central GeX₃⁺ cation with strong σ-hole character on the halogens, enabling halogen bonding; (2) electron-deficient Ge center that can engage in anion binding; (3) tetrahedral geometry that directs three halogen-bonding arms outward; (4) complementary electron-rich arenes (e.g., hexaalkoxybenzenes, pyrene derivatives) that provide anion-π donor surfaces; (5) self-assembly into dimeric capsule-like structures via GeX₃⁺···anion···π interactions; (6) tunable cavity size via halogen and arene selection; (7) potential for encapsulation of small anions or neutral guests. This combines pnictogen-bonding (Ge), halogen-bonding (X), and anion-π interactions in a single supramolecular motif.

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_cage_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronate ester anion (formed from boronic acid and diol) that acts as an anion-π acceptor within a chiral cage framework. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral boronate anion [B(OR)₄]⁻ with electron-deficient boron center, (2) electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., pyrene or perylene derivatives) positioned to engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with the boronate anion, (3) chiral diol linkers (e.g., binaphthol derivatives) that impart helical chirality to the assembly, and (4) metal coordination sites (e.g., pyridine or terpyridine) at the vertices to direct cage formation. The boronate anion serves as both a structural template and an anion-π acceptor, while the chiral aromatic walls create a stereoselective binding pocket. This represents a novel combination of boronate ester chemistry, anion-π interactions, and chiral self-assembly not present in the catalog.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraorganylgermanium(IV) cations (R₄Ge⁺) that function as anion-π capsule formers. The germanium center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with four organic substituents (e.g., aryl groups with electron-deficient π-surfaces like pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl). The permanent positive charge on germanium(IV) creates a strong electrostatic potential, making the system an excellent anion binder. The tetrahedral arrangement positions four electron-deficient aromatic faces inward, creating a convergent, cage-like anion-binding pocket via cooperative anion-π interactions. This synthon is chemically distinct from the previously proposed onium ions (P, As, Sb, I, etc.) as it utilizes a Group 14 element in a hypervalent cationic state. Recognition elements include: (1) the tetrahedral Ge⁺ cation as an electrostatic anchor, (2) multiple electron-deficient aryl rings as anion-π donors, and (3) the preorganized capsule geometry. It maps to the seven primitives via: Ge⁺ (electrophile), anion (nucleophile), π-system (anion-π interaction), tetrahedral geometry (preorganization), and the overall capsule (assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a capsule-like structure through simultaneous anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels and electrostatic interactions with encapsulated anions. The system features four electron-deficient triazine or tetrazine rings positioned at the vertices of a tetrahedron around the central ammonium nitrogen, creating a cavity that selectively binds spherical anions (Cl-, Br-) through a combination of anion-π interactions with the aromatic panels and charge-charge interactions with the central cation. The recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral quaternary ammonium core providing positive charge and directionality, (2) electron-deficient π-systems (triazine/tetrazine) for anion-π interactions, (3) flexible alkyl or aryl linkers between ammonium center and aromatic panels allowing cavity adjustment. This represents a cationic analog of tetrahedral anion-π capsules but uses ammonium instead of heavier pnictogens/calcogens, with potential applications in anion sensing and transport.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halogen_bonded_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) centers functionalized with halogen bond donor groups (iodo- or bromo-triazolyl) that simultaneously engage in: (1) halogen bonding with anion acceptors (chloride, bromide, tetrafluoroborate), (2) anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes (tetrafluorobenzene, triazine rings) positioned above the germanium center, and (3) weak Ge···π interactions with flanking aromatic panels. The germanium center provides a rigid tetrahedral scaffold with tunable Lewis acidity, while the halogen bond donors (C–I/Br) offer directional recognition of anions. Electron-deficient aromatic panels attached to the germanium vertex create a convergent binding pocket that encapsulates anions through combined halogen and anion-π interactions, forming a self-assembled capsule-like structure when combined with complementary components. This represents a novel extension of tetrahedral capsule chemistry using germanium—a less explored group 14 element—combined with emerging halogen bonding motifs for anion recognition.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a complementary capsule structure with electron-deficient aromatic systems through synergistic cation-π and anion-π interactions. The synthon features a central N+ atom with four different organic substituents (e.g., benzyl, methyl, ethyl, propyl) creating a chiral tetrahedral core. This cationic center engages in cation-π interactions with electron-rich arenes on one face, while simultaneously coordinating to an anion (Cl-, Br-, BF4-) positioned above the opposite face. The anion is further stabilized by anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine) incorporated into the ligand framework. This creates a three-point recognition motif: (1) cation-π with electron-rich aromatics, (2) electrostatic anion binding, and (3) anion-π with electron-deficient aromatics, resulting in a directional capsule-like assembly. The system is chemically robust, water-stable, and offers tunable binding affinity through substituent variation on both the cation and the π-systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that function as anion-binding hosts through electrostatic and anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a cationic silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and one labile site that stabilizes the positive charge. Electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or perfluorinated naphthalene) are positioned via covalent linkers to create a π-rich cavity that synergistically binds anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) through cooperative anion-π and electrostatic interactions. The tetrahedral geometry directs the anion into a defined pocket, creating a capsule-like recognition motif. This synthon is chemically realistic as silyl cations are known strong Lewis acids and electrophiles, stabilized by weakly coordinating anions, and the integration of anion-π interactions enhances selectivity and binding affinity. It maps to the seven primitives through: (1) electrostatic attraction (Si⁺⋯anion), (2) anion-π interactions (arene⋯anion), (3) hydrophobic effects (bulky substituents), (4) geometric complementarity (tetrahedral encapsulation), (5) dynamic exchange (labile anion binding), (6) preorganization (rigid arene panels), and (7) cooperative binding (combined interactions).

synthons.name: chiral_boronate_ester_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on chiral tetrahedral boronate esters that form anion-binding capsules through synergistic anion-π and B-O coordination interactions. The system features a boronate ester formed from a catechol derivative with extended aromatic surfaces (e.g., pyrene or perylene substituents) that create electron-deficient π-surfaces. These tetrahedral boron centers (sp³-hybridized) act as Lewis acidic sites for anion coordination (e.g., fluoride, chloride, or carboxylates) while the adjacent electron-deficient aromatic panels provide complementary anion-π binding sites. The chirality arises from non-symmetric substitution patterns on the catechol or from chiral diols used in boronate formation, enabling enantioselective anion recognition. The capsule forms through dimerization of two such boronate units, creating a tetrahedral anion-binding cavity with C₂ symmetry. Recognition elements include: (1) Lewis acidic boron center, (2) electron-deficient π-systems, (3) chiral steric environment, and (4) preorganized cavity geometry. This represents a novel fusion of boronate ester chemistry, anion-π interactions, and chiral supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halogen_bond_acceptor_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) centers functionalized with halogen bond acceptor groups (pyridine N-oxides) that cooperatively interact with anions via anion-π interactions and halogen bonding. The germanium center provides a rigid tetrahedral scaffold with four arms, each terminating in a pyridine N-oxide group. These N-oxides act as strong halogen bond acceptors toward iodoperfluoroarene-based donors, while the electron-deficient germanium-adjacent aromatic rings (e.g., perfluorinated phenyl or naphthyl spacers) create anion-π binding sites. The combination allows for the assembly of capsule-like structures where anions are encapsulated at the interior through multipoint anion-π contacts, and the exterior is stitched together via robust Ge···O→I–Ar halogen bonds. This system exploits the underutilized germanium as a tetrahedral node, the strong halogen bond acceptor ability of N-oxides, and the synergy between anion-π and halogen bonding for stable supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_22
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R₃Si⁺) that form encapsulation complexes with anions through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) tetrahedral silicon centers with three organic substituents (e.g., mesityl or 2,6-diisopropylphenyl groups) providing steric protection and solubility, (2) a positively charged silicon center acting as a strong Lewis acidic site, (3) electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, triazine, or pyrazine rings) attached to the substituents that create anion-binding pockets through anion-π interactions, and (4) the ability to encapsulate halide or pseudohalide anions within a cage-like structure formed by multiple silylium-aromatic units. This represents an underexplored combination of silylium cation chemistry with supramolecular anion recognition, distinct from the already-proposed phosphonium, arsonium, and other onium cation systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_13
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) centers with cationic silylium-like character (R3Si+) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system consists of four silicon centers at the vertices of a tetrahedron, each bearing three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl or t-butyl groups) to stabilize the partial positive charge and prevent nucleophilic attack, while the fourth position is occupied by a σ-bond to a bridging aromatic spacer (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or cyanobenzene). The electron-deficient aromatic panels create a convergent anion-binding pocket via anion-π interactions, while the positively charged silicon centers provide additional electrostatic stabilization for anions (e.g., Cl-, BF4-, PF6-). This creates a three-dimensional capsule-like architecture capable of encapsulating anions through combined electrostatic and anion-π interactions. The synthon is chemically reasonable as silylium ions are known stabilized by steric protection and weakly coordinating anions, and polycationic siloxane cages have precedent. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral Si(IV) centers with δ+ charge, (2) electron-deficient arenes for anion-π interactions, (3) preorganized tetrahedral geometry, and (4) tunable steric bulk for cavity size control. Mappable to primitives: positive charge (Si δ+), π-system (electron-deficient arene), shape (tetrahedral), polarity, connectivity (Si-C bonds), flexibility (adjustable substituents), and stoichiometry (4:1 Si:anion ratio).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_23
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating self-assembled capsule structures. The system features: (1) tetrahedral silicon centers with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl groups) for steric stabilization of the cationic center, (2) electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or perfluorinated benzene rings) attached via flexible linkers, (3) anion-π interactions between the silylium cation (acting as a strong Lewis acid that polarizes adjacent π-systems) and halide or tetrafluoroborate anions, (4) additional dispersion forces from the bulky substituents that guide capsule assembly. This represents an underexplored combination of main-group cation chemistry with supramolecular anion-π recognition, where the silicon center's tetrahedral geometry directs three-dimensional capsule formation rather than planar assemblies.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraorganylgermanium(IV) cations (R₄Ge⁺) that function as anion-π capsule-forming units. The germanium center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with four organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) that create a cationic, electron-deficient cavity. This cavity selectively binds anions (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, PF₆⁻) through a combination of electrostatic attraction and anion-π interactions with the π-systems of aromatic substituents. The synthon is modular: varying the substituents on germanium tunes cavity size, electron deficiency, and anion affinity. It can self-assemble into larger capsules or frameworks via additional weak interactions (C–H···anion, π–π stacking). This represents an underexplored extension of tetrahedral cation-anion-π chemistry to Group 14, offering distinct Lewis acidity and steric profiles compared to previously proposed ammonium, phosphonium, or iodonium analogues.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5_18_13
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a cationic ammonium core with four arms terminated in electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or pyridinium derivatives) that preorganize to form a capsule-like cavity. Anions (Cl-, Br-, PF6-, BF4-) are encapsulated through a combination of electrostatic attraction to the central cation and cooperative anion-π interactions with the surrounding electron-poor π-surfaces. This creates a three-dimensional recognition motif where the anion sits at the center of a tetrahedral array of π-acidic faces, stabilized by both charge-charge and anion-π forces. The synthon is modular—varying the aromatic panel and anion tunes binding affinity and selectivity. It maps to primitives: positive charge (ammonium), π-system (electron-deficient arenes), anion, 3D geometry (tetrahedral), and can be extended into dynamic/temporal systems via stimuli-responsive arms.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral germanium(IV) center (germonium cation, R₄Ge⁺) that acts as a cationic anchor point. The synthon exploits the combination of (1) electrostatic attraction between the positively charged germanium center and an electron-rich anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, PF₆⁻), and (2) synergistic anion-π interactions between the same anion and strategically positioned electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) built into the ligand framework. The rigid, three-dimensional arrangement of the aromatic panels around the central Ge⁺ creates a convergent binding pocket or 'capsule' that selectively encapsulates the anion via a cooperative multi-point interaction. This represents a novel extension of onium-cation-based supramolecular chemistry into the heavier Group 14 elements, leveraging the relatively underexplored chemistry of tetraorganogermonium cations and their potential for creating pre-organized, charge-assisted anion receptors.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_triflate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) triflate complexes that form anion-π capsules. The system features Ga³⁺ centers coordinated by three trifluoromethanesulfonate (triflate) anions and one neutral π-acidic aromatic ligand (e.g., hexafluorobenzene or s-tetrazine derivative) in a tetrahedral geometry. The electron-deficient Ga³⁺ center enhances the π-acidity of the coordinated arene, creating strong anion-π interactions with additional triflate anions in the second coordination sphere. These interactions lead to self-assembly into dimeric or tetrameric capsule structures where multiple Ga centers are bridged by shared triflate anions through both coordination bonds and anion-π contacts. The synthon exhibits directional recognition through: 1) metal-ligand coordination (Ga-O and Ga-π), 2) anion-π interactions between electron-deficient arenes and triflate oxygens, 3) electrostatic complementarity, and 4) shape-defined tetrahedral geometry enabling predictable capsule formation. This represents a novel combination of main-group metal coordination chemistry with supramolecular anion-π architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral organogermanium cations (R₄Ge⁺) that function as anion-π acceptors and capsule-forming building blocks. The synthon features a positively charged germanium center (germonium cation) with four organic substituents arranged tetrahedrally, creating an electron-deficient cavity. The electron-deficient π-surfaces of aromatic substituents (e.g., perfluorinated phenyl or electron-poor heteroaromatic groups) enable strong anion-π interactions with complementary anions (e.g., halides, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻). The tetrahedral geometry promotes self-assembly into dimeric or higher-order capsule structures through electrostatic complementarity and dispersion forces, encapsulating anion pairs or small molecules. This system combines pnictogen-bond-like character (Ge⁺ as electrophile) with anion-π interactions and geometric preorganization for supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_tris(8-hydroxyquinoline)_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular capsule synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) complexed with three 8-hydroxyquinoline ligands, creating a cationic metal-organic framework node with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The complex features: (1) tetrahedral Ga(III) center providing directional geometry, (2) three planar 8-hydroxyquinolate ligands arranged in propeller-like fashion creating concave electron-deficient π-surfaces, (3) cationic charge (+1) from Ga(III) center, (4) exposed Lewis acidic sites at the metal center, and (5) peripheral hydrogen-bonding capable hydroxyl groups. This synthon can engage in multiple interactions: anion-π interactions between anions and electron-deficient quinoline rings, cation-π interactions with additional cations, hydrogen bonding via hydroxyl groups, and metal coordination to additional ligands or anions. The tetrahedral geometry enables assembly into 3D capsule-like structures when combined with complementary anionic or π-donor components, suitable for host-guest chemistry and molecular encapsulation applications.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germonium cations (R4Ge+) that function as anion-π acceptors and capsule-forming building blocks. The germanium center, being larger than silicon and less explored than phosphorus/arsenic analogs, exhibits enhanced polarizability and distinctive tetrahedral geometry. The cationic charge is stabilized by electron-donating alkyl/aryl substituents, while the empty σ* orbitals of the Ge-C bonds and the overall cationic field create strong anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives or extended pyridinium rings). This synthon enables the construction of self-assembled coordination capsules via complementary electrostatic and anion-π interactions between the germonium vertices and anionic bridging units (e.g., tetrafluoroborate, carboxylates), creating a reversible, charge-assisted supramolecular assembly with potential for guest encapsulation and stimuli-responsive behavior.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features four positively charged nitrogen vertices arranged tetrahedrally, each bearing alkyl or aryl substituents, that electrostatically preorganize four electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-tetrazine derivatives) into a tetrahedral arrangement. These π-acidic panels engage in cooperative anion-π interactions with a central anion (e.g., chloride, bromide, or tetrafluoroborate) located at the capsule's interior. The recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic attraction between R4N+ and the anion, (2) anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient aromatics and the anion, (3) van der Waals contacts between substituents, and (4) possible C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from cation alkyl groups. This synthon maps to the seven primitives as: A (anion) as the guest, B (π-acidic surface) as the receptor panel, C (cationic center) as the organizing vertex, D (linker) as alkyl/aryl spacers, E (conformational preorganization) from tetrahedral geometry, F (cooperativity) from multiple simultaneous interactions, and G (complementarity) from size/shape matching of the anion to the cavity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_24
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silylium cations (R3Si+) that form encapsulation complexes with anions through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system consists of a silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., mesityl or t-butyl groups) to stabilize the highly electrophilic silylium cation, paired with an electron-deficient polyaromatic scaffold (such as perfluorinated coronene or hexaazatriphenylene) that provides multiple anion-π binding sites. The tetrahedral geometry of the silylium cation creates a directional electrostatic field that preorganizes the aromatic panels into a capsule-like arrangement, enabling selective anion recognition and encapsulation. This represents a novel extension of cation-anion-π chemistry into main-group element chemistry beyond the previously proposed phosphonium, arsonium, and iodonium systems, exploiting the unique Lewis acidity and tetrahedral geometry of silicon(IV) cations.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_25
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silylium cation (R3Si+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a positively charged silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., tert-butyl or aryl groups) that provide steric definition and prevent nucleophilic attack, while the fourth coordination site is occupied by a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., B(C6F5)4− or carborane anion). The electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes or cyanuric acid derivatives) are arranged in a tetrahedral geometry around the silylium center, creating a cavity that encapsulates the anion through multiple directional anion-π interactions. This represents a novel extension of tetrahedral cation-anion-π capsules into main-group element chemistry, exploiting the strong Lewis acidity and tetrahedral geometry of silylium ions—a relatively underexplored area compared to phosphonium, arsonium, or iodonium analogues. The synthon demonstrates clear recognition elements: (1) tetrahedral cationic silicon center, (2) electron-deficient π-systems as panels, (3) encapsulated anion, and (4) synergistic electrostatic and anion-π interactions. It maps to the seven primitives through charged species (cation/anion), directional non-covalent interactions (anion-π), defined geometry (tetrahedral), and encapsulation behavior.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_catecholate_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) center coordinated to two catecholate ligands, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped anion with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The catecholate oxygens provide strong hydrogen-bond acceptors, while the electron-deficient π-system of the gallium-bound catecholates enables anion-π interactions with electron-rich arenes. The tetrahedral geometry creates a concave, pre-organized cavity suitable for encapsulating small cations or neutral molecules through a combination of electrostatic, anion-π, and CH-π interactions. This system can act as a building block for self-assembled capsules or extended frameworks via coordination to additional metal centers or through hydrogen-bonding networks with complementary cationic or π-donor partners.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetravalent germanium(IV) centers forming cationic germyl species (R₃Ge⁺) that engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system consists of a tetrahedral germanium cation at each vertex of a capsule framework, with each Ge center bearing three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and one coordination site occupied by a labile ligand or solvent molecule that can be displaced. The cationic germanium centers create localized positive electrostatic potentials that enhance anion binding, while the electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, cyanophenyl, or triazine rings) between vertices provide complementary anion-π recognition sites. This creates a 3D capsule capable of encapsulating anions through combined electrostatic and π-acidic interactions, with the germanium centers also offering potential for further coordination expansion or dynamic ligand exchange. The synthon maps to primitives: (1) Ge⁺ as cationic electrophile, (2) anion as nucleophile, (3) electron-deficient π-system as polarizable surface, (4) tetrahedral geometry as structural scaffold, (5) labile ligands for temporal exchange, (6) capsule cavity as confinement space, and (7) synergistic multi-interaction recognition pattern.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that function as anion-π capsule-forming units. The system features: (1) a central silicon atom with three bulky aromatic substituents (e.g., mesityl or 2,6-diisopropylphenyl groups) to enforce tetrahedral geometry and provide π-surfaces, (2) a labile fourth position occupied by a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., [B(C₆F₅)₄]⁻ or [Al(ORF)₄]⁻) that can be displaced, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings on the substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) creating anion-π binding sites, and (4) preorganized cavity formation when two such silyl cations face each other, encapsulating an anion via cooperative anion-π interactions from multiple electron-deficient faces. This represents a novel extension of onium cation chemistry to silicon-based Lewis acidic cations, exploiting their strong electrophilicity and adjustable steric/electronic properties for anion recognition and encapsulation.

The system features a central ammonium cation with four alkyl/aryl arms, each terminating in an electron-deficient aromatic system (e.g., triazine, tetrazine, or perfluorinated benzene). These aromatic panels are oriented to create a concave, capsule-like cavity that can bind anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-, etc.) through cooperative anion-π interactions. The ammonium positive charge enhances anion binding affinity, while the tetrahedral geometry enforces a defined three-dimensional structure. Recognition elements include: (1) the cationic ammonium center for electrostatic attraction, (2) electron-deficient π-systems for anion-π interactions, and (3) the preorganized tetrahedral scaffold for encapsulation. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through: positive charge (electrostatic), π-system (polarizable surface), tetrahedral geometry (shape), anion binding (complementary interaction), and preorganization (constraint).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silylium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_26
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silylium cation (R3Si+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. This represents a novel extension of tetrahedral cation-anion-π capsules into main-group element chemistry with highly Lewis acidic, yet sterically shielded, silicon centers.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_silyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_15
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral silicon(IV) silyl cations (R₃Si⁺) that function as anion-π acceptors within a capsule framework. The synthon features a positively charged silicon center with three bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) creating a tetrahedral geometry, where the empty σ* orbital of the Si⁺ center acts as an electrophilic site for anion binding through σ-hole interactions. This cationic silicon center is integrated into a larger π-electron-deficient aromatic panel (e.g., perfluorinated arene or triazine) that provides additional anion-π interaction surfaces. The combination creates a three-dimensional, charge-assisted anion recognition pocket suitable for constructing self-assembled capsules through coordination with complementary anionic linkers or through dimerization with anionic species. The synthon is chemically realistic, drawing from known silylium ion chemistry and extended to supramolecular anion-π architectures, offering a distinct alternative to the previously proposed pnictogen and chalcogen-based cation capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) halonium cations (GeX₃⁺, where X = Cl, Br, I) that act as cationic vertices, interacting with electron-rich aromatic panels (e.g., hexaalkoxytriphenylenes or extended pyrenes) through anion-π interactions with bound halide counterions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻). The system self-assembles into a tetrahedral capsule where each face is defined by a planar π-system, each corner by a GeX₃⁺ center, and each edge by a combination of electrostatic attraction and halogen bonding between the germanium-bound halogens and the π-cloud of adjacent panels. The germanium center offers tunable Lewis acidity and halogen-bond donor ability distinct from lighter group 14 elements or earlier pnictogen-based capsules. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral GeX₃⁺ cations as structure-directing vertices, (2) planar electron-deficient or electron-rich aromatics as paneling units, (3) halide anions positioned above aromatic centers via anion-π interactions, and (4) secondary Ge–X···π halogen bonds stabilizing the assembly. This represents an unexplored combination of germanium-based hypervalent halogen bonding, anion-π contacts, and tetrahedral symmetry in capsule formation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_trifluoromethyl_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral gallium(III) centers coordinated to three trifluoromethyl groups and one labile site, creating a cationic host with strong anion-π interactions. The gallium center adopts tetrahedral geometry with three Ga-CF₃ bonds (σ-donor from carbon to empty p-orbital on Ga³⁺) and one coordination site occupied by a weakly-bound solvent molecule. The electron-deficient trifluoromethyl groups create a π-acidic cavity suitable for encapsulating anions via anion-π interactions. The labile fourth site allows for dynamic exchange, enabling adaptive recognition. This system combines p-block metal coordination chemistry with perfluoroalkyl groups to create a unique supramolecular capsule with programmable anion recognition properties.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_germyl_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral germanium(IV) germyl cations (R3Ge+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating self-assembled capsule architectures. synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_triflate_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2

This creates a directional, charge-assisted assembly motif where the triflate anions occupy three vertices of a tetrahedron and the arene occupies the fourth, leading to predictable capsule-like or framework architectures. The synthon exploits the high charge density of Ga(III), the weakly coordinating nature of triflate, and tunable π-donor strength, allowing for modular design of porous materials or host-guest systems.

synthons.name: chalcogen_bonded_selenocyanate_anion_π_rotaxane_synthon

synthons.name: temporal_redox_switchable_viologen_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A redox-active viologen (1,1'-disubstituted-4,4'-bipyridinium) core that switches between dicationic (V²⁺), radical cation (V⁺•), and neutral (V⁰) states through electrochemical or chemical reduction. In its dicationic state, it acts as a strong electron-deficient π-acceptor for anion-π interactions with anions like Cl⁻, Br⁻, or NO₃⁻. Upon one-electron reduction to the radical cation state, the anion-π interaction weakens significantly due to decreased π-acidity, while new radical-radical dimerization or π-π stacking interactions become possible. Full reduction to the neutral state eliminates anion binding entirely but enables strong π-π stacking of the now electron-rich aromatic system. This creates a temporally controlled, redox-switchable synthon where anion recognition, release, and subsequent self-assembly can be triggered on demand. The system includes recognition elements: electron-deficient π-surface (V²⁺), redox-active bipyridinium core, and complementary anions. It maps to primitives: electron transfer (redox switching), π-system (viologen core), electrostatic interaction (anion-π), and temporal control (state-dependent binding).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_schiff_base_anion_π_capsule_synthon_44

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_18_8

This synthon is chemically robust, air- and moisture-stable, and programmable through variation of R-groups and arene electronics.

This synthon exploits the underutilized germanium-based pnictogen bonding (Ge-centered σ-hole interactions) combined with anion-π effects, offering tunable cavity size and binding affinity through substituent variation on germanium and choice of aromatic panels. synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_stibonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_36
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral stibonium cations (R4Sb+) that function as anion-π capsule building blocks. This represents a novel extension of onium cation chemistry to heavier pnictogens (antimony) for designed supramolecular anion hosts.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_halonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_3

The recognition elements are: 1) the electrophilic silicon halonium cation (Si–X⁺), 2) the coordinated anion (A⁻), and 3) the electron-rich π-systems. The interaction pattern combines a strong, tunable halogen bond (Si–X⁺···A⁻) with three cooperative anion-π interactions (A⁻···π). This synthon features: 1) A tetrahedral borate anion core (B⁻) with three aryl substituents and one alkyl tether terminating in a quaternary ammonium group (N⁺R₃). 2) The electron-deficient, π-acidic faces of the fluorinated aryl rings (e.g., pentafluorophenyl) serve as potent anion-π recognition sites for complementary anions (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻). 3) The zwitterionic nature provides intrinsic charge neutrality while maintaining strong electrostatic fields for guest binding. 4) The system can form dimeric or higher-order capsules via synergistic anion-π interactions between the borate's aryl faces and anionic guests, with additional stabilization from cation-anion interactions between the tethered ammonium and external anions. 5) Recognition elements: tetrahedral borate anion, fluorinated π-acidic surfaces, cationic ammonium, and anion binding pockets. 6) Interaction patterns: anion-π (primary), electrostatic, hydrophobic, and potential C–H···π. 7) Mappable to all seven primitives: defined molecular framework (object), directional anion-π interactions (binding), encapsulation function (protection), potential for reversible guest exchange (regulation), modular substituents (adaptation), information encoded in shape/charge distribution (information), and capacity for assembly/disassembly (temporal).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_ester_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral borate esters with electron-deficient aromatic caps that create an anion-π capsule. The system features a central boron atom with three aryloxide ligands and one labile alkoxide ligand, forming a tetrahedral borate anion [B(OR)₃(OR')]⁻. This anion is encapsulated by two electron-deficient hexafluorobenzene rings positioned above and below the boron center via anion-π interactions with the negatively charged borate oxygen atoms. The aryloxide ligands contain ortho-fluorine substituents that provide additional C-F···π interactions with the capsule walls, while the labile alkoxide enables dynamic covalent chemistry and temporal control. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral borate anion as anionic hub, (2) electron-deficient arenes as π-acidic caps, (3) orthogonal C-F···π interactions for capsule stabilization, (4) dynamic B-O bond for temporal responsiveness. This system maps to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), borate anion (charge), arene caps (surface), fluorine substituents (handles), dynamic bond (switch), encapsulation (container), and anion-π interactions (binder).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_19_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage. The cation features four alkyl/aryl substituents arranged tetrahedrally around nitrogen, creating a positively charged core. This cation engages in synergistic interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction to electron-rich π-surfaces of host molecules, (2) C–H···π interactions from the cation's alkyl/aryl C–H bonds to electron-deficient arenes, and (3) potential anion-π interactions if counteranions are positioned near the aromatic walls. The π-capsule is constructed from multiple electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., triazine, pyromellitic diimide, or tetrafluorobenzene derivatives) that form a cavity through π-stacking and edge-to-face interactions. This system represents a charge-assisted supramolecular assembly with potential for selective encapsulation, molecular recognition, and stimuli-responsive release, mapping to primitives through its defined geometry, complementary electrostatic surfaces, and dynamic assembly/disassembly characteristics.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within a π-electron-rich aromatic cage, with anion binding at the exterior vertices. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral ammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium or a larger tetraalkylammonium) as the cationic center; (2) four convergent arene panels (e.g., 1,3,5-tris(4-pyridyl)benzene derivatives or extended pyrene-based walls) that form a capsule through edge-to-face and π-π stacking interactions, creating a complementary cavity for the ammonium ion; (3) cation-π interactions between the ammonium's positively charged nitrogen and the electron-rich π-surfaces of the cage interior; (4) anion binding sites at the exterior vertices where electron-deficient patches (e.g., fluorinated arenes or triazine rings) provide anion-π interactions with halides or oxoanions; (5) additional stabilization through C-H···π and van der Waals contacts. This synthon maps to the seven primitives via: (a) tetrahedral geometry (shape), (b) cationic and anionic charges (polarity), (c) aromatic π-systems (conjugation), (d) directional cation-π and anion-π interactions (directed bonding), (e) encapsulation (containment), (f) reversible assembly (dynamics), and (g) potential for redox-active components (reactivity). It represents an underexplored supramolecular motif combining cation-π and anion-π interactions in a single, structurally defined capsule.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage, with complementary anion binding sites. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or chiral variants like benzyltrimethylammonium) as the cationic core; (2) surrounding electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or perfluorinated naphthalene derivatives) that form an anion-π interaction network; (3) halide or tetrafluoroborate anions positioned at the vertices of the π-system cage through cooperative anion-π and C–H···anion interactions; (4) additional C–H···π interactions between the ammonium alkyl groups and the electron-deficient arenes; (5) potential for chiral recognition when using chiral ammonium cations; (6) tunable cavity size via arene substitution; (7) reversible assembly/disassembly under pH or solvent control. This represents an underexplored cation-anion-π ternary system with applications in selective anion sensing, chiral separation, and stimuli-responsive encapsulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_18_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage, with complementary anion binding sites. The system features: (1) a tetraalkylammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium or a functionalized derivative) as the cationic center; (2) multiple electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or nitrobenzene derivatives) arranged in a three-dimensional cage-like architecture through covalent or coordination linkages; (3) directional cation-π interactions between the ammonium cation and the electron-poor π-surfaces; (4) additional anion-binding sites (e.g., CH hydrogen-bond donors from alkyl groups, or Lewis acidic centers) positioned to capture an accompanying anion (Cl⁻, BF₄⁻, etc.), forming a stable ion-pair capsule. This synthon integrates electrostatic, cation-π, and hydrogen-bonding interactions, and is modular through variation of the ammonium substituents, π-acidic panels, and anion-binding motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation [R3B-L]+ (where R = aryl or alkyl, L = neutral Lewis base ligand like pyridine or THF) that engages in dual interaction modes: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the cationic boron center and (2) parallel-displaced anion-π interactions between the anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, Cl-) and the electron-deficient π-system of flanking aryl substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenyl, cyanophenyl) on the boron. The tetrahedral geometry creates a convergent binding pocket where the anion sits at the intersection of electrostatic attraction and multiple arene rings, mimicking a partial capsule. This system is chemically realistic with known boronium cation precedents, exploits underexplored boron-centered cation-anion-π cooperativity, and can be mapped to primitives: charge (cation/anion), shape (tetrahedral convergence), polarity (polarized B-L bond), π-system (electron-deficient arenes), H-bonding (absent here, but could be incorporated via functionalized aryl groups), metal coordination (boron as metalloid center), and redox (tunable by substituents).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) encapsulated within a π-electron-rich aromatic cavity, forming a cation-π capsule structure. The synthon features a quaternary ammonium center (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or a more elaborate tetraarylammonium) that engages in strong, directional cation-π interactions with the electron-rich faces of surrounding arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene, hexafluorobenzene derivatives, or extended pyrene panels). The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium cation provides a well-defined, three-dimensional recognition element, while the surrounding π-system acts as a complementary receptor. This interaction pattern can be mapped to the seven primitives: (1) the ammonium cation serves as an electrophilic site, (2) the π-system acts as a nucleophilic site, (3) the tetrahedral geometry defines spatial orientation, (4) the cation-π interaction provides attractive force, (5) the capsule-like arrangement creates a confined environment, (6) the system exhibits cooperativity through multiple simultaneous interactions, and (7) it can be extended into larger supramolecular architectures via additional non-covalent interactions (e.g., hydrogen bonding, halogen bonding) on functionalized arene peripheries. This synthon is distinct from previously proposed tetrahedral cation systems by focusing on the ubiquitous and highly tunable ammonium cation, which is fundamental in biological (e.g., choline, neurotransmitters) and materials chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral ammonium cations (R₄N⁺) that form encapsulation complexes with planar aromatic anions through a combination of electrostatic cation-anion attraction and anion-π interactions. The tetrahedral ammonium center (typically tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or functionalized variants) provides a positively charged core that attracts electron-rich planar anions like tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ⁻), tetracyanoethylene (TCNE⁻), or other extended π-systems with localized negative charge. The anion's π-system accepts additional stabilization from the ammonium's alkyl groups through C–H···π interactions, while the tetrahedral geometry creates a directional binding pocket. This synthon enables the construction of charge-assisted supramolecular capsules when combined with complementary anionic building blocks, and can be mapped to primitives: positive charge (electrostatic), tetrahedral geometry (shape), π-system (anion), directional interactions (C–H···π), and encapsulation (assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the encapsulation of a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R4N+) within a crown ether macrocycle. The recognition elements consist of: (1) the positively charged nitrogen center (electrophilic primitive), (2) four N–C bonds providing tetrahedral geometry (scaffold primitive), (3) multiple C–H bonds on the alkyl groups (donor primitive for weak hydrogen bonding), and (4) the crown ether oxygen atoms (nucleophilic primitive) that coordinate the cation via ion-dipole interactions. The interaction pattern involves size-selective inclusion, where the crown ether cavity diameter matches the ammonium ion's dimensions (e.g., 18-crown-6 for NH4+ or primary RNH3+). This system maps to the seven primitives through charge (electrophile/nucleophile pair), spatial arrangement (tetrahedral scaffold), and reversible binding (temporal domain via decomplexation kinetics). It represents an underexplored supramolecular motif in the catalog, distinct from the listed halogen/pnictogen-based capsules, focusing on classical host-guest chemistry with tunable selectivity via crown ether ring size and ammonium substituents.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation [R₃B-L]⁺ (where L is a neutral two-electron donor ligand like pyridine or THF) that engages in synergistic anion-π and cation-π interactions to form a capsule-like assembly. The cationic center features a boron atom in a formal +3 oxidation state with three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) and a fourth coordinate covalent bond to a Lewis base, creating a tetrahedral geometry and a localized positive charge. This cation can act as a dual interaction hub: (1) Its positively charged boron center can engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, s-triazines) on a complementary building block. (2) Simultaneously, the organic substituents on the boron (particularly if they are aryl groups like mesityl) can participate in cation-π interactions with electron-rich aromatic systems (e.g., naphthalene, anthracene) on another component. This combination, along with potential auxiliary interactions like C-H···π or van der Waals contacts, directs the assembly of a three-dimensional, capsule-like structure that can encapsulate small molecules or ions. The system is chemically realistic, drawing analogy to known triarylborane Lewis acids and their adducts, but explicitly leverages the underutilized boronium cation as a supramolecular tecton.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraalkylammonium cations (R4N+) encapsulated within electron-deficient aromatic π-surfaces, forming a cation-π interaction-driven capsule. The synthon features a tetrahedral ammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium) positioned within a concave, π-acidic aromatic cavity (e.g., hexafluorobenzene derivatives, tetracyanoquinodimethane-based macrocycles) through multiple directional cation-π interactions. The positive charge of the ammonium center is stabilized by the quadrupole moment of the electron-poor arenes, while the alkyl chains provide hydrophobic complementarity with the capsule walls. This system exhibits clear recognition elements: (1) the tetrahedral cation geometry matches the symmetric binding pocket, (2) electrostatic complementarity between cation and electron-deficient π-system, (3) size-dependent encapsulation selectivity. It can be mapped to the seven primitives through: atoms (N, C, H, F/CN groups), bonds (ionic, cation-π, van der Waals), angles (tetrahedral ~109.5°), dihedrals (rotatable alkyl chains), rings (aromatic panels), charges (+1 on N, partial charges on arenes), and non-covalent interactions (cation-π, hydrophobic effects). This represents an underexplored supramolecular motif combining ionic and aromatic recognition elements.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_zwitterion_anion_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral borate zwitterion with anionic character that engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces to form capsule-like assemblies. The core consists of a boron atom with three aryl substituents (e.g., pentafluorophenyl groups) and one anionic oxygen ligand (B-O⁻), creating a stable tetrahedral borate anion. This anionic borate is paired with a spatially separated cationic site (e.g., a remote ammonium or imidazolium group) within the same molecule, making it a zwitterion. The electron-deficient aryl groups on boron provide additional π-acidic surfaces. The primary recognition involves the anionic B-O⁻ moiety engaging in strong anion-π interactions with the face of an electron-poor aromatic ring (e.g., perfluorinated arene, triazine, or nitroaromatic) from a partner molecule. Secondary interactions include π-π stacking between the electron-deficient aryl groups on boron and complementary electron-rich aromatics, and electrostatic stabilization from the zwitterionic character. This combination directs the formation of dimeric or higher-order capsule-like structures with internal cavities suitable for guest encapsulation, representing a novel supramolecular motif distinct from purely cationic tetrahedral systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage. The system features a quaternary ammonium center (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or a more elaborate tetraarylammonium) that engages in electrostatic and cation-π interactions with a surrounding array of electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-trinitrobenzene, tetrafluoro- or tetracyanopyridine derivatives) arranged in a capsule-like geometry. The anion (e.g., PF6-, BF4-, or a halide) is positioned externally or at the portals of the capsule, participating in additional electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions with peripheral functional groups on the arene units. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) the cationic center, (2) the electron-deficient π-cavity, and (3) the accompanying anion, which together define a robust, charge-assisted supramolecular assembly unit. The synthon maps to primitives via: positive charge (cation), negative charge (anion), aromatic rings (π-system), hydrogen bond donors/acceptors (on anion or capsule periphery), and directional electrostatic/van der Waals interactions defining a specific spatial arrangement.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage, stabilized by synergistic anion-π and cation-π interactions. The system features a rigid tetrahedral cation (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or a more elaborate chiral variant) as the cationic core. This cation is surrounded by three or four electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-triazine derivatives) that form the walls of a supramolecular capsule or cage. The primary recognition elements are: 1) Anion-π interactions between the cationic nitrogen's localized positive charge and the π-acidic surfaces of the arenes. 2) Additional cation-π interactions between the alkyl substituents (R) of the ammonium ion and the same arene surfaces. 3) Potential edge-to-face CH-π interactions from the cation's alkyl groups. This creates a multi-point, three-dimensional recognition motif where the tetrahedral geometry of the cation is complemented by the spatial arrangement of the π-acidic panels. The synthon is chemically robust, operates in aprotic or low-polarity solvents, and can be used to direct the assembly of larger cage structures, molecular machines, or as a selective recognition element for ammonium species in sensing applications.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_2_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cations (R₄N⁺) that form encapsulation complexes with planar aromatic anions through combined electrostatic, cation-π, and anion-π interactions. The system features a tetrahedral cation (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or a chiral variant like benzyltrimethylammonium) that positions its four alkyl/aryl arms to create a partial hydrophobic pocket. This cation interacts with planar, electron-rich aromatic anions (such as tetraphenylborate, BPh₄⁻, or a substituted carboxylate with extended π-system like 1-naphthoate) through: (1) direct electrostatic attraction between N⁺ and the anion, (2) cation-π interactions between the ammonium's alkyl/aryl arms and the anion's π-system, and (3) potential anion-π interactions if the cation contains electron-deficient aromatic substituents. The tetrahedral geometry enforces a three-dimensional binding cavity that can selectively encapsulate specific anions based on size, shape, and π-electron density. This synthon is mappable to all seven primitives: atoms (N, C, H, B/O in anions), bonds (covalent C-N/C-H in cation, ionic/electrostatic), angles (tetrahedral ~109.5°), dihedrals (rotatable alkyl chains), planes (anion aromatic rings), centers of mass (cation core, anion centroid), and vectors (dipole moments, interaction axes).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_19_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cations (R₄N⁺) encapsulated within electron-deficient aromatic π-surfaces, forming a cation-π-anion sandwich motif. The system features a central NR₄⁺ cation (where R = methyl, ethyl, or benzyl groups) positioned between two parallel, electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-triazine derivatives) that provide complementary anion-π interactions with a coordinated halide or tetrafluoroborate anion positioned above one arene plane. This creates a three-layer recognition motif: anion-π (top), cation-π (middle), and additional electrostatic/van der Waals contacts with the alkyl substituents. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center ensures directional packing into extended frameworks or discrete capsules when combined with appropriate bridging ligands. The synthon is chemically robust, water-stable, and useful for constructing porous ionic crystals or supramolecular hosts for small molecules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetraalkylammonium cations (R4N+) that function as tetrahedral cationic centers with four alkyl arms, paired with electron-deficient aromatic systems (e.g., nitroaromatics, cyanuric acid derivatives, or perfluorinated arenes) that provide complementary anion-π interactions. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center creates a directional, charge-assisted recognition motif where the positively charged nitrogen is positioned above the π-face of the electron-deficient arene, while the four alkyl substituents (which can be tuned for sterics and solubility) help preorganize the system for encapsulation or capsule formation. This synthon exploits the underutilized combination of quaternary ammonium cations (common in phase-transfer catalysis and ionic liquids) with anion-π interactions—a less common supramolecular motif than cation-π. The system can be extended into dynamic or stimuli-responsive capsules by using redox-active or photoresponsive π-acceptors, enabling temporal control over capsule assembly/disassembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral ammonium cations (R4N+) encapsulated within crown ether macrocycles via ion-dipole interactions and hydrogen bonding. The system features a primary ammonium recognition site where the positively charged nitrogen accepts electron density from crown ether oxygen atoms (typically 18-crown-6 for primary ammonium or 15-crown-5 for smaller cations). The tetrahedral geometry creates directional N-H···O hydrogen bonds (3-4 interactions) complemented by electrostatic stabilization. This host-guest pair demonstrates high binding selectivity based on cation size, crown ether cavity diameter, and substituent sterics. The synthon can be mapped to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (shape), positive charge (polarity), hydrogen bond donors (N-H), and complementary hydrogen bond acceptors (crown ether oxygens). This represents a foundational supramolecular recognition motif with applications in molecular machines, sensors, and self-assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_ester_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral borate esters (B(OR)₄⁻ anions) encapsulated within electron-deficient aromatic π-surfaces. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral borate anion (e.g., B(OCH₃)₄⁻ or B(OPh)₄⁻) with four alkoxy/aryloxy substituents creating a spherical anion with localized negative charge; (2) a complementary electron-deficient aromatic capsule (e.g., hexafluorobenzene-based cyclophane or perfluorinated calixarene) providing multiple C-F···B⁻ and anion-π interactions; (3) directional C-H···O hydrogen bonds from the borate ester oxygen atoms to adjacent CH groups of the host; (4) size-selective encapsulation due to the match between the tetrahedral anion's van der Waals volume and the host cavity. This represents a novel anion recognition motif distinct from traditional Lewis acid-base adducts, exploiting both electrostatic and dispersion contributions for strong, selective binding in nonpolar media.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_2_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation [R3B-L]+ (where R = aryl or alkyl, L = neutral Lewis base ligand like pyridine or THF) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine derivatives) and electrostatic anion binding. The cationic boron center adopts tetrahedral geometry with a formal positive charge, creating a strong electrostatic anchor for anions (Cl-, BF4-, PF6-). The surrounding aromatic substituents on boron (e.g., mesityl, pentafluorophenyl) provide additional anion-π or π-π stacking surfaces. When combined with complementary electron-deficient aromatic panels in a capsule or cage architecture, this creates a multi-point recognition site: (1) electrostatic cation-anion, (2) anion-π between anion and electron-deficient arene, (3) potential π-π stacking between ligand aromatics, and (4) Lewis acid-base coordination at boron. This system is chemically realistic with known boronium cation syntheses and offers programmable cavity size via ligand and aromatic panel choice.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation [R3B-L]+ (where R = aryl or alkyl, L = neutral Lewis base ligand like pyridine or THF) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine derivatives) and electrostatic anion binding to a complementary anionic species (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, BArF-). The system forms a dynamic, reversible capsule-like assembly in solution, where the cationic boronium center acts as an electrostatic anchor, the anion provides charge balance and additional recognition, and the electron-deficient π-systems create a complementary binding pocket through cooperative anion-π and cation-π interactions. This represents an underexplored combination of boron-centered cations (boronium ions) with dual anion/π recognition motifs in supramolecular capsule formation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_anion_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral borate anion (e.g., B(CN)₄⁻ or B(aryl)₄⁻) that acts as a dual anion-π acceptor within a π-electron-rich capsule or tweezer structure. The synthon features: (1) a central tetrahedral boron anion with four electron-withdrawing substituents creating a region of positive electrostatic potential, (2) two or more electron-deficient faces that engage in simultaneous anion-π interactions with the π-systems of aromatic panels (e.g., triazine, tetrazine, or perfluorinated arenes), and (3) pre-organized aromatic panels that form a capsule or cleft via additional edge-to-face or π-π stacking interactions. This creates a cooperative, multi-point recognition motif where the anionic charge is stabilized by the electron-deficient π-clouds, a reversal of typical cation-π motifs. The system is chemically realistic, drawing from known weakly coordinating borate anions and electron-deficient aromatics, and can be mapped to primitives: A (tetrahedral boron center), B (anionic charge), C (π-system of panels), D (anion-π noncovalent interaction), E (pre-organized capsule geometry), F (cooperative binding), G (potential for dynamic assembly/disassembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage, forming a stable anion-π interaction complex. The system features a tetraalkylammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium or tetraethylammonium) where the positively charged nitrogen is surrounded by four alkyl groups, creating a spherical cation. This cation is selectively recognized by a preorganized receptor composed of multiple electron-deficient arenes (such as tetrafluorobenzene, cyanobenzene, or 1,3,5-triazine rings) arranged in a bowl or cage geometry. The primary interaction is anion-π (here effectively cation-π, but with the π-system acting as the electron-rich component relative to the cation's positive charge), supplemented by C–H···π interactions from the alkyl groups and potential electrostatic complementarity. The receptor's electron-deficient π-surfaces create a partial negative electrostatic potential pocket that attracts the cationic center, while the alkyl chains fill the cavity through van der Waals contacts. This synthon is chemically robust, water-stable, and useful for constructing cationic molecular capsules, ion-pair recognition systems, and functional supramolecular assemblies in aqueous or organic media.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces and electrostatic interactions with anions. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral ammonium core (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraalkylammonium, or benzyltrimethylammonium derivatives) providing cationic charge localization; (2) electron-deficient π-surfaces (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or nitroaromatic rings) positioned via flexible linkers to create a preorganized cavity; (3) encapsulated anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, BF₄⁻) stabilized by both electrostatic attraction to the ammonium center and anion-π interactions with the aromatic panels. This creates a three-dimensional recognition motif where the anion is sandwiched between the cationic center and electron-poor π-systems, mimicking enzyme active sites. The synthon maps to primitives: positive charge (ammonium), negative charge (anion), polarizability (π-system), hydrophobicity (alkyl/aryl groups), directional H-bond acceptors (anion), shape (tetrahedral + planar), and redox inactivity (stable ions).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage, with complementary anion binding sites. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or a more elaborate chiral derivative) as the cationic core; (2) a preorganized, concave electron-deficient aromatic scaffold (e.g., hexafluorobenzene-based macrocycles, perfluorinated cyclophanes, or triazine-based panels) that forms an anion-π capsule around the cation; (3) synergistic electrostatic and anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient π-surfaces and the ammonium cation's hydrogen atoms (C-H···π interactions, enhanced by cation polarization); (4) additional anion binding sites (e.g., Lewis acidic boron centers, halogen-bond donors, or hydrogen-bond donors) positioned at the capsule vertices to capture a complementary anion (e.g., Cl-, BF4-, PF6-), creating a stable ion-paired capsule. The primary recognition elements are: (1) cation-π interactions between the positively charged nitrogen and the π-faces of the electron-poor aromatics, (2) electrostatic complementarity between the cation and the partial negative electrostatic potential above the π-systems, and (3) shape complementarity of the tetrahedral cation with a tetrahedrally arranged π-cavity. This synthon maps to the seven primitives as: (1) tetrahedral geometry (ammonium center), (2) electrostatic interaction (cation-π), (3) shape recognition (capsule encapsulation), (4) directional preference (perpendicular approach of cation to π-face), (5) multivalency (multiple aromatic panels), (6) cooperativity (enhanced binding from multiple weak interactions), and (7) reversible assembly (dynamic encapsulation in solution). This represents an underexplored supramolecular motif distinct from the listed iodonium, phosphonium, and oxonium analogs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_13

The positively charged nitrogen interacts electrostatically with electron-rich anions (Cl-, Br-, PF6-, BF4-) positioned above the π-acidic surfaces, creating a synergistic cation-anion-π sandwich motif. This system exhibits directional recognition through combined electrostatic, anion-π, and van der Waals interactions, with potential for temporal control via pH-responsive ammonium formation/dissociation or redox-active π-systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_19_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage, stabilized by synergistic anion-π and cation-π interactions. The system features a rigid, shape-persistent organic cage composed of three electron-deficient 1,3,5-triazine panels linked by ethynylene spacers, creating a trigonal prismatic cavity. The tetra-n-butylammonium cation (Bu4N+) sits at the center, with its four alkyl chains extending into the corners of the cavity. The cationic nitrogen engages in strong anion-π interactions with the triazine rings, while the electron-deficient π-surfaces of the cage simultaneously engage in stabilizing interactions with a co-encapsulated tetrafluoroborate anion (BF4-) positioned above one triazine panel. This creates a three-component recognition motif: cation (R4N+), anion (BF4-), and electron-deficient π-cage, with all seven interaction primitives present: electrostatic (cation-anion), orbital (anion-π, cation-π), steric (shape complementarity), exchange (hydrophobic packing of butyl chains), dynamics (rotational freedom of butyl chains), field (quadrupole moment of triazine), and temporal (exchange dynamics of anion). The system represents a rare example of simultaneous stabilization of both cation and anion within the same π-acidic cavity.

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_diarylethene_π_π_stacking_synthon
synthons.description: A reversible photochromic molecular system based on diarylethene derivatives that undergo light-induced ring-closing/opening reactions, creating temporal switching of π-π stacking interactions. The open form features extended conjugation with thiophene or furan rings that enable strong face-to-face π-stacking between aromatic systems. Upon UV irradiation (λ~300 nm), the molecule undergoes a 6π-electrocyclization to form a closed, more planar, and highly conjugated structure with significantly enhanced π-stacking capability and red-shifted absorption. Visible light (λ>500 nm) reverses the process. Recognition elements include: (1) photochromic diarylethene core with heterocyclic aryl groups, (2) peripheral substituents (alkyl chains or polar groups) controlling solubility and stacking geometry, (3) complementary hydrogen bond acceptors/donors on peripheral positions for orthogonal interaction control. This temporal synthon enables time-programmable self-assembly, with the seven primitives mapped as: atoms (C, H, O, S in diarylethene), bonds (conjugated π-system, single/double bond switching), interactions (π-π stacking, van der Waals), topology (planar/non-planar switching), energy (photonic energy input), dynamics (ring-opening/closing kinetics), and function (temporal control of supramolecular assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_19_5
