The system features a tetrahedral ammonium cation (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium) positioned between two parallel, electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-triazine derivatives) that provide complementary anion-π interactions with an associated counteranion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, Cl⁻). This synthon is programmable through variation of alkyl substituents on nitrogen, electron-withdrawing groups on the arenes, and anion identity, enabling tunable assembly into capsules, grids, or layered structures. It maps to primitives: tetrahedral geometry (cation), electrostatic (+/-), π-system (arenes), directional H-bond-like alignment (cation-π/anion-π), and reversible association (supramolecular).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_27
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral ammonium cation (R4N+) that forms a capsule-like structure through synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces and electrostatic interactions with anions. The system features a quaternary ammonium center (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or a more elaborate chiral variant) positioned above a π-acidic aromatic platform (such as 1,3,5-triazine, tetracyanobenzene, or nitrobenzene derivatives). The cationic nitrogen's +1 charge creates a strong electrostatic field that polarizes the π-system, enhancing anion binding at the opposite face. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) cation-anion electrostatic attraction, (2) anion-π interaction with the electron-deficient arene, and (3) van der Waals/cavity encapsulation from substituents on the ammonium and arene units. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center provides directional control, while tunable aryl substituents allow for size-selective encapsulation of halide or oxoanions. This synthon is chemically robust, synthetically accessible, and can be incorporated into larger frameworks for anion sensing, transport, or templated assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation [R3B-L]+ (where R = aryl or alkyl, L = neutral Lewis base ligand like pyridine or THF) that engages in dual recognition: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the cationic boron center, and (2) parallel-displaced π-stacking interactions between the aromatic substituents (R) on boron and complementary electron-rich or electron-poor aromatic panels on a capsule-forming scaffold. The boronium center provides a strong, directional Coulombic anchor for anions (Cl-, BF4-, PF6-), while the appended aryl groups engage in programmed π-π interactions that guide assembly into a discrete capsule or cage architecture. This represents a novel combination of boron-centered cation-anion recognition with aromatic paneling for supramolecular assembly, distinct from previously proposed onium ions by using boron in its less common cationic coordination state.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_imidazolium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron center coordinated to two catecholate ligands, forming an anionic boronate complex that engages in synergistic anion-π and cation-π interactions with a complementary tetrahedral imidazolium cation. The boron anion features extended π-surfaces from the catecholate aromatic rings, which interact with the positively charged faces of the imidazolium's π-system. Simultaneously, the cationic imidazolium's hydrogen atoms (C2-H and N-H) engage in weak hydrogen bonds with the boronate oxygen atoms. This creates a three-dimensional, electrostatically complementary pair that can serve as a building block for self-assembled capsules or frameworks, where the boron anion acts as an electron-rich π-donor surface and the imidazolium cation as an electron-deficient π-acceptor surface. The system is chemically realistic, drawing from known boronate ester chemistry and imidazolium ionic liquids, and maps to primitives: donor/acceptor (anion/cation), positive/negative charge, π-system interactions, tetrahedral geometry, hydrogen bonding, and electrostatic complementarity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_19_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-system cage, stabilized by synergistic anion-π and cation-π interactions. The synthon features a central NR₄⁺ cation (where R can be methyl, ethyl, or aryl groups) positioned within a three-dimensional arrangement of electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-triazine derivatives) that form a π-acidic capsule. The negative electrostatic potential surface of the arenes engages in anion-π interactions with the positively charged nitrogen, while the cationic center simultaneously engages in cation-π interactions with the electron-rich faces of the arenes. This creates a dual-mode electrostatic encapsulation. The system can be further stabilized by peripheral anions (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, BArF⁻) occupying external sites through electrostatic complementarity. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (electrophilic center), (2) electron-deficient π-systems (nucleophilic surfaces via anion-π interactions), (3) complementary electrostatic fields, and (4) shape-persistent cavity for size-selective encapsulation. Mapped to primitives: donor/acceptor (π-system as acceptor, cation as donor), charged/charged (+, - electrostatic fields), container/contained (capsule/cation), and shape/shape (tetrahedral/concave complementarity).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_28
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R₄N⁺) encapsulated within an electron-deficient aromatic π-bowl (such as corannulene or sumanene derivatives) that simultaneously engages in anion-π interactions with a complementary anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or ClO₄⁻). The system features a three-component recognition motif: (1) cation-π interactions between the ammonium center and the concave π-surface of the bowl, (2) anion-π interactions between the anion and the convex π-surface of the same bowl, and (3) electrostatic complementarity between the cation and anion. This creates a stable, charge-separated capsule-like assembly driven by synergistic non-covalent forces. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center provides directional constraints, while the curvature of the π-bowl enhances binding through concave-convex π-surface complementarity. This synthon is particularly suitable for constructing charged supramolecular frameworks, ionic liquids with ordered structures, or molecular machines with redox-switchable encapsulation properties.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_anion_crown_ether_cation_π_capsule_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral borate anion (e.g., B(CN)₄⁻ or B(aryl)₄⁻) encapsulated within a π-rich cationic cage formed by two face-to-face, bowl-shaped tetra-cationic crown ether derivatives (e.g., tetracationic calix[4]arene or cyclotriveratrylene-based hosts with extended aromatic surfaces). Secondary interactions include electrostatic attraction between the anion and the host's cationic sites (often ammonium or pyridinium groups integrated into the crown ether framework), as well as C–H···anion hydrogen bonds and potential weak B–N dative interactions if cyanoborate is used. This system mimics enzyme-substrate binding pockets and is relevant for anion sensing, transport, and stabilization of reactive anions in confined spaces. It maps to the seven primitives via: (1) molecular recognition (anion-π, electrostatics), (2) defined geometry (tetrahedral anion in a complementary cavity), (3) reversible binding (supramolecular encapsulation), (4) cooperative interactions, (5) modular components (varying borates and host decorations), (6) environmental responsiveness (solvent/pH-dependent binding), and (7) potential for higher-order assembly into porous materials or capsules.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_anion_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the tetrahedral borate anion [B(OR)₄]⁻ (R = alkyl/aryl) as a guest, selectively bound within the cavity of a crown ether host (e.g., 18-crown-6) via multiple B–O···H–C hydrogen bonds and electrostatic stabilization. The tetrahedral geometry of the borate anion presents four oxygen atoms that can engage in CH···O hydrogen bonds with the crown ether's methylene protons, while the anionic charge is stabilized by the electron-rich ether oxygens. This represents a distinct anion recognition motif that differs from common metal cation–crown ether complexes. The synthon is chemically realistic, known in borate chemistry and supramolecular host–guest systems, and can be mapped to the seven primitives through its defined geometry, complementary electrostatic surfaces, and directional non-covalent interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_14

The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center enforces a well-defined, symmetric encapsulation motif, making it a robust building block for larger cage assemblies or porous frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_29

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_2_5

The system features a quaternary ammonium center (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or a more elaborate trialkylarylammonium) positioned inside a preorganized cavity formed by three or four parallel electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-triazine derivatives) that create an anion-π binding pocket. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center enforces a well-defined orientation of the surrounding π-walls and external binding sites.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_30

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_31

The system features a quaternary ammonium center (e.g., tetramethylammonium, choline derivative) as the cationic guest, which engages in strong, directional cation-π interactions with the electron-rich faces of arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-tris(4-pyridyl)-2,4,6-triazine or extended pyrene panels) in the host. The tetrahedral geometry of the ammonium center enforces a well-defined orientation within the cavity, while the π-acidic and π-basic panels in the cage provide orthogonal recognition sites. It maps to primitives: electrostatics (cation-anion), dispersion (π-π), directional H-bond-like (cation-π/anion-π), hydrophobicity (cavity inclusion), and constrained geometry (tetrahedral guest in defined cavity).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6_15

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_diarylethene_π_acid_base_synthon_pair

This creates a temporally controlled synthon pair where the dominant non-covalent interaction (anion-π vs cation-π) can be switched reversibly with light, enabling dynamic control of molecular assembly and disassembly. Recognition elements include the photochromic core, complementary substituents for tuning electron density, and planar aromatic surfaces for π-interactions. The system maps to all seven primitives: atoms (C, H, O, N, S), bonds (conjugated π-system, single/double bond switching), angles (planar vs non-planar conformations), torsion (ring-opening/closing), non-covalent interactions (π-π, anion-π, cation-π), charges (partial charges redistributed upon switching), and dynamics (light-induced conformational changes).

The synthon is chemically robust, widely tunable via substitution on both the ammonium and arene components, and relevant to areas like anion sensing, crystal engineering, and supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_diarylethene_anion_π_synthon_switch

The closed-ring form features an extended π-conjugated system with electron-deficient character, enabling strong anion-π interactions with halide anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻). The open-ring form lacks this extended conjugation and exhibits minimal anion binding. Recognition elements include: (1) the photochromic diarylethene core with thiophene or thiazole rings, (2) electron-withdrawing substituents (e.g., -CF₃, -CN) to enhance anion affinity in the closed form, and (3) complementary electrostatic and polarization interactions. This system maps to temporal primitives through light-triggered conformational switching that modulates binding affinity over time, creating a dynamic host-guest system with potential for molecular sensing, information storage, or gated catalysis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon_7

The crown ether (typically 18-crown-6 or 15-crown-5) wraps around the cation through cooperative N⁺···O interactions, forming a stable host-guest complex. This system exhibits high binding selectivity based on crown ether cavity size and ammonium ion diameter. The outer periphery of both components can be decorated with additional recognition elements (hydrogen bond donors/acceptors, π-systems, or hydrophobic groups) for hierarchical assembly. The tetrahedral geometry provides directional control, while the ion-dipole interactions offer strong, reversible binding typical of supramolecular chemistry.

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_spiropyran_merocyanine_zwitterion_synthon_2
synthons.description: A light-responsive molecular system based on spiropyran that undergoes reversible photoisomerization to merocyanine form. The closed spiropyran (colorless, nonpolar) converts under UV light to open merocyanine (colored, zwitterionic) with extended π-conjugation and intramolecular charge separation. The transformation creates temporal switching between: (1) neutral closed form with weak dispersion interactions, (2) zwitterionic open form capable of dipole-dipole interactions, salt bridges, and enhanced π-stacking. Recognition elements include: phenolate oxygen (hydrogen bond acceptor), indolinium nitrogen (hydrogen bond donor), extended conjugated system (π-π stacking), and zwitterionic charge distribution (electrostatic interactions). The system can be mapped to all seven primitives: atoms (C, N, O), bonds (covalent bonds in both forms), angles (tetrahedral sp³ vs. planar sp² regions), dihedrals (conformational flexibility), charges (formal charges in open form), polarization (π-conjugation changes), and dispersion (aromatic stacking). This represents a temporal synthon with time-dependent interaction patterns controlled by light exposure.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_anion_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon_2

The tetrahedral geometry of the borate anion presents four electronegative vertices (cyanide or fluoride) that engage in directional, non-covalent interactions with the inward-pointing C–H groups of the crown ether's ethylene bridges. This creates a well-defined, charge-assisted host-guest complex stabilized by electrostatic and dispersion forces. The synthon is modular: the borate anion's substituents (CN, F, OAr, etc.) tune guest size and basicity, while crown ether ring size and substitution control cavity fit and preorganization. It maps cleanly to the seven primitives: the borate anion acts as a polyvalent anionic acceptor (primitive: anion), the crown ether as a neutral macrocyclic donor (primitive: host), with interaction primitives including hydrogen bonds (C–H···X), electrostatic attraction, and geometric complementarity (tetrahedral-in-cavity). This represents an underexplored, charge-assisted variant of crown ether chemistry moving beyond metal cations to polyatomic anions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_anion_crown_ether_host_guest_synthon_3

The borate anion acts as a spherical, charge-dense guest. The primary recognition elements are (1) electrostatic attraction between the anion's negative charge and the electron-rich, dipolar ether oxygens of the crown, and (2) size-complementarity between the anion's van der Waals radius and the crown's cavity (e.g., B(CN)₄⁻ with 18-crown-6). The tetrahedral geometry prevents close ion-pairing with typical cations, making it available for crown capture. It represents an underexplored anion recognition motif distinct from common cation-crown systems.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_16_1

The cationic boron center adopts a tetrahedral geometry with three organic substituents (alkyl/aryl) and one labile donor ligand. This synthon combines: (1) electrostatic attraction between the boronium cation and an anionic partner (e.g., BF4-, PF6-), (2) anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-deficient arenes, (3) potential C-H···anion contacts from the cation's substituents, and (4) π-π stacking between electron-deficient panels. The system can form dimeric or cage-like capsules where the boronium cations occupy vertices, anions sit near aromatic faces, and the overall assembly is stabilized by complementary electrostatic and dispersion forces. This represents a novel entry in supramolecular boron chemistry, distinct from classical boronate esters or anionic boronates, leveraging underutilized boronium cations as structure-directing supramolecular cations.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_ammonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_4_32
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral quaternary ammonium cation (R4N+) encapsulated within a π-electron-rich aromatic cage, with anion binding at the exterior vertices. This synthon is distinct from previously proposed tetrahedral cations by using ammonium (not B, Si, P, I, etc.) and combining interior cation-π with exterior anion binding in a π-capsule architecture.

The synthon features a quaternary ammonium center (e.g., tetramethylammonium, tetraethylammonium, or a more elaborate chiral variant) as the cationic core. The primary recognition elements are: 1) anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient π-surfaces and the diffuse electron density of the ammonium's counteranion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or a halogen-bond acceptor anion), and 2) cation-π interactions between the same π-surfaces and the positively charged nitrogen center. This synthon is chemically realistic, drawing from known host-guest chemistry of ammonium ions in macrocycles and extended cages, but uniquely combines cation-π and anion-π interactions within a single, well-defined π-capsule architecture. It can be mapped to the seven primitives via its ionic (cation/anion) and arene components, directional non-covalent interactions, and potential for temporal control via pH-switchable ammonium formation/cleavage or redox-active π-panels.

The tetrahedral geometry provides predictable directional preferences, while the tunable substituents on phosphorus allow for steric and electronic modulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7_1

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that acts as a cationic π-capsule host for anions. The system features four aromatic substituents (e.g., phenyl, naphthyl) attached to phosphorus, creating a tetrahedral arrangement of π-surfaces. These electron-deficient aromatic rings (enhanced by the positive charge on phosphorus) create a convergent anion-π binding pocket capable of encapsulating small anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through cooperative multipoint anion-π interactions. The synthon exhibits clear recognition elements: (1) the tetrahedral cationic core (electrostatic anchor), (2) four oriented π-acidic aromatic panels (anion-π recognition), and (3) tunable substituents for cavity size/electronics control. It maps to the seven primitives through: 1) tetrahedral geometry (shape), 2) phosphonium center (charge), 3) aromatic rings (π-system), 4) anion binding (electrostatics), 5) convergent cavity (confinement), 6) substituent variation (modularity), and 7) reversible anion encapsulation (dynamics). This represents a distinct variation from the listed phosphine oxide anion capsule (which is anionic) and explores the underexplored supramolecular domain with anion-π interactions in a tetrahedral capsule architecture.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7_2

The telluronium center provides a strong, directional positive charge due to the large, polarizable tellurium atom, creating a potent cation for anion binding. The system exhibits enhanced binding compared to lighter chalcogen analogs (S, Se) due to tellurium's increased polarizability and softer Lewis acidity. Recognition elements include: (1) the telluronium cationic center for electrostatic attraction, (2) electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorophenyl, trifluoromethylphenyl) for anion-π interactions, (3) preorganized tetrahedral geometry for cavity formation, and (4) tunable substituents for size/complementarity matching. This represents an underexplored heavy chalcogen variant in supramolecular capsule chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that forms a complementary electrostatic and anion-π interaction network with electron-deficient aromatic panels. This cation acts as a guest or structural node that interacts with concave, electron-poor aromatic surfaces (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, triazine rings, or nitroaromatics) which serve as anion-π receptors. The combination of Coulombic attraction between the cation and surrounding anions (if present) or directly with the electron-deficient π-clouds, along with potential C–H···π and van der Waals contacts, enables the formation of dimeric or cage-like capsules. The tetrahedral geometry directs the assembly toward 3D architectures, making it useful for constructing porous materials, molecular containers, or selective recognition sites. This system maps to the primitives: charge (positive), shape (tetrahedral), polarity, aromaticity (electron-deficient), hydrogen bonding (weak C–H donors), van der Waals, and electrostatic complementarity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) encapsulated within an electron-rich aromatic π-bowl or π-cage. The synthon features: (1) a central tetrahedral phosphonium cation with four organic substituents (alkyl/aryl), creating a well-defined cationic charge center; (2) an electron-rich aromatic host system (e.g., corannulene derivatives, cyclotriveratrylene analogs, or curved polyaromatic hydrocarbons) that forms an anion-π interaction with the cation—where the cationic phosphorus sits above the π-face of the electron-rich arene; (3) additional secondary interactions such as C–H···π contacts from the phosphonium alkyl/aryl groups to the host periphery, and potential weak hydrogen bonds from host functional groups (e.g., methoxy, methyl) to the cation's C–H bonds; (4) the assembly forms a 'capsule-like' environment where the cation is partially enclosed by the concave π-surface, preorganizing the system for further supramolecular aggregation or incorporation into larger frameworks. This synthon is chemically distinct from the listed phosphine oxide anion variant and other tetrahedral cation examples, exploiting anion-π interactions with a permanent cationic center rather than an anionic one.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that acts as a cationic anchor point for anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or other π-acidic arenes) are arranged in a capsule-like geometry through covalent or coordination linkages, creating a preorganized cavity. Recognition elements include: (1) anion-π interactions between the phosphonium-bound anion (e.g., Cl⁻, BF₄⁻) and electron-deficient aryl rings, (2) electrostatic stabilization from the cationic center, (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from alkyl/aryl substituents, and (4) geometric preorganization from the tetrahedral phosphorus center enforcing a three-dimensional binding pocket. This synthon maps to the seven primitives through its charged centers (anion, cation), directional non-covalent interactions (anion-π), conformational preference (tetrahedral geometry), and ability to form higher-order assemblies via secondary interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_13
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphonium cations (R₄P⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating capsule-like architectures. The cationic phosphorus center provides a permanent +1 charge with tetrahedral geometry, while electron-deficient arenes (e.g., hexafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or tetrafluoropyrazine) serve as π-acidic surfaces that attract anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, PF₆⁻, etc.) through anion-π interactions. This system can be extended into 3D frameworks or molecular capsules by linking multiple phosphonium-arene units, enabling encapsulation of anion pairs or small molecules. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral phosphonium cation (electrostatic, hydrophobic), (2) electron-deficient π-system (anion-π acceptor), (3) anions (anion-π donor), and (4) optional auxiliary interactions (C–H···anion, π–π stacking). Mappable to primitives: charge (cation/anion), geometry (tetrahedral/planar), polarity, aromaticity, and coordination preference.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral telluronium cations (R₃Te⁺) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems, creating capsule-like architectures. The telluronium center exhibits strong σ-hole characteristics due to the heavy tellurium atom, enabling directional electrostatic interactions with anions. Simultaneously, the cationic telluronium's electron-deficient nature allows it to act as an anion-π acceptor with π-basic aromatic systems. This dual interaction capability enables the formation of three-dimensional capsule structures where telluronium cations bridge between anions and aromatic panels. The synthon features: (1) tetrahedral telluronium cation as electrostatic hub, (2) directional anion-σ-hole(tellurium) interactions, (3) complementary anion-π interactions with electron-rich aromatics, (4) potential for chalcogen bonding from tellurium, (5) encapsulation of anions within π-rich cavities, (6) tunable sterics via organic substituents on tellurium, and (7) redox-active tellurium centers for potential temporal control. This represents a novel heavy chalcogen variant of onium cation synthons with enhanced polarizability and interaction strength compared to lighter analogs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral telluronium cations (R3Te+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, creating self-assembled capsule architectures. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional positive charge due to the hypervalent nature of tellurium(IV), while the organic substituents (typically aryl groups with electron-withdrawing substituents) create π-acidic surfaces. These synthons combine: (1) electrostatic attraction between telluronium cation and anions, (2) anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-deficient arenes, (3) hydrophobic effects from organic substituents, and (4) geometric complementarity for capsule formation. The telluronium motif is chemically stable in non-reducing conditions and offers distinct properties from lighter chalcogen analogs due to tellurium's larger size, polarizability, and distinct coordination preferences.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral telluronium cations (R₃Te⁺) that form anion-π capsules with complementary electron-deficient aromatic panels. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional positive charge for anion binding, while its tetrahedral geometry directs three organic arms toward electron-deficient π-systems (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, triazines, or nitroaromatics). The synthon combines (1) electrostatic anion binding to Te⁺, (2) anion-π interactions between the encapsulated anion and the electron-deficient panels, (3) hydrophobic/fluorophilic effects from perfluoroaryl groups, and (4) geometric preorganization from the tetrahedral core. This creates a reversible, self-assembled capsule capable of selectively binding anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) via synergistic interactions. The telluronium moiety is chemically stable in non-reducing conditions and offers a heavier chalcogen analog to sulfonium/selenonium systems, with potentially stronger anion affinity and distinct stereoelectronic properties.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_7_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral telluronium cations (R3Te+) that form anion-π capsules with complementary electron-deficient aromatic panels. The telluronium center provides a permanent positive charge and tetrahedral geometry, while its polarizable tellurium atom enables secondary Te···π interactions. The system employs planar, electron-deficient arenes (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or s-tetrazine derivatives) as π-acidic walls that encapsulate anions (Cl-, Br-, NO3-) via cooperative anion-π and cation-π interactions. The telluronium's alkyl/aryl arms provide structural directionality, and the assembly is stabilized by additional C-H···anion and edge-to-face π-stacking between aromatic panels. This represents a heavier chalcogen analog of sulfonium/selenonium systems with enhanced polarizability and distinct coordination geometry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_telluronium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral telluronium cations (R3Te+) that form anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic capsules. The telluronium center exhibits strong σ-hole characteristics due to the heavy chalcogen, enabling directional electrostatic interactions with anions. The system combines: (1) tetrahedral telluronium cations as σ-hole donors, (2) electron-deficient perfluorinated aromatic panels (e.g., octafluoronaphthalene or decafluorobiphenyl) as anion-π acceptors, and (3) bridging anions (Cl-, Br-, BF4-) that mediate between cationic tellurium centers and π-acidic surfaces. This creates a three-component recognition motif where the telluronium's positive charge enhances both anion binding and π-acidity complementarity. The heavy atom effect of tellurium introduces potential redox-switchable behavior and distinctive NMR handles (125Te). This synthon maps to primitives: positive charge (telluronium), negative charge (anion), π-system (electron-deficient arene), tetrahedral geometry, directional electrostatic interaction, and potential temporal redox switching.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphonium cations (R₄P⁺) that engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features: (1) tetrahedral phosphonium cations as cationic recognition elements with well-defined geometry, (2) electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, cyanuric acid derivatives, or triazine panels) as π-acidic surfaces, (3) electrostatic complementarity where the positively charged phosphorus center directs anion binding while the aromatic panels provide additional stabilization through anion-π interactions, and (4) potential for capsule assembly through multiple such interactions forming a three-dimensional network. This represents an underexplored combination of pnictogen-based cations (phosphonium rather than ammonium or sulfonium) with anion-π motifs, creating a charge-assisted supramolecular building block suitable for self-assembly into capsules, cages, or extended frameworks.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_capsule_synthon_15
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on tetrahedral phosphonium cations (R₄P⁺) that engage in dual anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels, forming capsule-like architectures. The synthon combines: (1) tetrahedral phosphonium cation as cationic center, (2) electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or nitroaromatics) as π-acidic panels, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the cation's counteranion (Cl⁻, Br⁻, BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) and the arene panels, and (4) additional C–H···anion or C–H···π contacts from alkyl/aryl substituents on phosphorus. This creates a three-dimensional recognition motif where the anion bridges between the cationic phosphorus center and the electron-deficient π-systems, leading to predictable assembly into dimeric capsules or extended networks. The tetrahedral geometry of P⁺ provides structural rigidity, while tunable aryl substituents allow control over cavity size and binding affinity.

synthons.name: cavitand_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on deep cavitands with electron-deficient aromatic panels that create a preorganized binding pocket for anions via multiple anion-π interactions. The system features tetraoxacalix[2]arene[2]triazine cavitands with electron-withdrawing nitro and cyano substituents on the triazine rings, creating a convergent array of positive electrostatic potentials on the interior aromatic surfaces. This synthon exhibits selective binding of polyatomic anions (sulfate, phosphate, carboxylates) through cooperative anion-π interactions, complemented by weak C-H···anion hydrogen bonds from methylene bridges. The bowl-shaped architecture provides spatial organization and enhanced binding affinity through the multivalent effect, representing a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic aromatic systems are engineered to be π-acidic for anion recognition.

synthons.name: tetrazine_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the strong anion-π interaction between electron-deficient 1,2,4,5-tetrazine aromatic systems and anions. The tetrazine core possesses a significant quadrupole moment with a π-electron-deficient surface, creating a strong electrostatic attraction for anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻, NO₃⁻, etc.). Recognition elements include the electron-deficient aromatic ring (π-acidic) and the anion (electron-rich). Interaction patterns involve the anion positioning above the plane of the tetrazine ring, stabilized by electrostatic, charge-transfer, and polarization effects. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic arenes interact with cations; here the π-acidic arene attracts anions. It can be mapped to the seven primitives: donor (anion lone pair), acceptor (tetrazine π* orbital), linker (covalent framework holding tetrazine), insulator (alkyl spacers if needed), descriptor (anion binding constant), stereochemistry (planar recognition surface), and reactivity (anion transport or catalysis).

synthons.name: selenocyanate_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the interaction between a selenocyanate anion (SeCN⁻) and an electron-deficient aromatic π-system. The selenium atom in SeCN⁻ acts as a dual-character recognition element: (1) as a soft, polarizable Lewis base that can engage in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, s-triazine, or nitroaromatics), and (2) as a potential chalcogen bond donor via its σ-hole along the C–Se axis, allowing orthogonal interactions with additional Lewis bases. This creates a directional, modular synthon where the SeCN⁻ anion bridges between an electron-poor π-system (anion-π) and a complementary Lewis basic site (chalcogen bond), enabling programmable 2D or 3D assembly. The synthon is chemically robust, synthetically accessible, and offers tunability through variation of the π-acceptor strength and the chalcogen bond acceptor.

synthons.name: boron_dipyrromethene_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on BODIPY (boron dipyrromethene) fluorophores that function as π-acidic recognition sites for anions. The electron-deficient boron center and extended π-conjugated system create a strong electrostatic potential surface complementary to anions. The synthon features: (1) a central tetracoordinate boron atom with two fluorine atoms creating a Lewis acidic site, (2) a rigid, planar dipyrromethene framework providing extended π-acidic surface, (3) meso-position substituents (typically aryl groups) that can be functionalized to tune electron deficiency and sterics, and (4) methyl groups at the 1,3,5,7 positions providing solubility and preventing aggregation. This system exhibits strong anion-π interactions with halides, oxyanions, and carboxylates, with binding constants in the range of 10²-10⁴ M⁻¹ in organic solvents. The planar geometry allows for predictable directional interactions, making it useful for constructing supramolecular assemblies, sensors, and anion-responsive materials.

synthons.name: iodonium_zwitterion_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on iodonium zwitterions engaging in cooperative anion-π and charge-assisted interactions. The system features a rigid, electron-deficient polycyclic aromatic scaffold (e.g., naphthalenediimide or pyromellitic diimide core) substituted with a positively charged iodonium group (Ar-I⁺-R, where R is an alkyl tether linking to the π-scaffold). This creates a zwitterion with a localized positive charge adjacent to an electron-deficient π-surface. The synthon operates through two simultaneous recognition events: (1) anion binding to the iodonium center via strong electrostatic and charge-transfer interactions, and (2) anion-π interaction with the electron-deficient aromatic plane, enhanced by the proximal positive charge. This creates a convergent, chelate-like binding pocket for anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻, carboxylates). The iodonium moiety also offers potential for temporal control via reductive elimination or ligand exchange. The seven primitives map clearly: electron-deficient π-system (acceptor), iodonium (electrophile/cation), anion (nucleophile), tether (connector), with cooperativity creating emergent binding affinity and selectivity—a supramolecular umpolung where the typically π-basic anion interacts with a π-acidic surface guided by charge complementarity.

synthons.name: calixarene_anion_π_halogen_bond_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon combining three distinct non-covalent interactions within a calix[4]arene scaffold: (1) anion-π interactions between electron-deficient tetrafluorophenyl groups at the upper rim and anionic guests (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻), (2) halogen bonding from iodotetrafluorophenyl groups (C–I⋯X⁻) to enhance anion binding affinity and selectivity, and (3) preorganized cavity geometry from the calixarene cone conformation that provides spatial complementarity. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using typically π-electron-rich aromatic surfaces rendered electron-deficient through perfluorination to attract anions rather than cations. This triple-interaction motif creates a cooperative binding site where halogen bonds orient and preorganize the anion for optimal anion-π contact, enabling recognition of anions in competitive media with potential applications in sensing and extraction.

synthons.name: phosphonium_cation_π_anion_π_sandwich_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon featuring a central tetraarylphosphonium cation with electron-deficient aromatic rings that engage in simultaneous anion-π interactions with two different anions positioned above and below the π-system. The system exploits the strong electron-withdrawing effect of the phosphonium center to create an exceptionally electron-deficient π-surface, enabling cooperative binding of anions like tetrafluoroborate or hexafluorophosphate. The synthon exhibits a sandwich-like architecture where the cationic π-system acts as a dual-face receptor, with the anions positioned at optimal distances (3.0-3.5 Å) from the aromatic plane. Recognition elements include: (1) the electron-deficient aryl rings of the phosphonium cation, (2) the electrostatic complementarity between cation and anions, and (3) potential secondary C-H···anion hydrogen bonds from ortho-substituents. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-π interactions are favored, but here the cationic center creates enhanced anion-π binding.

synthons.name: telluroxane_anion_π_chalcogen_bond_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on the cooperative interaction between a telluroxane moiety (R-Te=O) and electron-deficient aromatic systems. The tellurium(IV) center in telluroxanes exhibits strong σ-hole characteristics perpendicular to the Te=O bond, creating a potent chalcogen bond donor site. This electrophilic region interacts with electron-rich anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through chalcogen bonding, while the oxygen of the Te=O group engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluoropyridine, trinitrobenzene). The system creates a three-point recognition motif: (1) Te···anion chalcogen bond (2.8-3.2 Å), (2) anion···π interaction with electron-deficient arene (3.0-3.5 Å), and (3) potential secondary Te···O/N interactions. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically π-basic aromatic system becomes π-acidic, cooperating with the main-group chalcogen bond to create a robust anion recognition pocket. The synthon is chemically realistic as telluroxanes are known stable compounds, and their chalcogen bonding capabilities have been experimentally demonstrated, though not yet systematically combined with anion-π interactions in designed synthons.

synthons.name: tetrathiafulvalene_radical_cation_anion_π_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular redox-active synthon based on tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) derivatives where the TTF radical cation (TTF•+) generated by partial oxidation engages in strong, directional anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The TTF core provides reversible redox behavior (temporal domain), while the planar, electron-rich radical cation exhibits enhanced electrostatic complementarity with anions compared to neutral TTF. Recognition elements include: (1) the TTF radical cation's positively charged, planar π-surface, (2) electron-deficient aromatic acceptors (e.g., perfluorinated arenes, nitroarenes, or s-triazines), and (3) potential secondary S•••anion chalcogen bonds from the sulfur atoms. This system enables supramolecular assembly driven by redox-switchable anion binding, with applications in molecular electronics and stimuli-responsive materials. The seven primitives map clearly: donor (TTF•+ π-system), acceptor (electron-deficient π-system), interaction (anion-π plus potential chalcogen bonds), geometry (planar stacking), environment (redox-controlled), dynamics (reversible oxidation/binding), and function (redox-switchable assembly).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_anion_π_cavitand_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral borate anion (e.g., B(CN)₄⁻, BF₄⁻, or BPh₄⁻) encapsulated within an electron-deficient, π-acidic cavitand host. The primary recognition elements are: 1) multiple, cooperative anion-π interactions between the negatively charged borate vertices and the electron-deficient aromatic panels of the cavitand (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene, triazine, or pyrazine walls), and 2) geometric complementarity where the tetrahedral anion fits into a pre-organized tetrahedral or pyramidal binding pocket. Secondary stabilization can come from C-H···anion interactions from the cavitand's methylene bridges or rim substituents. This represents a supramolecular umpolung, as the typically repulsive anion-π interaction is harnessed for selective binding through multipoint contact and cavity pre-organization. It maps to the primitives as: A (anion), D (π-system), E (cavity/concave shape), F (directional electrostatic interactions), and G (pre-organized geometry).

synthons.name: zwitterionic_phosphonium_carboxylate_anion_π_sandwich_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a zwitterionic phosphonium carboxylate unit that simultaneously engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes. The system features a positively charged tetraalkylphosphonium cation covalently linked to a carboxylate anion via a short alkyl tether (e.g., -CH2-CH2-), creating an intramolecular zwitterion. The anionic carboxylate group is positioned to engage in strong, directional anion-π interactions with the face of an adjacent electron-deficient aromatic ring (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine, tetrafluorobenzene, or nitrobenzene). This creates a sandwich-like motif where the π-acidic arene is positioned between the anionic carboxylate (above) and the cationic phosphonium (below, via the tether), resulting in a synergistic electrostatic and polarization-driven assembly. Recognition elements include: (1) the zwitterion's dipole and charge complementarity, (2) the geometrically constrained anion-π interaction, and (3) potential auxiliary C-H···O or C-H···π contacts. This synthon enables the programmed assembly of charge-assisted supramolecular architectures and represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic arenes are avoided in favor of π-acidic partners.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_anion_π_cage_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that acts as a cationic scaffold for anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels. The system features a rigid tetrahedral geometry with four aromatic arms (e.g., pentafluorophenyl or cyanophenyl groups) extending from the phosphorus center, creating a convergent, cage-like electrostatic environment. Each arm engages in simultaneous anion-π interactions with a single encapsulated anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) positioned near the centroid of the tetrahedron. Recognition elements include: (1) the permanent positive charge on phosphorus for electrostatic preorganization, (2) electron-deficient π-systems on each arm for anion binding, and (3) tetrahedral symmetry enabling multivalent, cooperative interactions. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-binding π-systems are inverted to bind anions, and the phosphonium core prevents collapse via steric and electrostatic repulsion. Mappable primitives: positive charge (phosphonium), π-system (electron-deficient arenes), tetrahedral geometry (scaffold), anion (guest), multivalency (four interactions), complementarity (convergent electrostatic surfaces), and preorganization (rigid cage).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_cage_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion where a cationic stibonium center (R₄Sb⁺) is charge-balanced by an anionic carboxylate group tethered via a flexible alkyl linker. The zwitterion adopts a conformation where the carboxylate anion engages in intramolecular anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or trinitrobenzene derivatives) incorporated into the ligand framework. This creates a pre-organized, cage-like pocket that can further bind an external anion (e.g., Cl⁻, BF₄⁻) via a combination of anion-π interactions with the same electron-deficient arenes and electrostatic attraction to the stibonium center. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using the normally repulsive anion-π interaction as an organizing force, while the antimony center provides both structural rigidity (via its tetrahedral geometry) and additional electrostatic complementarity. Recognition elements include: (1) the stibonium cation (pnictogen-based Lewis acidic site), (2) the tethered carboxylate anion, (3) electron-deficient π-systems, and (4) the external anion guest. Interaction patterns involve anion-π (carboxylate-internal arene and guest anion-internal arene), electrostatic (cation-anion), and conformational pre-organization. This maps to primitives: A (anion), C (cation), π (arene), H (hydrophobic/van der Waals cage), S (shape complementarity), E (electrostatic), and D (directional coordination from tetrahedral geometry).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_anion_π_cavitand_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation encapsulated within a π-electron-rich cavitand host. The system features: (1) a tetraalkylphosphonium cation (e.g., PPh4⁺ or P(n-Bu)4⁺) as the cationic guest, (2) a deep cavitand with electron-rich aromatic walls (e.g., resorcin[4]arene-based cavitand with extended π-surfaces), and (3) multiple synergistic non-covalent interactions: strong cation-π interactions between the phosphonium cation and the electron-rich cavitand interior, electrostatic interactions with any anionic counterions positioned outside the cavity, and potential C–H···π interactions from alkyl chains. This represents a supramolecular umpolung synthon where the typically repulsive cation-π interaction (between cation and electron-deficient π-system) is inverted to an attractive one with an electron-rich π-system, enabling controlled encapsulation and release of phosphonium species in supramolecular chemistry and catalysis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boronium_cation_anion_π_calixpyrrole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon featuring a tetrahedral boronium cation [R3B]+ (where R = aryl or alkyl groups) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]pyrrole anion receptor. The synthon involves: (1) anion-π interactions between the boronium cation's positively charged boron center and the electron-rich π-system of the calixpyrrole's pyrrole rings, and (2) electrostatic complementarity where the calix[4]pyrrole acts as an anion receptor for the boronium cation's counteranion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-). This creates a three-component recognition motif: boronium cation ↔ calixpyrrole π-system ↔ anion in cavity. The tetrahedral geometry of the boronium cation provides directional constraints, while the calixpyrrole's conformational flexibility allows adaptive binding. This represents a supramolecular umpolung approach where typically π-basic systems interact with a cationic boron center, contrasting with traditional boron Lewis acid behavior.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_cryptand_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a neutral cryptand host containing tetrahedral germanium(IV) centers that adopt zwitterionic character through intramolecular charge separation. Each germanium center bears one positively charged substituent (e.g., -GeR2+) and one negatively charged substituent (e.g., -Ge-O-), creating localized dipole moments within the cage framework. The cryptand's preorganized cavity exhibits convergent, electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., 1,3,5-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene rings) that provide multiple anion-π recognition sites. Anionic guests (e.g., Cl-, NO3-, PF6-) are bound cooperatively through: (1) electrostatic interactions with the positively charged germanium sites, (2) anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic rings, and (3) geometric complementarity within the three-dimensional cryptand cavity. This represents a supramolecular umpolung synthon because the typically π-basic aromatic systems are rendered π-acidic to attract anions, while the germanium centers provide unusual zwitterionic stabilization. The system maps to primitives: Ge (tetrahedral node), aromatic rings (planar nodes), anions (guest nodes), Coulombic and anion-π interactions (edges), with temporal dynamics possible through anion exchange.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_calixarene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon(IV) center functionalized with both cationic (e.g., ammonium) and anionic (e.g., siloxide) groups, creating a zwitterionic structure. The anionic siloxide moiety acts as a strong anion-π donor, selectively binding to electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., triazine or tetrazine rings) integrated into a calix[4]arene scaffold. The cationic ammonium group provides additional electrostatic steering and potential for hydrogen bonding with auxiliary groups on the calixarene rim. This system combines (1) a directional anion-π interaction (primitive: attractive between anion and π-system), (2) electrostatic complementarity from the zwitterion, (3) shape-persistent preorganization from the calixarene host, and (4) the tunable Lewis acidity/basicity of the silicon center. It enables the assembly of charged, layered architectures through umpolung of typical π-system interactions, where the π-acidic surface accepts electron density from an anion, a reversal of common cation-π motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_anion_π_crown_ether_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganylborate anion (e.g., BPh4⁻) that engages in simultaneous anion-π interactions with an electron-deficient aromatic ring (e.g., a s-triazine or perfluorinated arene) and is encapsulated within a crown ether-like macrocycle via electrostatic and C–H···anion interactions. The synthon features a three-point recognition pattern: 1) the anionic boron center (tetrahedral geometry) provides a diffuse, non-coordinating charge, 2) one of the borate's aryl groups participates in an anion-π interaction with an adjacent electron-deficient π-system, and 3) the oxygen atoms of a benzo-crown ether (e.g., dibenzo-18-crown-6) wrap around the anion, stabilizing it through weak C–H···anion contacts and creating a pre-organized cavity. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically 'soft' borate anion is directionally recognized and stabilized by a combination of a π-acidic surface and a neutral macrocyclic host, enabling its use as a templating or self-assembly unit.

synthons.name: selenonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calixpyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenium(IV) zwitterion containing a cationic selenonium center (R3Se+) and an anionic carboxylate group (R-COO-) within the same molecule. The zwitterion's electron-deficient aromatic rings engage in anion-π interactions with anionic guests, while the calix[4]pyridine macrocycle provides a preorganized cavity with convergent pyridine nitrogen lone pairs for cooperative Se⁺...N chalcogen bonding and hydrogen bonding. This creates a three-point recognition system: (1) electrostatic stabilization between zwitterion charges, (2) directional Se⁺...N pnictogen/chalcogen bonds to the calixpyridine rim, and (3) anion-π interactions between the zwitterion's π-acidic arenes and anionic species. The system enables supramolecular umpolung by using a cationic selenium center to attract electron-rich anions via complementary interactions, suitable for anion recognition and transport applications.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_zwitterion_anion_π_calixarene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron zwitterion (boronium cation with anionic substituent) that engages in dual anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels of a calixarene host. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral boron center with one cationic boronium site (R3B+) and one anionic site (e.g., borate or carboxylate) creating a zwitterionic structure, (2) a calixarene scaffold with electron-deficient arene rings (e.g., tetrafluorophenylene or trinitrophenyl groups) providing multiple anion-π binding sites, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the anionic moiety of the zwitterion and the electron-deficient π-systems of the calixarene, (4) potential cation-π interactions between the boronium cation and adjacent arene rings, (5) conformational preorganization of the calixarene enhancing binding selectivity, (6) tunable electronic properties via substituent effects on both components, and (7) potential for temporal control through pH or redox modulation of the zwitterion charge state. This represents a supramolecular umpolung synthon where typically repulsive anion-arene interactions are exploited for binding through strategic electronic tuning.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_cavitand_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a rigid cavitand scaffold functionalized with electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene or triazine rings) that create a convergent anion-π binding pocket. At the portal or within the cavity, a tetraalkylphosphazenium cation ([R3P=N-PR3]+) is strategically positioned via covalent tethering or supramolecular pre-organization. The synthon operates through a synergistic, umpolung-like interaction pattern: the strongly Lewis-acidic, charge-diffuse phosphazenium cation engages in electrostatic and polarization interactions with an anionic guest (e.g., Cl-, BF4-, or a carboxylate), while the electron-deficient aromatic panels provide stabilizing anion-π interactions with the same guest, creating a unique 'cation-anion-π' ternary cooperative binding motif. This represents a supramolecular umpolung by using a cationic site to attract and pre-organize an anion for further stabilization by typically anion-repulsive aromatic systems, now rendered attractive through electronic tuning. The system maps to primitives: electrostatics (cation-anion), polarization (anion-π), dispersion (π-system stacking if present), shape (cavitand cavity), dynamics (guest binding/release), information (convergent functional group arrangement), and energy (cooperative binding energy).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_cavitand_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral germanium(IV) center functionalized with both cationic and anionic groups to form a zwitterion, designed to bind anions through anion-π interactions within a preorganized cavitand scaffold. The germanium center bears three electron-withdrawing substituents (e.g., trifluoromethyl groups) to enhance the Lewis acidity and π-acidity of an adjacent aromatic panel, while one arm terminates in a permanently charged ammonium group (R-Ge(NR3)+). The cavitand structure incorporates electron-deficient aromatic panels (e.g., triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) that provide strong anion-π binding sites. This creates a synergistic, multi-point recognition motif where the anion is stabilized by both electrostatic interaction with the ammonium group and anion-π interaction with the electron-deficient aromatic cavity, enabling selective anion binding and transport. The germanium center's tetrahedral geometry preorganizes the binding elements, and its relative rarity in supramolecular chemistry offers novel stereoelectronic tuning possibilities.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_cavitand_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral germanium(IV) center functionalized with three electron-withdrawing groups (trifluoromethyl) and one cationic pyridinium arm, creating a zwitterionic structure. The cationic pyridinium moiety provides anion-π interaction capability with electron-deficient aromatic systems, while the tetrahedral germanium center offers geometric directionality. This synthon is embedded within a cavitand scaffold (resorcinarene-based) that preorganizes the binding pocket, enhancing selectivity for planar anionic species (nitrate, perchlorate, tetrafluoroborate) through cooperative anion-π and electrostatic interactions. The germanium center provides enhanced Lewis acidity compared to silicon analogs, strengthening electrostatic components, while maintaining hydrolytic stability. Recognition elements include: (1) tetrahedral Ge(IV) zwitterion core, (2) electron-deficient pyridinium for anion-π interactions, (3) cavitand-enforced preorganization, (4) trifluoromethyl groups for additional electrostatic and hydrophobic effects. This represents a supramolecular umpolung approach where typically cation-binding π-systems are inverted to bind anions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_zwitterion_anion_π_cryptand_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arsenic(V) zwitterion containing both cationic and anionic moieties within the same molecule. The system features an arsonium cation center (R4As+) with one alkyl substituent replaced by a carboxylate anion (R3As+-CH2-COO-), creating an intramolecular zwitterion. This zwitterion acts as an anion-π donor through its carboxylate group, which interacts with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluoropyrimidine or s-tetrazine derivatives) incorporated into a cryptand host. The cryptand provides preorganization through its cavity, enhancing the anion-π interaction strength and selectivity. The arsenic center's tetrahedral geometry prevents self-association, while its polarizability enhances dispersion forces. This synthon enables supramolecular umpolung by using an anionic group (typically nucleophilic) as an electron donor to electron-poor π-systems, creating directional assembly motifs for hierarchical structures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_zwitterion_anion_π_calixpyrrole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon combining a tetrahedral boron zwitterion (e.g., from a borate ester with an adjacent ammonium group) with an anion-π interaction to an electron-deficient aromatic ring, all within a calixpyrrole scaffold. The calixpyrrole acts as a preorganized host that positions: (1) a tetrahedral boron center bearing a formal negative charge, (2) a cationic ammonium group for intramolecular charge balance (zwitterion), and (3) an electron-deficient arene (e.g., tetrafluorobenzene) bridge for anion-π binding. This creates a multi-point recognition site that can bind an external anion via synergistic interactions: electrostatic attraction to the ammonium, Lewis acid-base interaction with boron, and anion-π stacking with the arene. The system enables supramolecular umpolung by using the electron-deficient arene to attract anions rather than cations.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]arene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraalkylphosphonium cation encapsulated within a calix[4]arene scaffold that has been functionalized with electron-deficient aromatic rings (e.g., tetrafluorophenyl or trinitrophenyl groups) at the upper rim. The synthon features three distinct recognition elements: (1) electrostatic and hydrophobic encapsulation of the phosphonium cation within the calixarene cavity (cation-host interaction), (2) anion-π interactions between an anionic species (e.g., chloride, tetrafluoroborate) and the electron-deficient aromatic rings on the upper rim, and (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from the alkyl chains of the phosphonium cation. This creates a convergent binding site where both cation and anion are coordinated through complementary supramolecular forces, enabling a form of 'supramolecular umpolung' where typically repulsive anion-π interactions are enhanced and directed by the pre-organized, cation-loaded host. The system maps to primitives: electrostatics (cation-anion, cation-dipole), dispersion (cavity inclusion, π-stacking), polarization (anion-π), repulsion (steric pre-organization), and directionality (cavity shape, anion-π geometry).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calixarene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraalkylphosphonium cation (e.g., tetrabutylphosphonium) that engages in two simultaneous, cooperative interactions: (1) a strong electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interaction between the cationic phosphorus center and an anionic carboxylate group (e.g., from a benzoate derivative), and (2) an anion-π interaction where the same carboxylate anion is positioned over the electron-deficient aromatic cavity of a pentafluorophenyl-substituted calix[4]arene. The calixarene acts as a rigid, pre-organized platform that orients its fluorinated aryl rings to create a convergent binding pocket. The phosphonium cation, with its bulky alkyl groups, provides steric definition and enhances the anion's electrophilicity for the anion-π interaction. This creates a three-component recognition motif (cation-anion-calixarene) that exemplifies supramolecular umpolung by using a cation to template and strengthen an typically weaker anion-π interaction, enabling the assembly of larger architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_zwitterion_anion_π_cryptand_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arsenic(V) zwitterion with an intramolecular cationic charge (e.g., -AsR2+-) paired with an electron-deficient aromatic system (e.g., s-triazine or tetrafluorobenzene) within a cryptand-like macrocyclic framework. The synthon features three distinct recognition elements: (1) a strong, directional anion-π interaction between the anionic oxygen/nitrogen ligand on arsenic and the π-acidic arena, (2) electrostatic stabilization from the proximal onium center, and (3) preorganization and cavity-defined selectivity provided by the cryptand scaffold. This represents an umpolung strategy where typically π-basic systems are inverted to act as π-acids for anion binding, combined with the underexplored hypervalent arsenic zwitterion chemistry. The system can be mapped to the seven primitives: atoms (As, C, N, O, F), bonds (covalent As-C/N/O, non-covalent anion-π, electrostatic), angles (tetrahedral around As), dihedrals (in macrocycle), planes (aromatic ring), primitives (the assembled recognition pocket), and assemblies (the host-guest complex).

synthons.name: selenonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenium(IV) center in a selenonium zwitterion (R3Se+–X− where X− is an anionic group like carboxylate or sulfonate tethered to the same molecule) that engages in dual noncovalent interactions: (1) anion-π interaction between the anionic portion and the electron-deficient π-system of a nitro- or cyano-substituted calix[4]resorcinarene cavity, and (2) chalcogen bonding between the σ-hole on the selenium atom and a Lewis basic site (e.g., carbonyl oxygen or pyridine nitrogen) on the same host framework. This creates a convergent, chelate-like supramolecular assembly where the zwitterion acts as a bidentate guest, exploiting both electrostatic and orbital-directed interactions. The calix[4]resorcinarene provides a preorganized, electron-poor aromatic cavity for anion-π recognition and additional donor sites for chalcogen bonding, enabling strong, directional binding with potential for umpolung behavior—the cationic selenium center attracts electron density via chalcogen bonding, while the anionic moiety engages an electron-deficient π-surface.

synthons.name: selenonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium zwitterion (R3Se+-CH2-COO-) interacting with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces of a calix[4]resorcinarene scaffold via anion-π interactions. The system features: (1) a permanent selenonium cation center (Se+) providing strong electrostatic potential, (2) a carboxylate anion tethered through a methylene linker creating an intramolecular zwitterion, (3) a bowl-shaped calix[4]resorcinarene host with electron-deficient nitro-substituted aromatic rings at the upper rim, and (4) directional anion-π interactions between the carboxylate oxygen atoms and the π-acidic aromatic cavities. The synthon combines pnictogen bonding (from Se+), electrostatic interactions, and complementary shape matching for selective molecular recognition. This represents a rare example of main-group element zwitterions integrated with macrocyclic π-acidic hosts for supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_cavitand_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a bowl-shaped cavitand host functionalized with tetrahedral phosphonium cations at its upper rim, designed to engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic surfaces. The system features: (1) a rigid resorcin[4]arene cavitand scaffold providing a preorganized concave binding pocket, (2) four peripheral -P⁺(CH₃)₃ groups serving as strong cationic recognition sites for anions (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, PF₆⁻), and (3) electron-deficient triazine or tetrazine panels lining the cavitand interior to provide complementary anion-π interaction surfaces. The phosphonium cations create a convergent electrostatic field that draws anions into the cavity, where they engage in multipoint anion-π contacts with the electron-poor aromatic walls. This represents a supramolecular umpolung strategy—using cationic groups to bind anions, which then become oriented to interact with π-acidic surfaces rather than typical π-basic ones. The synthon can be mapped to the seven primitives: recognition (phosphonium-anion electrostatic + anion-π), complementarity (convergent binding pocket), cooperativity (synergistic interactions), preorganization (rigid cavitand), adaptability (anion size selectivity), reversibility (non-covalent interactions), and function (anion sensing or transport).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral hypervalent iodonium(III) zwitterion (R-I⁺-R' with adjacent carboxylate group creating zwitterionic character) interacting through simultaneous anion-π and halogen bonding with a calix[4]pyrrole host. The iodonium center acts as both a halogen bond donor (σ-hole on iodine) and an electrostatic partner, while the calix[4]pyrrole provides a π-rich cavity for anion binding and complementary NH···anion hydrogen bonds. This creates a three-point recognition motif: (1) halogen bond from iodonium σ-hole to electron-rich pyrrole π-system, (2) anion-π interaction between iodonium-bound anion and calix[4]pyrrole cavity, and (3) hydrogen bonding between pyrrole NH groups and anion. The system represents supramolecular umpolung by using typically electrophilic iodonium in a zwitterionic structure that enables anion binding and transport.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_cucurbituril_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a zwitterionic tetrahedral silicon center with an anionic substituent (e.g., -OSiR2-O-) that engages in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient outer surface of cucurbit[n]uril hosts. The silicon center bears one cationic substituent (e.g., -N+R3) and one anionic oxygen-based substituent, creating a zwitterion with a permanent dipole. The anionic moiety (formally O-) acts as an anion-π donor to the carbonyl-laced, quadrupole-positive portal or outer wall of cucurbiturils. This combines (1) a tetrahedral silicon primitive, (2) a zwitterion charge-separation primitive, (3) an anionic primitive, (4) a π-system primitive (from the host), (5) a recognition primitive (anion-π interaction), (6) a container primitive (cucurbituril macrocycle), and (7) a dipole alignment primitive. This synthon enables directed assembly of silicon-based zwitterions into host-guest networks and provides a supramolecular umpolung strategy by using an anionic site for attraction to electron-deficient π-surfaces rather than conventional cation binding.

synthons.name: selenonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium zwitterion (R3Se+-CH2-COO-) interacting with the electron-rich aromatic cavity of a calix[4]resorcinarene derivative via anion-π interactions. The negatively charged carboxylate group of the zwitterion is positioned above the π-acidic cavity of the calixarene, stabilized by complementary electrostatic and dispersion forces. This creates a directional, charge-assisted recognition motif where the zwitterion's anionic moiety engages the arene cavity while the selenonium cation remains solvated or interacts with peripheral electron donors. The system demonstrates supramolecular umpolung by using an anion (typically repelled by π-systems) as the recognition element through careful charge distribution and cavity design.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_stibonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]quinone_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral stibonium cation (R₄Sb⁺) interacting with a calix[4]quinone receptor through cooperative anion-π and electrostatic interactions. The calix[4]quinone provides a preorganized, electron-deficient cavity with four quinone units creating a strong, convergent anion-binding site via anion-π interactions. The positively charged stibonium center (Sb⁺), located above the cavity, further stabilizes an anionic guest (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻) through direct electrostatic attraction and potential pnictogen bonding. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) tetrahedral onium cation (electrophilic Sb center), (2) anionic guest (nucleophile), and (3) electron-deficient π-cavity (anion-π acceptor). The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using an electron-deficient aromatic system to bind anions (reverse of typical cation-π). It maps to primitives: A (stibonium cation as electrophile), B (anion as nucleophile), C (anion-π interaction as connector), D (calixarene scaffold as scaffold), E (convergent binding site as constraint), F (cooperative electrostatic/anion-π as effector), and G (tunable via quinone redox states as regulator).

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) electrostatically paired with an anionic species, with additional synergistic anion-π interactions to an electron-deficient calix[4]thiophene macrocycle. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional pnictogen bond donor site (σ-hole along the R-Te+ bond axis) and a permanent positive charge for Coulombic attraction. The calix[4]thiophene, with its sulfur atoms oxidized to sulfones, creates a rigid, bowl-shaped electron-deficient cavity ideal for binding anions via cooperative anion-π interactions with its four thiophene-S,S-dioxide rings. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) strong ion pair between telluronium and anion, (2) directional σ-hole pnictogen bonding from Te+ to anion, and (3) multiple anion-π contacts within the preorganized macrocyclic cavity. This system enables 'supramolecular umpolung' by using a cationic p-block element to template and stabilize anionic species within an electron-deficient aromatic environment, potentially for anion transport, sensing, or organocatalysis.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon center bearing both cationic and anionic substituents (zwitterionic R3Si+-CH2-COO- structure) that engages in dual recognition with calix[4]pyrrole hosts. The cationic silicon center (σ-hole donor) participates in anion-π interactions with the electron-rich pyrrole rings of the calixarene, while the carboxylate anion engages in hydrogen bonding with the NH groups of the pyrrole units. This creates a synergistic three-point recognition system: (1) electrostatic stabilization between zwitterion poles, (2) directional anion-π interaction between Si+ and pyrrole π-cloud, and (3) hydrogen bonding between carboxylate and pyrrole NH. The system demonstrates supramolecular umpolung by using a typically electrophilic silicon center to attract electron-rich aromatics via anion-π geometry, while maintaining conventional hydrogen bonding patterns. Mapped to primitives: recognition (calix[4]pyrrole cavity), interaction (anion-π + H-bonding), polarity (zwitterion), geometry (tetrahedral Si), connectivity (three-point binding), environment (supramolecular host-guest), and dynamics (guest exchange).

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) positioned above a π-electron rich calix[4]thiophene macrocycle. The synthon features three distinct recognition elements: (1) electrostatic cation-π interaction between the positively charged tellurium center and the electron-rich thiophene rings of the calixarene, (2) secondary Te···S chalcogen bonding between the telluronium cation and the sulfur atoms of the thiophene units, and (3) shape complementarity provided by the concave cavity of the calix[4]thiophene, which partially encapsulates the cation. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung approach, using a heavy pnictogen cation (typically electrophilic) to engage in attractive non-covalent interactions with an electron-rich π-system. The telluronium center, with its large, polarizable electron cloud, enhances both electrostatic and dispersion contributions to the binding. This synthon is chemically realistic, as telluronium salts are known stable species, and calix[4]thiophenes are synthetically accessible π-rich hosts.

synthons.name: iodonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium(III) zwitterion center (R-I⁺-R') interacting with an electron-rich anion (e.g., tetrafluoroborate, hexafluorophosphate) via electrostatic attraction, while simultaneously engaging in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient cavity of a calix[4]triazole macrocycle. The calix[4]triazole provides a preorganized, π-acidic aromatic cavity from four 1,2,3-triazole rings oriented inward, enhancing anion binding. The iodonium center exhibits umpolung character, acting as both an electrophilic iodine(III) and a source of stabilized positive charge. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) zwitterionic iodonium charge separation, (2) anion binding to the iodonium cation, and (3) synergistic anion-π stabilization within the triazole cavity. The system is chemically realistic, drawing from known hypervalent iodine chemistry and anion-binding triazole macrocycles, and maps to primitives including charge, polarity, aromaticity, and preorganization.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_1
