synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon center bearing both cationic and anionic substituents (zwitterionic R3Si+-CH2-COO-), designed to interact with electron-deficient aromatic systems via anion-π interactions. The silicon zwitterion is conformationally pre-organized by coordination to a calix[4]pyrrole scaffold through the carboxylate anion, which sits in the pyrrolic NH binding pocket. This creates a rigid, bowl-shaped architecture where the positively charged silicon center is positioned above the electron-deficient cavity of a separate, complementary π-acidic arene (e.g., tetracyanobenzene or nitroaromatic). Key interactions include: (1) ion pairing within the zwitterion, (2) hydrogen bonding between carboxylate and calixpyrrole NH groups, (3) anion-π interaction between the carboxylate and the electron-deficient arena, and (4) potential cation-π interaction between Si+ and the same arena. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung synthon, where typically repulsive anion-π and cation-π interactions are combined in a cooperative, orthogonal binding motif for assembling complex architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon center bearing both cationic (silylium-like) and anionic (silanolate) character in a zwitterionic arrangement, designed to interact with π-electron-rich cavities of calix[4]pyrrole hosts. The synthon features: (1) a positively polarized silicon center (R3Si⁺δ) that engages in strong anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient π-surface of the calix[4]pyrrole's pyrrolic rings in their diprotonated or metal-coordinated form; (2) a proximal silanolate group (SiO⁻) that can form charge-assisted hydrogen bonds with the NH groups of the calix[4]pyrrole or engage in ion-pairing with cationic guests; (3) three organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) that provide steric control and additional weak interactions (C–H···π, dispersion). This system combines p-block element zwitterion chemistry with macrocyclic host-guest recognition, enabling unique supramolecular assembly through simultaneous anion-π and cation-π interactions, as well as potential silicon-centered Lewis acidity for substrate activation. The calix[4]pyrrole scaffold offers conformational flexibility and tunable π-acidity, making this a versatile synthon for constructing hierarchical supramolecular architectures or sensing arrays.

synthons.name: iodonium_zwitterion_anion_π_porphyrinoid_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent iodine(III) center in a zwitterionic structure, where the iodine bears both a cationic formal charge and an anionic ligand (typically carboxylate or sulfonate). This hypervalent iodine center engages in strong anion-π interactions with electron-deficient porphyrinoid macrocycles (such as tetrafluorophenylporphyrins or N-confused porphyrins). The iodine(III) center exhibits a T-shaped geometry with two covalent bonds and one coordinative/ionic interaction, creating a polarized recognition site. The synthon combines: (1) electrostatic attraction between the iodonium cation and the anionic ligand, (2) anion-π interaction between the anionic ligand and the electron-deficient porphyrinoid π-system, (3) potential halogen bonding from the iodine σ-hole to electron donors on the macrocycle periphery, and (4) shape complementarity between the planar porphyrinoid and the planar anionic moiety. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-binding porphyrins instead engage anions through π-acidic surfaces, while the hypervalent iodine provides orthogonal polarization.

synthons.name: iodonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium(III) zwitterion center (R-I⁺-R') interacting through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient triazole rings embedded in a calix[4]arene scaffold. The iodonium center bears both cationic character (I⁺) and an anionic sulfonate group (-SO₃⁻) on one ligand, creating a zwitterionic structure. This interacts with the π-acidic 1,2,3-triazole rings of a conformationally locked calix[4]arene where one phenol oxygen per repeat unit is replaced by a 1,2,3-triazole. The synthon exploits: (1) electrostatic stabilization between the zwitterion's charges, (2) strong anion-π interaction between the sulfonate anion and electron-deficient triazole rings, (3) potential halogen bonding from the σ-hole on the iodonium center to triazole nitrogens, and (4) shape complementarity from the calixarene cavity. This represents a supramolecular umpolung system where typically π-basic arenes are replaced by π-acidic heterocycles to attract anions, combined with a hypervalent iodine center that can act as both electrophile and anion binder.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent iodonium(III) zwitterion center where the iodine atom bears both a cationic formal charge and is covalently bonded to an anionic carboxylate group (R-I⁺-COO⁻). This unique zwitterionic structure engages in two simultaneous supramolecular interactions: 1) Anion-π interaction between the iodonium-bound carboxylate anion and the electron-deficient π-system of a proximal 1,2,4-triazole ring, and 2) The entire assembly is pre-organized within a calix[4]arene scaffold where one upper rim phenolic oxygen is replaced by a 1,2,4-triazole unit, creating a convergent binding pocket. The synthon exploits hypervalent iodine chemistry for umpolung character, uses the electron-deficient triazole for strong anion-π recognition (Eₐₙᵢₒₙ‑π ≈ 15-30 kJ/mol), and employs the calixarene framework for spatial control and preorganization. This represents a supramolecular umpolung system where the normally π-basic arene is made π-acidic via heterocyclic substitution, inverting its interaction preferences.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral hypervalent iodonium(III) zwitterion interacting with an electron-deficient aromatic system through anion-π interactions, embedded within a calix[4]triazole macrocyclic scaffold. The iodonium center bears one aryl group and two anionic ligands (e.g., carboxylates) creating a zwitterionic structure with a formal positive charge on iodine and delocalized negative charges on the ligands. The calix[4]triazole framework provides preorganization through four 1,2,3-triazole rings linked by methylene bridges, creating a π-electron-deficient cavity ideal for anion-π interactions with the anionic ligands of the iodonium moiety. This system combines: (1) hypervalent iodine chemistry (electrophilic iodonium center), (2) zwitterionic charge distribution, (3) anion-π interactions between the anionic carboxylates and electron-deficient triazole rings, (4) preorganized macrocyclic geometry, and (5) potential for temporal control through redox modulation of the iodonium center. The seven primitives map as: atoms (I, O, N, C), bonds (covalent I-C, I-O; non-covalent anion-π, hydrogen bonds from triazole CH), angles (tetrahedral around iodine), dihedrals (calixarene-like cone conformation), charges (zwitterionic iodonium), spins (closed-shell), and masses (heavy iodine isotope effects possible).

synthons.name: iodonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium(III) zwitterion center (R-I⁺-R') where the iodine bears both cationic character and adjacent anionic group (e.g., carboxylate) creating a zwitterionic structure. This iodonium center engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes integrated into a calix[4]triazole macrocyclic scaffold. The calix[4]triazole (composed of alternating 1,2,3-triazole and methylene bridges) provides preorganized concave geometry with electron-poor aromatic surfaces ideal for anion binding via anion-π contacts. The iodonium zwitterion acts as both an anion donor (via carboxylate) and acceptor (via σ-hole on iodine), while the calixarene-like framework offers multiple interaction sites for cooperative binding. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-binding macrocycles are repurposed for anion stabilization through complementary electrostatic and orbital interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arsonium cation (R4As+) interacting through anion-π interactions with an electron-deficient calix[4]thiophene macrocycle. The arsonium center provides a permanent cationic charge (+1) with tetrahedral geometry, while the calix[4]thiophene scaffold features four thiophene rings arranged in a cone conformation, creating an electron-deficient π-cavity suitable for anion binding. The synthon combines (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) anion-π interactions between the anion and electron-deficient thiophene rings, (3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from methyl/alkyl groups on the arsonium, (4) conformational preorganization of the calixarene-like host, (5) directional binding geometry enforced by the tetrahedral cation and cone-shaped macrocycle, (6) tunable electron deficiency via thiophene oxidation or substitution, and (7) potential for temporal control via redox-switching of the thiophene units. This represents a supramolecular umpolung approach where typically cation-binding π-systems are repurposed for anion recognition via electron-deficient aromatics, paired with an unconventional pnictogen-based cation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arsonium cation (R₄As⁺) interacting through anion-π interactions with electron-deficient calix[4]thiophene macrocycles. The arsonium center provides a strong, permanent positive charge due to arsenic's lower electronegativity compared to phosphorus, creating a potent cationic site. The calix[4]thiophene scaffold incorporates thiophene rings instead of traditional phenol or pyrrole units, offering a distinct π-surface with tunable electron deficiency through sulfur oxidation states (sulfone formation). The synthon combines: (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) anion-π interactions between the tetrahedral anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) and the electron-deficient thiophene π-systems, (3) potential As···S secondary interactions, and (4) conformational preorganization of the calixarene cavity. This represents a supramolecular umpolung approach where typically cation-π dominant systems are inverted to anion-π recognition, using the arsonium cation as an electrostatic anchor while exploiting the underutilized anion-π capability of heteroaromatic macrocycles.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arsonium cation (R₄As⁺) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]thiophene macrocycle via anion-π interactions. The calix[4]thiophene adopts a cone conformation with four thiophene units replacing traditional phenol/pyrrole rings, creating a π-basic cavity. The tetrahedral arsonium cation (e.g., tetraphenylarsonium) provides a bulky, shape-persistent cation that can sit above the cavity. The key recognition involves: (1) anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient As⁺ center (through its σ-hole along As-C bonds) and the π-cloud of the thiophene rings, (2) complementary electrostatic interactions between the cationic As center and the partially negative sulfur atoms of the thiophenes, (3) secondary C-H···π interactions between alkyl/aryl substituents on arsenic and the macrocycle. This synthon represents a pnictogen-bond-driven assembly motif with potential for constructing charged supramolecular frameworks. It maps to primitives: positive charge (As⁺), π-system (thiophene macrocycle), tetrahedral geometry, directional pnictogen bonds, aromatic rings, conformational preference (cone), and electrostatic complementarity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon featuring a tetrahedral arsenonium cation (R₄As⁺) with four organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) that engages in simultaneous anion-π interactions with a calix[4]thiophene macrocycle. The calix[4]thiophene adopts a cone conformation with four thiophene units replacing traditional phenol/pyrrole rings, creating an electron-deficient π-cavity ideal for anion binding. The arsenonium cation provides a stable, directional positive charge center, while the thiophene-based calixarene analog offers enhanced π-acidity compared to conventional calixarenes. This creates a complementary pair where the cation's positive charge is stabilized by through-space interaction with the anion-bound π-system, representing a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-π interactions are reversed to anion-π assisted cation stabilization. The system demonstrates pnictogen bonding (from arsenic), anion-π interactions, and conformational preorganization.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]imidazole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral germanium(IV) zwitterion with a cationic Ge center and anionic carboxylate arm, engaging in dual anion-π interactions with electron-deficient calix[4]imidazole aromatic cavities. The germanium center bears two phenyl groups and one alkyl chain, with the fourth position occupied by a -CH₂COO⁻ group creating zwitterionic character. The calix[4]imidazole host features four electron-deficient imidazole rings in a cone conformation, creating π-acidic cavities. Recognition involves: (1) electrostatic attraction between Ge⁺ and peripheral host carboxylates, (2) anion-π interactions between the carboxylate arm and imidazole rings, and (3) hydrophobic complementarity of phenyl/alkyl groups with host cavity. This represents a rare example of germanium-based zwitterions in supramolecular chemistry with anion-π recognition, enabling assembly of charge-complementary architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent germanium(IV) cation (R4Ge+) electrostatically paired with a suitable anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-). The cation features bulky, electron-donating alkyl or aryl substituents to stabilize the positive charge and prevent nucleophilic attack. The key supramolecular recognition element is the anion-π interaction between the associated anion and the electron-deficient π-system of a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The calix[4]pyridine, in its cone conformation, presents a convergent array of four pyridine N-atoms at its lower rim, which can secondarily coordinate to the anion or the germanium center, and a pre-organized, cavity-lining electron-poor aromatic surface at its upper rim for anion binding. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) ionic pair (Ge+/A-), (2) primary anion-π interaction (A- to calixarene π-cavity), and (3) potential secondary N...anion or N...Ge+ interactions. This synthon enables the assembly of charged species into larger architectures via umpolung of typical cation-π to anion-π interactions, exploiting the underexplored tetraorganogermanium cation chemistry and integrating it with a classic electron-deficient host.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]imidazole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganogermanium zwitterion (R₃Ge⁺-X⁻) where germanium(IV) bears three organic substituents and is covalently linked to a negatively charged functional group (e.g., carboxylate, sulfonate) to form an intramolecular zwitterion. This cationic Ge center engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient arenes, specifically the π-acidic cavities of a calix[4]imidazole scaffold. The calix[4]imidazole, composed of four imidazole units linked at the 2- and 5- positions, provides a conformationally flexible, electron-poor aromatic cavity due to the electron-withdrawing nature of the imidazole heterocycle. The primary recognition elements are: 1) the electrostatic and orbital (σ-hole) attraction from the tetrahedral Ge(IV) center toward the anion-π-accepting cavity, and 2) potential secondary C–H···anion or lone pair-π interactions from the imidazole N-atoms. This represents a supramolecular umpolung, as the typically π-basic calixarene-like cavity is inverted to π-acidic, actively attracting the anionic portion of the zwitterion. The synthon is mappable to primitives: Ge⁺ (electrophilic node), anion (nucleophilic node), π-acidic ring (electrophilic surface), and directional Ge–anion covalent bond (connector).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_gallium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral gallium(III) cation (GaR3+, where R = alkyl or aryl) that engages in two simultaneous, orthogonal non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The primary interaction is an electrostatic and coordinative attraction between the Lewis acidic Ga(III) center and a pyridyl nitrogen lone pair (a dative bond or strong Lewis acid-base interaction). The secondary, orthogonal interaction is an anion-π interaction between a weakly coordinating anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or BArF-) associated with the gallium cation and the electron-deficient π-surface of an adjacent pyridine ring within the same calixarene scaffold. The calix[4]pyridine adopts a cone conformation, presenting a convergent binding pocket that pre-organizes the system for this dual interaction. This represents a supramolecular umpolung motif where the typically π-basic pyridine ring acts as an anion-π acceptor due to its involvement in coordination to the highly charged Ga(III), making its π-system electron-deficient. The synthon is modular through variation of the gallium substituents (R), the counteranion (X-), and pyridine ring substituents.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_siliconium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]arene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral organosilicon cation (R3Si+) electrostatically paired with an anion, with additional cooperative anion-π interactions to an electron-deficient calix[4]arene platform. The siliconium center (e.g., trialkylsilylium) acts as a strong Lewis acid and electrophile, binding a halide or weakly coordinating anion (BF4-, PF6-, etc.). The anion simultaneously engages in anion-π interactions with the π-acidic cavity of a tetrafluoro-calix[4]arene derivative. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) Coulombic cation-anion pair, (2) directional anion-π interaction to the arene cavity, and (3) potential cation-π stabilization from the calixarene methylene bridges. The system exemplifies supramolecular umpolung by using an electron-deficient macrocycle to stabilize an anion that is already ion-paired with a cation, creating a polarized yet aggregated assembly. It maps to primitives: charge (cation/anion), polarity (polarized Si+ center), aromaticity (calixarene π-system), confinement (macrocyclic cavity), coordination (Si-anion dative/ionic bond), hydrophobicity (alkyl groups on Si), and dynamics (anion exchange within cavity).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]imidazole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon(IV) center bearing both cationic and anionic substituents, creating a zwitterionic structure that engages in dual anion-π interactions with an electron-deficient calix[4]imidazole aromatic cavity. The silicon center carries one positively charged ammoniumalkyl group (R-NR3+) and one negatively charged silanolate group (Si-O-), resulting in overall charge neutrality but significant local dipole moments. The calix[4]imidazole scaffold provides four electron-deficient imidazole rings arranged in a cone conformation, creating a π-acidic pocket that selectively binds anions through anion-π interactions. The synthon operates through: (1) electrostatic complementarity between the zwitterion's dipole and the cavity's quadrupole moment, (2) directional anion-π interactions between the silanolate oxygen and imidazole rings, (3) potential cation-π interactions between the ammonium group and adjacent aromatic systems, and (4) conformational preorganization of the calixarene scaffold. This represents a supramolecular umpolung approach where typically π-basic cavities are replaced with π-acidic ones, and conventional cation-anion pairing is augmented with oriented dipole interactions. The system is chemically realistic using established silane chemistry and known electron-deficient heterocyclic calixarenes.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]imidazole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon(IV) center bearing both cationic and anionic substituents, creating a zwitterionic structure that interacts with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The silicon center has one imidazolium substituent (providing positive charge), one carboxylate substituent (providing negative charge), and two aryl groups that anchor the system to a calix[4]imidazole scaffold. The calixarene framework provides preorganized imidazole rings that engage in anion-π interactions with the carboxylate group, while the cationic imidazolium moiety participates in cation-π interactions with adjacent electron-rich aromatic systems. This creates a unique supramolecular assembly where the zwitterionic silicon center acts as a polarized recognition element, with the calixarene scaffold providing geometric constraint and additional interaction sites. The system demonstrates supramolecular umpolung through simultaneous anion-π and cation-π interactions from a single molecular entity.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]imidazole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon(IV) center bearing both cationic and anionic substituents, creating a zwitterionic structure that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient calix[4]imidazole macrocycles. The silicon center carries one positively charged ammoniumalkyl substituent (R-NR3+) and one negatively charged carboxylate substituent (R-COO-), while the remaining two substituents are inert alkyl chains. The zwitterion's carboxylate anion interacts with the electron-deficient π-surface of the fluorinated calix[4]imidazole cavity via anion-π interactions, while the cationic ammonium moiety provides additional electrostatic complementarity with peripheral electron-rich regions of the macrocycle. This represents a supramolecular umpolung approach where both cationic and anionic components are integrated into a single molecular entity that recognizes complementary π-acidic aromatic surfaces.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]selenophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium cation (R3Se+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a complementary π-electron-rich calix[4]selenophene receptor. The synthon features: (1) a strong electrostatic cation-anion interaction between the positively charged selenium center and an anionic counterion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-), (2) a directional anion-π interaction between that same anion and the electron-deficient face of one of the selenophene rings in the calixarene scaffold, and (3) secondary Se···O chalcogen bonding between the selenonium center and ether-like oxygen atoms in the calixarene bridge. The calix[4]selenophene provides a pre-organized, electron-rich cavity that enhances anion binding and stabilizes the selenonium cation through complementary electrostatic and van der Waals contacts. This represents a supramolecular umpolung system where the typically π-basic heterocycle (selenophene) participates in anion-π interactions due to polarization effects from the cationic guest, creating a cooperative recognition motif.

synthons.name: selenonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]selenophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium cation (R3Se+) paired with an appropriate anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or BArF-) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with an electron-deficient, bowl-shaped calix[4]selenophene host. The calix[4]selenophene is composed of four selenophene rings linked at the 2,5-positions, creating a π-acidic cavity. The synthon operates through: (1) electrostatic attraction between the selenonium cation and the anion, (2) directional anion-π interactions between the anion and the electron-deficient selenophene rings of the calixarene, and (3) potential secondary C–H···anion and Se···anion contacts. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically repulsive anion-anion interaction (between the anion and the electron-rich π-cloud of a typical arene) is inverted to an attractive one via the π-acidic cavity. The seven primitives map as: Donor = anion (electron density), Acceptor = calix[4]selenophene π-system, Positive = selenonium cation, Negative = anion, Hydrophobic = organic R groups on Se+ and calixarene rim, Aromatic = selenophene rings, and Ionic = Se+···anion pair.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]selenophene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium cation (R3Se+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a π-electron-rich calix[4]selenophene macrocycle. The synthon features: (1) a strong, directional chalcogen bond between the σ-hole on the selenium atom of the cation and a lone pair of a selenophene sulfur atom in the macrocycle, and (2) a stabilizing anion-π interaction between the associated counter-anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) and the electron-deficient interior of the selenonium cation's aromatic substituents or the electron-rich cavity of the calixarene. This creates a three-component recognition motif (cation-chalcogen bond-macrocycle-anion-π-cation) that enables the assembly of charged, layered supramolecular architectures. The calix[4]selenophene provides a conformationally flexible, electron-rich platform that enhances both chalcogen bonding and π-system interactions, making this a versatile synthon for supramolecular umpolung, where the typically π-basic calixarene participates in anion-π interactions due to polarization effects from the proximal selenonium center.

synthons.name: selenonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]selenophene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium cation (R3Se+) paired with an anionic species through anion-π interactions with a calix[4]selenophene host. The system features: (1) a selenonium cation as the cationic recognition element (selenium in +IV oxidation state with three organic substituents), (2) a complementary anion (e.g., tetrafluoroborate, hexafluorophosphate, or halide), (3) a calix[4]selenophene macrocycle containing four selenophene rings bridged by methylene groups, providing a π-electron-deficient cavity for anion binding via anion-π interactions, and (4) additional stabilization through electrostatic interactions and potential Se···anion chalcogen bonding. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-binding calixarenes are adapted for anion recognition through electron-deficient heterocyclic components. The seven primitives map as: atoms (Se, C, H, anion), bonds (covalent Se-C, electrostatic, anion-π), topology (tetrahedral cation, cone-shaped macrocycle), interactions (electrostatic, anion-π, chalcogen bonding), reactivity (anion exchange, redox activity of selenium), energy (binding enthalpy for anion recognition), and time (dynamics of anion encapsulation/release).

synthons.name: selenonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]selenophene_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium cation (R3Se+) electrostatically paired with an appropriate anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or BArF-), which is further engaged in cooperative anion-π interactions with an electron-deficient, bowl-shaped calix[4]selenophene host. The calix[4]selenophene, composed of four selenophene rings linked at the 2,5-positions, provides a convergent, π-acidic cavity. The synthon exploits three key interactions: 1) a strong, charge-assisted electrostatic bond between the selenonium cation and the anion, 2) an anion-π interaction between the anion and the electron-deficient selenophene rings of the calixarene, and 3) potential secondary C–H···anion and Se···anion contacts. This creates a stable, pre-organized ternary assembly (cation···anion···host) that can function as a synthon for constructing larger supramolecular architectures or materials via its exposed cation and calixarene rim. It represents a supramolecular umpolung by using a cationic chalcogen center (Se+) to template and stabilize an anion-binding motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphazenium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphazenium cation (R3P=N+=PR3) engaging in simultaneous anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic panels of a calix[4]resorcinarene scaffold. The synthon features: (1) a cationic tetrahedral P(V) center with high charge density, (2) a complementary bowl-shaped calix[4]resorcinarene host with four electron-deficient resorcinol-derived aromatic rings, (3) directional anion-π interactions between the cation's counter-anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) and the π-acidic aromatic cavities, and (4) secondary C-H···π and van der Waals contacts that preorganize the assembly. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic cavities are inverted to π-acidic for anion recognition, combined with a robust, hydrolysis-resistant phosphazenium cation that avoids the decomposition pathways of simpler onium ions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_siliconium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral siliconium cation (R3Si+) electrostatically paired with a suitable anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-), which engages in cooperative anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic rings of a bowl-shaped calix[4]resorcinarene host. The calix[4]resorcinarene provides a convergent, pre-organized cavity lined with four electron-poor resorcinol-derived arenes, ideal for stabilizing the anion through multipoint anion-π contacts. The primary recognition elements are: (1) the ionic pair (cation-anion), (2) the anion-π interaction between the anion and the arene rings, and (3) potential weak C–H···anion or C–H···O contacts from the methylene bridges or upper rim substituents of the calixarene. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung, as the typically repulsive anion-arene interaction is turned into a stabilizing one by using electron-deficient rings and the electrostatic field of the proximal siliconium cation. It can be mapped to the seven primitives: atoms (Si, C, H, O, B/F/P), bonds (covalent Si–C, ionic interactions), motifs (tetrahedral cation, macrocyclic bowl), interactions (ionic, anion-π, van der Waals), roles (cation as organizer, anion as linker, arene as acceptor), properties (pre-organized cavity, convergent binding sites), and contexts (supramolecular assembly, host-guest chemistry).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]selenophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium zwitterion (R3Se+-CH2-COO-) interacting with a calix[4]selenophene macrocycle through multiple simultaneous interactions: (1) anion-π interaction between the carboxylate anion (COO-) and the electron-deficient π-system of the selenophene rings, (2) chalcogen bonding between the positively charged selenium (Se+) and the lone pairs of the selenophene sulfur/selenium atoms, and (3) electrostatic complementarity between the zwitterion's charges and the polarized calixarene cavity. The calix[4]selenophene provides a preorganized, electron-deficient π-cavity with four selenophene units offering both π-acidic surfaces and chalcogen bond acceptor sites. This represents a supramolecular umpolung synthon where typically π-basic calixarenes are replaced with π-acidic counterparts to reverse interaction preferences, enabling recognition of anionic species through anion-π interactions while maintaining cation binding through the selenonium center.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]selenophene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium zwitterion (R3Se+–CH2–COO−) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]selenophene receptor. The positively charged selenium center (Se+) acts as a pnictogen bond donor to an anion (e.g., chloride or tetrafluoroborate), while the carboxylate anion of the zwitterion engages in electrostatic attraction with the electron-deficient selenium atoms in the calixarene rim. Simultaneously, the electron-rich π-surface of the calix[4]selenophene cavity participates in anion-π interactions with the same anion, creating a cooperative three-component recognition motif. This system combines zwitterion self-assembly, pnictogen bonding, anion-π interactions, and macrocyclic preorganization, representing a novel supramolecular umpolung approach where both cationic and anionic moieties of the zwitterion participate in orthogonal recognition events.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotelluronium cation (R₄Te⁺) interacting with an anion via anion-π interactions with a π-electron-deficient calix[4]tellurophene scaffold. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional pnictogen bond donor site (σ-hole on Te), while the calix[4]tellurophene—a macrocycle incorporating four tellurophene (C₄H₄Te) units—offers a preorganized, electron-poor aromatic cavity for anion binding. Key recognition elements: (1) Te⁺...X⁻ pnictogen bond (electrostatic + orbital mixing), (2) anion-π interactions between the anion and the electron-deficient tellurophene rings, (3) preorganization from the calixarene-like bowl shape. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic arenes are made π-acidic via heavy heteroatom incorporation, creating a dual-action receptor for anions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_silicon_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral silicon zwitterion (R3Si+–X− where X is a negatively charged functional group like carboxylate or sulfonate tethered to the same silicon center) interacting with the electron-rich π-system of a calix[4]resorcinarene cavity. The synthon features three distinct recognition elements: (1) electrostatic attraction between the cationic silicon center (Si+) and the partial negative charge on the aromatic rings of the resorcinarene, (2) anion-π interactions between the anionic group (X−) and the electron-deficient centers of the resorcinarene's upper rim (often decorated with electron-withdrawing groups like NO2 or CN), and (3) potential C–H···π or van der Waals contacts from the organic substituents (R) on silicon with the cavity walls. This represents a rare example of a main-group zwitterion (silicon) engaging in dual, complementary non-covalent interactions with a well-defined macrocyclic host, enabling controlled assembly and potential applications in molecular recognition or supramolecular catalysis. The system maps to primitives: charge (cation and anion), shape (tetrahedral Si, bowl-shaped calixarene), polarity (zwitterion), connectivity (non-covalent assembly), dynamics (host-guest exchange), energy (electrostatic/anion-π stabilization), and information (complementary interaction pattern).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenonium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]selenophene_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenonium zwitterion center (R3Se+–C–COO−) that engages in multiple simultaneous non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]selenophene host. The synthon features: (1) a permanent selenonium cation (Se+) that acts as a strong electrophilic site for chalcogen bonding with electron-rich atoms, (2) a carboxylate anion (COO−) for electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions, (3) an aromatic π-system on the calix[4]selenophene that participates in anion-π interactions with the carboxylate, and (4) the bowl-shaped calixarene architecture providing preorganization and additional π-π stacking surfaces. The zwitterion's tetrahedral geometry creates a directional, multi-point recognition pattern where the Se+ engages in Se···O/N chalcogen bonds, the carboxylate sits in the electron-deficient cavity of the selenophene rings (anion-π), and alkyl/aryl substituents on the selenonium enhance hydrophobic complementarity. This represents a supramolecular umpolung system where both cationic (Se+) and anionic (COO−) centers are present in the same molecule, enabling orthogonal recognition with complementary hosts.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_siliconium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral siliconium cation (R3Si+) electrostatically paired with a suitable anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-). The cation features aromatic substituents (e.g., phenyl groups) that engage in simultaneous anion-π interactions with the bound anion and π-π stacking with the electron-rich aromatic walls of a cone-shaped calix[4]resorcinarene host. The calixarene provides a preorganized, concave π-surface and upper-rim hydroxyl groups for additional hydrogen bonding or coordination. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) strong ion-pair electrostatic interaction, (2) stabilizing anion-π interaction between the anion and the cation's aryl groups, and (3) complementary π-π stacking/hydrophobic encapsulation within the calixarene cavity. The system exemplifies a supramolecular umpolung by using a cationic silicon center (typically electrophilic) to organize an anion and a neutral electron-rich host into a stable assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent germanium(IV) center bearing both cationic and anionic substituents, creating a zwitterionic structure. The germanium atom is coordinated to three organic groups (e.g., phenyl or alkyl) and one anionic group (e.g., carboxylate or sulfonate), resulting in a formal positive charge on Ge balanced by the anionic substituent. This tetrahedral germanium zwitterion acts as a dual-mode recognition unit: (1) the electron-deficient germanium center (due to σ-hole formation) can engage in pnictogen bonding with electron donors, and (2) the anionic moiety can participate in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient aromatic systems. The synthon is specifically designed to bind to the π-deficient cavity of a calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle, where the anion-π interaction occurs between the germanium-bound anion and the pyrrole rings, while the germanium σ-hole interacts with the pyrrole nitrogen lone pairs or with additional anion guests bound in the calix[4]pyrrole cavity. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-binding calix[4]pyrrole is engaged via anion-π interactions with an anionic component of a zwitterion.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_siliconium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral siliconium cation (R3Si+) electrostatically paired with a suitable anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-). The cation's positive charge is stabilized by hyperconjugation with its alkyl/aryl substituents. The key supramolecular recognition involves the anion engaging in dual interactions: 1) a direct electrostatic interaction with the siliconium center, and 2) a strong, directional anion-π interaction with the electron-deficient, quadrupole-positive cavity of a fluorinated calix[4]resorcinarene derivative. The calixarene scaffold provides a pre-organized, concave π-surface ideal for anion binding. This creates a three-component recognition motif (cation-anion-π-acidic host) that enables the assembly of larger architectures through orthogonal interactions, representing a supramolecular umpolung where a typically π-basic arene is engineered to attract anions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]furan_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent germanium(IV) cation (germonium) with four organic substituents (e.g., aryl or alkyl groups) creating a tetrahedral cationic center. This positively charged center is designed to engage in anion binding via electrostatic and potentially σ-hole (pnictogen bond-like) interactions. The synthon is integrated into a calix[4]furan macrocyclic scaffold, where the four furan rings provide a pre-organized, electron-rich π-surface. This architecture enables a synergistic, convergent binding mode: the germonium cation binds an anionic guest (e.g., Cl⁻, BF₄⁻), while the calix[4]furan's π-system engages in stabilizing anion-π interactions with the same or a co-bound anion. The system represents a supramolecular umpolung, using a typically π-basic furan system in an anion-π context, guided and enhanced by the adjacent strong cationic site. Recognition elements: (1) tetrahedral germonium cation (electrostatic/pnictogen bond donor), (2) calix[4]furan π-cavity (anion-π acceptor), (3) convergent binding pocket. Interaction patterns: cation-anion electrostatic, potential Ge···anion σ-hole interaction, anion-π, and macrocyclic pre-organization.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]furan_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent germanium center bearing one cationic substituent (e.g., trimethylammoniumethyl) and three electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., trifluoromethyl) to create a strong σ-hole on germanium, paired with a planar, electron-rich calix[4]furan macrocycle. The synthon features three simultaneous interactions: (1) a pnictogen bond (Ge···N) from the σ-hole on Ge(IV) to a nitrogen lone pair from a neighboring synthon or external base, (2) an anion-π interaction between a halide anion (Cl⁻, Br⁻) and the electron-deficient π-face of one of the furan rings in the calixarene, and (3) π-π stacking between the electron-rich furan rings of adjacent macrocycles. This creates a zwitterionic assembly where the cationic ammonium arm and the anion are held in close proximity by the germanium pnictogen bond and anion-π interaction, respectively, while the calix[4]furan provides a rigid, preorganized platform. The system enables supramolecular umpolung by using an electron-deficient metaloid center (Ge) to attract nucleophiles (anion binding via anion-π and pnictogen bond assistance) despite the overall cationic nature of the ammonium arm, facilitating novel anion transport or catalysis motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_siliconium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]furan_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral siliconium cation (R3Si+) electrostatically paired with a complementary anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or BArF-). The cation is integrated into a calix[4]furan scaffold, where the four furan rings provide a pre-organized, electron-rich π-cavity. The primary supramolecular recognition involves: 1) Coulombic attraction between the siliconium center and the anion, 2) cooperative anion-π interactions between the anion and the electron-deficient faces of the furan rings (enhanced by the cationic silicon's inductive effect), and 3) potential C–H···anion hydrogen bonds from alkyl/aryl substituents on the silicon. This system represents a silicon-based umpolung, where the typically electrophilic silicon center is rendered highly cationic, creating a strong, directional binding site for anions within a π-acidic aromatic cavity—a motif distinct from common ammonium or phosphonium-based receptors. It maps to primitives: charged (cation/anion), π-system, tetrahedral geometry, pre-organized macrocycle, directional electrostatic/ion-dipole interactions, and cooperative binding.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]furan_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent germanium center bearing one cationic substituent (e.g., -NMe3+) and three neutral electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., -CF3), creating a zwitterionic structure with a localized positive charge. This acts as a dual-mode tecton: 1) The electron-deficient germanium center serves as a strong pnictogen bond donor (Ge-centered σ-hole) for anion binding (e.g., Cl-, NO3-). 2) The surrounding aromatic system is a calix[4]furan macrocycle, where the four furan rings provide convergent, electron-rich π-surfaces. This creates an anion-π interaction site *orthogonal* to the pnictogen bond axis, enabling cooperative binding. The synthon thus combines Ge(IV) pnictogen bonding and anion-π interactions within a preorganized macrocyclic framework, enabling the assembly of 3D anionic networks or cages. It represents a supramolecular umpolung by using an electron-deficient π-system (enhanced by the Ge(IV) and -CF3 substituents) for anion binding, contrary to typical cation-π motifs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]phosphole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetracoordinated antimony(V) center in a zwitterionic configuration, where antimony bears both cationic character (from formal positive charge) and anionic character (via an Sb-O^- group). This zwitterion is designed to interact with electron-deficient aromatic systems through anion-π interactions involving the negatively charged oxygen atom. The recognition scaffold is a calix[4]phosphole macrocycle, where four phosphole units (aromatic phosphorus heterocycles) provide a preorganized, electron-rich π-cavity that can also engage in secondary π-π stacking and lone pair-π interactions. The synthon combines: (1) a directional Sb···O^- electrostatic component (zwitterion internal charge separation), (2) anion-π interaction between the Sb-O^- moiety and electron-deficient arenes, (3) potential pnictogen bonding from the antimony's σ-hole, (4) π-π stacking between phosphole rings and guest aromatics, (5) conformational rigidity from the calixarene-like framework, (6) tunable electronics via phosphole P-substituents, and (7) potential temporal control via redox-switching of the phosphole units. This system explores underexplored supramolecular domains by combining pnictogen bonding (Sb), anion-π interactions, and phosphole aromaticity within a macrocyclic host.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]furan_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral arsenic(V) zwitterion (R₃As⁺-X⁻) interacting with electron-rich aromatic systems of a calix[4]furan macrocycle via anion-π interactions. The arsenic center bears three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl or alkyl groups) and one anionic group (e.g., carboxylate or sulfonate) that forms an intramolecular ion pair, creating a zwitterion. This zwitterion's anionic moiety is positioned to engage in directional anion-π interactions with the π-cloud of the electron-rich furan rings within the pre-organized calix[4]furan cavity. The calix[4]furan provides a convergent, bowl-shaped array of four furan units, enhancing binding through multipoint interactions. This system combines pnictogen (arsenic) coordination geometry, electrostatic zwitterion character, and supramolecular anion-π recognition in a single, programmable assembly motif.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]furan_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent arsenic(V) zwitterion center embedded within a calix[4]furan macrocycle. The system features a positively charged arsenic center (R4As+) with four organic substituents, creating a tetrahedral geometry. One substituent is a negatively charged carboxylate group tethered to the arsenic, forming an intramolecular zwitterion. The electron-deficient arsenic center and its associated positive charge create a potent anion-binding site via anion-π interactions with the electron-rich π-system of the adjacent furan rings in the calixarene-like scaffold. The calix[4]furan structure provides a pre-organized, concave binding pocket that enhances anion selectivity and binding affinity through cooperative interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction to the As+ center, (2) anion-π interactions with the furan rings, and (3) potential hydrogen bonding from the furan oxygen lone pairs. This represents a supramolecular umpolung synthon where the typically π-basic furan rings are engaged in anion-π interactions due to the proximal positive charge, enabling the recognition and assembly of anionic species in a modular fashion.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiazole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent arsenic(V) center embedded within a calix[4]thiazole macrocycle, creating a zwitterionic structure. The arsenic center bears a formal positive charge stabilized by four covalent bonds to electron-withdrawing substituents (e.g., -CF₃ groups), while the macrocyclic cavity, constructed from four electron-deficient thiazole rings, provides a convergent, π-acidic surface. This creates a dual recognition site: (1) an electrostatic and Lewis acidic site at the tetrahedral As⁺ center for anion binding (e.g., halides, BF₄⁻) and (2) a complementary anion-π binding pocket from the electron-poor thiazole rings of the calixarene-like structure, which can cooperatively stabilize the anion. This represents a supramolecular umpolung, where typically π-basic arenes are used for cation binding; here, an electron-deficient π-system is designed for anion recognition, working in concert with a main-group cationic center. The system maps to primitives: As⁺ (electrophile), anion (nucleophile), π-acidic surface (anion-π interaction), and the macrocyclic scaffold (preorganization).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_arsenic_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]furan_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent arsenic(V) center incorporated into a calix[4]furan macrocycle scaffold. The arsenic atom is functionalized with two electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., -CF₃) and one cationic substituent (e.g., -N⁺R₃), creating a zwitterionic structure with a formal positive charge on the nitrogen and a negative charge delocalized on the arsenic-oxygen bonds. This creates a strong, directional Lewis acidic pocket at the arsenic center, capable of anion binding. Simultaneously, the electron-deficient cavity formed by the four furan rings of the calixarene provides a complementary anion-π interaction site. The synthon operates through a cooperative binding mechanism: 1) electrostatic attraction between the cationic ammonium and the anion, 2) σ-hole bonding from the tetrahedral arsenic (pnictogen bond), and 3) multipoint anion-π interactions with the four furan rings. This represents a supramolecular umpolung by using an electron-deficient π-system (typically repulsive to anions) in concert with a zwitterionic pnictogen bond donor to create a potent, selective anion receptor.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_selenium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral selenium(IV) zwitterion center embedded within a calix[4]thiophene scaffold. The system features: 1) A central Se(IV) atom with two covalent bonds to organic substituents (e.g., phenyl groups), one coordinate bond to a Lewis base (e.g., pyridine N-oxide), and a formal positive charge, balanced by a tethered sulfonate anion (R-SO₃⁻) creating an intramolecular zwitterion. 2) The entire assembly is built on a calix[4]thiophene macrocycle, providing a pre-organized, electron-rich π-cavity. 3) Key recognition elements include: (a) the tetrahedral Se(IV) center acting as a dual pnictogen/chalcogen bond donor, (b) the anionic sulfonate for electrostatic and hydrogen bonding, (c) the thiophene-based calixarene π-system for anion-π interactions (the electron-deficient Se(IV) center polarizes the cavity, enhancing its affinity for anions), and (d) the macrocyclic structure enforcing a convergent binding pocket. This synthon enables 'supramolecular umpolung' by using the polarized cavity to bind and activate anions or neutral Lewis bases, facilitating novel assembly pathways distinct from typical cation-binding calixarenes.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where a cationic stannonium center (R₄Sn⁺) is intramolecularly stabilized by an adjacent anionic sulfonate group (-SO₃⁻), creating a zwitterionic motif. This charged yet overall neutral unit is designed to interact via multiple orthogonal non-covalent forces with a complementary π-electron-rich calix[4]thiophene receptor. Key recognition elements include: 1) Strong, directional anion-π interaction between the sulfonate anion and the electron-deficient cavity of the partially oxidized (or metal-coordinated) calix[4]thiophene, 2) Secondary cation-π interaction between the stannonium center and the adjacent thiophene sulfur lone pairs or aromatic rings, 3) Potential weak Sn...S chalcogen bonding or coordination. The calix[4]thiophene scaffold provides a pre-organized, convergent binding site. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically π-basic thiophene array is rendered π-acidic to bind an anion, while simultaneously engaging a cationic center. It is chemically realistic, drawing on known tetraorganotin chemistry and the tunable redox/coordination properties of thiophene macrocycles.

synthons.name: chalcogen_bonded_iodoethynyl_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a calix[4]thiophene macrocycle with electron-deficient iodoethynyl groups (-C≡C-I) positioned at the upper rim. The iodine atoms act as σ-hole donors (chalcogen bond donors) to coordinate anionic species (e.g., halides, carboxylates) above the macrocycle cavity. Simultaneously, the electron-rich thiophene sulfur atoms and the π-system of the calixarene scaffold engage in anion-π interactions with the bound anion, creating a synergistic, multi-point recognition motif. The linear iodoethynyl groups provide directional chalcogen bonds, while the pre-organized calixarene cone conformation offers a convergent binding pocket. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically electron-rich alkyne is rendered electrophilic at the iodine terminus, and the entire assembly functions as an anion receptor through combined chalcogen bonding and anion-π interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where the tin center bears both cationic (Sn⁺) and anionic (Sn⁻) character through intramolecular charge separation, stabilized by coordination to a calix[4]thiophene macrocycle. The calix[4]thiophene provides a π-rich cavity for anion binding via anion-π interactions, while the electron-deficient tin center can engage in pnictogen bonding with electron donors. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral tin center with zwitterionic character, (2) a calix[4]thiophene scaffold with four thiophene rings creating a π-acidic cavity, (3) anion-π interactions between the cavity and anionic guests, (4) potential Sn···N/Sn···O pnictogen bonds, (5) conformational flexibility of the calixarene for adaptive binding, (6) redox-active thiophene units enabling temporal switching, and (7) cooperative multi-point recognition. This synthon enables supramolecular umpolung by using the electron-deficient tin to attract nucleophiles while the π-acidic cavity attracts anions, creating dual electrophilic/nucleophilic recognition sites.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where a stannonium cation center (R₃Sn⁺) is intramolecularly stabilized by a covalently attached sulfonate anion (R-SO₃⁻) via electrostatic interaction, creating a zwitterionic motif. This zwitterion is designed to interact with an electron-deficient π-system, specifically a calix[4]thiophene macrocycle. The calix[4]thiophene provides a pre-organized, concave π-surface rich in electron density from the thiophene sulfur atoms, enabling dual-mode supramolecular recognition: (1) anion-π interaction between the sulfonate anion and the electron-deficient cavities of the fluorinated aryl rings incorporated into the calixarene scaffold, and (2) cation-π interaction between the stannonium center and the electron-rich thiophene π-systems. The tetrahedral geometry of the tin center enforces a specific spatial orientation of the interacting groups. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung synthon, as the typically anion-binding calixarene engages in anion-π interactions, while the organotin cation, often an electrophile, participates in stabilizing cation-π contacts. The seven primitives map as follows: Donor = sulfonate oxygen (anion) & thiophene π-system; Acceptor = electron-deficient aryl π-cavity & stannonium cation; Chassis = calix[4]thiophene macrocycle & tetrahedral tin core; Connector = covalent alkyl tether between Sn and SO₃ groups; Block = aryl fluorination on calixarene; Polarity = zwitterionic; Stereochemistry = tetrahedral Sn and cone conformation of calixarene.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where a positively charged stannonium center (R₃Sn⁺) is intramolecularly stabilized by a covalently attached sulfonate anion (R-SO₃⁻) through electrostatic and coordinative interactions. This zwitterion is further designed with extended aromatic arms terminating in thiophene rings. The synthon's recognition elements enable: (1) anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient stannonium-adjacent arenes and anionic guests, (2) π-π stacking of the calix[4]thiophene-like arrangement of the four thiophene arms, creating a pre-organized electron-rich cavity, and (3) Lewis acidic character at the tin center for additional substrate coordination. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using the formally cationic tin center to attract electron-rich species via its associated anion and cavity, while the electron-rich thiophene cavity can simultaneously engage electron-deficient guests. This creates a dual, tunable binding environment. It maps to the seven primitives as: atoms (Sn, S, O, C, H), bonds (covalent Sn-C, S-C, C-C; ionic/electrostatic; anion-π; π-π), intermolecular interactions (anion-π, π-π, electrostatic, coordinative), topology (tetrahedral at Sn, macrocyclic-like from thiophene arrangement), electrons (charge-separated zwitterion, aromatic systems), dynamics (conformational flexibility of the calix-like arms, exchange of coordinated guests), and energy (binding energies of supramolecular interactions, strain in the pre-organized structure).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where the tin center bears a formal positive charge stabilized by intramolecular coordination from a pendant anionic group (e.g., carboxylate or phenolate), while the overall molecule adopts a conformation that presents an electron-deficient π-surface. This π-surface is provided by a calix[4]thiophene scaffold, where four thiophene rings replace the traditional phenol units of a calixarene. The electron-deficient nature of the thiophene rings in this oxidized or metal-coordinated state creates a potent anion-π recognition site. The synthon operates through a dual interaction pattern: (1) the zwitterionic tin center acts as a Lewis acidic, electrophilic site for anion binding or substrate activation (molecular primitive), and (2) the pre-organized calix[4]thiophene cavity provides a complementary supramolecular anion-π binding pocket, enabling the assembly of larger architectures or the stabilization of anionic intermediates. This represents a supramolecular umpolung, as the typically electron-rich thiophene π-system is engineered to attract anions, working in concert with the electrophilic metal center.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where a cationic stannonium center (R₃Sn⁺) is intramolecularly stabilized by a covalently attached anionic sulfonate group (-SO₃⁻) on one organic arm, creating a zwitterionic structure. This charged moiety is designed to interact via synergistic anion-π and cation-π interactions with a complementary π-electron-rich, bowl-shaped calix[4]thiophene host. The calix[4]thiophene provides a preorganized, electron-rich cavity from four thiophene rings, facilitating strong, directional binding. The synthon exploits (1) electrostatic attraction between the Sn⁺ center and the π-cloud (cation-π), (2) attraction between the -SO₃⁻ anion and the δ+ rim of the thiophene rings (anion-π), and (3) potential CH-π and van der Waals contacts. This represents a supramolecular umpolung system where both cationic and anionic sites on the same molecule engage a neutral, polarized π-surface, enabling novel assembly and recognition pathways distinct from standard ion pairing.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where a cationic stannonium center (R₄Sn⁺) is intramolecularly stabilized by an adjacent anionic sulfonate group (-SO₃⁻) on one ligand arm, creating a zwitterionic motif. This charged moiety is integrated into a calix[4]thiophene macrocyclic scaffold, where the four thiophene rings provide a preorganized, electron-rich π-cavity. The synthon operates through two primary, orthogonal recognition modes: 1) The tetrahedral stannonium center acts as a potent Lewis acidic/cationic site for anion binding (e.g., halides, carboxylates) via dative/electrostatic interactions. 2) The calix[4]thiophene basket engages in strong anion-π interactions with the bound anion, utilizing the electron-deficient character induced in the π-system by the adjacent positively charged Sn center and the intrinsic polarizability of the thiophene S atoms. This creates a synergistic, chelate-like binding environment for anions. The system is chemically realistic, drawing on known organotin chemistry and the tunable electronics of thiophene-based macrocycles. It maps to the seven primitives via its charged sites (anion, cation), directional non-covalent bonds (anion-π, coordination), and preorganized macrocyclic structure (cavity).

synthons.name: diboronate_ester_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle with two boronate ester groups bridging opposite pyridine nitrogen atoms. The system features: 1) A tetrahedral boron center at each bridge, creating a zwitterionic character with partial negative charge on boron-bound oxygen and partial positive charge on boron; 2) An electron-deficient cavity formed by the four pyridine rings, creating a strong anion-π recognition site; 3) The boronate ester groups provide additional Lewis acid character for anion binding. Recognition elements include: anion-π interactions between the cavity and anionic guests, Lewis acid-base interactions at boron centers, and potential hydrogen bonding from boronate ester OH groups. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically electron-rich calixarene cavities are made electron-deficient, and neutral boron centers become anion-binding sites through geometric constraint and electronic modulation.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where the tin center bears both cationic (R₃Sn⁺) and anionic (Sn⁻-heteroatom) character within the same molecule, positioned above a calix[4]thiophene macrocycle. The calixarene-like structure incorporates four thiophene units linked at the 2,5-positions, creating an electron-rich π-bowl. The zwitterionic tin complex features: (1) three aryl groups providing steric bulk and potential π-surface, (2) a fourth tin-heteroatom bond (Sn⁻-O⁻ or Sn⁻-N⁻) creating an intramolecular anion, and (3) overall charge separation stabilized by through-space electrostatic interactions. The synthon operates via: (a) anion-π interactions between the tin-bound anionic site and the electron-deficient regions of the thiophene π-system, (b) potential cation-π interactions from the tin-centered partial positive charge to adjacent arene rings, and (c) directional coordination of the tin center to sulfur lone pairs. This represents a supramolecular umpolung system where both electrophilic and nucleophilic sites coexist and are spatially organized for selective binding or reactivity. The seven primitives map as: atoms (Sn, S, C, H, O/N), bonds (covalent Sn-C, Sn-heteroatom; non-covalent anion-π, cation-π, coordination), angles (tetrahedral around Sn, thiophene ring angles), dihedrals (calixarene conformation, aryl group rotation), charges (zwitterionic separation), polarization (Sn-heteroatom bond polarization, π-system polarization), and spatial (preorganized bowl-shaped cavity with directional interactions).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where a positively charged stannonium center (R₄Sn⁺) is intramolecularly stabilized by a covalently attached sulfonate anion (R-SO₃⁻) via electrostatic and coordinative interactions. This zwitterion is further functionalized with a calix[4]thiophene macrocycle at one of its organic substituents. The calix[4]thiophene provides a pre-organized, electron-rich π-cavity (via four thiophene rings) capable of strong anion-π interactions with an external anionic guest (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, NO₃⁻). The overall system exhibits a dual supramolecular recognition motif: 1) the intrinsic zwitterionic pair (Sn⁺···⁻O₃S) represents an intramolecular ion pair synthon, and 2) the calixarene-derived cavity provides an anion-binding site via cooperative anion-π and dipole interactions from the polarized thiophene S atoms. This creates a 'tweezer-like' system where the stannonium center can influence the electron density of the cavity, potentially enabling redox-switchable anion binding. It maps to the seven primitives via: Donor (sulfonate O, thiophene S/π), Acceptor (stannonium Sn, thiophene ring centroid), Positive (Sn⁺), Negative (SO₃⁻), Hydrophobic (alkyl/aryl substituents on Sn and calixarene), Aromatic (thiophene rings), and Polarizable (Sn center, S atoms, π-system).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion where a cationic stannonium center (R₄Sn⁺) is intramolecularly stabilized by an adjacent anionic carboxylate group, creating a zwitterionic structure. This zwitterion features a calix[4]pyridine scaffold that provides a preorganized, electron-deficient π-cavity. The synthon operates through two primary supramolecular interactions: 1) The electron-deficient cavity engages in strong anion-π interactions with anionic guests (e.g., halides, carboxylates), and 2) The positively charged tin center acts as a Lewis acidic site for additional coordination or electrostatic attraction. The calix[4]pyridine structure offers conformational rigidity and tunable electronics through pyridine N-oxide or N-alkylation, while the tetrahedral tin center introduces stereogenicity and potential for chirality transfer. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung by using a traditionally σ-electron-deficient metal center (Sn⁺) embedded within a π-acidic cavity to create a potent receptor for anions, inverting typical charge-affinity patterns.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tin_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]thiophene_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraorganotin(IV) zwitterion featuring a positively charged tin center (R₃Sn⁺) and a negatively charged sulfonate group (SO₃⁻) on a pendant arm, designed to interact with a complementary calix[4]thiophene receptor via a synergistic combination of anion-π interactions (between the sulfonate and the electron-deficient thiophene rings of the calixarene), cation-π interactions (between the Sn⁺ center and the π-system), and potential weak Sn···S tetrel bonds. The calix[4]thiophene scaffold provides a pre-organized, electron-poor π-cavity ideal for binding the anionic moiety, while the zwitterionic nature of the tin compound introduces an umpolung character—the typically electrophilic tin center is part of a cation, yet the molecule overall carries a net zero charge with separated positive and negative regions. This system exemplifies a supramolecular umpolung synthon where complementary electrostatic and non-covalent interactions (anion-π, cation-π, tetrel bonding) enable reversible, directional assembly for constructing metallo-supramolecular architectures.

synthons.name: iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle that simultaneously engages in three distinct non-covalent interactions to bind a reactive iodonium cation (R-I⁺-R'). The synthon features: 1) Anion-π interactions between the electron-deficient pyridine rings of the calixarene and a weakly-coordinating counter-anion (e.g., [B(C₆F₅)₄]⁻ or [Al(ORF)₄]⁻). 2) Cation-π interactions between the electron-rich aromatic cavity of the calixarene and the positively charged iodine center of the iodonium cation. 3) Secondary halogen bonding between the iodine σ-hole and a nitrogen lone pair of a pyridine, further orienting the cation. This creates a stabilized, pre-organized assembly where the calixarene acts as a 'supramolecular umpolung' template, shielding and activating the typically electrophilic iodonium species for subsequent nucleophilic attack in a controlled, regioselective manner. The system is chemically realistic, drawing from known iodonium salt chemistry and the host-guest capabilities of heterocalixarenes.

synthons.name: iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle that simultaneously engages in three distinct non-covalent interactions: (1) an iodonium cation (I⁺ center, e.g., from a diaryliodonium salt) positioned in the macrocycle cavity via cation-π interactions with the electron-rich pyridine rings, (2) a complementary anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or BArF₄⁻) held above the cavity via anion-π interactions with the partially positive electrostatic potential of the pyridine nitrogens, and (3) halogen bonding between the iodonium's σ-hole (along the I–C axis) and a lone pair from a pyridine nitrogen or an external nucleophile. This creates a stable, three-point recognition motif where the calixarene scaffold pre-organizes the interaction sites. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using the typically π-basic pyridine rings in an anion-π binding mode while also engaging in strong cation-π and halogen bonding. It can be mapped to the seven primitives: recognition (cation, anion, halogen bond donor/acceptor), interaction (electrostatic, polarization), assembly (macrocyclic pre-organization), and function (host-guest binding, potential catalysis or transport).

synthons.name: iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a calix[4]triazole macrocycle that simultaneously engages in three distinct non-covalent interactions: (1) an iodonium cation (I⁺) centered within the macrocyclic cavity via cation-π interactions with the electron-rich triazole rings, (2) anion binding (e.g., Cl⁻, BF₄⁻) via cooperative hydrogen bonding from the triazole N-H groups at the lower rim, and (3) π-stacking interactions between adjacent macrocycles facilitated by the planar triazole units. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung synthon where the typically σ-hole donating iodine is instead a cationic center (I⁺), creating a strong, polarized binding pocket. The calix[4]triazole scaffold provides preorganization and convergent binding sites, making it effective for assembling higher-order architectures through halogen bonding (via the iodonium), hydrogen bonding, and π-stacking. It maps cleanly to the seven primitives: atoms (C, H, N, I), bonds (covalent bonds in macrocycle, coordinate bond to I⁺), interactions (cation-π, hydrogen bonding, anion-π, halogen bonding), rings (triazole, macrocycle), chains (alkyl groups at lower rim), groups (iodonium, triazole), and frameworks (calixarene-like 3D structure).

synthons.name: iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent iodine(III) center (iodonium cation) embedded within a calix[4]triazole scaffold. The system features: 1) A central hypervalent iodine atom with two covalent bonds to the triazole nitrogen atoms of the calixarene framework, creating a rigid, bowl-shaped iodonium cation. 2) An inherent positive charge on the iodine center, making it a potent electrophilic halogen bond donor. 3) A convergent π-electron-rich cavity formed by the four electron-deficient 1,2,4-triazole rings, which is pre-organized for anion-π interactions. The synthon operates via a dual recognition mechanism: the iodonium center acts as a strong halogen bond (XB) acceptor for anions (e.g., halides, tetrafluoroborate), while the triazole-lined cavity provides complementary anion-π binding sites. This creates a synergistic, charge-assisted supramolecular assembly motif. The system is chemically realistic, drawing on established hypervalent iodine chemistry and the known anion-binding properties of triazoles and calixarenes. It maps to primitives: Atom (I, N), Charge (+1 on I), Orbital (σ-hole of I, π* of triazole), Geometry (tetrahedral at I, cone conformation of calixarene), Connectivity (covalent I-N bonds, non-covalent XB and anion-π), Energy (electrostatic and polarization components), and Time (dynamic conformational adjustment of the calixarene rim).

synthons.name: iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a calix[4]triazole macrocycle that simultaneously engages in three distinct non-covalent interactions: (1) an iodonium cation (I⁺ center stabilized by two aryl groups) as a strong halogen bond donor, (2) an anion (e.g., tetrafluoroborate, hexafluorophosphate) for charge balance and electrostatic interaction, and (3) π-electron-rich triazole rings for anion-π interactions. The calix[4]triazole scaffold provides a pre-organized, electron-deficient cavity due to the combined effect of four 1,2,3-triazole units, which are known for their strong dipole moments and ability to engage in anion binding. The iodonium cation, positioned on the upper rim or a pendant arm, acts as a powerful electrophilic recognition site for Lewis bases (halogen bond acceptor), enabling umpolung behavior where the typically nucleophilic iodine acts as an electrophile. This creates a zwitterionic-like supramolecular building block capable of orthogonal recognition events—simultaneous binding of an anion via the cavity and a neutral or anionic Lewis base via the iodonium center. The system is chemically realistic, with iodonium salts and triazole-based macrocycles being well-documented in the literature. It maps cleanly to the seven primitives: recognition (triazole cavity, I⁺), interaction (anion-π, halogen bonding, electrostatic), reactivity (electrophilic I⁺), stability (aromatic stabilization, charge separation), transformation (anion exchange, coordination), building block (macrocyclic scaffold), and environment (solvent-dependent assembly).

synthons.name: iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent iodonium cation (I⁺ center) stabilized by two pyridine ligands in a calix[4]pyridine macrocyclic scaffold. The system features: (1) a strong iodonium cation (I⁺) as an electrophilic recognition site, (2) an electron-deficient cavity formed by four pyridine rings in a cone conformation, creating an anion-π binding pocket, and (3) zwitterionic character through charge separation. The iodonium center engages in pnictogen bonding (I⁺···N) with the pyridine nitrogens, while the electron-poor pyridine rings provide multiple anion-π interaction sites for anions like Cl⁻, Br⁻, or BF₄⁻. This creates a dual recognition motif where the cationic iodonium attracts anions electrostatically, and the π-acidic cavity provides directional stabilization via anion-π interactions. The calix[4]pyridine framework enforces preorganization and enhances binding selectivity. This synthon enables supramolecular umpolung by using a typically π-basic heterocycle (pyridine) in an electron-deficient, anion-binding role when incorporated into the rigid macrocycle.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral iodonium cation (I⁺ center with three organic substituents) interacting with an electron-deficient calix[4]pyridine macrocycle through anion-π and cation-π cooperative interactions. The iodonium center bears a positive charge stabilized by hypervalent 3-center-4-electron bonds with two aryl groups and one alkyl group, creating a strong electrophilic region. The calix[4]pyridine adopts a cone conformation with four electron-deficient pyridine rings oriented inward, creating a π-acidic cavity. The synthon involves: (1) electrostatic attraction between I⁺ and the electron-rich regions of the pyridine nitrogens, (2) anion-π interactions between the iodonium's associated anion (e.g., BF₄⁻ or PF₆⁻) and the electron-deficient pyridine rings, and (3) CH-π interactions between alkyl substituents on iodonium and the aromatic walls.
