This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic calixarenes are replaced by π-acidic counterparts, and conventional cation binding is augmented by simultaneous anion recognition within the same cavity.

synthons.name: iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon_3

The synthon features: 1) Anion-π interaction between the electron-deficient iodonium cation's counter-anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) and the electron-rich π-surface of the triazole rings in the calixarene cavity. 2) Cation-π interaction between the positively charged iodine center (I⁺) and the same π-system. 3) Halogen bonding between the σ-hole on the iodine atom and nitrogen lone pairs on the triazole moieties. This creates a synergistic, three-point recognition motif ideal for supramolecular assembly and crystal engineering. The calix[4]triazole scaffold provides preorganization and tunable electron density, while the iodonium cation serves as a unique, linear bifunctional electrophile with both cationic and halogen bonding character.

synthons.name: iodonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]triazole_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on an iodonium cation (R₂I⁺) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]triazole macrocycle through anion-π and charge-assisted interactions. The system features: (1) a positively charged tetravalent iodine center (hypervalent iodonium) as the cationic recognition element, (2) a bowl-shaped calix[4]arene scaffold where four aromatic rings are replaced by 1,2,4-triazole units, creating an electron-deficient π-cavity, (3) an accompanying weakly-coordinating anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻, or BArF₂₄⁻) that can engage in anion-π interactions with the triazole rings, and (4) additional secondary interactions such as C–H···π and lone pair–π between iodonium substituents and the macrocycle rim. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic calixarenes are made π-acidic via heterocycle substitution, creating a complementary pair for iodonium electrophiles rarely explored in host-guest chemistry.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion with a cationic stibonium center (R4Sb+) and an anionic carboxylate arm, designed to interact with electron-deficient π-systems of a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The zwitterion features: (1) a permanent positive charge on antimony (pnictogen bond donor), (2) a flexible anionic carboxylate group (hydrogen bond acceptor/ionic interaction site), and (3) hydrophobic aryl substituents. The calix[4]pyridine provides convergent pyridine N-oxides as anion-π acceptors and electron-deficient aromatic cavities. Recognition occurs through simultaneous: anion-π interaction between carboxylate and pyridine N-oxide rings, pnictogen bonding between Sb+ and pyridine lone pairs, and hydrophobic complementarity. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cationic metal centers are paired with anion receptors—here a cationic pnictogen center cooperatively binds an anion receptor via its own anionic arm.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion with a cationic stibonium center (R4Sb+) and an anionic carboxylate arm, designed to interact with electron-deficient π-systems of a complementary calix[4]pyridine receptor. The zwitterion features: (1) a tetrahedral Sb(V) center with three aryl groups and one alkyl chain terminating in a carboxylate anion, creating intramolecular charge separation; (2) the cationic stibonium center acts as a strong hydrogen bond acceptor and weak Lewis acid; (3) the anionic carboxylate provides hydrogen bond acceptor sites; (4) the system engages in multiple simultaneous interactions with calix[4]pyridine: anion-π interactions between carboxylate and electron-deficient pyridine rings, cation-π interactions between stibonium and pyridine rings, and potential C–H···O hydrogen bonds from pyridine C–H to carboxylate. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where both cationic and anionic moieties of the same molecule participate in complementary π-interactions with a neutral receptor.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion with a cationic antimony center bearing three organic substituents and an intramolecular anionic carboxylate group, designed to engage in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient pyridine rings of a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The antimony center exhibits σ-hole characteristics enabling pnictogen bonding, while the zwitterion's overall positive charge enhances anion binding. The calix[4]pyridine provides a convergent π-acidic cavity for anion recognition through cooperative anion-π interactions with all four pyridine rings. This system combines pnictogen bonding (Sb), electrostatic interactions, and multi-point anion-π recognition in a preorganized supramolecular assembly, representing a supramolecular umpolung approach where typically π-basic aromatic systems are engineered as π-acidic anion receptors.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion center (R₃Sb⁺-X⁻ where X = carboxylate or sulfonate) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The positively charged antimony center participates in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient pyridine rings of the calixarene, while the anionic moiety (X⁻) forms electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding contacts with the pyridine N atoms or pendant hydroxyl groups on the upper rim. This creates a three-point recognition motif: (1) electrostatic attraction between Sb⁺ and electron-rich π-cloud edges, (2) anion binding to the macrocycle's Lewis basic sites, and (3) potential CH-π or dipole-dipole stabilization from alkyl/aryl substituents on antimony. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using a normally cationic pnictogen center to attract electron-deficient aromatics via anion-π geometry, while the anionic counterion acts as an organizing element. The calix[4]pyridine scaffold provides preorganization and additional binding sites for cooperative assembly.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetracoordinated antimony(V) center bearing both cationic and anionic substituents, creating a zwitterionic structure. The antimony atom is bound to two pyridine rings of a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle via Sb–N coordination bonds, positioning it within the electron-deficient cavity. The remaining two substituents are a positively charged trimethylammonium group (via Sb–C bond) and a negatively charged carboxylate group (via Sb–O bond), establishing a permanent zwitterion. This creates a convergent binding site where: 1) The cationic ammonium moiety engages in anion binding (electrostatic/hydrogen bonding) to external anions, 2) The anionic carboxylate engages in cation binding to external cations, and 3) The electron-deficient cavity of the calix[4]pyridine provides an anion-π binding site for additional anionic guests. This system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by simultaneously presenting orthogonal anion- and cation-binding motifs from a single metal center, enabling the assembly of complex ionic networks or the co‑templation of salt bridges within confined spaces.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion with a cationic antimony center bearing three organic substituents and one anionic oxygen ligand, paired with a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The synthon exploits multiple orthogonal interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction between the cationic Sb(V) center and the electron-rich pyridine nitrogens, (2) anion-π interactions between the anionic oxygen ligand bound to antimony and the electron-deficient cavity of the protonated pyridinium forms of the calixarene, (3) potential halogen bonding if halogenated substituents are present on the antimony, and (4) conformational complementarity where the tetrahedral geometry of the antimony center fits into the cone-shaped cavity of the calix[4]pyridine. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cationic metal centers are paired with anion receptors; here, the cationic metal center acts as an electrophile for heteroatom lone pairs while its anionic ligand acts as a nucleophile for π-acidic surfaces.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_6

The system features: (1) a central Sb(V) atom bonded to three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl groups) and one positively charged ammonium arm, creating a zwitterionic structure; (2) a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle that provides convergent π-basic pyridine N-atoms for anion binding (anion-π interactions with electron-deficient pyridines) and a preorganized cavity; (3) the cationic ammonium arm of the zwitterion can engage in electrostatic attraction with an anionic guest (e.g., halide, sulfate) bound within the calixarene cavity; (4) the electron-deficient Sb center can participate in pnictogen bonding with lone pairs from the pyridine N or the anion; (5) the phenyl substituents on Sb provide additional π-stacking surfaces with the aromatic walls of the calixarene. This creates a multi-point recognition system where the zwitterion acts as a supramolecular 'glue' that bridges anionic guests and the electron-deficient macrocycle through combined electrostatic, pnictogen, anion-π, and π-stacking interactions, enabling temporal assembly and disassembly under redox or pH control.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_7

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_8

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]phosphole_synthon_1

This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically π-basic calixarene-like cavity is inverted to π-acidic, and a zwitterion (not a simple anion) is used as the recognition partner. The seven primitives map as: (1) Atoms: Sb, P, C, H, O; (2) Bonds: covalent Sb-C, P-C, C-C, C-H, C=O; (3) Topology: tetrahedral at Sb, macrocyclic bowl; (4) Interactions: electrostatic (zwitterion), anion-π, van der Waals; (5) Dynamics: guest orientation within cavity; (6) Energy: anion-π binding energy (~20-50 kJ/mol); (7) Function: directed assembly of hybrid organic-inorganic architectures.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_9

The calix[4]pyridine, with its four electron-deficient pyridine rings, creates a complementary π-acidic cavity that selectively binds anions through cooperative anion-π interactions. The cationic stibonium center participates in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient pyridine rings of the calixarene, while the carboxylate arm forms strong hydrogen bonds with the pyridine N-H groups (if protonated) or engages in charge-assisted hydrogen bonding with water/co-solvent networks. synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion center (R₃Sb⁺-X⁻) that simultaneously engages in three orthogonal non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction between the positively charged antimony center and an anionic species (halide, carboxylate, or sulfonate), (2) anion-π interaction between the same anion and the electron-deficient π-system of a proximal pyridine ring within a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle scaffold, and (3) secondary Sb···N pnictogen bonding from the antimony to a nitrogen atom of an adjacent pyridine unit. The calix[4]pyridine provides a rigid, pre-organized cavity that positions the electron-deficient aromatic rings to cooperatively enhance anion binding. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically π-basic arene is rendered π-acidic via incorporation into an electron-withdrawing heterocycle and proximity to a permanent positive charge, creating a synergistic anion recognition pocket. The tetrahedral geometry of the antimony center enforces directional interactions, while the zwitterionic nature provides solubility in polar media. This synthon is mappable to the seven primitives through its defined interaction vectors (electrostatic, anion-π, pnictogen bond), spatial arrangement (tetrahedral node, macrocyclic scaffold), and dynamic exchange potential (anion binding/release).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]phosphole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion center (R₃Sb⁺-X⁻) where the positively charged antimony acts as a strong anion-π acceptor. The system incorporates a calix[4]phosphole scaffold—a macrocycle composed of four phosphole units—which provides a preorganized, electron-deficient π-surface. The zwitterion's anionic component (X⁻ = halide, carboxylate, or sulfonate) is positioned above the phosphole π-system via intramolecular electrostatic guidance, creating a robust intramolecular anion-π interaction. This synthon can further engage in intermolecular interactions through the remaining antimony Lewis acidity, the exposed anion, and the electron-deficient aromatic rings, enabling hierarchical assembly. It represents a supramolecular umpolung by using a formally cationic pnictogen center to template and stabilize an anionic moiety over an aromatic surface, combining pnictogen bonding, anion-π interactions, and macrocyclic preorganization.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion with a cationic stibonium center (R4Sb+) and an anionic carboxylate group (COO-) on the same molecule. This zwitterion acts as a dual recognition element: (1) the positively charged antimony center engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient pyridine rings of a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle, and (2) the carboxylate anion participates in hydrogen bonding with NH groups of the calixarene scaffold or with additional complementary partners. The calix[4]pyridine provides a preorganized, electron-poor π-surface ideal for anion-π interactions with the stibonium cation, while its alternating pyridine-nitrogen sites offer additional coordination or hydrogen-bonding opportunities. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-binding calixarenes are repurposed to bind anions through anion-π interactions with an embedded cationic center, creating a novel three-component recognition pattern (zwitterion electrostatic, anion-π, hydrogen bonding) that can direct assembly in solution or the solid state.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_13
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion center (R₃Sb⁺-X⁻) interacting with a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle through cooperative anion-π and cation-π interactions. The antimony center bears three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl groups) and a formal positive charge, balanced by a tightly associated anion (e.g., Cl⁻, Br⁻, or BF₄⁻) positioned above the electron-deficient cavity of the calix[4]pyridine. The calixarene's four pyridine rings provide a convergent, π-acidic surface for anion binding, while their nitrogen lone pairs can engage in secondary interactions with the antimony-bound substituents. This creates a three-point recognition motif: (1) electrostatic attraction between the Sb⁺ center and the electron-rich pyridine nitrogens (cation-π), (2) anion-π interaction between the associated halide and the pyridine rings, and (3) potential CH-π contacts from the calixarene methylene bridges to the antimony substituents. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using a typically π-basic aromatic cavity for anion recognition (π-acidic behavior) in concert with a heavy pnictogen cation. It maps to the seven primitives through its defined interaction surfaces, complementary charges, directional preferences, and dynamic anion association/dissociation that could be temporally controlled.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion center (R₃Sb⁺-X⁻) where the cationic antimony center engages in anion-π interactions with electron-deficient pyridine rings of a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral antimony(V) atom bearing three organic substituents (e.g., phenyl groups) and a formal positive charge, stabilized by an adjacent anionic group (e.g., carboxylate, sulfonate) creating a zwitterion; (2) a calix[4]pyridine host with four electron-deficient pyridine rings in a cone conformation; (3) strong electrostatic anion-π interactions between the cationic Sb center and the π-acidic pyridine rings; (4) potential secondary interactions including C–H···π, π-π stacking of aromatic substituents, and hydrogen bonding involving the anionic moiety. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic arenes would avoid cations, but here electron-deficient arenes attract the cationic antimony center. The seven primitives map as: atoms (Sb, C, N, O), bonds (covalent Sb–C, ionic interactions, anion-π), motifs (tetrahedral Sb center, macrocyclic cone), geometries (tetrahedral, cone conformation), interactions (anion-π, electrostatic, van der Waals), assemblies (host-guest complex), and functions (molecular recognition, supramolecular catalysis).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon_15
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion with a cationic stibonium center (R₄Sb⁺) and an anionic carboxylate arm (COO⁻) that engages in dual interactions with a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The zwitterion's cationic stibonium center forms a strong pnictogen bond (Sb⁺···N) with the pyridine nitrogen atoms of the calixarene, while its anionic carboxylate group participates in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient pyridine rings of the same macrocycle. This creates a cooperative, chelate-like supramolecular assembly where the calix[4]pyridine acts as a convergent receptor for both cationic and anionic sites of the same zwitterion. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using both positively charged (Sb⁺) and negatively charged (COO⁻) regions of the same molecule to bind to complementary sites on the macrocycle, enabling directional assembly. The antimony center provides heavy atom characteristics that could enable temporal control via redox or photochemical switching between Sb(V) and Sb(III) states.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]phosphole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral germanium(IV) center with zwitterionic character, featuring a positively charged germanium atom (Ge⁺) bound to three aromatic substituents and one anionic ligand (e.g., borate or carboxylate). This Ge(IV) zwitterion engages in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient π-system of a calix[4]phosphole macrocycle. The calix[4]phosphole consists of four phosphole rings (aromatic phosphorus heterocycles) linked by methylene bridges, creating a concave, electron-poor cavity ideal for stabilizing the anionic component of the zwitterion via cooperative anion-π and electrostatic interactions. This system combines pnictogen bonding (from phosphorus in phosphole), anion-π interactions, and zwitterion stabilization, representing a novel supramolecular assembly motif with potential for hierarchical organization and dynamic exchange (temporal domain).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]phosphole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral germanium(IV) zwitterion center embedded within a calix[4]phosphole macrocycle. The synthon features: 1) A central Ge(IV) atom bonded to three alkyl/aryl groups and one anionic site (e.g., -O⁻ or -S⁻), creating a permanent zwitterion with a formal positive charge on Ge and a localized negative charge on the heteroatom. 2) The germanium center is integrated into the lower rim of a calix[4]arene scaffold where one or more benzene rings are replaced by phosphole units (C₄PH₄). The phosphole provides a σ-hole on phosphorus for pnictogen bonding and an expanded, electron-deficient π-surface. 3) Key recognition elements include: (a) The tetrahedral Ge⁺-centered cation as a strong electrostatic anchor, (b) The adjacent anion (O⁻/S⁻) for charge complementarity, (c) The electron-deficient, bowl-shaped π-system of the calix[4]phosphole for anion-π interactions with guest anions, and (d) The σ-hole on phosphorus for orthogonal pnictogen bonding. This creates a multi-modal, Umpolung-type receptor where the typically cation-binding calixarene cavity is engineered to selectively bind anions through combined anion-π, electrostatic, and pnictogen bonding, suitable for constructing supramolecular assemblies and sensors.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_germanium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]phosphole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral germanium(IV) zwitterion center embedded within a calix[4]phosphole macrocycle. The system features: 1) A central Ge(IV) atom with two anionic oxygen ligands (e.g., from carboxylates or phenoxides) and two cationic nitrogen ligands from pyridinium-type groups, creating an overall zwitterionic charge-separated core. 2) A calix[4]arene-like scaffold where four phosphole (C₄H₃P) units replace the traditional benzene rings, providing a conformationally flexible, electron-deficient π-bowl. 3) The anionic oxygen ligands on germanium project into the π-concave cavity of the phosphole calix, enabling strong, directional anion-π interactions with the electron-poor phosphole rings. 4) The cationic pyridinium arms extend outward, available for additional electrostatic or hydrogen-bonding interactions with external species. This creates a polarized, multifunctional recognition site that combines anion-π, electrostatic, and potential P···O pnictogen bonding (from phosphole P to Ge-O) in a single, pre-organized assembly. It is a supramolecular umpolung synthon as the typically π-basic calixarene cavity is rendered π-acidic by phosphole substitution, inverting its recognition preferences to bind anions rather than cations.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π and chalcogen-chalcogen interactions. The telluronium center bears a positive charge stabilized by three organic substituents (e.g., aryl groups), while the calix[4]tellurophene consists of four tellurophene rings linked by methylene bridges, creating a π-electron-rich, bowl-shaped cavity. The primary recognition involves: 1) electrostatic anion-π interaction between the telluronium cation (acting as a 'cationic guest') and the electron-rich tellurophene π-system of the macrocycle, 2) secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonding between the telluronium center and the tellurium atoms in the macrocycle, and 3) potential C–H···π interactions from the telluronium's aryl substituents. This system represents a rare example of heavy chalcogen-based supramolecular assembly with dual interaction modes, enabling the preorganization of reactants for subsequent tellurium-centered transformations or as a building block for supramolecular polymers.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π and cation-π cooperative interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic charge and potential for chalcogen bonding, while the calix[4]tellurophene offers a preorganized π-basic cavity with four tellurophene units creating an electron-rich aromatic surface. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung as the typically π-basic calixarene-like structure is inverted to serve as an anion binder through anion-π interactions, while simultaneously engaging the cation through cation-π effects. Recognition elements include: (1) telluronium cationic center, (2) calix[4]tellurophene π-basic cavity, (3) anion-π interactions between anions and tellurophene rings, (4) cation-π interactions between telluronium and aromatic systems, (5) potential Te···anion chalcogen bonds, and (6) conformational preorganization of the macrocycle. This represents a novel combination of heavy pnictogen chemistry with macrocyclic π-systems for orthogonal recognition.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via cooperative anion-π and chalcogen-chalcogen interactions. The system features: (1) a tetrahedral telluronium center as the cationic recognition element, (2) a calix[4]tellurophene host with four tellurophene rings creating a π-electron rich, bowl-shaped cavity, (3) an anion (e.g., Cl-, Br-, I-) that bridges the cation and host through electrostatic interactions with Te+ and anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient face of the tellurophene rings, and (4) secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonding between the telluronium and tellurophene sulfur analogs. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic tellurophenes engage in anion-π interactions due to polarization effects from the cationic telluronium, creating a three-component recognition motif applicable to hierarchical assembly and anion transport applications.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_tellurium_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent tellurium center in a zwitterionic structure, where the tellurium atom bears both positive and negative formal charges through hypervalent bonding. The system features a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle composed of four tellurophene (C₄H₄Te) units, creating an electron-rich π-cavity. The tellurium zwitterion (e.g., R-Te⁺-X⁻ where X is an anionic ligand like hydroxide or halide) engages in dual interactions: (1) anion-π interactions between the anionic part of the zwitterion and the electron-deficient face of the tellurophene rings, and (2) chalcogen bonding between the Te⁺ center and electron-rich regions of adjacent synthons. This creates a reversible, directional assembly motif with potential for temporal control via redox switching between Te(IV) and Te(II) states. The system demonstrates supramolecular umpolung by using an anion-π interaction (typically considered repulsive) as an attractive force within the zwitterionic context.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_antimony_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral antimony(V) zwitterion with a cationic antimony center bearing three organic substituents and one anionic oxygen ligand, paired with a π-acidic calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The antimony center acts as a strong pnictogen bond donor through its σ-hole along the Sb–O bond axis. The calix[4]tellurophene, composed of four tellurophene rings linked by methylene bridges, provides a pre-organized, electron-deficient cavity with tellurium atoms contributing to both σ-holes (for secondary Te···O interactions) and a π-acidic aromatic surface. The primary recognition involves: 1) a directional pnictogen bond (Sb···π) from the σ-hole on Sb(V) to the electron-deficient π-cloud of the tellurophene rings, and 2) anion-π interactions between the anionic oxygen ligand on antimony and the same π-acidic surface. The calixarene-like conformation enforces a convergent binding site, making this a modular, charge-assisted supramolecular synthon for constructing ordered assemblies with orthogonal interaction vectors.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a π-electron rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The synthon features: 1) A strong electrostatic cation-anion interaction between the telluronium center and a nearby anionic site (e.g., carboxylate, tetrafluoroborate). 2) A simultaneous, orthogonal anion-π interaction where the same anion is positioned over the electron-deficient face of one of the tellurophene rings in the calixarene scaffold. 3) The calix[4]tellurophene provides a pre-organized, electron-rich cavity with four tellurophene units, creating a unique π-surface for anion binding. 4) The telluronium cation's large, polarizable Te center enhances both electrostatic and dispersion components of the binding. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically π-basic tellurophene ring participates in anion-π interactions due to the electron-withdrawing effect of the Te atoms and the macrocyclic strain, while the telluronium acts as a strong cationic anchor. The synthon is chemically realistic, with known telluronium salts and tellurophene-containing macrocycles reported in the literature.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral telluronium cation (R3Te+) paired with an anion through anion-π interactions with a calix[4]tellurophene host. The system features: (1) a telluronium cation as the cationic recognition element (rare heavy pnictogen center), (2) a complementary anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-, or ClO4-), and (3) a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle containing four tellurophene rings that provides a convergent, electron-deficient π-surface for anion binding via anion-π interactions. The tellurophene rings enhance the electron-deficient character compared to traditional arenes, strengthening anion binding. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-binding calixarenes are repurposed via electron-deficient heterocycles to bind anions, while maintaining charge complementarity with the telluronium counter-cation. The system can be mapped to the seven primitives through electrostatic interactions (cation-anion), anion-π contacts, hydrophobic effects from alkyl substituents on telluronium, and conformational preorganization of the calixarene scaffold.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron zwitterion (boronium cation with anionic substituent) interacting with a calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle via anion-π interactions. The boronium center bears a positive charge (R3B+), while one substituent is an anionic group (e.g., borate, carboxylate, or phenolate), creating a zwitterionic structure. The anionic portion engages in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient cavity of a fluorinated calix[4]pyrrole, which acts as a π-acidic host. The calix[4]pyrrole is conformationally locked in the cone conformation and decorated with electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., pentafluorophenyl at meso-positions) to enhance π-acidity. Additional secondary interactions include C–H···F contacts and possible dipole alignment between the boronium dipole and the macrocycle dipole. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically cation-binding calixpyrroles are repurposed to bind anions via π-acidity, and the zwitterion provides both electrostatic complementarity and directional interactions.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_6
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π and chalcogen-chalcogen interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic charge and polarizability, while the calix[4]tellurophene (composed of four tellurophene rings linked at the 2,5 positions) creates a π-basic, electron-rich cavity with four tellurium atoms positioned for secondary Te···Te interactions. The synthon combines: (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and π-cloud, (2) anion-π interaction between the cationic center (acting as an 'anion hole' for counterions) and the arene π-system, (3) Te···Te chalcogen bonding between the telluronium and macrocyclic tellurium atoms, and (4) conformational preorganization of the calixarene-like structure. This represents a heavy chalcogen variant of supramolecular cation-π systems with enhanced polarizability and potential redox activity.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_7
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via synergistic anion-π and chalcogen-chalcogen interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic charge, while the electron-deficient tellurophene rings in the calixarene-like scaffold create a complementary anion-π binding pocket. The system features: 1) electrostatic attraction between cation and partial negative charge on tellurophene sulfurs, 2) anion-π interactions between Te+ and electron-deficient tellurophene π-systems, 3) secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonding between cation and macrocycle heteroatoms, 4) preorganized cavity from calix[4] conformation, 5) potential for temporal control via redox switching of tellurium oxidation states, 6) directionality from tetrahedral telluronium geometry, and 7) enhanced stability from cooperative multi-point binding. This represents a novel heavy chalcogen-based supramolecular assembly motif with potential for molecular recognition and dynamic materials.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_8
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle through synergistic anion-π and cation-π interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional electrostatic interaction site, while the calix[4]tellurophene offers a preorganized, electron-rich π-cavity with four tellurophene rings. The system exhibits umpolung characteristics: the typically π-basic calixarene-like cavity engages in anion-π interactions with the cationic telluronium's counteranion (e.g., BF4-), while simultaneously engaging in cation-π interactions with the telluronium cation itself. This creates a three-component recognition motif (cation-anion-π) with orthogonal interaction vectors. The tellurophene rings provide enhanced polarizability and potential for secondary chalcogen bonding interactions. This synthon is chemically reasonable as telluronium salts are known stable species, and tellurophene-containing macrocycles are synthetically accessible analogs of thiophene and selenophene calixarenes.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_9
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) paired with an anionic π-system derived from calix[4]tellurophene. The telluronium center exhibits strong σ-hole character along the Te–R bonds, enabling directional pnictogen bonding with electron-rich sites. The calix[4]tellurophene scaffold provides a concave, electron-rich π-surface (anion-π compatible) and four tellurophene rings that can engage in secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonding or Te···π interactions. The system combines: (1) electrostatic cation-anion attraction, (2) σ-hole pnictogen bonding from Te(IV), (3) anion-π interactions between the telluronium cation and the electron-deficient regions of the tellurophene rings, (4) potential Te···Te supramolecular contacts, (5) conformational flexibility of the calixarene-like scaffold for adaptive binding, (6) redox-active tellurium centers enabling temporal switching between Te(II)/Te(IV) states, and (7) integration of heavy chalcogen chemistry with macrocyclic π-systems for multi-modal recognition.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_10
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic anion binding to the positively charged tellurium center, and (2) anion-π interactions with an electron-deficient π-system provided by a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The calix[4]tellurophene consists of four tellurophene rings (five-membered C4Te aromatic heterocycles) linked at the 2,5-positions, creating a bowl-shaped cavity with electron-poor character due to the electronegativity of tellurium. The telluronium cation is positioned above the cavity, allowing an anion (e.g., Cl-, Br-, BF4-) to bridge between the Te+ center (via Coulombic/dative interaction) and the tellurophene π-cloud. This creates a three-component recognition motif that combines pnictogen bonding (from Te+), anion-π interactions, and macrocyclic preorganization. The system is chemically realistic as telluronium salts are known stable species, and tellurophenes are synthetically accessible aromatic systems with demonstrated electron-deficient character suitable for anion-π interactions.

synthons.name: temporal_redox_switchable_selenoxide_selenide_host_guest_synthon
synthons.description: A temporally controlled supramolecular synthon based on redox-switchable selenium chemistry. The system consists of a selenoxide-functionalized crown ether host that can be reversibly reduced to a selenide. In the selenoxide state, the Se=O group acts as a strong hydrogen bond acceptor and weak anion binding site through chalcogen bonding. Upon reduction to selenide, the selenium atom becomes a soft Lewis base capable of metal coordination and cation-π interactions with aromatic guests. The temporal control comes from electrochemical or chemical redox switching that alters the host's binding preferences between cationic (selenoxide state prefers ammonium cations via crown ether + Se=O...H-N) and anionic guests (selenide state prefers halide anions via Se...X- chalcogen bonds). This creates a time-dependent molecular recognition system with orthogonal binding modes controlled by redox state, featuring: 1) crown ether macrocycle for cation binding, 2) redox-active selenium center, 3) chalcogen bonding interactions, 4) hydrogen bonding capability, 5) π-system for stacking interactions, 6) metal coordination sites, and 7) electrostatic complementarity that flips with redox state.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_1_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via cooperative anion-π and cation-π interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic site for anion binding (e.g., halides, BF4-, PF6-), while the electron-deficient nature of the telluronium's σ-hole region (along the R-Te+ axis) can engage in secondary pnictogen bonding. The calix[4]tellurophene, composed of four tellurophene rings linked at α-positions, creates a π-basic cavity ideal for cation-π interactions with the telluronium cation. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) electrostatic cation-anion interaction, (2) anion-π interaction between the bound anion and the electron-deficient tellurophene rings, and (3) cation-π interaction between the telluronium and the π-system. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung as the typically π-basic tellurophene rings engage in anion-π interactions due to the electron-withdrawing effect of the tellurium atoms and the macrocyclic strain. This synthon is chemically reasonable as telluronium salts are known stable species, and tellurophene chemistry is established, though calix[4]tellurophenes represent an underexplored macrocyclic class. The seven primitives map as: Donor (calix π-system), Acceptor (telluronium σ-hole, anion), Positive (telluronium cation), Negative (anion), Hydrophobic (aryl groups), Aromatic (tellurophene rings), and Conformational (calixarene-like flexibility).

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_11
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The synthon features: (1) a strong electrostatic cation-anion interaction between the telluronium center and a proximal anionic site (e.g., carboxylate, sulfonate, or halide), and (2) a complementary anion-π interaction where the same anion is positioned over the electron-deficient π-surface of the tellurophene aromatic rings in the calixarene-like macrocycle. The calix[4]tellurophene scaffold provides a pre-organized, electron-poor cavity due to the incorporation of tellurium heteroatoms, enhancing anion binding affinity. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically cation-binding calixarene framework is engineered for anion recognition through heteroatom substitution and cation co-binding. The system is chemically realistic with known telluronium salt stability and emerging tellurophene chemistry, offering orthogonal recognition elements for hierarchical assembly.

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_azobenzene_anion_π_crown_ether_synthon
synthons.description: A time-dependent supramolecular synthon based on photochromic azobenzene units integrated into a crown ether framework that undergoes reversible cis-trans isomerization upon light exposure. The trans-azobenzene conformation presents an electron-deficient π-system capable of anion-π interactions with halide anions (Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻), while the cis-conformation disrupts this binding pocket and instead enhances cation binding to the crown ether oxygens. This creates a temporal switching system where UV light (365 nm) induces trans→cis isomerization, switching binding preference from anions to cations, and visible light (450 nm) or thermal relaxation reverses this. The system incorporates: (1) azobenzene photochromic units as temporal control elements, (2) crown ether macrocycle for cation recognition, (3) electron-deficient aromatic rings for anion-π interactions, (4) reversible light-induced conformational switching, (5) orthogonal binding modes (anion-π vs. cation coordination), (6) predictable kinetics (cis half-life tunable via substitution), and (7) potential for feedback-controlled assembly. This represents a true temporal synthon where binding affinity and selectivity are time-programmable via light sequences.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_12
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a telluronium cation (R3Te+) paired with an anion-π interaction to an electron-deficient calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional electrostatic interaction site for anions (halides, carboxylates), while the calix[4]tellurophene—a macrocycle composed of four tellurophene units—offers a preorganized, electron-deficient cavity for anion binding via anion-π interactions. The tellurophene rings incorporate both the heavy chalcogen (Te) for polarizability and potential secondary Te···anion contacts, and an electron-withdrawing substituent (e.g., perfluoroalkyl) to enhance the π-acidity of the cavity. This creates a synergistic, multi-point supramolecular recognition motif: (1) primary electrostatic R3Te+···anion bond, (2) secondary anion-π interaction with the tellurophene cavity, and (3) potential weak chalcogen bonding from Te sites. The system enables 'supramolecular umpolung' by using a cationic heavy chalcogen center to attract and orient anions into a complementary π-acidic host, a motif distinct from lighter chalcogen or pnictogen analogs.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_13
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π and cation-π cooperative interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic charge and potential for secondary Te···O/N chalcogen bonds. The calix[4]tellurophene host features four tellurophene rings arranged in a bowl-shaped conformation, creating an electron-rich π-surface ideal for anion binding (anion-π) while the tellurium atoms offer additional Lewis basic sites. The counter-anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) bridges the interaction by engaging in anion-π interactions with the calixarene cavity while being electrostatically attracted to the telluronium cation. This creates a three-component recognition motif with orthogonal interaction vectors: (1) electrostatic cation-anion, (2) anion-π to the macrocycle, and (3) potential secondary Te···anion or Te···π contacts. The system demonstrates supramolecular umpolung by using a typically π-basic arene for anion binding (anion-π) while cooperating with a strong cation, enabling recognition of ion pairs or charged species in non-polar media.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_14
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π and chalcogen-chalcogen interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic charge, while the calix[4]tellurophene (composed of four tellurophene rings linked at 2,5-positions) offers a π-basic, electron-rich cavity with polarizable tellurium atoms. The synthon involves: (1) electrostatic attraction between the cation and the electron-rich π-system of the macrocycle (anion-π type, but with reversed polarity), (2) secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonding between the telluronium and macrocycle tellurium atoms, and (3) potential cation-π interactions with aromatic rings. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-acidic systems are used for anion binding; here, a π-basic system interacts with a cation, stabilized by polarizable heavy chalcogen atoms. The seven primitives map as: atoms (C, H, Te), bonds (covalent C-C, C-Te; non-covalent Te···Te, cation-π), angles (tetrahedral around Te+, ring conformations), dihedrals (macrocycle folding), rings (tellurophene, calixarene-like macrocycle), cages/assemblies (host-guest complex), and groups (telluronium cation, tellurophene units).

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_15

It can be mapped to the seven primitives through its charged centers (telluronium), directional interactions (anion-π, chalcogen bonds), and preorganized macrocyclic scaffold enabling predictable supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_16
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in simultaneous anion binding through electrostatic interaction and π-stacking with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic site for anion recognition (e.g., halides, tetrafluoroborate), while the planar tellurophene rings in the calixarene-like scaffold offer extended π-surfaces for complementary stacking with electron-deficient aromatic guests. This creates a three-point supramolecular recognition motif: (1) electrostatic cation-anion, (2) anion-π between the bound anion and adjacent tellurophene rings, and (3) π-π stacking between the macrocycle and complementary arenes. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using a heavy pnictogen/chalcogen hybrid center (Te) in an unconventional +4 oxidation state to invert typical polarity patterns, enabling simultaneous stabilization of both anions and electron-deficient π-systems.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_17
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The telluronium center acts as: 1) a strong σ-hole donor for chalcogen bonding to the electron-rich tellurophene sulfur atoms, and 2) a cation for cation-π interactions with the aromatic tellurophene rings. The calixarene-like bowl-shaped conformation of calix[4]tellurophene provides a preorganized cavity that can encapsulate the telluronium cation, creating a stable host-guest complex. This represents a rare example combining heavy pnictogen (tellurium) cationic centers with heterocalixarene π-systems, exploiting both electrostatic and orbital-controlled interactions for supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_18
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π and chalcogen bonding. The telluronium center acts as a strong Lewis acidic cation, while the calix[4]tellurophene provides a concave π-surface with four tellurophene rings containing hypervalent tellurium atoms that can participate in secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonds. The system exhibits multiple recognition elements: (1) electrostatic cation-π interaction between Te+ and the electron-rich tellurophene π-system, (2) anion binding to the telluronium center (counterion mediation), (3) Te···Te chalcogen bonds between the telluronium and macrocycle tellurium atoms, and (4) conformational preorganization of the calixarene-like structure. This represents a rare example of heavy pnictogen (tellurium) centered supramolecular assembly with dual cation-π and chalcogen bonding motifs, expanding beyond the more common phosphorus/arsenic analogs.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_19
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) paired with an anionic π-system derived from a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The telluronium center acts as a strong σ-hole donor for chalcogen bonding interactions with electron-rich sites, while its positive charge enables electrostatic attraction to the electron-rich cavity of the calixarene analog. The calix[4]tellurophene provides a preorganized, electron-rich aromatic bowl with four tellurophene units, creating a complementary anion-π binding site for the telluronium cation. This system combines pnictogen/chalcogen bonding (Te···N/O/π), electrostatic attraction, and conformational preorganization for selective molecular recognition. The telluronium's redox-active nature and the tellurophene's tunable π-system offer potential for temporal control via electrochemical switching between binding states.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_20
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π and chalcogen bonding. synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_21
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The synthon features: (1) a strong electrostatic cation-anion interaction between the telluronium center and a suitable counter-anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-), and (2) a synergistic anion-π interaction where the same anion is positioned over the electron-deficient π-surface of the tellurophene rings in the calixarene-like macrocycle. The tellurophene units, being heavier chalcogen analogs of thiophene, provide a polarizable, electron-poor aromatic surface ideal for anion binding. The telluronium cation, with its pronounced σ-hole character perpendicular to the C-Te bonds, can also engage in secondary chalcogen bonding with electron donors. This creates a three-point supramolecular recognition motif (electrostatic, anion-π, and potential chalcogen bonding) that directs assembly. The system is chemically realistic, with known telluronium salts and tellurophene-containing macrocycles reported in the literature, and represents an underexplored combination of p-block cationic centers with anion-responsive π-systems for supramolecular umpolung strategies.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_22
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via synergistic anion-π and chalcogen-chalcogen interactions. Simultaneously, the positively charged telluronium is electrostatically stabilized by an associated anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-), which in turn engages in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient centers of the polarized tellurophene heterocycles. The calix[4]tellurophene scaffold provides a preorganized, concave π-surface with four tellurium atoms that can participate in secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonding with the telluronium cation, creating a multi-point recognition motif. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where the typically π-basic heterocycle acts as a π-acidic receptor for a cationic electrophile, facilitated by the polarizing effect of the tellurium atoms and the associated anion.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_cation_anion_π_calix[4]benzothiadiazole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation (R3B+) electrostatically paired with a complementary anion, both integrated into a calix[4]arene scaffold where one aromatic ring is replaced by a benzothiadiazole unit. The benzothiadiazole provides a strong electron-deficient π-surface for anion-π interactions with the counteranion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-). The boronium center acts as a strong Lewis acidic cationic site, while the calixarene cone conformation preorganizes the anion-binding pocket. Recognition elements include: (1) electrostatic cation-anion attraction, (2) anion-π interaction with the electron-deficient benzothiadiazole ring, (3) potential C-H···anion hydrogen bonds from methylene bridges, and (4) conformational rigidity of the calixarene scaffold. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung motif where typically π-basic arenes are replaced by π-acidic heterocycles to invert recognition preferences, enabling binding of anions through cooperative effects.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_23
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) paired with an anion through anion-π interactions with a calix[4]tellurophene host. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic charge, while the calix[4]tellurophene—a macrocycle composed of four tellurophene (C4H4Te) units—offers a π-electron-deficient cavity due to the electron-withdrawing nature of tellurium. The telluronium cation can be further stabilized by bulky organic substituents (e.g., aryl groups) to prevent reduction. Recognition elements include: (1) the telluronium cation (electrostatic, σ-hole), (2) the calix[4]tellurophene (anion-π, chalcogen bonding from Te), and (3) the anion. This maps to primitives: donor (telluronium), acceptor (anion), scaffold (calixarene-like macrocycle), connector (anion-π), regulator (steric bulk on Te), effector (redox-active Te), and environment (solvent polarity).

The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung, as the typically π-basic aromatic system participates in attractive interactions with anions. Recognition primitives include: (1) electrostatic (cation-anion), (2) anion-π (tellurophene Te σ-hole to anion), (3) van der Waals, (4) conformational pre-organization (calixarene-like structure), (5) geometric complementarity, (6) polarization (enhanced by heavy atom effect of Te), and (7) co-operativity between multiple interaction types.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]imidazole_synthon

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon

The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using an electron-rich π-system (typically nucleophilic) to bind anions (also nucleophilic) through polarizability and quadrupole moments, reversed from typical cation-π motifs.
