synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation (R3B+) electrostatically paired with an anion, both encapsulated within a calix[4]pyrrole host. The calix[4]pyrrole provides a π-rich, electron-donating cavity that engages in anion-π interactions with the anion and cation-π interactions with the boronium center. The boron center features three aryl substituents (e.g., mesityl groups) for steric protection and enhanced Lewis acidity upon methylation to form the cationic species. The anion (e.g., chloride, tetrafluoroborate) is held within the pyrrole-lined pocket via multiple N-H···anion hydrogen bonds and complementary anion-π contacts. This creates a stable, charge-assisted ternary complex with orthogonal recognition motifs: (1) electrostatic cation-anion attraction, (2) hydrogen bonding from pyrrole NH to anion, (3) cation-π between B+ and electron-rich pyrrole/aryl walls, and (4) anion-π between the anion and the electron-deficient faces of the cationic boron's aryl substituents. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung by using a typically Lewis acidic boron center in a cationic, electrophilic role within a preorganized host that also binds anions, enabling dual-ion recognition and templated assembly.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_30
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R₃Te⁺) paired with an anionic π-system derived from calix[4]tellurophene. The telluronium center acts as a strong σ-hole donor (pnictogen bond donor) due to its positive charge and polarizable heavy atom nature. The calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle provides a concave, electron-rich π-surface with four tellurophene rings, creating a potent anion-π acceptor site. The synthon combines: (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) σ-hole (Te⁺) to anion interaction (pnictogen bonding), (3) anion-π interaction with the tellurophene rings, (4) potential secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonding between the telluronium and macrocycle tellurium atoms, and (5) conformational preorganization of the calixarene scaffold. This represents a heavy pnictogen/heavy chalcogen hybrid supramolecular system with orthogonal interaction modes, suitable for constructing hierarchical assemblies and sensing anions in competitive media.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_31
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The synthon features: 1) A strong, directional electrostatic interaction between the positively charged telluronium center and the electron-rich π-surface of the tellurophene aromatic rings (cation-π interaction). 2) Concurrent secondary anion-π interactions, where an associated anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) interacts with the electron-deficient central cavity or the slightly δ+ tellurium atoms of the macrocycle. The calix[4]tellurophene provides a pre-organized, electron-rich concave π-surface with polarizable tellurium heteroatoms that enhance both cation binding and anion recognition. This represents a rare example of pnictogen/chalcogen-based cationic building blocks combined with a heavy chalcogen-containing macrocycle, enabling orthogonal recognition and assembly through cooperative cation-π and anion-π interactions—a supramolecular umpolung where both cationic and anionic partners are simultaneously bound to the same π-system.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon combining a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) with a calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle. The phosphonium cation serves as a strong electrostatic anchor through anion binding to chloride or tetrafluoroborate counterions, while the electron-deficient cavity of the calix[4]pyrrole engages in complementary anion-π interactions with the same anion. This creates a synergistic three-component recognition system: (1) Coulombic attraction between phosphonium cation and anion, (2) anion-π interaction between the anion and the calix[4]pyrrole's π-deficient cavity, and (3) potential C-H···π interactions between alkyl substituents on phosphorus and the pyrrole rings. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using an electron-deficient aromatic system (normally π-basic) to bind anions through anion-π interactions, while maintaining classical cation-anion pairing. This synthon enables programmable assembly through variation of phosphonium substituents (alkyl, aryl) and anion identity, mapping to primitives: electrostatic (cation-anion), anion-π, C-H···π, and van der Waals interactions.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]imidazole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraalkylphosphonium cation (e.g., tetrabutylphosphonium) paired with a calix[4]imidazole macrocycle. The synthon exploits multiple orthogonal interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction between the cationic phosphorus center and the electron-rich π-surface of the imidazole rings (cation-π interaction), (2) potential anion-π interactions if the cation is paired with a coordinating anion (e.g., BF₄⁻, PF₆⁻) that can interact with the electron-deficient cavity of the protonated imidazolium form, and (3) hydrogen bonding between the NH groups of the imidazole rings and the anion. The calix[4]imidazole scaffold provides a conformationally flexible, electron-rich aromatic cavity that can adapt to encapsulate the phosphonium cation, while the tetrahedral geometry of P⁺ prevents self-aggregation and directs binding outward. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic aromatics attract cations, but the system can be tuned to attract anions via protonation. The seven primitives map clearly: atoms (P, C, H, N), bonds (covalent P-C, N-C; non-covalent electrostatic, H-bond, π-interactions), motifs (tetrahedral cation, macrocyclic cavity), interactions (cation-π, anion-π, H-bonding), roles (cation as guest, macrocycle as host), rules (electrostatics, complementarity), and context (solvent-dependent assembly).

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_32
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π and cation-π cooperative interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional cationic site, while the calix[4]tellurophene offers a pre-organized, electron-rich π-cavity with four tellurophene rings. The synthon exploits the dual interaction: (1) the telluronium cation engages in cation-π interactions with the electron-rich tellurophene rings, and (2) an associated anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) is positioned above the centroid of a tellurophene ring, engaging in anion-π interactions. This creates a three-component recognition motif (cation-macrocycle-anion) with high directionality and complementarity, suitable for constructing supramolecular assemblies and materials. The use of tellurium in both the cation and the macrocycle explores heavy chalcogen chemistry, offering polarizability and distinct geometric constraints compared to lighter analogs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that engages in simultaneous anion-π interactions with a calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle. The calix[4]pyrrole adopts a cone conformation with its electron-deficient π-cavity oriented upward, creating an anion-binding site. The phosphonium cation positions one of its substituents to direct a positively charged phosphorus center toward the π-system of the macrocycle, while the calix[4]pyrrole simultaneously coordinates a halide anion (Cl⁻, Br⁻) via its pyrrole NH hydrogen bonds. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) electrostatic and anion-π interaction between the phosphonium cation and the electron-deficient calixarene π-surface, (2) hydrogen bonding between the calix[4]pyrrole and the anion, and (3) potential secondary C–H···anion interactions from the phosphonium alkyl groups. The system demonstrates supramolecular umpolung by using a cation to engage in anion-π interactions rather than conventional cation-π, and integrates multiple non-covalent interactions in a convergent binding site.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphole_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphorus(III) center embedded within a phosphole ring system, where the phosphorus lone pair creates a zwitterionic structure through intramolecular charge transfer with an adjacent electron-withdrawing group. This zwitterion features a positively polarized phosphorus center that engages in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient cavity of a calix[4]pyridine macrocycle. The calix[4]pyridine provides a rigid, π-acidic aromatic platform with four pyridine rings in a cone conformation, creating a complementary binding site for the phosphole zwitterion's anionic moiety. Key interactions include: (1) anion-π between the partially negative region of the zwitterion and the π-acidic pyridine rings, (2) dipole-dipole alignment between the zwitterion's charge-separated structure and the macrocycle's polarized cavity, (3) potential C-H···π contacts from the calixarene methylene bridges to the phosphole aromatic system, and (4) conformational preorganization of both components for selective recognition. This system represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic aromatic systems are inverted to π-acidic receptors for anion recognition, paired with a main-group zwitterion that provides both electrostatic and directional binding elements.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_33
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The telluronium cation acts as a σ-hole donor for chalcogen bonding with the electron-rich tellurophene sulfur/selenium analogs (Te), while its positive charge simultaneously engages in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient π-system of the tellurophene aromatic rings. The calix[4]tellurophene provides a preorganized, electron-deficient cavity that complements the telluronium's electrophilic character, creating a synergistic binding motif. This represents a rare example of combined pnictogen/chalcogen bonding (from Te(IV)) with anion-π interactions in a single supramolecular assembly.

synthons.name: temporal_photochromic_azobenzene_anion_π_calix[4]resorcinarene_synthon
synthons.description: A time-dependent supramolecular synthon based on a photochromic azobenzene-functionalized calix[4]resorcinarene host that undergoes reversible cis-trans photoisomerization, modulating its affinity for anion-π interactions with tetrahedral anions like perchlorate (ClO₄⁻) or tetrafluoroborate (BF₄⁻). The trans-azobenzene conformation creates a preorganized electron-deficient cavity with four electron-poor arene rings from resorcinarene, enhancing anion binding via anion-π interactions. UV irradiation converts the system to cis-azobenzene, distorting the cavity and reducing anion affinity, while visible light or thermal relaxation reverses the process. This creates a temporal synthon with light-switchable recognition properties, combining photochromism, host-guest chemistry, and anion-π interactions in a single dynamic system.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_4
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraalkylphosphonium cation paired with a calix[4]pyrrole anion-π receptor. The calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle adopts a cone conformation with four pyrrole NH groups oriented inward, creating a polarized electron-deficient cavity ideal for anion binding via hydrogen bonding and anion-π interactions. The tetrahedral phosphonium cation (e.g., tetrabutylphosphonium) provides a complementary electrostatic partner. The synthon combines: (1) electrostatic attraction between cation and anion, (2) anion-π interactions within the calix[4]pyrrole cavity, (3) hydrogen bonding from pyrrole NH to anion, (4) potential C-H···anion interactions from alkyl chains, (5) conformational rigidity of the macrocycle, (6) tunable cavity size via pyrrole substitution, and (7) reversible anion binding for temporal control. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically electron-rich pyrroles are arranged to create an electron-deficient, anion-binding environment.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_34
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions: (1) electrostatic attraction with an anionic species (e.g., tetrafluoroborate, perchlorate) and (2) anion-π interaction with the electron-deficient π-surface of a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The calix[4]tellurophene is a cyclic tetramer of tellurophene (C4H4Te), creating a preorganized, electron-poor aromatic cavity. The telluronium center provides strong electrophilicity and polarizability, while the calixarene-like architecture offers shape-persistent recognition. This system represents a chalcogen-bond-enhanced supramolecular assembly with potential for redox-responsive behavior due to the tellurium centers.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_borate_anion_cation_π_calix[4]quinoline_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral borate anion (e.g., B(CN)₄⁻ or BArF⁻) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a cationic π-extended calix[4]quinoline receptor. The synthon features: (1) electrostatic attraction between the borate anion and a cationic nitrogen center (e.g., N-methylpyridinium) incorporated into the calixarene upper rim, and (2) simultaneous anion-π interaction between the borate anion and the electron-deficient π-surface of the quinoline rings in the calixarene cavity. The calix[4]quinoline scaffold provides a preorganized, concave π-acidic cavity that selectively binds the tetrahedral anion through complementary shape and charge distribution. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic arenes are used for cation binding; here, electron-deficient π-systems attract anions. The system can be mapped to the seven primitives: recognition (borate shape/charge), interaction (electrostatic + anion-π), stability (chelate effect from multiple interactions), reactivity (anion activation), transformation (anion transfer), control (preorganized cavity), and time (kinetic stability of the host-guest complex).

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_35
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) that engages in simultaneous anion binding through electrostatic interaction and anion-π interactions with an electron-deficient calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic binding site for anions (Cl-, Br-, I-), while the calix[4]tellurophene scaffold, with its electron-deficient tellurophene rings and preorganized bowl-shaped geometry, creates a complementary anion-π binding pocket. This creates a synergistic three-point recognition system: (1) electrostatic cation-anion attraction, (2) anion-π interactions with the tellurophene π-systems, and (3) shape complementarity from the calixarene conformation. The system represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic arenes are replaced with π-acidic heterocycles containing heavy chalcogens, creating novel anion recognition motifs.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_36
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via anion-π interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong cationic charge, while the calix[4]tellurophene (containing four tellurophene rings) offers a concave, electron-rich π-surface due to the polarizable tellurium atoms enhancing the aromatic character. The primary recognition involves the telluronium cation's associated anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) engaging in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient faces of the tellurophene rings. Secondary interactions include Te···Te chalcogen bonding between the telluronium center and the macrocycle tellurium atoms, and potential C-H···π contacts from alkyl substituents on the telluronium. This system represents a heavy chalcogen variant of pnictogen/cation-π chemistry, exploiting the large size and polarizability of tellurium for strong, directional supramolecular assembly with potential redox-active or photoresponsive behavior.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_37
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via cooperative anion-π and cation-π interactions. The synthon features: (1) a tetrahedral telluronium cation as the cationic recognition element, (2) a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle with four tellurophene rings creating a convergent, electron-rich π-cavity, (3) an accompanying weakly-coordinating anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) that participates in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient faces of the tellurophene rings, and (4) complementary cation-π interactions between the positively charged tellurium center and the π-electron clouds of adjacent macrocycles or aromatic substituents. This creates a three-component recognition motif (cation/anion/π-system) suitable for constructing supramolecular polymers or frameworks. The heavy chalcogen (Te) provides polarizability and distinct geometry compared to lighter analogs.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron zwitterion (boronium cation with anionic substituent) that engages in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient cavity of a calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle. The boronium center bears a positive charge stabilized by three aryl groups and one anionic borate substituent (e.g., BAr3⁺-B⁻(C6F5)3), creating a zwitterionic structure. The anionic portion of the zwitterion interacts with the δ⁺ electrostatic potential surface inside the calix[4]pyrrole cavity via anion-π interactions, while the cationic boronium moiety can engage in additional electrostatic or C–H···π interactions with the pyrrole N–H edges. This system combines zwitterionic character, macrocyclic recognition, and anion-π bonding, enabling modular assembly of charged supramolecular architectures with potential for temporal control via boronate ester formation/dissociation.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_38
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an anion-π system of a calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional electrostatic interaction with an electron-rich anion (e.g., chloride, bromide). This anion is then positioned to engage in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient, bowl-shaped cavity of the calix[4]tellurophene, which contains four tellurophene rings (C4Te) creating a π-acidic surface. The system demonstrates supramolecular umpolung: the typically π-basic calixarene scaffold is replaced by a π-acidic heterocalixarene, while a heavy chalcogen-based cation (telluronium) acts as the anion-binding site. Recognition elements include: (1) the telluronium cation (electrostatic, σ-hole), (2) the anion (charge, size), (3) the calix[4]tellurophene π-acidic cavity (anion-π, conformational preorganization). This maps to primitives: A (telluronium cation), B (anion), C (π-system of tellurophene), D (macrocyclic scaffold), E (electrostatic and anion-π interactions), F (conformational selection of calixarene), G (formation of a ternary host-anion-guest complex).

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_39
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetravalent telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via dual anion-π and chalcogen-chalcogen interactions. The telluronium center bears three organic substituents (e.g., methyl, phenyl) and a weakly coordinating counteranion (e.g., BF4-). The calix[4]tellurophene host features four tellurophene rings in a cone conformation, creating an electron-rich π-cavity. Recognition occurs through: (1) anion-π interaction between the Te+ center's partial positive electrostatic potential and the π-cloud of the tellurophene rings, and (2) secondary Te···Te chalcogen bonding between the cationic Te and the neutral Te atoms of the macrocycle. This system represents a rare example of heavy pnictogen/chalcogen-based supramolecular assembly with potential for redox-switchable binding due to the accessible redox states of tellurium.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_1
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron cation (boronium ion, R3B+) electrostatically paired with an anion, with additional synergistic anion-π interactions to the electron-deficient cavity of a calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle. The boronium center acts as a strong Lewis acid-derived cation, binding halide or pseudohalide anions. The calix[4]pyrrole, in its cone conformation, provides a preorganized π-acidic cavity that further stabilizes the anion through multipoint anion-π interactions with its pyrrole rings. This creates a three-component recognition motif: (1) strong ionic bond between boronium and anion, (2) directional anion-π interactions with the macrocycle, and (3) potential C-H···anion contacts from pyrrole CH groups. The system exhibits supramolecular umpolung by using an electron-deficient π-system (normally repulsive to anions) to attract anions through anion-π interactions, working cooperatively with the cationic boronium. This synthon can direct the assembly of larger architectures through the orthogonal presentation of additional functional groups on the boronium substituents or calix[4]pyrrole upper rim.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_5
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetraalkylphosphonium cation paired with a calix[4]pyrrole anion receptor. The calix[4]pyrrole adopts a cone conformation with four pyrrole NH groups oriented inward, creating a deep electron-rich cavity. The tetrahedral phosphonium cation (e.g., tetrabutylphosphonium) provides a sterically defined, positively charged core. The primary interaction is anion-π between the phosphonium's localized positive charge and the electron-rich π-surface of the calix[4]pyrrole's aromatic rings. Secondary interactions include weak C-H···π contacts from the phosphonium alkyl chains to the pyrrole rings and potential dipole alignment from the pyrrole NH dipoles. This represents a charge-inverted host-guest system (anion-π instead of cation-π) with potential for temporal control via anion exchange or conformational switching of the calix[4]pyrrole upon binding.

synthons.name: telluronium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tellurophene_synthon_40
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a telluronium cation (R3Te+) interacting with an electron-rich calix[4]tellurophene macrocycle via cooperative anion-π and cation-π interactions. The telluronium center provides a strong, directional electrostatic interaction with the electron-rich π-surface of the tellurophene rings, while the associated anion (e.g., BF4-, PF6-) engages in complementary anion-π interactions with the same aromatic surface. The calix[4]tellurophene scaffold, composed of four tellurophene heterocycles linked by methylene bridges, adopts a cone conformation that presents a convergent, electron-rich cavity. This creates a unique 'umpolung' supramolecular environment where both a cation and an anion are simultaneously coordinated to the same π-basic surface, facilitated by the polarizable, heavy chalcogen atoms in the ring system. The synthon exhibits temporal stability due to the dynamic exchange of ion pairs, and maps to primitives: positive charge (telluronium), negative charge (anion), polarizability (tellurophene π-system), hydrophobicity (alkyl groups), shape (calixarene cone), hydrogen bonding (absent here, but can be introduced via R groups), and metal coordination (potential for Te coordination chemistry).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphole_borane_adduct_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon combining a tetrahedral phosphorus(III) center in a phosphole ring that forms a Lewis acid-base adduct with a borane group, creating a zwitterionic structure with a localized negative charge on boron. This anionic borohydride moiety engages in anion-π interactions with the electron-deficient cavity of a fluorinated calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle. The phosphole provides aromatic character and potential for further functionalization, while the calix[4]pyrrole offers a preorganized, convergent binding site. Recognition elements include: (1) B–P dative bond (Lewis acid-base), (2) anion-π interaction between [BH3]⁻ and electron-poor arene of fluorinated pyrroles, (3) potential C–H···π contacts from calix methylene bridges, and (4) dipole alignment from polarized P→B bond. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically π-basic calixpyrrole is made π-acidic via perfluorination, inverting its interaction preference to bind anions rather than cations.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_cation_anion_π_calix[4]tetrazine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation (R₃B⁺) electrostatically paired with a complementary anion (e.g., BF₄⁻ or PF₆⁻), which additionally engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with an electron-deficient calix[4]tetrazine macrocycle. The calix[4]tetrazine provides a preorganized, concave π-acidic cavity lined with four s-tetrazine units, creating a strong multi-point anion binding site. The boronium cation serves as a stable, tunable cationic center (via substituent R groups), while the anion bridges the cationic center and the tetrazine π-system, forming a three-component recognition motif. This system enables supramolecular umpolung by using an anion (typically nucleophilic) as an electrostatic bridge between two electrophilic components (B⁺ and π-acidic arena). The synthon maps to primitives: (1) boronium cation as positive charge, (2) anion as negative charge, (3) tetrazine as π-acidic surface, (4) calixarene scaffold as preorganization element, (5) electrostatic and anion-π interactions as recognition patterns, (6) tunable via R groups on boron and anion choice, (7) applicable in hierarchical assembly or responsive systems.

synthons.name: selenium_centered_chalcogen_bond_donor_acceptor_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on selenium-centered chalcogen bonding interactions, featuring a selenocyanate (R-Se-C≡N) donor group and a pyridine N-oxide acceptor. The selenium atom acts as a σ-hole donor through its electrophilic region along the R-Se-C axis, forming a directional chalcogen bond with the oxygen atom of the pyridine N-oxide. This interaction is orthogonal to potential hydrogen bonding sites, allowing for orthogonal self-assembly. The synthon combines a strong, directional chalcogen bond (Se···O interaction, ~2.5-3.0 Å) with secondary electrostatic complementarity between the electron-deficient selenium region and the electron-rich oxygen. This represents a supramolecular umpolung where typically nucleophilic selenium exhibits electrophilic character. The system is chemically realistic with known selenocyanate stability and pyridine N-oxide availability, enabling programmable assembly in crystal engineering and materials design.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron cation (boronium species, R3B+) electrostatically paired with an anion, both integrated into a calix[4]pyrrole scaffold. The calix[4]pyrrole provides a rigid, bowl-shaped π-surface for anion binding via NH···anion hydrogen bonds from the pyrrole rings, while the tetrahedral boronium center (e.g., Mes3B+) embedded in the upper rim or a bridging position acts as a strong cationic site for anion attraction or for engaging additional anionic components. This creates a synergistic, charge-assisted anion recognition pocket combining electrostatic (boronium–anion), hydrogen bonding (pyrrole NH–anion), and potential anion–π interactions with the electron-deficient aromatic walls of the calixarene-like structure. The system enables umpolung of typical anion binding—here, the cation is part of the host framework—and can be used to assemble larger architectures via anion bridging or external cation coordination.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_phosphonium_cation_anion_π_calix[4]imidazole_synthon_2
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral phosphonium cation (R₄P⁺) that engages in dual non-covalent interactions with a calix[4]imidazole macrocycle. The synthon features: (1) electrostatic anion-π interaction between the positively charged phosphorus center and the electron-deficient π-surface of the imidazole rings in the calixarene, and (2) complementary C–H···π interactions between the alkyl substituents on phosphorus and the aromatic rings. The calix[4]imidazole adopts a cone conformation, providing a preorganized cavity for cation recognition. This represents a supramolecular umpolung approach where a typically π-basic aromatic system (imidazole) is rendered π-acidic through N-alkylation or metal coordination, creating an electron-deficient cavity that attracts cations via anion-π interactions—a reversal of typical cation-π trends. The system can be mapped to the seven primitives: recognition (phosphonium and calixarene), complementarity (charge and shape), interaction (electrostatic and dispersion), stability (chelate effect), reactivity (potential for further functionalization), transformation (host-guest complexation), and reversibility (dynamic binding).

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_zwitterion_anion_π_calix[4]pyridine_synthon
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boron zwitterion (boronium cation with anionic substituent) that engages in synergistic anion-π interactions with electron-deficient calix[4]pyridine macrocycles. The boron center is sp³-hybridized with one cationic substituent (e.g., N-methylpyridinium) and three anionic groups (e.g., trifluoroborate or borate ester anions), creating a zwitterionic tetrahedral geometry. The electron-deficient pyridine rings of the calixarene provide multiple anion-π binding sites for the anionic borate moieties, while the cationic portion can engage in additional electrostatic or cation-π interactions. This system demonstrates supramolecular umpolung by using an anionic component (typically repelled by electron-rich π-systems) to bind strongly to electron-deficient aromatic surfaces, creating a directional, charge-complementary assembly motif with potential for hierarchical organization.

synthons.name: tetrahedral_boron_cation_anion_π_calix[4]pyrrole_synthon_3
synthons.description: A supramolecular synthon based on a tetrahedral boronium cation (R3B+) electrostatically paired with an anion, both hosted within a calix[4]pyrrole macrocycle. The boronium cation engages in cation-π interactions with the electron-rich pyrrole rings of the calixarene, while the anion (e.g., chloride or tetrafluoroborate) is held within the cavity via hydrogen bonding to the pyrrole NH groups. synthons.description: A temporal supramolecular system featuring a [2]rotaxane with an extended allene axle containing two recognition sites: a dibenzo-24-crown-8 macrocycle and a secondary ammonium center. The closed temporal cycle consists of: (1) base-induced deprotonation triggers shuttling, (2) macrocycle moves to allene station, (3) acid-induced reprotonation, (4) macrocycle returns to ammonium station. The extended allene provides a rigid, linear spacer with unique polarizability that influences the shuttling kinetics and provides a secondary supramolecular recognition motif distinct from traditional aromatic stations.
